commits.subject: Natalia Lerena's own baptism: born 15 May 1834 at San Jose, the fifth child of Alejandro and Margarita

commits.body:
Seven chapters on the home page's own tree, with the joint that is missing left open: Félix Llerena and Rosalía
Aguilar of Córdoba; Sancho Llerena and María Fernández at Canelones and Montevideo (1789-1812); the house in the
Cordón and the 1866 Rosario act, ending where the tree breaks; Juan Carlos and María Lerena on the enrolment card;
Pablo Armando Lerena and Mary Septima Taylor at the Cape; Nuno Fernando at Rondebosch, Johannesburg and Germiston;
and a closing chapter for the living by relationship and town, with no dates. Every paragraph graded doc, inf or
lore; world passages marked archive or history (two history notes to approve); seven trees, four maps on the
archive's era-towns coordinates (Córdoba and Asturias from the Record Atlas); five conflicts between the archive's
own pages shown as to be confirmed.
First place: front matter after the cover in book.json, a "Start with the story" note on the home page, and
"The story" under Start in the menu (shared: site/src/layouts/Base.astro). check:story runs the kit's
checkfamilystory.py against the built page with the autolink living list, and its selftest, after check:book
(shared: site/package.json). The prose gate reads story.json as hand-edited data and allows the living ribbon
card's structural fields (chapter, glyph, origin, originGrade, person, spouseLiving).

commits.body:
The roster now records him (name, relationships; no date). The two dates a 2026-09 commit message
gave for him are replaced on /changes/ by a marker (the commit cannot be rewritten). On /taylor/

commits.subject: Living: a public source no longer makes a dated person "not living"; a gate on every birth printed without a death
commits.body:
ROOT CAUSE. The kit's living_rule.is_living returns "not living" for ANY person who carries a
public-source citation, whatever the birth year, so a person aged 78 with no death recorded would
be published as dead with their year and records (Mazza leaked a man this way). build-people.py
and livingcheck.py now withhold the citations from the rule for anyone with a birth year
(cites_for_living); an undated person is unchanged. The kit is not edited; its gap is reported.
WHY OTHER PAGES PRINTED A DATE THE PERSON PAGE DID NOT. The rule reads a birth year from the
register and the chart's working files only. A year typed into a commit message (which /changes/
prints word for word), a passenger-list transcription or a research note is in neither, so that
person had no year, was "not living", and the standard gate had no name to look for.
tools/check-living-years.py starts from the SHAPE of a birth in the text (b. YEAR, born ...,
(YEAR-), birthDate) and fails when one on or after the living line (this year minus 80, derived
once in livingcheck.current_cutoff) has no death beside it, in any built page, data file or
tracked file. data/living-year-allow.json registers the people the data records dead but no
page prints (for David to confirm; no tool adds a death). build-changes.py withholds a roster
person's dates from a commit message before /changes/ prints it. In the build chain after
check:living-standard; 26 new planted-fault controls in test-living-gates.py (89 in all) and 4
in plant-faults.py; two older controls that planted nothing now plant. /method/ no longer says
a public source makes a known-year person not living.

commits.subject: The third child of Ramon Fernandez and Maria Lerena, the fourth daughter of the 1853 petition, and the family's baptisms at Trinidad 1858-1866
commits.body: Walked all 238 images of Santisima Trinidad Baptism Records October 1857 - August 1866 (film 008163892, item 3) by their machine transcripts: Ramon de la Asuncion Fernandez (born 14 August 1859), Jesus Modesto del Carmen (January 1866, the third of the 'tres hijos mayores de edad' of 1887), Maria's sister Natalia Lerena and her husband Manuel Vaquero, whose son Manuel Indalecio (born 21 May 1862) is very likely the procurador Manuel Vaquero of 1892 and 1902, and about twenty baptisms of the cousins' children (log only). A second Ramon Fernandez, married to a Maria Teresa, is told apart. Ramon the younger's civil record of 4 March 1911 is indexed. Local check:standard still reads L2 123 against floor 122 as at the previous commits; this adds none.

Maria Lerena's husband is Ramon Fernandez, her first cousin: the Trinidad baptism of their daughter, July 1857
commits.body:
Found by stepping through film 008163892 (Trinidad Baptism Records 1848-1857) and scanning each image's machine index while looking for Vitalino Lerena (not found in 1849-1857):
image 229, 'Maria del Carmen, que nacio el dia diez y seis del que rige, e hija legitima de Ramon Fernandez y de Maria Lerena, naturales y vecinos de esta Parroquia. Abs. Pat.s Manuel
Fernandez y Maria de los Reyes Gonzales, Mat.s D.n Alejandro Lerena y D.a Margarita Fernandez, y fueron los Pad.s Serapio Fernandez y Socorro Lerena'. Ramon is a son of Manuel
Fernandez Alvarez, Margarita's brother, as Serapio is, so two Lerena sisters married two first-cousin brothers. By-catch from the same scan: Estefania Lerena godmother at Trinidad in
October 1850 beside Ramon Fernandez, and a Clara Lerena godmother in 1852. The dispensation for Maria and Ramon (before 1857) is the lead. Rows for Ramon and the daughter;
earlier 'husband not named' statements marked superseded; pair reasons from each row's own birth year; linking-standard floor locked at the lower count.

commits.subject: Marcos de Leon Gonzalez: a Canary Islander, Maria Josefa's brother, married to Margarita's sister Casilda at San Jose in 1815
commits.body:
Found from the index and read at the plate on a certified copy of the San Jose marriage act of 17 December 1815 (the index misdates it): 'D. Marcos Leon Gonzalez,
natural de las Islas de Canarias, hijo legitimo de Marcial de Leon Gonzalez y de Da. Isabel Lorenzo Araquea, con Da. Casilda Fernandez Alvarez, natural de esta Villa e hija
legitima de Don Juan Fernandez Alvarez y de Dona Barbara Sotura ya difunta'. So Marcos is Alejandro Lerena's maternal uncle AND his wife's brother-in-law, which is why he
stood godfather in 1825 and 1827, and why the eldest child is Maria CASILDA. Barbara Sotura was already dead in 1815, so her 'alive at 1825' tier is withdrawn. Rows for
Casilda, Marcial, Isabel and four godparents; aliases for stated spellings (not 'Alexandro Florencio', which raised two pages' name counts); an era-ground row for the
Canary Islands; the linking-standard floor locked in at the lower counts.

Maria Casilda, baptised at San Jose on 11 April 1827: the eldest of Alejandro and Margarita's five, identified with the Maria of the 1892 death act
commits.body:
Film 008163861, image 792 of 815 (San Jose de Mayo Baptism Records 1822-1828), read at the plate: 'bautice solemnemente a Maria Casilda, hija legitima de Alexandro
Lerena y Margarita Fernandez. Abuelos paternos Ramon y Maria de Leon. Maternos Juan [y] Barbara Sotura. Padrinos Marcos de Leon Gonzalez y [Maria] Fernandez Albarez'.
No birth date is written, so she was born on or before that day; the 1892 age of 64 was about a year low. Identification with the Maria of 1892 is strong and not proved.
The godmother is Margarita's own sister; 'Maria de Leon' and 'Maria Gonzalez' are almost certainly one grandmother. Every child of the couple now has a baptism.
The film is listed in the sources file; two new same-name pairs are reasoned.

Sampling the links: a name that starts a longer name, or is a given name and the family surname, goes to the people list; record labels; old roll numbers are not films
commits.body:
- tools/run-autolink.py: a name that is the start of another person's longer name (Arturo Lerena / Arturo Lerena Garcia) or is a given name
  and the family's own surname with nothing else (Juan Lerena, Socorro Lerena) is shared, not one person: it links to the people list
  filtered on the name, like any shared name (126 entries). A sample of 150 links had found four wrong namesake links of exactly these two
  kinds, all of them already live (the 1894 dispensation's Juan Lerena linked to a one-line row 'child of Felisa, arrived 1923')
- tools/build-records.py: a number under 3,000,000 is an old microfilm roll number, never a DGS film (film 1091419 is DGS 4531018, and the
  passage that wrote the old number is linked to the DGS by the archive's own mapping); data/record-labels.json gives the arks that
  data/record-links.tsv links to a label that describes the record, where the data's own dossier title would mislead

commits.body:
- data/lerena-register.tsv: Bartolome Munoz (the regiment's chaplain, 1793), Carlota Munoz (a godmother, 1865), and the bride of
  Candido Jaime Lerena Juanico with her parents (certificate of 15 February 1922)
- tools/run-autolink.py --standard builds the config it hands the kit from site/standard.json plus, with names.surname_words_from_register,
  every word the register writes in capitals (its mark of a surname) as names.surname_words, so a person named Given SURNAME Surname

commits.subject: Citations link to their records, held scans sit beside the passage that cites them, and the linking standard's gate holds the numbers
commits.body:
- site/src/data/records.json (tools/build-records.py): the records table, from data the archive commits (ark-to-film, film-register,
  sources-consulted, person-evidence, the arks and films its data and pages print, data/record-plates.json for the 20 family papers
  /family-papers/ publishes); the 1971 and 1973 death notices are held, no row; a FamilySearch plate is never held: link only
- tools/link-records.py (after the names are linked): a DGS or film number in a passage becomes the link to that film or image;
  data/record-links.tsv gives the exact words that become the link to a record, the passages that cite no record a reader could be
  sent to (data-cite-exempt, with a reason) and the scan placed beside a passage; the markup is the kit's Rec (a.lk-rec, data-cite,
  figure.rec-fig); src/components/Rec.astro is the archive's wrapper for authors
- site/standard.json (eleven narrative pages; /dna/ out of scope; tables read as records), site/.standardfloor.json (counts only),
  tools/build-given-names.py; npm run build ends with check:standard (run-autolink.py --standard); CI runs the kit's self-test of the gate

Bernabe Lerena's own baptism: born 10 June 1836 at San Jose, with both sets of grandparents named
commits.body:
Act 1256 (film 008143327, image 203), read at the plate: 'Bernabe ... que nacio el dia diez del mismo mes, hijo legitimo de D.n Alejandro Lerena y de Da.
Margarita Fernandez. Abuelos paternos Ramon y Maria Gonzalez. Maternos Juan y Barbara Sotura', godparents Paulino Larriera and Dolores Morales. Corrects his birth
from about 1835 (the 1897 age was a year high) to 1836. All five children of Alejandro and Margarita are now documented, four by their own baptism and Maria by
her death act; the sibship is spaced about two years until Bernabe, who follows Socorro by nearly four. The film's row in the sources file is updated.

/changes/ opt out with data-no-autolink on <main>.

after the record index and full text had not returned them. Act 149: 'Ana Estefania, de quince dias de edad, hija legitima de Alejandro Lerena y de

Pedro Antonio Lerena confirmed by the Vicario's own register; a third Pedro A. Lerena household (wife Trinidad Morales) at the Cordon, 1862-63
commits.body:
The clerk's register of dispensations, entry no. 422 under Junio de 1861, reads 'El ocho de Junio de mil ochocientos sesenta y uno, S.S. dispenso a Don Pedro
Antonio Lerena dos conciliares proclamas ... con Da. Teresa Leonard, parroquiana de la Matriz', which confirms the day and writes out the petition's 'A.'.
A full-text query rebuilt from those spellings also returned the Cordon christening of 8 February 1863 of Amelia, born 2 May 1862, to 'D. Pedro A. Lerena
y Da. Trinidad Morales, orientales', with a godmother Amelia LERENA (the index says Serena). He cannot be Teresa's husband; Pedro Lerena Vega is the best
candidate and is not merged. The 1871 Cordon death entry of a nine-year-old Amelia Lerena is cross-linked as a candidate for the same girl.

Teresa Leonard and Pedro A. Lerena's marriage dispensation, June 1861: found by full-text search, read at the plate
commits.body:
Expediente no. 422 (Libro de Dispensas, f. 110): 'Don Pedro A. Lerena ... habiendo concertado contraer matrimonio ... con Dona Teresa Leonard,
parroquiana de la Matriz', asking dispensation of two of the three banns because the bride's mother had gone to the country to nurse a sick
daughter; granted 8 June 1861. New: the marriage date (June 1861 or soon after) and a sister of Teresa. Not new: Pedro's parentage, and the marriage
act itself is still not found. The log also corrects the last three rounds: the full-text 'Something Went Wrong' was my own fullTextCountry URL
parameter; the working place filter and a note on OR-query blowups are recorded.

commits.body:
Found while searching for Teresa's own baptism (no baptism or sibling indexed: index null, not an exclusion). The La Union christening of Fermin
Rodolfo Balinas, read at the plate, gives a Teresa Leonar with father Antonio and mother Manuela Ortin, where the Lerena household's Teresa has
mother Manuela Iturriaga. Probably two women, not settled; the register row says do not merge and notes a tree profile already attached to the
1874 record. No full dates added to the row so its death tier is unchanged.

commits.subject: Eusebio Congenio Lerena, born 14 August 1816 at the Cordon: a new son of Ramon Lerena and Maria Josefa Gonzalez, read at the plate
commits.body:
The same parents-plus-birth-window query one generation up returned Alejandro's marriage (held), Manuel Lorenzo (1812, already read by this archive)
and Eusebio Congenio, new: 'hijo legitimo de [Ramon] Lerena, natural de Madrid, y de Maria de Leon Gonzalez', grandparents Salvador Lerena and Ana
de Cubas / Marcial de Leon Gonzalez, agreeing with the 1812 act's Valdemoro and Lanzarote. Rows for Eusebio, Salvador and Ana added with
parent links; Salvador and Ana carry no dates so the date tool does not mark them alive in 1816, and Maria Josefa's 1825 alive tier is
preserved. Log notes that the Manuel Lorenzo plate was re-read without checking data/ first.

commits.subject: Alejandro and Margarita Fernandez had five children: the younger Alejandro's 1829 baptism, a new sister Maria (d. 1892), and Socorro's 1921 act naming all four grandparents
commits.body:
Read at the plate from one parents-plus-birth-window index query: San Jose christening of Alexandro Florencio, born 23 February 1829 (the
index mis-keys 1823); Trinidad death act 49 of 3 May 1892 for Maria Lerena de Fernandez, 64, a daughter; Trinidad death act 116 of 8 July 1921
for Socorro, 88, born at San Jose, naming Ramon Lerena and Maria and Juan Fernandez and Barbara as grandparents. Estefania (60 in 1892) is
the elder of Socorro (88 in 1921) by a year or less, so the twin reading is less likely; not proved. Parent links added for all four
siblings; Maria and a godmother Clara Llerena entered; generated same-name pair reasons state where no birth year is held.

commits.subject: Log index nulls for Vitalino Lerena's birth and marriage; full text still down (not exclusions)
The 1867 Trinidad godparents Vitalino and Alejandrina Lerena: register candidates entered, not identified
commits.body:
Alejandrina (b. about 1852, daughter of Alejandro the younger) fits as the baby's first cousin and unmarried (no 'de Pelaez');
Vitalino Lerena of Trinidad (wife Andrea Echeverry) fits as a young man. A godparent line is a name and a role, so both are
candidates only. No marriage entry is indexed for Alejandrina and Pelaez 1860-1880 (null, not an exclusion); Vitalino's parents
are not found.

commits.subject: Log two index nulls for the Pereyra parents and a full-text outage (not exclusions)
Log a null: no marriage entry for Pedro Lerena and Teresa Leonor 1855-64 in the Catholic index (not an exclusion)
A second act names Alejandro and Margarita Fernandez as Estefania's parents: the Trinidad baptism of 1867
commits.body:
Act 303, Santisima Trinidad, read at the plate: Estefania Fausta Leopoldina, born 13 October 1867 (the clerk corrected the date in the
line), 'hija legitima de Cervando Gonzalez y Estefania Lerena ... Ab. paternos Juan y Manuela Muniz. Maternos Alejandro y Margarita
Fernandez. Padrinos Vitalino y Alejandrina Lerena'. Different parish, different priest and five years before the San Jose act, same four
grandparents; the identification now rests on two acts though still not on a document listing Estefania beside Socorro and Bernabe.
Her daughter Estefania is born 1867, so the 1930-32 Campana marriage cards are downgraded to possible and not used.

commits.subject: Estefania Lerena's parents named: Alejandro and Margarita Fernandez, at the plate of her daughter Cesarea's San Jose christening
commits.body:
Folio 198, 30 April 1872: 'hija legitima de Don Servando Gonzalez y Dona Estefania Lerena, natural de esta Villa. Ab. pt. D. Juan y
Da. Manuela Muniz: mat. Dn. Alejandro y Da. Margarita Fernandez'. The paternal pair matches the 1892 act. Identified with Alejandro
Lerena the elder and Margarita Fernandez Alvarez of Trinidad on surname, forenames, Fernandez and San Jose; no act names Estefania beside
Socorro, Alejandro the younger and Bernabe, so the tier is probable, not proved. Socorro is the same age (about 1832); twins, a stated age
out, or a younger sister are all left open. Edges, kindred row, Uruguay-page row and research log added.

commits.subject: Layout: table cells stop breaking mid-word; row headers and dates wrap and hold sensibly
commits.body: Cells carried overflow-wrap:anywhere, which lets a table column shrink to one character, so prose columns beside inline rem widths came out 62px wide and 1,000px tall and a long row header (nowrap) made a table 2,833px wide. Cells now use break-word, row headers in tbody may wrap, dates and short codes (td.mono, the When cell) stay on one line, external links and code in a cell can still break, and on a phone column labels wrap. CSS only.

commits.subject: Re-pin the kit to dabcb63: the DNA-result flag in the prose gate, refuse-on-nothing gates, the optional youngest_child_year/said_living inputs, AlsoIn and the person-page components
Teresa Leonar's husband is not Pedro Lerena Vega: the 1864 christening of their daughter names his parents as Pedro and Maria Pereyra
commits.body:
Catedral, 30 April 1864, read at the plate: Manuela, born 9 April, 'hija legitima de Pedro Lerena y de Teresa Leonar.
Abuelos Paternos Pedro y Maria Pereyra. Maternos Antonio y Manuela Barriaga'. Pedro Lerena Vega's mother was Vicenta
Vega, so the two Pedros (and the two wives, Manuela Lemos and Teresa Leonar) are two men, which closes the question
written earlier today; every 'open' statement is rewritten and the two older log rows marked superseded. Teresa had
a daughter as well as a son. Three rows added; the index's La Union is the Catedral's volume. The marriage and the
father 'Pedro' are still not found.

commits.subject: Pedro Lerena Vega was born 1 December 1828 and is named Pedro Antonio Natalio: his baptism read at the plate
commits.body:
Found as a side result of the index search for Teresa Leonar's husband. Cordon baptism of 12 December 1828, parents
Pedro Antonio Llerena (natural de Canelones) and Vicenta Vega. The row label moves from b. c.1834 to b. 1828 with no
URL change (slug kept, old key kept); his census age was six years late. Carrying Antonio, he stays a candidate for
Teresa Leonar's husband. The father's 'natural de Canelones' conflicts with the register's Montevideo birth and is
recorded as a conflict.

commits.subject: The Cordon widow of 1901 is Teresa Leonard: her civil death act names her parents, her husband's death and her son
commits.body:
Act 252 of 27 August 1901, read at the plate: Teresa Leonar de Lerena, 60, born in Montevideo, widow of Pedro Antonio
Lerena, daughter of Antonio Leonar (dead) and Manuela Iturriaga (82, alive in the same house), one son Manuel, who
declared the act as a married soldier of about 38. The Cordon clerk spelled her surname Leonor; the note that took
it for a given name, and the 11 October guess that her surname was English or Irish, are retracted. Three rows added.
Whether her husband is the Pedro A. Lerena of 1896 (wife Manuela Lemos) is a new open question; the 13 same-name
pairs are each given a reason.

commits.subject: The Servando buried at the Cordon in 1892 is Estefania Lerena's husband: his civil death act names her, his parents and nine children
commits.body:
Montevideo Death Records 1892, act 194, read at the plate: Servando Tomas Gonzalez, 65, married to Estefania
Lerena (60, born about 1832), son of Juan Nepomuceno Gonzalez and Manuela Muniz, declared by his son-in-law
Damaso Negrotto and by his lawyer son Leopoldo Gonzalez Lerena, who signed. The two earlier 'candidate'
statements are rewritten as confirmed and marked superseded in the log; the doubt about the 1930-32 Campana
cards is retracted (they are the daughters). Seven rows added; Leopoldo's birth moved to about 1863.
Estefania's own parents are still not found.

commits.subject: Corina Francisca's 1858 baptism read at the plate: Estefania Lerena is named in the act, the index had lost her surname
commits.body:
Trinidad, 31 August 1858: 'hija legitima de Servando Gonzalez y de Estefania Lerena, orientales'.
Corina moves from probable to confirmed and gets her own row; the index's 'Nefania' was the garble.

commits.subject: Estefania Lerena's daughter married at Trinidad in 1884: the Gonzalez family was there from 1858
commits.body:
Index-level. Esperanza Gonzalez (26) and Damaso Negrotto added; the parents are entered as
Servando Santa Marina Gonzalez and Estefania Lerena. Estefania's own baptism is not in the index.
A family-tree user's 'Lerena Fernandez b. 1832' attachment is recorded as unsourced and not used.

commits.subject: Regenerate the public search index after the Gonzalez rows
The San Jose couple tested against the 1892 Cordon burial: children 1854-1872, two sons dead at Montevideo
commits.body:
Index-level: Leopoldo (d. 1922, father of Juan Carlos Gonzalez Lerena) and Servando Cecilio (d. 1911)
are added with his wife. The candidate survives and is stronger, and is not merged; the 1930-32
Campana index cards that give the same parents are flagged as unexplained.

commits.subject: Regenerate the changes log after the collection-level row
Log the two Larranaga civil acts at collection level, so the atlas can mark them
Regenerate the search index and changes log after the Larranaga rows
Martina Lerena's husband was a Spaniard who died in 1885, and her son was a coachman: two civil acts read at the plate
commits.body:
An exact-phrase full-text search on Martina Lerena found the Montevideo civil death act of 29 March 1885:
Benito Larranaga, Spanish, seventy, married to Martina Lerena, Oriental, thirty-nine (so born about 1846),
with seven children named. Her son Jose Maria's own civil act (no. 121, 1 August 1890) gives his trade,
cochero, and a death of consumption. Six siblings are added as named-only rows. Martina's baptism is not in
the index for 1840-1852 and her parents are still unfound; the Sinforiano forename search is recorded as
too wide to be a handle.

commits.subject: Regenerate the search index and changes log after removing the Booyzen page
Families: Lerena points to the Booyzen archive instead of a one-person Booyzen page
commits.body:
The Booyzen line has its own archive with its own pages; a page here repeated it for one person. The
page, its menu entry, its families.json and families.tsv rows and the marriages-page link are removed,
and /families/ now has a Booyzen row that links to the Booyzen archive's page. Temple stays.
All gates pass (tools/verify.sh).

commits.subject: check-families: tolerate Astro's scoped-style attributes when planting its faults
Merge origin/main into family-pages
Twelve family pages: Brayley, Temple, Booyzen, Fernandez, Pelaez, Gonzalez, Lenguas, Cardozo, Juanico, Traibel, Alvarez, Larriera
commits.body:
Built from the register (src/lib/families.js, data/families.tsv): who carries each name, where, between which
years, how the archive knows them, which other families they are joined to, and where the archive already writes
the family up. A /families/ index on the kit's Families card, a The families menu group (the Taylors moved into it),
the Marriages page pointing at each, and tools/check-families.py: a second reckoning of who each page may list,
with nine planted faults, wired into the build.

commits.subject: The Cordon death and burial pages are all opened: seven new people, and the four of Sarandi 229 are not in them
commits.body:
Eleven more of the thirteen pages full text returns for the surname are read, six at the plate.
New: Jose Maria Larranaga (buried 1890, son of Benito and Martina Lerena), Sara Lerena (1892, hija
natural de Teresa Lerena), Jose Maria Reyes and Maria Lerena (1920). Candidates, not merges:
Servando Gonzalez m. Estefana Lerena (1892) for the San Jose couple, and Teresa Leonor de Lerena
(1901, the plate says Leonor) for Teresa Leonard. Carlos Alberto Fein was buried 18 May 1919, 27
years before the registration that named him. Julia Juanico's burial gives her age 62 against 67.
Amelia Lerena (1871) upgraded from transcript to plate. The four adults are not found, and the
errand says that is a limit on the instrument, not a null on the books.

commits.subject: The Gazette sweep on nine spellings: still not one Lerena before 1951
commits.body:
Every year 1905 to 1950, through the site's own search and its year filter. The control
reproduced the earliest LERENA (April 1951). The other eight spellings return places,
given names and OCR debris. Stronger than the one-spelling null of 12 October, still not
a closed one: the 1950 estate notice does not turn up under any spelling either.

commits.subject: Two wrong death dates are logged in the corrections ledger
Six findings from the cloud audit, checked on the live pages
commits.body:
Four were real; one was a lag in this archive's own build; one is not a duplicate.
- A mother's page said she died in 1910: that is her DAUGHTER's death, lifted out of her note
  by the death parser. The note is reworded; she has no recorded death.
- A second woman's page said she died in 1933 (her first husband's death, same cause); she
  died in 1950, which her note now says.
- Both of those made children 'born after the mother's death' on three pages.
- The machine-indexed alias of the founder carried parent edges the parents did not return;
  an alias is not a child, so the two edges are removed and the alias keeps its pointer.
- Two ship passengers of the same name and birth year, sixteen years apart, are declared a
  pair that is not merged and not settled, with the reason.
- verify.sh ran last-alive.py near the end but build-people.py read its output near the
  start, so every page's death date was one run behind the register. It now runs first.
Not changed: the two 'parent over 55' items (a father, labelled father); a man the Booyzen
archive also holds (the two archives share a marriage on purpose).

commits.subject: The generated data files now carry the trimmed prose too
commits.body:
The build regenerated 8 data files from the trimmed data after the last commit; the deploy
builds from these, so they have to travel with it. Same change, no new content.

commits.subject: The living standard now covers what is typed, not just what is built
commits.body:
Adopts the kit's prose gate (checkprose.py, kit 575409a) through tools/check-prose.py,
which writes the feed of who is living OUTSIDE the repository on every run, from the
raw data and living_rule.py, and adds one supplement the kit skips by design: a living
person's given name alone, beside a date or life-event word. In verify.sh and in CI;
exit 2 (not run) fails both.
Trimmed only what went past the standard (name, relationships, town and country): 4 pages
(/direct-line/, /estate/, /family-papers/, /hypotheses/), 11 data files, 6 notes and the
README. The person is now named by relationship ("his daughter") wherever a statement,
age, date or DNA result sat beside a name; the testimony itself is kept.
Gate result: 110 files read, 5 living phrases, 30 places name a living person, 0 fail, 0
allowances; supplement 108 files, 24 places, 0 carry a detail. Four planted faults (a name
beside a year, a given name beside a full date, a name beside a life-event word, an emptied
roster) all fail the gate; the emptied roster exits 2, never a pass.

commits.subject: Re-pin the kit to 575409a (the prose gate: checkprose.py)
Change log regenerated after the kit re-pin
The 1942-44 war diaries were read by machine: no Lerena, and it proves little
commits.body:
2,892 images from four digitised pieces, each checked against TNA's image ranges,
run through text recognition and searched with fuzzy matching for the surname and
for the other archives' surnames. Near-misses were checked on the page images
(A/Sgt Levin, Mc Laren). Crew lists name aircrew, not ground crew, so this does
not show he was not in 12 Squadron. Scans kept outside the repository.

commits.subject: Re-pin the kit to 27af004
commits.body:
The kit gates now refuse to pass on nothing: a GEDCOM date in capitals is
caught, an empty sitemap, a crashed astro check, an empty template root and a
page floor of 15 all fail instead of passing. Built clean through the full gated build,
with the installed kit checked, not only the lockfile.

commits.subject: The 1943-44 war diaries are in a basket and waiting on David's sign-in
commits.body:
Four free PDFs, about 1.8 GB (AIR 54/52, 53, 54 and 185). TNA says free downloads
need a sign-in or registration, and this archive does not sign in or register, so
the order stopped at checkout. Licence: private research only, never republished.
The scans have no text layer and this machine has no OCR.

commits.subject: The Documentation Centre email and the SAAF Forum read are recorded as research
commits.body:
Two rows in searched.json, so the atlas importer marks them: the email to the
SANDF Documentation Centre (written, waiting, no reply) and the forum read (found).
The forum post itself is still only a draft.

commits.subject: Twelve Squadron's war diaries are mapped: eight books could cover Nuno
commits.body:
The National Archives catalogue lists 16 items for No 12 Squadron SAAF in AIR 54;
the eight for 1942 to 1945 sit in six digitised pieces. Recorded in searched.json,
the war-service errand and the work list. Not opened: the downloads are large and
need David's say-so, and an operations record book names aircrew far more than
ground crew, so a miss would not disprove service.

commits.subject: A living man's family history and parentage inference are out of the repository
commits.body:
At David's request, alongside the estate's living standard (which removed the date):
the paragraph about her first husband's family and a DNA-based inference about his
parentage, from her row in data/direct-line.tsv and from notes/findings.md; the
family's movements and marriages from the README and notes; and the paragraph on
/south-africa/ that named living people moving to Brisbane. Her row keeps what the
standard allows (a name, relationships, a town). Whether to go further, to a name
only, is David's call.
Not removed: old values remain in git history on GitHub.

commits.subject: Re-pin the kit to fcf629a
commits.body:
User-built trees that MyHeritage files under research (Geni World Family Tree,
WikiTree, Filae, GenealogieOnline) are no longer counted as public record sources
by the shared living rule. Built clean through the full gated build at the new pin,
with the installed kit checked, not only the lockfile.

commits.subject: Harness: full builds use the default output the repo's own checks read
Merge origin/main (aa5057e) into living-v2
commits.body:
check-living-places keeps the v2 rule and gains the refuse-at-zero behaviour (an empty build,
an empty roster); tools/plant-faults.py's living cases now plant the v2 faults (living.json
no longer exists, and no real date is a literal in any tracked file). The new CI steps for
errands, nulls and addresses are kept.

commits.subject: Harness: copy the notes, and prove the known-child ruling
Declare the living roster as a generator input, not a page
Living standard: no living person's date in any public file; a roster records who is living
commits.body:
The living person's birth date is removed from the three working files that held it (and a
year from the findings notes), without touching their research prose. Who is living is
recorded in data/living-roster.tsv (name, slug, town, country, no date) and the generator
refuses a roster row for anyone the data records dead. The gates fail if a date or year sits
against a living person's name in any tracked file or built file, and refuse an empty or
dated roster. A known child follows the standard like any living person; only an undated
person with a living parent is held out. The harness plants a date back in each of the four
files and a fault for every roster rule.

commits.subject: Re-pin the kit to 6cefc79 (a known child follows the standard; the National Archives of Australia)
Twelve checks passed when given nothing, and three never ran in CI
commits.body:
Planted one fault in each of 28 checks (54 faults; tools/plant-faults.py re-runs
it). First pass: 23 of 42 caught. Twelve repo tools printed "0 examined" and
passed on an empty input; check-nulls could not see a four-word name. Each now
prints what it examined and refuses at zero, with a floor where the input only
grows. check-errands, check-nulls and check-addresses ran only in the local gate;
they are now CI steps. Now 50 of 54 caught; the four that are not (last-alive and
drift by design, two kit checks) are listed in notes/.

commits.subject: Living standard: gates enforce the new rule and are shown to fail
commits.body:
check-living-places is inverted (a living person must show their town and country,
and no other place); check-living-standard is new (noindex, sitemap, search index,
JSON-LD, table, image, year, full dates, held-out people, named people with pages).
Both reckon who is living independently of the generator. test-living-gates plants a
fault for every rule.

commits.subject: Living standard: a living person's page is a name, relationships, a town and a country
commits.body:
Person, name, people, register pages and the chart render the shared rule; the
spine links every name; the About, method, footer, README and home sentences say
what the archive now does.

commits.subject: Living standard: the generator applies the shared rule and scrubs a living person at the source
commits.body:
Who is living is now the kit's living_rule.py over the register's births, deaths and
citations, not a hand-set cell. A living person leaves build-people.py as a name,
relationships, town and country; a possible minor is held out. The two people
recorded dead only by a burial registration are read as dead. Nine people the chart
already named get pages (the third generation, its parents and spouses). The old
living.json, which held a living person's birth date, is gone.

commits.subject: Re-pin the kit to 0a56c86 (one definition of who is living)
A SAAF Forum post drafted, and the squadron diaries found
commits.body:
The forum needs an account to post and this archive does not register or sign in,
so the post is a draft for David. It names no living person and gives no address.
The forum's sticky thread led to the UK National Archives' AIR 54 squadron
operations record books, the unit-side route for 12 Squadron; added to the
war-service errand.

commits.subject: Change log regenerated after merging the kit and page updates
The Documentation Centre email has gone, and the errand now says so
commits.body:
Sent on 16 October from David's own address, with Nuno's birth and death
certificates in the body. Its address is unconfirmed on any current official page,
so the errand tells David to watch for a bounce; the postal letter stays a draft
as the fallback.

commits.subject: Re-pin the kit to 3efc89e
commits.body:
Picks up the kit's accessibility defaults: work-list state colours that clear AA in
both schemes, person-tree tiles that follow the panel colour, external links in

commits.subject: emph(): keep escaping quotes, so a literal href="/x/" in a note stays text (the link checker read it as a link)
Contrast: muted ink and label colours reach 4.5:1 in both schemes; labels under 10px go to 11px
commits.body:
--ink-3 (and --ochre, four place-tag colours) darkened in the light scheme, --ink-3
lightened in the dark one; text on accent fills, person-chart nodes (--paper), the
work-list state colours, errand tags and Leaflet attribution fixed for dark.

commits.subject: Render markdown and entities properly: emph() now goes through the kit's md()
commits.body:
Backticks, **bold** and *italic* printed their markers on 11 pages; the register
and /sources/ printed markup as text (double-escaped); the name page's chart
tooltips and the open-questions arrow labels printed entities. Text is not
edited: only how it is rendered.

commits.subject: Phone width: person pages and /sources/ no longer scroll sideways at 390px
commits.body:
The person pages' provenance column (.rec .w) is nowrap and the one-column grid
track could not shrink below it, so all 692 pages overflowed. Tracks now use
minmax(0,1fr) and the note wraps under its value on a phone. /sources/: let a

commits.subject: Re-pin the archive kit to 9c66e9c (sitemap leaves out pages whose canonical names another page)
The "Air Force's own page" was an unofficial fan site
commits.body:
The Documentation Centre letter said its address was checked against the Air
Force's own page. The site's footer calls itself the unofficial website on the
South African Air Force. The postal address also appears in the Department of
Defence's own (dated) access-to-information manual, so it stands; the email
addresses are confirmed on no current official page and are no longer relied on.
Logged in corrections. An email version is in David's Gmail drafts, unsent.

commits.subject: A sixth letter, for Nuno's service record, drafted and left for David to send
commits.body:
To the Defence Documentation Centre in Pretoria, by post. The postal address is
checked against the Air Force's own page; the email is hidden there and two other
sources disagree, so none is used. The letter asks them to say what permission and
fee they need rather than asserting rules this archive could not verify. It names
no living person, and it needs David's address, signature and two certificate

commits.subject: Printed pages now show the archive's own address, not the old github.io one
commits.body:
Kit pinned to 8fdc6b0, which prints only the path in print.css and emits the full
rule from the archive's origin. Built output: 1,496 real pages carry the rule with
lerena.defranceski.com; the other 24 are redirect stubs. daviddef.github.io
remains only in this archive's own /method/ and /changes/ prose.

commits.subject: Nuno's documents stacked in one column at desktop width
commits.body:
The grid used minmax(280px,520px), which a browser sizes by the 520 maximum, so a
1,024px column fitted one track and seven scans ran down the page. Now two columns
from about 800px, one below.

commits.subject: A 1916 marriage extract says 1905, and Nuno's papers now sit on his page
commits.body:
David supplied Nuno Fernando's birth, marriage and death certificates, identity
card, headstone, wedding invitation and a 1971 notice from 12 Squadron S.A.A.F.,
and a further set for Pablo Armando and Mary Septima. Person pages can now show
documents (site/src/data/person-documents.json), and /family-papers/ carries two
tables of what each one reads, adds and does not add.
The one to read first: St Dominic's extract certified 7 April 1916 gives the
marriage as 3 September 1905; the register has the same day, priest and
witnesses and the year 1911. 1911 stands on the ages and Roque's baptism.
Not published, by rule: the 1971 notice and tennis cutting (name the living), the
1997 letter (a private address), the UK passenger list (National Archives), two
2026 photographs (living people). The 1925 'Taylor, Mary S.' passenger is a weak
candidate, not an identification. A Queensland marriage certificate and a Croatian
parish page in the folder belong to other archives and were left out.

commits.subject: Person-page columns collided at tablet width
commits.body:
Found by looking at a rendered page at the pane's width: on every person
page, the grey provenance notes in "What the record says" ("as the record
gives it") ran underneath the "Where this comes from" column beside them.
MEASURED, not eyeballed: at an 800px viewport the grid gives each column
357px, but a row needs about 480px - a label, a value, and a right-aligned
provenance note set nowrap on purpose. The notes reached x=486; the next
column began at x=400. At 1280px the columns are 505px and nothing crosses,
which is why no desktop check could see it, and below 600px the grid already
collapses, which is why a phone check could not either. It lived in the band
between.
The two columns now stack below 1060px, the width at which each first gets
495px. That is the whole fix: the nowrap stays, because a wrapped provenance
note is a ragged right-hand column, and a stacked page is simply full width.

commits.subject: Person pages opened with their whole note, then printed it again
commits.body:
Found by looking at a rendered page. Leonarda's opened with a 25-line wall of
unemphasised text, and no width, overflow or broken-image measurement could
have seen it: the page was technically fine.
people/[slug].astro passed the ENTIRE note as the page's dek - the line under
the title, and the page's meta description - and then printed the same note
again, with its emphasis, under "What is known". 588 of 692 people have a
note over 160 characters; 112 are over 1,500; the longest is 21,547. So most
person pages opened with a block of plain text that the page then repeated,
and every one carried that block as its search-engine description.
A new lead() in lib/text.js takes the first sentence when it is a sensible
length and otherwise cuts at a word boundary. Notes of 160 characters or fewer
come back whole, exactly as before; the full note is still printed with its
emphasis in its own section, so nothing is lost.
RESULT, MEASURED ON ALL 692 BUILT PAGES: the median opening is 106 characters
and the maximum 230, down from 21,547.
THE FIRST VERSION WAS WRONG IN A WAY THE MEASUREMENT CAUGHT. It treated any
full stop before a capital as a sentence end, so it cut six pages off
mid-name - "...named by the cura Dr." and "...recorded as D." - because Dr.
and D. were read as sentence ends. The splitter now skips honorifics,
abbreviations and lone-capital initials (Pedro A. Lerena). My first test of
the fix used strings shorter than the 160-character threshold, so they came
back whole and tested nothing; redone with realistic long notes. Zero of 692
pages now end on an abbreviation or run over.

commits.subject: Dates that would have been wrong by next week, and three that were wrong already
commits.body:
Found by the checklist: 139 phrases across 60 files said "this morning",
"yesterday", "an hour ago" or "on Monday" in permanent site copy. Relative to
nothing, they read wrongly within days. One heading said a woman was "found
on Monday"; it is a Tuesday.
THE REWRITE IS DATED BY GIT, NOT BY GUESSWORK. Each phrase was dated by the
first commit that introduced that exact string, "yesterday" counted back a
day, and "on Monday" resolved to the Monday it meant (12 October), not the
commit date. 27 phrases in 7 files were anchored to explicit dates. A
dry run printed every replacement first, and caught the one the script would
have got wrong - "on Monday" had mapped to the commit date.
90 MORE WERE LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE. They predate this session, and git blame
cannot date them: a long TSV row last edited today can hold a "yesterday"
written in September, so a mechanical rewrite would put wrong dates on the
site, which is worse than the vagueness. 13 remain in files touched this
session; they are older text, reported rather than guessed at.
AND THE CHECK EXPOSED THREE FACTUAL ERRORS IN MY OWN PUBLISHED COPY, which
the rewrite alone would have papered over:
 - /method/ said the dispensation novelty claim was published "on 11
   October". Git says Mon 12 Oct 12:00, corrected 12:26 - twenty-six minutes
   later, the same day. The corrections log said "published yesterday". The
   data file said "yesterday" in two places.
 - /name/ said the variants table was published on 11 October and turned on
   the central question on 12 October. Both happened on 12 October, at 11:05
   and 11:44.
All now say what the timestamps say.

commits.subject: The link checker had been reading nothing since the move, and said "ok"
commits.body:
Reported by a sibling session who found the same fault in Booyzen, where it
failed silently and committed wrong data. Measured here before any change:
    internal hrefs in the built site .......... 136,414
    examined by tools/check-links.py ..........       0
tools/check-links.py hard-coded BASE = "/TheLerena" and skipped every href
that did not start with it. After the move to base "/" every link is
root-relative (/about/), so EVERY cross-page link, every asset and every
fragment was skipped. For about a day the only thing it checked was same-page
#anchors and the contents lists. It kept printing "ok" because it guarded
against an EMPTY dist but not against a full one it could not see into.
THE FIX READS THE BASE FROM site/astro.config.mjs, as Booyzen did, treats
root-relative hrefs as internal (never protocol-relative ones), refuses to
guess if it cannot find a base, and FAILS if it examined fewer than 1,000
links. The real figure is ~136,000, so the floor never fires on a healthy
build; it exists so a blind pass can never be mistaken for a clean one. The
count is now printed in verify.sh's output.
PROVEN CAPABLE, NOT ASSUMED. It now examines all 136,414 and finds 0 broken -
the site really is clean - so the first run proves nothing about the gate.
In a scratch copy with three faults planted (a dead page, a dead fragment, a
missing stylesheet) it reports all three. And the OLD base against the same
tree now exits 1 with "examined only 0 internal links (floor 1000)" rather
than passing, which is the future case the floor is for.
THE KIT'S OWN checkarchive WAS NEVER BLIND and was tested the same way:
it reports the same three planted faults. Only this repo's two local tools
were.
tools/audit.py HAD THE OPPOSITE FAULT. It built routes as "/TheLerena" + path
and compared them with root-relative links, so its orphan check reported
1,519 pages as linked from nowhere - every page on the site. A report that
cries wolf on everything is as useless as silence, since it buries a real
orphan under 1,518 fakes. It reads the base too now, and skips redirect
stubs, which are unlinked on purpose: all 24 remaining "orphans" were stubs.
Findings fell from 1,523 to 4, and there are zero genuine orphans.

commits.subject: Body text now runs the full width of the column, and the letters are findable
commits.body:
David asked for text to run full width. It did not, and it can be measured.
AT A 1600px VIEWPORT THE CONTENT COLUMN IS 1,024px. Headings, tables, panels,
key-value lists and code blocks all fill it. But the 179 paragraphs on
/uruguay/ were 730px - about 71% of the column - because styles.css capped
.prose at 80ch, .dek at 76ch, .cap at 92ch and .note at 82ch. Callouts were
narrower than the paragraphs beside them and paragraphs narrower than the
headings above them.
THE FIX LIFTS THOSE FOUR CAPS and leaves display type alone (.lead, the hero
and opener headings, the footer). The trade-off is real and written into the
stylesheet: a line can now run to ~110 characters, longer than the usual
75-80 recommendation. One line on .prose restores a cap if it reads too wide.
THE LETTERS WERE 21,000px DOWN THE ERRANDS PAGE, beneath every other errand,
which is not what "add them to my errands page" meant. A callout at the top
now says five letters are waiting, which two cannot go yet and why, and
jumps to them. And the letter bodies were in monospace; they are in the body
typeface at a readable size, since they exist to be copied into an email.
Also in this commit, from the same checklist: Leandro Lerena and Lucia
Llanos added to the unplaced lines on /name/, as a fourth Spanish arrival
not shown connected to the three the Spain lane already draws.

commits.subject: Twelve published edges cited a census date that was withdrawn, and 33 new people had no family
commits.body:
Found by the checklist David asked for, and both are real.
1 · A RETRACTION THAT HAD NOT PROPAGATED. data/relations.tsv still drew Emilia,
    Pedro and Vicenta LERENA Vega as children of Pedro Antonio, son of Sancho,
    in twelve edges whose notes said "household 229 of the c.1833 census".
    That date was withdrawn on 12 October - the household is the padron of
    1850, libro 264 - and the identification of its head with Sancho's son was
    published as UNRESOLVED, since he is entered at 40, which fits a man born
    about 1810, not 1793. The pages were still asserting both.
    The edges are KEPT, because the couple's names (Pedro A. Lerena, Vicenta
    Vega) are genuinely what the census reads and Leonarda b.1837 is tied to
    Pedro Antonio by an 1837 baptism - but every note now says it is a
    CANDIDATE, gives the correct date, and points at /corrections/.
2 · A PAGE IS NOT A CONNECTION. 36 people were added this session and 33 had
    a page but no relationship drawn, including people explicitly named as
    someone's child or spouse in acts that were read at the plate - Salvador
    is "hijo legitimo" of Leandro Lerena and Lucia Llanos on his own baptism.
    No gate saw it: check-evidence only fails when a person NAMED in
    relations.tsv has no edge, never the reverse.
    77 edges written, in the file's convention of both directions, each
    carrying how it is known. Only what a record states is drawn; the weaker
    ones say so on the edge itself - INDEX-LEVEL where no act was opened,
    INFERRED for the younger Xavier Lavina's parents, CANDIDATE for his
    marriage to Leonarda, and a household census listing carries a note that
    a census does not state kinship.
    SIX PEOPLE ARE LEFT ISOLATED ON PURPOSE: the declarant and witness of the
    1896 death act, Amelia (nine, parents unnamed), and the four adults of
    casa 229 of Calle Sarandi, whose kinship to anyone no record states.
    An isolated person is the honest picture for them.
The first isolation test used field names that do not exist on a person
(parents, kin), reported 33 of 36, and would have reported every person in
the register as isolated. It was caught by running it against Pablo Armando as
a control before trusting it, and redone with the real fields.

commits.subject: Estate-wide cleanup of old github.io addresses: robots.txt, three siblings, the atlas
commits.body:
Requested by the landing-site session, who measured two faults here and were
right about both. Verified in this repo before anything was changed.
1 · robots.txt STILL NAMED THE OLD SITEMAP. site/public/robots.txt said
    Sitemap: https://daviddef.github.io/TheLerena/sitemap.xml, live as well as
    in source. The kit's sitemap.py only writes robots.txt when none exists,
    so the old origin survived the move untouched. A crawler following it
    would have been handed a sitemap of a host that now redirects.
2 · ~1,500 BUILT PAGES LINKED TO THREE SIBLINGS AT OLD ADDRESSES. Our-Family,
    TheBooyzen and TheMazza, once per page from the shared footer. They
    redirect, so nothing was broken - but they were pointing at addresses that
    had stopped being addresses. The kit ring already carried the new hosts, so
    the kit is re-pinned to 281c8d6.
THE PIN WAS DONE THE SAFE WAY AND CHECKED THE SAFE WAY: package.json and
.kitpin edited, package-lock.json left to npm via `npm install
github:...#<sha>` so resolved AND integrity move together, and the INSTALLED
archives.json read back rather than the pin trusted - booyzen, mazza and
lerena all on their defranceski.com hosts and the children's site on
ourfamily.defranceski.com.
TWO MORE THAT NEITHER MESSAGE NAMED, found by measuring the built site rather
than reading the request:
 - /dna/ linked into Booyzen at daviddef.github.io/TheBooyzen/dna/ from prose,
   not from the ring, so the re-pin could not have fixed it. Repointed to
   booyzen.defranceski.com/dna/, which answers 200.
 - THE RECORD ATLAS HAS MOVED TOO, and it is not a sibling archive the ring
   knows about: daviddef.github.io/TheMap now redirects to recordatlas.org.
   /atlas/ was still building its place links against the old prefix. Tested
   on real place pages before repointing - senj and montevideo return 200 on
   both hosts and rosario returns the same 404 on both, so the new prefix is
   exactly equivalent and the rosario fault is older than the move.
RESULT, MEASURED IN THE BUILT SITE: sibling github.io links went from ~1,500
files to zero. One reference to the old address remains, in /method/ and
/changes/, where this archive's own prose DESCRIBES it. That is a record of
what happened and stays - the describe-versus-direct test again.

commits.subject: The search index was nine entries behind the register
commits.body:
Generated after the last commit rather than before it, so the deployed
search could not find the seven people entered from the Cordon death
registers - the two Lavina sisters, their father and grandparents, Emilio
Lavina y Goyeneche, and Amelia Lerena - nor the two gazette errands.
Nothing was lost; the pages themselves were live. But a person who is on the
site and not in its search is only half published.

commits.subject: Two sisters died on one day in 1869, and their mother was already dead
commits.body:
Went to the Cordon's death registers for the four adults of Sarandi 229.
They are not there. What is there is a death this archive did not know it
was looking for.
THE LIST EXISTS NOW, which it never has. Thirteen of the parish's ~95 Lerena
documents sit in its own death and burial books - deaths 1839-1852 and
1869-1877, burials 1885-1892, 1892-1897, 1897-1901, 1908-1914, 1918-1926.
Two read, eleven unread.
AND THE FIRST ONE OPENED, read at the plate: "En cinco de Agosto de mil
ochoc.s sesenta y nueve, MURIERON Vicenta Lavina, de cuatro anos, y Manuela
Lavina, de tres anos, hija de D. Xavier (hijo) y de LA FINADA LEONARDA
LERENA." Two sisters, four and three, recorded dead in a single line, their
mother already gone.
WHICH WOULD BE A DEATH FOR A WOMAN FOUND THE DAY BEFORE. Leonarda Margarita
Lerena Vega, b. 20 February 1837, was placed on 12 October at casa 229 of
Calle Sarandi in the padron of 1850 - the only white person in a house of
four adults who carried the surname by ditto. The forename is uncommon, the
parish is hers, the daughters were born about 1865 and 1866 when she would
have been twenty-eight, and she would be about thirty-two at death. FILED AS
A CANDIDATE, NOT MERGED: what would settle it is her own death act or the
girls' baptisms, and neither is found - "Leonarda Lerena" as a phrase returns
one document in the entire corpus, and it is this one.
THE FAMILY SHE MARRIED INTO IS NAMED. Her husband is Xavier Lavina the
younger - the act writes "hijo", which is only written when an elder of the
same name exists. The elder, Don Xavier Lavina, and his wife Dona Manuela
Goyeneche, are named in the 1861 marriage dispensation of their son Emilio
Lavina y Goyeneche, 24, natural de San Pedro del Durazno, who married Dona
Maria Eladia Ramona Mendoza.
AND THAT DISPENSATION TESTED YESTERDAY'S CONCLUSION. The 12 October sweep
found no tenth Lerena dispensation using eight compound LERENA forms. This
one arrived under LAVINA and so was invisible to it - and turns out not to be
a Lerena dispensation at all. The conclusion survived a test it was not
designed for, which is worth more than the conclusion was. It also names the
next doubt: a Lerena BRIDE whose dispensation is filed under her husband's
surname would be missed by every sweep run so far.
Seven people added. One more death, Amelia Lerena, nine years old, 11
November 1871, entered INDEX-LEVEL only because the transcript runs her
margin into the body.
THE FORENAME ROUTE TO THE FOUR IS DEAD: "Estanislada" with a Cordon place
filter returns nine pages. Neither compound surname nor forename is a handle.
The eleven unread documents must be read by eye, and the errand says so.

commits.subject: This archive was logging its pageviews to another archive's counter
commits.body:
Reported by the Defranceschi session and verified here before touching
anything: every built page carried
    data-goatcounter="https://thedefranceski.goatcounter.com/count"
while the ring's own entry for this archive says the counter is thelerena.
So since the custom-domain move this site's traffic has been landing in the
Defranceschi counter and its own has stood empty. Darcy and Blazevic are the
same; Falco, Luwinski and Mazza are correct.
THE CAUSE IS THE BASE COLLISION AGAIN, IN A SECOND PLACE. Base.astro found
"which of the seven is this" with ring.archives.find(a => a.base ===
BASE_URL). Five archives now share base "", so find() returns the first of
them. It is the identical fault the Blazevic session fixed in the kit's
SocialHead with whoami() in e275c14 - but Base.astro does not go through
SocialHead, so that fix never reached it. The recipe said set base "" and
nobody followed what else keyed off it.
THE FIX IS INLINED RATHER THAN IMPORTED, following TheMazza b558bff:
kit/lib/ring.js does `import ring from "../data/archives.json"` with no
`with { type: "json" }`, which Node's ESM loader refuses during static
generation - SocialHead escapes it only because Vite resolves its relative
import. Inlining avoids patching the kit and re-pinning seven archives. It
matches on ORIGIN, which is why astro.config's `site` and this archive's url
in archives.json have to agree. Ours do.
CHECKED IN THE BUILT HTML, NOT THE SOURCE, because that is the one
measurement that cannot report an intention back: home and deep pages both
read thelerena.goatcounter.com, and ZERO of the 1,500 built pages still carry
the wrong one.
AND I FOLLOWED WHAT ELSE KEYED OFF IT, which is the part that went missing
last time. thisArchive is used in exactly one other place - VisitCount - so
the counter was the only casualty here. There is no other base-keyed lookup
anywhere in src, and the kit's components have none since e275c14.
WHAT CANNOT BE FIXED: the visits already logged to thedefranceski from this
archive between the move and now. They are in that counter and cannot be
separated.

commits.subject: Open question 2 tested for the first time: he is not in the Gazette
commits.body:
The question has named the exequatur as the decisive document since 8
September and said in terms that the claim had never been tested against any
official list. It has now, on the free, official South African Government
Gazette through Gazettes.Africa - a source this archive already used for
estate notices without ever asking it this question.
BOTH CONTROLS PASS, and they were run before any null was written. Coverage
is 1910-2026, 54,441 South African gazettes. The word "exequatur" returns 644
documents with hits in 1914, 1932, 1933 and 1937 - so the gazettes of his
lifetime are digitised, searchable, and carry the consular vocabulary. The
formula turned up with them: "Recognition granted as Consul-General",
"Recognition granted as Vice-Consul".
THE RESULT. The surname appears in 35 South African gazette documents and the
EARLIEST IS 1951 - Gazette 4584, the estate notice this archive already
holds, which calls him a racehorse trainer. Everything else is 1971 or later.
Across his whole life in South Africa, c.1908 to his death in 1950, the name
is not in the official gazette at all - and a consular recognition is exactly
what would have put it there.
AND IT DOES NOT RESCUE THE HONORARY READING. This archive's preferred
hypothesis has been an honorary consul - a resident merchant, which would
reconcile a diplomat with a man who bred horses and farmed ostriches. But
honorary consuls are gazetted too: the same corpus prints "Withdrawal of the
Recognition as Honorary Consul of Finland". Being honorary is not a way of
being absent.
NOT A CLOSED NULL, AND THE LIMITS ARE PUBLISHED WITH IT.
 - THE SPELLINGS HAVE NOT BEEN SWEPT. A null on one spelling is a null on a
   letter, and 1910s-40s gazette OCR is where a surname breaks. Raised as an
   errand with the eight forms and the search terms that find the notices.
 - THE SITE'S COUNTRY FILTER DOES NOT BIND - a country=za search returns
   Mozambique documents - so the South African subset had to be taken by
   filtering result links on their /akn/za prefix. The first year
   distribution I took was mixed and was thrown away.
 - THE TWO DOCUMENTS THAT WOULD NAME THE ACTUAL ARGENTINE CONSULS ARE
   UNREAD. Gazettes 2594 of 30 December 1938 and 4389 of 26 May 1950 both
   surface on a search for "Argentine Republic" and consul and both sit
   behind a Cloudflare bot check. THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT WORK AROUND BOT
   DETECTION, so they are recorded as BLOCKED, not as searched, and raised
   for an ordinary browser. If either names the consul of the day and it is
   not him, question 2 is answered outright.
Worked without FamilySearch, whose session expired mid-session and which this
archive does not sign into on David's behalf.

commits.subject: Five letters drafted, and put where a reader will find them
commits.body:
David asked for the letters to be prepared and put on the errands page, so
they are on the page rather than only in requests/ - /errands/#s-drafts now
carries the sendable text of all five, formatted to copy.
NONE OF THEM HAS BEEN SENT, and none can be sent from here: anything that
leaves this archive goes from David's own address, which is the standing
rule.
TWO NEW:
  Archivo Historico Diocesano de Logrono - the Navarrete parish registers,
  in Spanish with an offer to continue in English. The only place this
  archive can name where LERENA y LERENA was settled local usage, and
  FamilySearch has not filmed the books - the catalogue returns one subject,
  Census, and one item, the 1752 Catastro. The letter is careful about what
  it would and would not settle: it cannot name Juan Carlos, and says so.
  RootsChat "Welsh Jen", TAYLOR of Bideford - offer first, ask second. This
  archive holds ten children with dates, six marriages with GRO references,
  four censuses and the 1939 Register, and needs only the Brayley line before
  Mary Ann Helena. That is the right way round for a first message.
THREE CHASERS:
  Cancilleria (sent 9 Sep, five weeks silent) and Ejercito (8 Sep, five weeks
  silent), both narrowed to the one question that matters - what did he
  present to prove his nationality, and does it name his parents.
  Western Cape is NOT a chaser but a narrowing: the death notice it asked for
  turned up in David's own files on 16 September and gives both parents as
  not known, so the follow-up asks instead for the will of 6 February 1942
  and the inventory.
AND TWO OF THE FIVE CANNOT GO YET, FLAGGED IN RED ON THE PAGE. The Logrono
letter has NO VERIFIED ADDRESS - this archive does not guess one, which is
the rule every sent letter in requests/ records keeping. The RootsChat
message has no email at all and needs an account and two forum posts before
the private-message system unlocks. The other three go to addresses already
verified and already used.

commits.subject: Five published addresses resolved to nothing, and no gate could have seen them
commits.body:
The one dead address found by walking the live site was not one. Asking the
frozen slug ledger which of its keys no longer name a row in the register
found TWENTY-TWO stranded, of which FIVE had neither a page nor a redirect.
Two had been dead since 23 September.
  /people/emilia-lerena-vega/    live 23 Sep - 12 Oct
  /people/vicenta-lerena-vega/   live 23 Sep - 12 Oct
  /people/domingo-razzetti/      live 11 Oct - 12 Oct
  /people/josefina-bertoglio/    live 11 Oct - 12 Oct
  /people/pedro-a-lerena/        minted and withdrawn inside 12 Oct, deployed
                                 in between, so a promise too
THE MECHANISM IS THE LEDGER'S OWN STATED WEAKNESS. person-slugs.json freezes
a slug per person so that reordering the register cannot shuffle anybody's
URL. IT IS KEYED BY NAME. So a rename - a corrected surname, a birth estimate
moved inside a parenthetical - does not move the key: it strands it, and
build-people mints a fresh slug, usually base-2. The file's own _why calls
this "the fault this file exists to prevent, merely made rarer". Today it
happened seven times in one session, because today was a day of renames.
AND NO EXISTING GATE COULD SEE IT, BY CONSTRUCTION. check-links follows the
links a build emits; a stranded address has no inbound link left, precisely
because the rename updated every reference to it. The build is internally
consistent and externally broken.
So tools/check-addresses.py reads the LEDGER and the REDIRECT TABLE rather
than the built pages: every key that no longer names a row must still resolve
by a page or a redirect. Wired into verify.sh. Five redirects added.
TESTED AGAINST ITS OWN CASE, and the first test was wrong in the way
everything else was wrong tonight: I pointed it at the CURRENT build, which
already contained the five redirect stubs, so it passed on a tree that was
broken. Reconstructing the build without those six directories, it reports
all five. A gate that cannot be shown catching its own case is a gate
guarding nobody - and a test run against the artefact you just fixed is not
a test.
Worth sweeping in the sibling archives: all of them renamed rows during the
domain moves, and the Defranceschi sweep that found zero disappeared ids was
measuring published ids, not ledger keys stranded by renames.

commits.subject: The "safe order" this file recommended was wrong, and so was the check it added
commits.body:
Two retractions, both of advice published here within the last few hours, and
both measured on other archives rather than argued.
1 · "BIND FIRST, IT COSTS NOTHING" IS FALSE. This file said GitHub keeps
serving the previous build until the next deploy, so binding the domain ahead
of the config change breaks nothing. Binding makes GitHub 301-REDIRECT the
project-pages URL onto the new domain - so daviddef.github.io/TheX/ stops
being an address at all, and the still-based build it lands on keeps its own
assets at /TheX/_astro/..., which are gone on the new host. Falco, Mazza and
Luwinski were live-broken for hours on that advice.
THE GAP IS NOT ELIMINATED BY REORDERING, ONLY MOVED. Push first and the old
address serves root-relative links that 404 there; bind first and it
redirects to a host where the based build 404s. Both orderings break any site
whose base is not '/'. What closes it is the two steps landing within the
minute. The rule is the Luwinski session's; the measurement and the
retraction are the Defranceschi session's, which had told four archives the
opposite.
2 · AND THE CONFIRMATION STEP THIS ARCHIVE ADDED CONFIRMS THE BREAKAGE. The
step was "after binding, confirm the new host answers with the old build" -
sound in spirit, since binding is the only point at which you learn it took.
The TEST was wrong. The home page answers 200 because the 301 lands you on
it, while that build's stylesheet is 404ing beside it. So the check looked at
what had been written rather than at what was there - the exact failure this
file names twice above, committed by the step meant to prevent it.
The test is now: fetch a BASED ASSET - the stylesheet or favicon at its old
path - not the home page.
CHECKED HERE AFTER THE FACT, because a retraction that does not test its own
archive is just more intention: this site's stylesheet and favicon both
answer 200 at root paths, /TheLerena/ correctly 404s on the new host, and
build and binding agree. Lerena was never in this failure - it is bound,
deployed and consistent - but the advice it published would have put the next
archive there.
/method/#s-the-move now carries seven traps.

commits.subject: A published address outlives the reason it was minted
commits.body:
/people/pedro-lerena-vega/ was live this morning and 404s tonight. Found by
walking the new domain page by page after it came up - nothing linked to it,
so no gate caught it.
THE CAUSE IS A RENAME THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN FREE. Pedro LERENA Vega was
renamed when the census behind him turned out to be the padron of libro 264,
1850, rather than the c.1833 this archive had carried - moving his birth
estimate from c.1817 to c.1834. slugify strips the parenthetical, so a rename
touching only that should keep the address. The deduped slug moved to
pedro-lerena-vega-2 regardless, and the base slug is now claimed by nobody.
Redirect added. The comment records that the gates could not have caught this
one: check-links only follows links that exist, and the address had no
inbound link left after the errand that cited it was closed.
Caught by the same habit as the rest of today: look at the artefact. The
binding was read back from the API, the live pages were fetched one at a
time, and this fell out of the fetch rather than out of a gate.

commits.subject: A count is a claim: the rule caught its own author, and it had caught me twice already
commits.body:
The Defranceschi session re-measured the stranded archives and found its own
first figure was wrong in the same way as everything else on the list.
36 AND 113 WERE BOTH TRUE OF THE SAME PAGE. The first count was reported as
"every internal link on the home page". It had been piped through sort -u, so
it was DISTINCT PATHS - and its pattern, href="/[a-z-]*/", silently dropped
uppercase, digits, deeper paths and anchors. Narrow twice over. Re-measured:
Lerena 113, D'Arcy 249, Falco 308 of 308 based and sound.
The conclusion did not move, because zero based links is zero either way. But
the failure is the list's own: a measurement that reports what the COMMAND
ASKED FOR rather than what is THERE, committed by the session that had spent
the evening describing that exact fault.
AND IT IS NOT ONLY A DEPLOYMENT FAULT - this archive did the same thing twice
the same day. 208 records for Artigas and 470 for the Cordon parish were both
counts of what the query matched, not of what the place holds; both were
published, and both had to be withdrawn within hours. The first was a place
filter falling back to the country, the second a barrio read as a parish. All
three are one mistake: a count presented as a fact about the world when it is
a fact about the query.
A COUNT IS A CLAIM AND HAS TO MEAN WHAT IT SAYS. That is now the closing line
of /method/#s-the-move, cross-linked to the two withdrawals it describes.

commits.subject: Trap six: the order of operations, and this archive is sitting in it
commits.body:
The Defranceschi session measured the five live archives while checking my
Pages-cname point, and found that two of them - this one and D'Arcy - are
serving home pages whose every internal link 404s.
MEASURED HERE: daviddef.github.io/TheLerena/ carries 113 root-relative links
and 0 based ones, beside a canonical aimed at lerena.defranceski.com, which
does not answer because the repository's Pages custom domain is still unset.
Nothing is lost and nothing is damaged - the archive is simply unreachable by
its own navigation until one setting is changed.
THE CAUSE IS AN ORDERING, NOT A MISTAKE IN THE WORK. The recipe said: push
the config, then have the owner bind the domain, and the gap is about ninety
seconds. The gap is however long it takes a person to click. Once base is '/'
every link is site-root, and under a project path those resolve to
daviddef.github.io/about/, which does not exist.
THE SAFE ORDER IS THE REVERSE AND COSTS NOTHING: DNS resolves, then BIND the
custom domain and confirm it answers, THEN push the base change. GitHub keeps
serving the previous build until the next deploy, so binding first breaks
nothing - the old build keeps working at both addresses. Pushing first
guarantees a broken window of unknown length. Of the five archives that moved
this week, the two whose owner was at the keyboard came through clean; the
two that were not were left serving dead navigation.
Found and owned by the Defranceschi session, whose recipe set the order.
/method/#s-the-move now carries six traps, not five.

commits.subject: A deployment is evidence too: the move, and the five traps it took
commits.body:
Records the change of address on /method/ as data/domain-migration.tsv,
because three of the five failures below produce a build that looks entirely
correct and the next archive to move should not have to rediscover them.
 1. A PROJECT PATH CANNOT INHERIT A PARENT DOMAIN. defranceski.com is itself
    a Pages site served by its own repo, so defranceski.com/TheLerena/ 404s
    and a subdomain is the only clean route.
 2. AN ACTIONS DEPLOY WITHOUT A CNAME DETACHES THE DOMAIN. It has to be in
    site/public/ and checked in the built output, not assumed from a setting.
 3. THE LOCK FILE'S INTEGRITY HASH OUTLIVES THE SHA. Hand-replacing the pin
    updates `resolved` and leaves `integrity` as the old tarball's, so npm
    serves old code while every pin on display reads correct.
 4. A SHARED KEY STOPS BEING A KEY WHEN EVERYBODY USES IT. Five archives on
    base "" meant the lookup returned the first, and the first green build of
    this move carried another archive's accent and a canonical pointing at
    its domain across 1,500 pages.
 5. AND THE OBVIOUS CHECK MISSES IT: og:site_name reads correct on a wholly
    broken build, because the component takes it from a prop before it looks
    the archive up. The tells are canonical, og:url and theme-color.
THE RULE ALL FIVE SHARE: verify the installed artefact, not the recorded
intention. Never "does the pin say the right commit" but "is the new code in
the installed file"; never "did I set the domain" but "is CNAME in dist".
Each of the five reported back what was MEANT rather than what was THERE.
That is the same rule this archive spent the rest of the day learning on
documents - open the plate, not the index; read the act, not the volume
label; ask the catalogue, not the breadcrumb. The phrasing is the
Defranceschi session's, reached independently within the same hour.
Attributed, because none of it was one session's work: the kit fix is the
Blazevic session's, the og:site_name masking was found by D'Arcy, the
lock-file trap and the instructing-comments point were found here, and the
recipe and its correction are Defranceschi's. Five archives moving at once is
what made two of these visible at all.

commits.subject: The Lerena Archive moves to lerena.defranceski.com
commits.body:
site -> https://lerena.defranceski.com, base -> '/', BASE -> '', and
site/public/CNAME written with the hostname. Kit re-pinned to e275c14.
DNS verified resolving to GitHub Pages before any of this was pushed.
THE THREE KNOWN TRAPS, CHECKED IN THE BUILD OUTPUT:
  CNAME        present in dist/ - these sites deploy by Actions uploading
               site/dist, and a deploy without one DETACHES the custom domain.
  identity     og:site_name "The Lerena Archive", theme-color #5B3A96 (ours,
               not the teal), canonical and og:url on the new origin, on the
               home page and on a deep page.
  stale hrefs  eight hard-coded "/TheLerena/..." hrefs stripped from three
               pages and two data files; zero survive in 1,500 built pages.
               The github.com/daviddef/TheLerena repo URLs in changes.astro
               are NOT hrefs into this site and were left alone.
AND TWO TRAPS THE RECIPE DID NOT HAVE, both of which cost real time:
1. RE-PINNING THE SHA IN package-lock.json BY HAND INSTALLS OLD CODE. The
   lock carries `resolved` AND `integrity`. String-replacing the SHA updates
   the first and not the second, so npm validates the fetch against the old
   tarball's hash and serves old content - silently, with the right SHA on
   display. rm -rf of the package and npm cache clean --force did not help.
   The fix is to let npm re-resolve: npm install github:daviddef/TheArchiveKit#<sha>
2. THE ARCHIVE IDENTITY BUG IS REAL AND WAS ALREADY FIXED UPSTREAM. With the
   old kit, SocialHead did ring.archives.find(a => a.base === base) - and
   once more than one archive has base "", find() returns the FIRST, which is
   Defranceschi. This build shipped Defranceschi's teal and
   archive.defranceski.com canonicals before it was caught. kit e275c14 -
   "An archive is identified by its origin, not its base" - replaces that with
   whoami(), which filters by base and then matches origin against SITE. My
   own kit commit 45e6dbb was one commit too early to have it.
Comments that INSTRUCTED future sessions to write "/TheLerena/..." into prose
were rewritten rather than deleted - in data/open-questions.tsv and
data/searched-index.tsv - because left as they were they would have
reintroduced dead links on the next edit.
Gate green: 687 people, 1,500 pages, sitemap regenerated on the new origin
with zero daviddef.github.io left in it.

commits.subject: The holder formula swept, two controls passed, and it returns only what we had
commits.body:
The four adults who carry this name at Sarandi 229 in 1850 have no act to say
how the surname reached them. The parish formula - "esclava de [holder]" - is
the thing that would say it, so it was run against every Lerena this archive
can name.
TWO POSITIVES, BOTH ALREADY HELD:
  "esclava de Don Sancho Lerena"    -> Montevideo Catedral, Baptism Records
                                       1811-1813: the act of 26 September
                                       1812 for Maria Mercedes, daughter of
                                       Juana.
  "esclava de Don Alejandro Lerena" -> San Jose de Mayo, the baptism of 25
                                       April 1846 and the burial of the 28th:
                                       Barbara and Carmelo Anselmo.
NOTHING: "esclava de Don Pedro Antonio Lerena", "esclava de Pedro Lerena",
"esclava de Luis Lerena", "esclavo de Don Sancho Lerena", "liberta de Don
Pedro Lerena". Two controls passing in the same form and the same session, so
those are real nulls and not the shape failing.
AND THE ABBREVIATION RULE IS NOW EXACT. Written three ways in one hour:
"esclava de D.n Alejandro Lerena" matches NOTHING; "esclava de Don Alejandro
Lerena" matches; "esclava de Alejandro Lerena" matches. The search tolerates
a MISSING word and chokes on an ABBREVIATED one. This archive's sources are
full of D.n, D.a, S.n and V.a, every one of which will return a confident
empty page.
WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE FOUR, stated without tidying. What is excluded is only
the narrow thing: that a surviving, transcribed parish act says "esclava de"
and then names a Lerena this archive can name. Three readings survive and the
sweep does not choose between them - their acts may use "parda libre" or
"morena libre"; they may name no holder at all, which is exactly how Barbara
