appears on the BURIAL even though her baptism names hers; or their acts are
not transcribed.
So the Cordon burials of 1839-1852 must be read by eye, and that errand is
now the only route left. It carries the abbreviation trap with it.

commits.subject: An abbreviation hid Barbara's baptism, and the act gives her a surname in writing
commits.body:
Looking for parish acts that state the condition of the four who carry this
name at Sarandi 229 found none - but found something else, and a false zero
worth more than either.
THE CONTROL FAILED, WHICH SAVED TWO NULLS. "esclava de D.n Alejandro Lerena"
- a phrase this archive has read word for word off a plate - returns "No
Results Found" in full text. The same phrase without the abbreviation,
"esclava de Alejandro Lerena", returns BOTH documents at once. The machine
transcript expands or drops D.n, so the abbreviation breaks the match.
Two nulls built on that shape - "esclava de Don Pedro Lerena" and "liberta de
Don Pedro Lerena" - were about to be written down. A phrase search is only as
good as the transcriber's abbreviations, and this archive's sources are full
of D.n, D.a, S.n and V.a. Logged in false-zeros.
AND THE SECOND DOCUMENT WAS THE BAPTISM, which this archive did not have.
San Jose de Mayo, 25 April 1846: "bautice solemnemente a Car[melo] Anselmo,
que nacio el VEINTIUNO del mismo, hijo natural de BARBARA LERENA, NATURAL DE
ESTA VILLA, ESCLAVA DE DON ALEJANDRO LERENA: fueron Padrinos Jose Carreras y
Petronila Escobar."
Three things the burial does not give:
 - THE ACT WRITES HER AS BARBARA LERENA. This register says she was not a
   Lerena, and as to family that stands - but the priest gave her the surname
   of the man who held her, in writing, and that is a fact to record rather
   than tidy away.
 - She was born at San Jose de Mayo - "natural de esta Villa" - a field this
   row had blank.
 - The child was born on the 21st, not the 20th, which also squares with the
   burial's "de edad de siete dias" on the 28th. Corrected.
Two godparents entered: JOSE CARRERAS and PETRONILA ESCOBAR, who stood for
the son of an enslaved woman four days before he died. No role is furniture.
The whole of Carmelo Anselmo's life is now on two facing acts: baptised on the
25th, dead on the 27th, buried on the 28th.
The four of Sarandi 229 are still unfound. The nulls there are weak and said
to be: the compound surname is the wrong shape, since such people are entered
by forename alone - as Barbara is on the burial - and the forenames alone are
too common to sweep. What IS established is that the vocabulary is
searchable: "esclava" with a Cordon filter returns 49 pages. The errand
stands.

commits.subject: Casa 229 of Calle Sarandi, and four people who carry this name
commits.body:
Looking for one missing child found four adults who had never been named.
LEONARDA WAS NEVER MISSING FROM THE PADRON - only from her parents' house.
Born 20 February 1837, she is entered at CASA 229 OF CALLE SARANDI in the
padron of 1850, blanca and oriental, aged eleven where thirteen would be
right. This archive had used her absence to date the census; that inference
is now doubly gone.
AND THE NUMBER WAS A TRAP. Her parents are at a DIFFERENT casa 229, on
another street. There are at least two houses numbered 229 in one padron, so
"household 229" - which this archive has used as a name for weeks and named a
file after - was never an identifier at all.
SHE IS ALSO THE ONLY WHITE PERSON IN THAT HOUSE. The four adults entered with
her carry the surname by ditto - D.o - and the other columns say what the
names do not:
  Estanislada  20  morena
  Sinforiano   19  the same
  Manuela      60  casada, and her PATRIA IS AFRICA
  Rosa         46  oriental, casada
This archive has documented five people this family held in slavery, among
them BARBARA, named on an act of 1846 as "esclava de D.n Alejandro Lerena",
whose son was baptised with no surname of his own. Slavery was abolished in
Uruguay in 1842, so in 1850 these four are legally free, still in the house,
still under the name. MANUELA IS THE FIRST AFRICAN-BORN PERSON THIS ARCHIVE
HAS BEEN ABLE TO NAME in connection with this family - the others are known
only as "Barbara, esclava", or by a forename on a baptism. Born about 1790,
she was carried across the Atlantic as a child or a young woman.
WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. The padron has no column for condition. What is
established is four adults recorded with this surname by ditto, three of them
morena and one born in Africa, at one address in 1850. That the surname
reached them as Barbara's reached her son is AN INFERENCE AND IS FILED AS
ONE. What would settle it is a baptism or burial at the Cordon or the
Catedral, where the word is written outright - and the Cordon death register
of 1839-1852 is already in this archive's hands, unread. Raised as an errand.
Manuela and Rosa are both casada, so each has a husband who is not in that
house.
All four are entered in the register as people in their own right, because no
role is furniture.

commits.subject: The film carries no padron before 1843, so c.1833 was never on the table
commits.body:
Propagating yesterday's dating correction turned up the file that had held
the error, and a check inside it that cuts the other way - so I went back to
the catalogue before letting the correction stand.
data/household-229-pedro-antonio.tsv offered TWO internal arguments for
c.1833: the head's age of forty against a birth of 1793, and the absence of
LEONARDA MARGARITA LERENA VEGA, born 20 February 1837 - "at a census of about
1833 she is not yet born, and that is the check". A child missing from the
house is a real argument for an earlier book.
IT DOES NOT SURVIVE THE FILM. FamilySearch catalogue koha:1408224 lists film
7499042 (physical 1263686) item by item, all six:
  item 1  libro 263        1843        item 4  libros 265, 258  1852-1853
  item 2  LIBRO 264        1850        item 5  libro 267        1858
  item 3  libro 257        1852-1853   item 6  libro 268        1860
There is no padron earlier than 1843 on this reel at all - the 1836 books,
libros 147-149, are on film 7499043. So a census "of about 1833" was never
available to be read here, whatever the ages seemed to say. Household 229 is
in item 2: the padron of 1850.
BOTH OF THE OLD ARGUMENTS WERE THE SAME CIRCLE. The date was inferred from
the identification and the identification then rested on the date; the
Leonarda check inherited the circle, since it only dates the page if an
earlier page exists. Her absence is now a QUESTION - at the padron of 1850
she would be thirteen and should be in her parents' house - and it is raised
as its own errand, with the 1843 book named as the place to narrow it.
PROPAGATED, not just logged: the household file rewritten with its old
reasoning left visible and marked, Leonarda's row, Pedro Antonio's row (which
no longer claims household 229), relations.tsv, the person-pairs
declarations, the errand, the work list, and the plate added to
sources-consulted.tsv - which is the gate that caught me not listing it.

commits.subject: The census is the padron of 1850, and the head of household 229 is not Sancho's son
commits.body:
The catalogue settles what the plate could not. FamilySearch koha:1408224,
"Uruguay, Montevideo, censos, 1726-1860", lists film 7499042 item by item:
  item 1 = Padrones de habitantes, LIBRO 263, 1843
  item 2 = Padrones de habitantes, LIBRO 264, 1850
  item 3 = Padrones de habitantes, libro 257, 1852-1853
Household 229 sits in item 2. So the enumeration is the PADRON OF 1850 -
libro 264 - and the catalogue names the actual register book, which no label
had. The viewer breadcrumb and the catalogue now agree. c.1833 is withdrawn.
AND THE ERROR WAS CIRCULAR, which is why it stood for weeks. The c.1833 was
inferred from the head's age of forty matching Pedro Antonio Lerena, born 31
July 1793 - and the identification then rested on the date. Entered at forty
in 1850 he was born about 1810. The correction survives the neighbouring
book too: in the 1843 padron he would be born about 1803. Under EITHER
candidate volume he is too young, so household 229 stops being evidence of
Sancho's son whichever way it falls.
What it still is: a Pedro A. Lerena married to a Vicenta Vega with three
children - the same couple the Catedral baptism of 4 July 1837 attests. So
either that couple is not Sancho's son's either, or one of the two records is
badly wrong about an age. Published unresolved rather than argued either way.
THREE BIRTH YEARS MOVED SEVENTEEN YEARS LATER. Emilia c.1815 to c.1832, Pedro
c.1817 to c.1834, Vicenta c.1821 to c.1838. The ages on the plate are
unchanged - 18, 16 and an age struck through - only the subtraction changed.
The register rows, relations.tsv and the person-pairs declarations were moved
together, which is the part that usually gets missed.
One residue, recorded and not reconciled: the 1896 death act makes Pedro
sixty-nine, implying about 1827, where the padron implies 1834. Seven years,
on an age given by a son at a desk.

commits.subject: The 1850 is item-level, and accepting it would detach household 229 from Sancho
commits.body:
A follow-up on the contested census date, and it tilts - without settling.
THE DATE IS NOT A FILM LABEL. This archive's standing rule, learned the hard
way at DGS 005497886, is that a FILM's label describes only its first segment
and must never be trusted for frames deeper in. That rule does not rescue the
c.1833 here: the viewer's breadcrumb reads "Montevideo. Census 1850 -
#007499042 > Item 2", on a film titled generically "Uruguay, Canelones,
censos". The 1850 is ITEM 2's OWN TITLE - the level the rule says to trust.
SO THE EVIDENCE TILTS TO 1850, AND THE COST IS LARGE. A head entered at forty
in 1850 was born about 1810. That is NOT Pedro Antonio Lerena, son of Sancho,
born 31 July 1793 - it is a different Pedro A. Lerena, and this register
already warns that more than one exists, naming a separate Pedro Antonio who
married Teresa Leonard. The children's years would move to about 1832, 1834
and 1838, and household 229 would stop being evidence of Sancho's son at all.
THAT IS TOO MUCH TO CHANGE ON A BREADCRUMB, so nothing is changed. The
conflict is published rather than resolved by preference, the three derived
birth years stay flagged as resting on it, and the errand carries both the
tilt and what would settle it: the enumeration's own date inside the volume,
or the catalogue entry for item 2 of film 007499042.

commits.subject: Household 229 is undated, and three birth years in this register rest on that
commits.body:
An errand raised an hour earlier assumed the c.1833 dating of Montevideo
household 229 was a loose guess that the 1896 death act would overturn. It is
not a loose guess, and the answer is worse than either option: the date is
contested and three birth years here rest on it.
READ AT THE PLATE (ark 3:1:3QS7-99ZP-BBKX, apid TH-1951-36718-25784-7):
  229  D. Pedro A. Lerena   varon  40
       D.a Vicenta Vega     muger  35
       D.a Emilia Lerena            18
       D.n Pedro    D.o     varon  16
       D.a Vicenta  D.o     muger  [age struck]
The children carry the surname only as D.o - dicho, ditto - which is worth
noting in an archive whose whole problem is how this name gets written down.
THE CONFLICT. FamilySearch labels the volume "Montevideo. Census 1850". This
archive dates the household c.1833 - and that inference is sound: the head at
FORTY matches Pedro Antonio Lerena, born 31 July 1793, husband of a Vicenta
Vega of Cerro Largo, a couple attested independently by a Catedral baptism of
4 July 1837 and by both standing godparents at the Aguada on 21 November
1852. A man born in 1793 is forty in 1833 and fifty-seven in 1850.
AND A THIRD ANCHOR AGREES WITH NEITHER. The son's death act, read earlier
this evening, makes him sixty-nine in November 1896 - which wants a census of
about 1843. Three anchors, three answers: 1817, 1827, 1834.
WHAT IS AND IS NOT AFFECTED. The attachment is safe: the death act names his
parents outright. What is not safe is a date - so Emilia, Pedro and Vicenta
LERENA Vega, carried here as c.1815, c.1817 and c.1821, are now marked in
their rows as resting on an unestablished enumeration, and the errand is
rewritten from "re-date it" to "date it", still open, with what would settle
it: a title page or certifying signature elsewhere in the volume, or the
catalogue entry behind image group M9Z3-PQJ.
This is a worse position than this archive thought it was in an hour ago. It
is the true one, and it was reached by opening the plate instead of trusting
either label.

commits.subject: The act was opened the same evening, and it names his parents
commits.body:
An hour after calling Montevideo death act 353 "the cheapest act in the
archive", it is read at the plate. It confirms the index and settles a
question this register asked on 11 October.
ACTA No. 353, 15a Seccion de la Capital, 7 November 1896, before Vicente
Carricaonde. PEDRO LERENA, nacido en Montevideo, SESENTA Y NUEVE anos,
casado, died at five in the afternoon of the previous day at calle Rivera
No. 163, of tisis pulmonar, certified by Dr Vitale. "HIJO LEGITIMO DE DON
PEDRO A. LERENA, ORIENTAL, FALLECIDO, Y DE DONA VICENTA DE LA VEGA,
ORIENTAL, FALLECIDA."
So the Pedro who married Manuela Lemos is a son of Pedro Antonio Lerena and
Vicenta de la Vega - which is the parentage of Pedro LERENA Vega, counted in
Montevideo household 229. The row entered on 11 October said in terms that
which Pedro she married was not settled. It is now, from the act rather than
from an index.
AND THE CLOSING PARAGRAPH NAMES THE FAMILY. "El finado era casado con Dona
Manuela, oriental, de 53 anos, y de cuyo matrimonio existen ... Antonio =
Carlos Teodoro = Manuel Antonio ... y que el primer declarante es hijo del
fallecido." Two sons new to this archive - ANTONIO and CARLOS TEODORO - a
third already held, and a fourth standing at the desk: Don Pedro A. Lerena,
soltero, empleado, the third Pedro of the line in a row. Second declarant
Angel V. Garcia, 25. Four people entered; no role is furniture.
AND IT BREAKS A DATE, WHICH IS A BETTER PROBLEM THAN THE ONE IT REPLACES.
Sixty-nine in November 1896 means born about 1827. A man born in 1827 is SIX
in 1833, not sixteen - he is sixteen in 1843. This archive dates household
229 c.1833 and takes his birth year from his age there. The act names his
parents outright, so the attachment is safe whichever way it falls; the
census date is not. Re-dating household 229 is raised as its own errand and
work-list row, because if the enumeration is 1843 then every age-derived
birth year taken from it needs re-checking - his sister Emilia LERENA Vega
among them.
18 person-pairs compared and kept apart by hand, including Pedro LERENA Vega
against Pedro A. LERENA the younger - father and son, two rows on purpose,
and the act is what says so.

commits.subject: Two questions asked from opposite ends meet on one 1896 death record
commits.body:
Working the last of the Cordon's four leads - a Manuel Antonio Lerena the
machine transcript calls "araguayo" - produced something better than a
Paraguayan branch.
HE IS NOT PARAGUAYAN. The only Manuel Antonio Lerena the index places in
Montevideo was born there on 31 March 1883, christened 9 April, son of PEDRO
A. LERENA and MANUELA LEMOS; he later married Esther EVIA, with sons Manuel
Walter (b. 16 Nov 1921) and Alberto Nestor. So the Cordon record is either a
different man or a misreading - the same transcript writes Montevideo as
"Monterdes" - and the whole index holds ONE Lerena record in Paraguay. Not
closed, not tiered, and no Paraguayan branch written down.
THE CONVERGENCE. On 11 October this archive entered MANUELA LEMOS, wife of an
unidentified "Pedro A. LERENA", with two children fifteen years apart, and
wrote on her row in terms: WHICH PEDRO LERENA SHE MARRIED IS NOT SETTLED.
Today's 1896 death record - found while chasing an Artigas place filter that
turned out to be Montevideo - names that man's parents: PEDRO A. LERENA and
VICENTA DE LA VEGA, with spouse MANUELA LEMOS. That is exactly the parentage
of PEDRO LERENA VEGA, counted at sixteen in Montevideo household 229 about
1833. Two questions asked from opposite ends land on one certificate.
AND THE AGE PROBLEM INVERTS. This afternoon this archive declined to merge
partly because the census implies c.1817 and the death age implies 1827. A
man born 1827 fathers a child in 1883 at fifty-six; one born 1817 does it at
sixty-six. The death record's estimate fits the children better, so the
census age is the one to doubt - the reverse of how the rows were weighted a
few hours ago.
STILL NOT MERGED. Both sides are index-level. So the act is raised as an
errand and a work-list row: open Montevideo death certificate 353 of 7
November 1896, ark 1:1:6YDY-GP3T. It is the cheapest act in the archive right
now - if it confirms the index, a whole Montevideo line attaches to the
trunk: Felicia Clementina b. c.1868, Pedro Antonio b.1875, Manuel Antonio
b.1883, and Manuel Antonio's sons by Esther Evia.

commits.subject: The Cordon's 470 was the barrio, not the parish - and the parish is an afternoon
commits.body:
This morning this file said the Cordon parish holds 470 documents of the
surname, called it the largest unworked seam in the archive, and warned - in
the same breath - that an errand understating its own size is how a seam
stays unopened for a month. It then overstated its own size by five times.
q.anyPlace=Cordon scopes the NEIGHBOURHOOD. Paged to the end: 95 of the first
100 hits are Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor volumes and PAGES 2 AND 3
CONTAIN NOT ONE. The rest are La Union, Pocitos, San Francisco de Asis, the
Catedral and the Montevideo civil marriage registers - records of people who
merely lived in the Cordon. The parish's own share is about 95.
SECOND PLACE-FILTER ERROR OF THE DAY, DIFFERENT CAUSE. At Artigas the filter
fell back to the country when the department would not resolve. Here it
resolved correctly and the archive read a barrio as a parish. Controlled this
time: a fake sub-place, "Nonesuch, Montevideo", returns 26 pages - the whole
department - while Cordon returns 5.
AND THE CORRECTION IS GOOD NEWS. 95 documents across 43 volumes is an
afternoon, not a campaign, and the errand and work-list row now say so.
Baptisms 1828-1923, marriages 1842-1931, burials and deaths 1839-1926, with
the surname across the whole span.
A BOOK NOBODY HERE KNEW EXISTED. Among the densest volumes is a bundled
parish register: Religious Rite Registers 1895-1898, MARRIAGE DISPENSATION
RECORDS 1895-1898, Religious Marriage Records 1895-1898 - five Lerena hits.
This morning's sweep concluded there is no tenth Lerena dispensation; that
conclusion was about the ARQUIDIOCESIS register and it stands, but a parish
kept dispensation records of its own. Two of the five opened: both are civil
marriage testimonios copied into the parish book rather than dispensations,
so it is not yet a tenth. Three are unread.
CARVALLO LERENA, one of this morning's four untouched leads, is partly
worked: a civil marriage testimonio of 8 July 1896, expediente 60, parties at
Calle Chana 61, signed "C. Carvallo Lerena". A second hit gives an Arturo
Rivas Lerena b. 13 August 1872, but his parents carry no Lerena between them,
so the compound may be the machine's. The transcript writes Montevideo as
"Monterdes" - nothing here is tiered and both need the plate.
Still untouched: the Manuel Antonio Lerena recorded PARAGUAYO.

commits.subject: The Cordon's first four leads, and three of them corrected this archive instead
commits.body:
The parish was sized this morning - 42 volumes, 470 documents - and four
leads written down off the first page. This is what happened to them.
THE PRIZE WAS ALREADY ANSWERED. The lead was a Cordon baptism that might name
AVELINO LERENA's own parents and so attach the Traibel branch to Sancho,
which data/compound-surname-sweep.tsv has called unattached since 14
September: "NO record found names his own parents." It does not hold. Two
baptisms of his children at San Francisco de Asis on 12 March 1858 name them,
and his register row has cited them for weeks. He is Avelino LERENA
Fernandez, son of Sancho, b. c.1815, d. Montevideo 23 August 1890. The note
was stale for a month and is corrected in place, not deleted.
Worth noting against the gate built earlier today: that sentence is a SCOPED
null - "no record names his PARENTS" - so check-nulls does not catch it. The
gate guards blanket claims. This one needed a human reading the register.
THE SECOND WIFE IS NOT ONE. Cordon christenings 1866-1870 name Avelino Lerena
with CELEDONIA VILLADEMOROS, which looks like a remarriage. They belong to his
son, Avelino Eduardo Lerena Traibel - already in this register with four
children and a note on the spellings of her surname.
That is three times in one day that something which looked new was already
here. It is the strongest argument this archive has for reading itself before
it writes.
ONE RECORD GENUINELY UNACCOUNTED FOR. An AVELINO LERENA buried at the
CEMENTERIO CENTRAL DE MONTEVIDEO on 2 June 1860. The Avelino held here died in
1890; his son was fathering children in 1866. So a third man of the name was
buried in 1860 and nobody in this register answers to it. Most likely an
infant named for his father - this family reuses names constantly - and filed
as a guess. Find a Grave is a derivative index, not an act, and its photograph
is cited, not republished. The burial register has not been opened.
AND THE CORDON IS STILL UNREAD. The Paraguayan Manuel Antonio Lerena and the
Carvallo Lerena household are untouched; 469 of 470 pages are unturned. The
errand stays open. What this afternoon bought at the Cordon was three
corrections and one unexplained burial - a fair afternoon, and not a reading
of the parish.

commits.subject: Salvador's baptism settles the Leandro identification - and withdraws this afternoon's Artigas count
commits.body:
TWO THINGS, and the second is a correction of work published three hours ago.
SETTLED. The San Cristobal baptism register of Buenos Aires, 1896, certificate
288, read at the plate: "bautizo solemnemente a Salvador que nacio el dia
veinte y uno de Setiembre del ano corriente. Hijo legitimo de D.n LEANDRO
LERENA, de cuarenta y dos anos, natural de Espana, y de D.a LUCIA LLANOS, de
treinta y cuatro anos, natural de Espana, domiciliados en Calle PICHINCHA
N.o 929." Godparents Salvador Angulo, 23, and Catalina Martinez, 27.
That closes an identification published this morning on a fitted birth year,
and kills the 10 October "true null" for good: the army card's LORENA is the
census's LERENA, and its "Lucio Llanos" is LUCIA. It also hands the household
a street address, a real birth date, and a three-year disagreement about
Leandro's age that is recorded rather than averaged. Salvador's row renamed
to what the act says, with a redirect.
WITHDRAWN: "ARTIGAS HOLDS 208 LERENA RECORDS AGAINST 699 FOR FLORES."
q.anyPlace falls back to the country. "Nonesuch, Uruguay" - a department that
does not exist - returns 1,787, which is the whole-country figure, and
records indexed only to "Uruguay" satisfy every departmental query. Of the
first hundred Artigas hits, 15 name Artigas, 28 name somewhere else entirely,
and 57 carry no place at all.
Caught by opening a record the Artigas query returned: the 1896 death of
"Pedro a Lerena" sits in "Montevideo. Death Records 1896". The control that
was run - Osaka returning 0 - proved the filter binds on COUNTRY and was read
as proving it binds on DEPARTMENT. A control licenses the shape of a query,
not the value it returns. The useful control is a department that does not
exist, and it takes one query.
WHAT SURVIVES. The Artigas nulls are if anything stronger, because a filter
that widens cannot hide a record. Benito Lerena's household is real - five
infant deaths explicitly registered at Artigas 1893-1902, and Teodoro Alves
Lerena's birth registered there in 1907. WHAT DOES NOT: Domingo and Asuncion
Lerena are not shown to be of Artigas, and the Pedro death is Montevideo -
which makes it a BETTER fit for Pedro LERENA Vega, counted at Montevideo
about 1833, not a worse one. Still not merged: two age-derived birth years a
decade apart. His spouse is given as Manuela Lemos, and a second death names
the same Manuela as the mother of a Pedro Antonio Lerena born 1875.

commits.subject: A gate that asks whether the archive agrees with itself - and it catches yesterday
commits.body:
Today this archive made the same serious mistake twice and no gate could see
either: a null published while the register held the man under another
spelling, and a mechanism published as new that another file had carried for
a month. Neither was a retraction, so check-superseded was blind; neither was
drift. Nothing asked whether two LIVE claims in two files contradicted each
other.
tools/check-nulls.py reads every data row asserting a BLANKET null - true
null, only record, in any country, on earth - pulls the names out, folds the
surname through the fourteen spellings /name/ publishes, and compares the
claim with that person's register row.
IT COMPARES SOURCES, NOT PRESENCE, AND THE FIRST VERSION GOT THAT WRONG.
Failing on any name the register held reported 91, which is nonsense: half
this register is people known from a single document, and "the card is the
only record of this household" does not conflict with the household having a
row. Being in the register is not the same as having records. It now asks
whether the register cites the very record the claim concedes.
TWO MORE PRECISION BUGS, BOTH FOUND BY RUNNING IT. Keying on the first
forename alone - which is what check-duplicates does - matched "Juan Carlos
Lerena" to Juan JOSE Lerena and "Angelica Maria" to Angelica TERESA; a gate
that ASSERTS a contradiction needs the whole forename sequence. And scoped
nulls ("no marriage of Fidel Lerena TO Maria Rueda") are not in conflict with
anything, so only blanket claims count now.
PROVED AGAINST ITS OWN CASE. Run on the tree as it stood before the error was
found, it reports: cajon-985-last-two.tsv says 'LEANDRO LORENA' has no
record, but 'Leandro LERENA' is in the register from a source the claim never
mentions: 1895 census, Seccion 18. A gate that cannot be shown catching the
thing it was built for is a gate guarding nobody.
AND IT FOUND DRIFT INSIDE THE TOOLCHAIN. check-duplicates.py carried its own
hard-coded SIX spellings while /name/ published fourteen - the same
two-rows-that-never-meet failure, in the gates themselves. Both now read the
published list. Folding PERENA onto LERENA surfaced ELEVEN same-name pairs
the gate had been under-reading for weeks; all eleven compared and kept apart
by hand.
Also closes the date warning I raised this morning. Seven register rows carry
an 1879 date; five are from other sources, two are bare CEMLA years, and
exactly one comes from the suspect collection - day-level, and corroborated
by an independent christening. The artefact produces MONTH-level dates. No
held date needed changing, and the audit says so rather than leaving a
warning hanging.

commits.subject: A null this archive published as a model was broken by a record it already held
commits.body:
On 10 October this archive published Leandro Lorena and his wife Llanos as a
true null - the army card of their son Salvador their only record in the
index, in any country - and offered it as the model of what a properly
controlled null looks like. The search was signed in, the constraint bound,
eleven LLANOS rows came back across five countries and exactly one was
theirs.
THE SEARCH WAS SOUND AND THE CONCLUSION WAS WRONG. They are on lines 7 to 11
of the 1895 Buenos Aires census, Seccion 18 Subdivision 34, read at the plate
today: LERENA Leandro, varon, 38, casado, espanol, born at SEGOVIA, literate,
trade written "F.te de Aceite" - an oil maker; LLANOS Lucia, 32; LERENA
Emilia, 9, born in Spain; LERENA Francisco, 5, born at LA PLATA; and Paulina,
EIGHT MONTHS old, portena. The surname is settled at the plate: its initial
matches the Ll of "Llanos" on the line below and differs from the S of
"Sanchez" two lines above.
WHY THE NULL HELD, which is the part worth keeping. A spouse-pair query
constrains on a MARRIAGE RELATIONSHIP. A census has none - it is a list of
people in a dwelling, each indexed on their own - so no census can satisfy
that query however well it binds. The query was structurally blind to the
record type the answer was in. Logged in false-zeros as the first disguise in
that file where the search WORKED and still produced a false null: a control
proves the query is running, it cannot prove the query can see the record.
AND THE ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD THE ANSWER. Leandro, Emilia, Francisco and
Paulina were all four in this register before the null was written, marked
"Leandro's household" and described as a separate, Spanish-born family. The
one name that would have joined them to the card was the wife's, and LUCIA
LLANOS had never been entered. An archive does not need a new record to make
this mistake; it needs two rows that never meet.
Salvador, b.1896, fits the gap exactly - the year after a census complete to
an eight-month-old. Not proved by an act, and the row says so: his 1896 birth
registration would settle it.
2 people added (Lucia Llanos, Salvador), 4 enriched, open question 1 rewritten.

commits.subject: Artigas: 208 records of this name, 500km north, and nobody had opened it
commits.body:
Artigas sits on the Brazilian border and appears nowhere in this archive's
searched list. Everything here assumes the family runs Canelones to
Montevideo to Trinidad. The department arrived this morning by accident, when
a cross-spelling sweep turned up a birth act at San Eugenio.
Asked directly it returns 208 LERENA records - against 699 for Flores, the
heartland this archive was built on - plus 103 Serena, 99 Perena, 37 Lorena,
32 Llerena, 28 Larena, 21 Gerena, 3 Lerina. Controlled at Osaka, which is 0.
IT DOES NOT ANSWER THE CENTRAL QUESTION, and the null is published rather
than left unsaid: Juan Carlos exact as subject 0, as father 0, and a Lerena
father against a Lerena mother 0, all inside Artigas. An unworked department
is exactly where a reader would assume we simply had not looked.
WHAT IT HOLDS. Benito Lerena - the jornalero who could not sign his name -
registered FIVE INFANT DEATHS at Artigas between 1893 and 1902. Gumersindo,
born 1898, died 8 March 1899, ten weeks before Benito walked into the Juzgado
de Paz to register a grandson. And the index gives that one mother four
surnames in nine years - Araujo, Cordero, Cuestima, Araujo Cardozo - because
the act calls her only "Dona Maria Cristina" and the index has a field that
must be filled. The mother-manufacturing failure, caught five times over.
Anastasia Lerena and Honorio Alvarez have a second son, Teodoro, born 22
April 1907 under the spelling ALVES - so Juan Ildebel has a brother.
AND ONE IDENTIFICATION NOT MADE. The Artigas index holds a "Pedro a Lerena"
who died 6 November 1896, father Pedro A. Lerena, mother VICENTA DE LA VEGA -
the same parents, and the same odd "Pedro a" form, as Pedro LERENA Vega,
counted at 16 in Montevideo household 229 about 1833. Rather than create a
second row I folded a CANDIDATE death into his, untiered, and said what it
would mean: a Montevideo boy of 1833 dying on the Brazilian frontier would
tie the Artigas Lerenas to this archive's own trunk. That is too large a
claim to rest on an index, so it rests on nothing until the act is opened.
5 people added, 5 person-pairs compared and kept apart. Everything here is a
survey from the record index; one Artigas act has been read at the plate.

commits.subject: The Cordon is forty-two volumes and 470 documents - sized, not searched
commits.body:
A standing errand since September said only "search the Iglesia del Cordon".
Nobody had established that the registers were filmed, let alone how big the
job was. They are filmed to an unusual degree and machine-read throughout.
Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Montevideo: FORTY-TWO VOLUMES - baptisms
1828-1923, marriages 1842-1931, burials and deaths 1839-1926. A near-unbroken
century, every volume in the full-text corpus. It holds 470 documents
mentioning this surname.
That is the largest unworked seam in this archive and it was being carried as
an afternoon's skim. The number is published and the errand stays OPEN, with
the scale written into it, because an errand that understates its own size is
how a seam goes a month untouched - which is exactly what the dispensation
errand did, corrected earlier today.
ONE QUESTION ANSWERED ON THE WAY. A "Juan Carlos" appears beside the surname
in the results, and any Juan Carlos near this name has to be checked. Run as
a phrase it is a single document in the Cordon marriage register of
1916-1926: Juan Carlos GONZALEZ LERENA, a Gonzalez by his father and a Lerena
by his mother, already in this register. Ours fathered a child in 1882. Forty
years out and the wrong surname.
WHERE THE NEXT SESSION STARTS - four leads off the first page, none opened
and none tiered: a Cordon baptism of a daughter of AVELINO LERENA and
AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, the branch this archive still cannot attach to Sancho;
Avelino the younger standing godfather; a MANUEL ANTONIO LERENA recorded
PARAGUAYO, a nationality never met here; and a CARVALLO LERENA household.

commits.subject: There is no tenth dispensation - and the errand had been stale for a month
commits.body:
Yesterday this archive published, as a new finding, a mechanism it had
written down on 14 September. The correction is logged as serious and the
file is rewritten rather than deleted, because an archive that quietly
removes its duplicated findings cannot tell how often it duplicates them.
WHAT WAS ALREADY KNOWN. data/compound-surname-sweep.tsv, 14 September: the
September dispensation sweep's formula was "LERENA FELIGRESA" and the
compound surname sits between the two words. It had already run Lerena
Juanico, Lerena Lenguas and Lerena Traibel, and had already found the NINTH
dispensation through it - Jose Pedro Massera's petition of 19 June 1913 to
marry Dona Ema Sixta LERENA JUANICO, feligresa de la metropolitana. The
errand "re-run the dispensation sweep on COMPOUND surnames" had been sitting
ready for a month against work that was half done.
Caught by finishing the job rather than describing it: opening the 1913 plate
to check whether it was new led to a grep that returned the September file.
WHAT TODAY ADDS. The six forms nobody had run - Lerena Pelaez, Lerena
Fernandez, Lerena Villademoros, Lerena Cardozo, Lerena Larriera, Lerena
Razzetti - each read to the END of its result set. FamilySearch's full-text
results URL takes count=100, which turns a top-ranked first page into a whole
result set; without it this would have been the ranked-list mistake this
archive has already made at "290 records" and at herencia.
THE RESULT. Two of the eight forms reach the dispensation register and both
land on dispensations already held: 1911 through Lerena Cardozo, 1913 through
Lerena Juanico. That makes them controls rather than finds - the queries
demonstrably hit the target, and there is nothing else in it. NO TENTH LERENA
DISPENSATION. The errand is closed.
One detail worth keeping: the machine transcript of the 1913 petition renders
the groom's surname as Massera once and Tomasera once, in one short document.
That is /name/'s lesson in a Latin alphabet and a modern hand.

commits.subject: The dispensation sweep was blind to the opposite of what the errand assumed
commits.body:
The errand has stood ready since September on a one-line reason: by 1900
Lerena is largely a MATERNAL surname inside compounds, so a surname-first
sweep under-reads this family. The reason was half wrong, and which half is
the useful part.
The September sweep used two of the register's own formulae - "Lerena el
impedimento" for a groom, "Lerena feligresa" for a bride. A phrase search is
an adjacency. A compound where Lerena comes SECOND survives it intact:
"Gonzalez Lerena el impedimento" still contains the phrase. A compound where
Lerena comes FIRST does not, because a second surname is pushed into the
middle: "Lerena Pelaez el impedimento" contains neither formula.
So the sweep was already catching the maternal-surname case the errand was
raised to fix, and was blind to the paternal one nobody had thought about.
AND THE GAP IS NOT EMPTY. Clerks do write the compound. "Lerena Pelaez"
returns the Trinidad (Flores) confirmation register 1891-1905; "Lerena
Lenguas" three Montevideo volumes; "Lerena Fernandez" two more. "Lerena
Traibel" - the best-documented branch in this archive - returns nothing at
all corpus-wide, which is its own small fact. Controlled against "Lerena y
Lerena" in the same form and session, which returns a full page of volumes.
PUBLISHED UNFINISHED, ON PURPOSE. None of those searches put the dispensation
register in its top results, and that is suggestive, not proof: the result
sets were not paged. A ranked list is not a searched volume, and this archive
has been caught by that twice - at "290 records" and at herencia. The errand
stays OPEN, now carrying the eight compound forms to run it with.
Free, from the control: the Iglesia del Cordon registers ARE in the full-text
corpus (Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, baptisms 1891-1892 and
1900-1902), so that standing errand is cheaper than it looked. Its note says
so, and no Cordon entry has yet been opened.

commits.subject: Navarrete's registers are not filmed, and the record that looked like a second doubling was Guadalajara
commits.body:
Open question 1 has called Navarrete worth a day since 11 October - not
because anyone believes Pablo Armando's father came from there, but because
it is the one place this archive can name where LERENA y LERENA was settled
local usage. Isabela LERENA y BASARAN, widow, and her sons Prudencio Benito
and Juan Jose LERENA y LERENA, naturales de Navarrete, signed escritura 368
at the Spanish consulate in Buenos Aires on 14 November 1900.
THE CATALOGUE ANSWER IS A HARD ONE. FamilySearch's catalogue for Navarrete,
Logrono returns one subject - Census - and one item: the Catastro del Marques
de la Ensenada of 1752. No baptisms, no marriages, no burials, and no
Navarrete volume in the full-text corpus either. The registers cannot be read
from this desk; they need the Archivo Historico Diocesano de Logrono, which
is now a letter on the work list.
THE RECORD THAT LOOKED LIKE A SECOND INSTANCE IS NOT ONE. The index offers a
mother "Wenceslaa Maria Lerena Lerena" among 26 records it files under
Navarrete. Opened at the plate it is a marriage at San Gil de esta ciudad de
GUADALAJARA, 21 December 1863 - two hundred kilometres away - and margin and
body both write Lerena ONCE: "hija de Andres, ya difunto, y de Joaquina
Lozano". Her mother was a Lozano. So the archive's own compound test of 14
September survives intact, and this is the forty-fourth machine doubling
rather than the first Spanish compound. Said plainly rather than quietly
dropped, because for an hour it looked like the opposite.
A CORRECTION TO THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN METHOD. It is recorded here that
q.anyPlace RANKS and does not FILTER. Controlled today - the same Lerena
query at Reykjavik and at Osaka returns 0 - it DOES filter, once
m.queryRequireDefault=on is sent. The earlier finding was the missing
parameter, not the parameter's behaviour. What does not hold is the place
FIELD underneath it, as the Guadalajara act shows.
WHAT CAME BACK INSTEAD, all index-level and none of it tiered: three
Spanish-born Prudencio Lerenas emigrating 1921-1946, one of them from Najera
twenty kilometres from Navarrete - Prudencio being the forename of one of the
two brothers; and Leandro Lerena, b.1857 in SPAIN, with Emilia Lerena b.1886,
in the 1895 Buenos Aires census, five years before the brothers signed, in a
city where almost every Lerena this archive has traced is Uruguayan-born.
3 errands and 3 work-list rows raised, each with a covers token so the
reconciliation gate accounts for them.

commits.subject: The central null was only ever asked in one spelling, and it survives all thirteen
commits.body:
/name/ published fourteen forms on 11 October and closed on a sentence: the
null may be a letter rather than a fact. On 12 October that sentence was
turned on the question this archive exists to answer.
Every parent-pair search ever run here set the surname to LERENA. Thirteen
spellings were available, so the whole grid was run - each spelling as the
father's surname against each as the mother's, 121 cells, both exact, no
place filter and no date filter. 110 of those cells had never been asked.
WHAT IT COST FIRST. The initial pass returned 3,405 couples where the web
page shows 38, and a control designed to fail - Sancho Lerena x Maria
Fernandez, a couple with five known records - returned 17,448,030. The
personas API RANKS by default and FILTERS only when m.queryRequireDefault=on
is sent, which the UI sends and a hand-built URL does not. Replaying the
UI's own request out of the network log found it. Recorded in false-zeros as
a disguise that hides a null by burying it in a large number.
THE ANSWER. Juan Carlos as a father returns 2 under LERENA, 1 under LLERENA,
1 under PERENA and nothing under the other ten. The two Lerena hits are the
1983 Montevideo infant death already ruled out and Pablo Armando's own
enrolment card; the others are Cartagena 2006 and Caracas 2003. The null is
a fact about the family, not about a spelling - and it is now a better null
than the one it replaces.
WHAT THE SWEEP FOUND INSTEAD. 24 of 121 cells non-zero, 14 of them cross
spellings, holding 16 records. All sixteen opened; twelve are elsewhere.
Two are Uruguayan and both were read at the plate:
- SAN EUGENIO, ARTIGAS, act 110 of 2 June 1899. The index gives a Lerena
  father and a Serena mother and then names the same man again as maternal
  grandfather. The act says the Lerena is the DECLARANT and grandfather,
  and at 6,000 pixels the mother's capital is the same letterform he is
  given eleven lines below - Anastasia LERENA, not Serena. The pair is
  Alvarez x Lerena. A new household: Benito Lerena, who could not sign.
- MAL ABRIGO, SAN JOSE, act 98 of 14 September 1910. Margin reads Lerena
  Antonina. Ramona LERENA, 24 and soltera, registering a natural daughter;
  her father PEDRO LERENA, 68, ITALIANO, labrador of Jesus Maria. An
  Italian-born Lerena in the department this archive rests an 1846 couple
  on - so the Italian stock can no longer be separated from this family by
  country alone. Kept UNPLACED, because that is the honest position.
AND A COLLECTION-WIDE WARNING. Both acts were dated 1879 by the index; one
is 1899 and one is 1910, and their volume labels say so. Uruguay Civil
Registration 1879-2020 appears to give unread acts the collection's opening
year, so 1879 is an artefact bucket and a date-filtered search of cc=1837849
measures the index rather than the register.
9 people added (659 -> 668), 16 person-pairs compared and kept apart by hand
including one - Pedro S. Lerena of Tejera, Durazno - where the note says
plainly that the grounds for keeping them apart are weaker than the rest.

commits.subject: Fourteen spellings, published at last — the register counted them and never showed them
commits.body:
The register's notes have been counting upward for weeks — "a seventh
spelling", "an eighth spelling" — without the list ever reaching a reader.
/name/ held two sections: Lerena against Llerena as a Badajoz toponym, and
the Italian stock kept apart on purpose. Neither told anyone searching what
to type.
data/name-variants.tsv now carries fourteen forms, each taken from a
document this archive has actually read, with what the form cost or gave:
- LERENA, the ordinary form, and the only one every sweep ran for a month
- LLERENA, the real spelling, not an error — and the 1889 Buenos Aires
  probate that writes one man both ways, twice each, in one paragraph
- SERENA, which on 12 October 2026 returned children for two couples
  worked for weeks with no children found
- GERENA, PERENA, LOREÑA/LEREÑA, LEVENA, LORENA, LERESA, LARENA, LERINA,
  LERRENA — clerk's ears and clerk's hands
- HERENCIA, which is not a name at all, and cost this archive a person
Twelve are the same name; one is a different family; one is a word.
The 1879 act that writes one family four ways on a single page is the
argument for the whole page.

commits.subject: Four spellings swept, and each one held people the others did not
commits.body:
SERENA proved this morning that the Trinidad sweeps had missed a variant. The
other three are now done, each paged to where the matches stop.
PERENA (3 Flores records) gave AMABELIA, born about 1880 and dead on 9 January
1899, a fourth child for Cipriano Lerena and Lauriana Beloqui; and ANTONINO,
born 10 May 1891, for Doroteo Lerena and Isidora Cardozo.
GERENA (7) gave CASTO LINDOLFO, born 1 July 1882, a fifth child for Cipriano;
JUAN PEDRO, born 13 May 1909, a second child for Buenaventura Olivera and Luisa
Lerena - whose brother came out of the SERENA sweep an hour earlier, so one
household needed two spellings and two sweeps; and VENANCIO, married at
Santisima Trinidad on 24 April 1885, who is THE FIRST CHILD THIS ARCHIVE HAS
FOUND OF EITHER MARRIAGE OF ALEJANDRO LERENA THE YOUNGER.
LLERENA (11) completed the household of FERMIN LERENA and PAULINA BARRAGAN with
ISABEL, married to Juan Rodriguez on 29 January 1902, and a younger FERMIN
married in 1924; gave FAUSTINO a wife, VITERBA DE ARRASCAETA, a son PEDRO born
and dead in 1911, and a death of his own on 1 June 1914; and identified the
"Fermin" who was the only named parent of the Juana Maria entered from the
SERENA sweep this morning.
AND IT GAVE BERNABE AND CASIMIRA TWO DAUGHTERS ELEVEN YEARS EARLIER THAN
ANYTHING HELD HERE. MARGARITA MEDARDA DEL CORAZON DE JESUS, christened at
Trinidad in 1859 - a year after their marriage expediente of 15 February 1858,
which is exactly where a first child belongs - and MARIA, born 13 May 1866. This
row's six known children all ran from 1871.
SERENA WITH A TILDE IS NOT A SEPARATE SEAM. "Serena" returns the identical 290
records as "Serena", so FamilySearch normalises the n-tilde and no tilde variant
anywhere needs its own sweep. That is worth more than any one person in this
commit, because this archive was about to spend a session on it.
Fifteen people entered, all index-level. Two pairs written by hand for the Maria
of 1866 against the two Marias already held - same parents, so sisters or one
woman, and only the acts will say which.
659 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: "290 records, 190 unread" was the size of a surname, not of a seam
commits.body:
q.anyPlace RANKS results, it does not filter them. The search returns every
SERENA in Uruguay - an ordinary Italian surname there - sorted so the Flores
ones come first. Page one carried 22 Flores records; pages two and three
carried ZERO between them. So the Flores seam is about twenty-two records and
they were all read an hour ago, and the "190 unread" are other families in
other departments.
The findings are unaffected: the children of Custodio and Ema, of Juan Bernardo
and Eduviges, Cipriano's 1875 marriage and the rest were all on page one.
This is the herencia lesson again, eight days later. On 11 October this archive
wrote that "a result count is not a finding... every hit has to be read before
it is counted", and then reported a count as a finding the next day. The
difference worth recording is that a PLACE PARAMETER LOOKS LIKE A FILTER, and
the only way to tell is to page to where the matches stop.
The worklist row is rewritten to what is actually left: the same sweep for
PERENA, SERENA-with-a-tilde and GERENA.

commits.subject: The Trinidad sweeps were run on LERENA, and SERENA holds 290 records
commits.body:
Acting on this morning's finding. A sweep on SERENA with a Flores place filter
returns 290 records that the LERENA sweeps never saw. The first hundred are read.
IT PRODUCED CHILDREN FOR TWO COUPLES THIS ARCHIVE SPENT WEEKS ON AND HAD NO
CHILDREN FOR.
  CUSTODIO LERENA and EMA CARDOZO - the 1911 double-first-cousin dispensation,
  the knot this archive worked hardest - now have RISILIO MARIA, born 26
  September 1917 and christened that December, and ENRIQUE RENE, born 1927 and
  dead in 1981.
  JUAN BERNARDO LERENA PELAEZ and EDUVIGES PELAEZ - the 1894 dispensation - now
  have MARIA ELENA, born 22 July 1910, and TERESA MARIA EVA, born 17 June 1911.
THE CONTROL IS INSIDE THE SWEEP. It also returns events this archive already
holds, under the other spelling: Cipriano's marriage of 6 March 1875 naming
MAURICIO SERENA and CASIMIRA MONTANO; Alejandro the younger's of 24 December
1854 naming ALEJANDRO SERENA and MARGARITA FERNANDEZ; the 1894 intended marriage
of Juan and Eduviges. So the query finds what it should, and the LERENA sweeps
simply never asked it.
A FOURTH SPELLING APPEARS: "SERENA" with a tilde, beside Lerena, Serena and
Perena, all at Trinidad in the same decade.
Twenty-one people entered, ALL INDEX-LEVEL. Two of them carry a birth date LATER
than their own christening - the index's arithmetic, not the register's, and
recorded as it stands.
AND ONE ROW NEARLY BECAME TWO AGAIN. Isidora Cardozo went in from the Serena
sweep before the build refused her on an exact name match: the Trinidad sweep had
her all along under LERENA, with three children. Backed out, and her row now
carries the fourth child and the near-miss - including that a child of 1934 sits
forty years from her others, so either she bore children across four decades or
Angel Custodio belongs to a younger Doroteo. Not resolved.
190 results remain unread, and a worklist row now carries them along with the
same sweep for PERENA, SERENA-with-a-tilde and GERENA.
644 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: All fifteen "Lerena y Lerena" volumes read, and the Trinidad sweep missed a spelling
commits.body:
Worklist row 203: twelve volumes unread after three were worked yesterday. All
fifteen are now read, and the seam's real shape is plain. The phrase finds TWO
LERENAS STANDING TOGETHER, nearly always as godparents, and most of the pairs
are people this register already holds - Bernabe with Alejandrina, Bernabe with
Natalia, Juan with Margarita, Vitaliano with Andrea twice, Alejandro with
Clorinda.
THREE THINGS CAME OUT OF IT WORTH MORE THAN THE PAIRS.
A "MONTEVIDEO" VOLUME IS NOT A MONTEVIDEO ACT. The 1890-91 page is the capital's
CIVIL register transcribing a parish certificate signed by the Cura Vicario
Brana "en TRINIDAD a catorce de [noviembre] de mil ochocientos noventa". A place
filter will not separate the two towns, and this archive has been assuming it
does.
THE TRINIDAD SWEEP MISSED THE SERENA SPELLING. One volume pair of 1905-09 alone
carries SARA SERENA, PIO C. SERENA - written PERENA on the facing volume -
ALEJANDRO SERENA and ALBA LERENA. Trinidad has had a dedicated sweep and a
founding kindred drawn from three expedientes, and none of these four is in any
of it. The sweep was run on LERENA.
AND TWO MORE CHILDREN for Fernando Moratorio and Josefa Lerena Traibel - MARIA
DOLORES and FERNANDO - with the grandparents named on both sides, AVELINO and
AMBROSIA TRAIBEL among them. But the volume's label cannot be trusted for a
date: it is catalogued September 1917 to September 1918, its own year metadata
runs 1871, 1874, 1888 and 1918, and a woman born in 1851 does not bear children
in 1917. Recorded as a tension and not resolved.
Nine people entered. ALL INDEX-LEVEL, NO PLATE OPENED - which, after four
index-level couples collapsed on their plates this same morning, is said louder
than usual and is on every row.
624 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: "El Doctor Lerena" is a man, not the word herencia
commits.body:
Worklist row 205 carried him as a one-line snippet with a warning attached,
because in the Buenos Aires probate corpus "lerena" is usually the transcriber
reading HERENCIA. The warning was right to be there, and he is real.
The Agente Fiscal's opinion in the Feliciano Aguirre probate of 1889:
  "no lo hace el DOCTOR LERENA si la intervencion del CONSUL ESPANOL en este
   estado del juicio es o no oportuna. Lo que debe resolverse es si el
   nombramiento del CURADOR DON LLERENA es o no arreglado a derecho. Al simple
   pedido de f.46, el Juzgado nombra CURADOR AL DOCTOR LLERENA, sin oir a este
   Ministerio... hubiera dictaminado que se librase nuevo oficio al Senor CONSUL
   DE ESPANA, para que si deseare intervenir en este juicio lo hiciere dentro de
   un termino perentorio."
A lawyer appointed curador of an estate, with the Fiscal complaining that the
court appointed him without consulting the Ministry or inviting the Spanish
consul - whose interest means the deceased was most likely a Spanish subject.
THE SAME PASSAGE SPELLS HIM LERENA AND LLERENA, TWICE EACH, IN ONE HAND. That is
the clearest demonstration in this register that the two spellings are one name,
and it is worth more than the man.
And "Doctor" is again the style of an ABOGADO and not a physician - the second
time in one day, after Arturo Lerena of Montevideo.
Not merged with Carlos A. Lerena, the commission agent who sued the Escalada
estate in the same courts in February 1890: one is a party suing, the other an
officer of the court, and the 1889 act gives the curador no forename at all.
The phrase search returns 64 hits and opens three seams nobody has worked: the
same Doctor Lerena in the Buenos Aires probates of 1890, 1894 and 1897; a
DOCTOR LERENA signing medical certificates on Montevideo death records of 1949
and 1967, who IS a physician and is a different man; and "Senores Doctor Lerena"
in the student files of the Universidad de Toledo in the 1790s-1830s.
615 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: All four couples opened, and not one is a couple of two Lerenas
commits.body:
Yesterday's parent-pair query produced four Uruguayan Lerena-married-a-Lerena
couples nobody here had met. All four acts are now read.
  SAN JOSE DE MAYO, 1846 - "hijo natural de BARBARA, ESCLAVA DE D.n ALEJANDRO
  LERENA". An enslaved woman given her holder's surname, and no marriage at all.
  TRINIDAD, 1906 - "hija legitima de Don VITALIANO LERENA y de Dona ANDREA
  ETCHEBERSE", the mother's surname broken across the page opening and replaced
  by the father's.
  MONTEVIDEO, 1865 - "hija de ANTONIO y de SABINA SERENA". ONE surname between
  two parents, which the index duplicated into two.
  CERRO LARGO, 1938 - "FLORENCIO SERENA, fallecido... y de TERESA SERENA, DE
  ESTADO VIUDA". Both named, but a widow is written under her late husband's
  name as a matter of course.
Two disproved outright, two unproved. The query is a good way to find Lerena
households and a bad way to count marriages.
THE SIX COUPLES THIS ARCHIVE HELD BEFORE THE QUERY ARE UNTOUCHED - the two
Trinidad couples, the 1911 dispensation, Alejandro, Eloy x Felisa and the
Navarrete household all rest on ACTS, not on an index's parent fields. The
pattern stands; the thing that seemed to multiply it does not.
The 1865 act turned out to be the best of the four for its own sake. Joaquin
Costales married Maria Serena IN ARTICULO MORTIS - a deathbed ceremony whose
purpose was to legitimise the two sons they declared, CANDIDO DE DIEZ ANOS Y
LUIS DE CUATRO. He was BRASILERO. So the couple had been together since about
1855, and the marriage of 25 May 1865 is the end of that story, not its start.
And the 1938 act closed a question by place rather than leaving it open: the
Florencio there is of CERRO LARGO, four departments from Trinidad, so the
Florencio Lerena of Trinidad who married Juana Recuero is a different man. It
also carries two conflicts left standing - her birth registration at Melo says
18 MAY 1908 where the marriage act says 6 MARCH 1908, and that registration
names TERESA LLERENA ALONE, with no father; he appears thirty years later,
already dead. She could not sign her own marriage act.
Twelve more people entered from the four acts. 614 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: Twice in one morning, an index built a Lerena mother out of a man's surname
commits.body:
The second of the four new couples, opened straight after the first turned out
to be an enslaved woman. Santisima Trinidad, 26 March 1906:
  "contrajo DON ANTONIO ETCHEBERSE, oriental, soltero, de TREINTA Y TRES anos,
   HIJO [legitimo struck out] NATURAL de Don ANTONIO ETCHEBERSE y de Dona
   FRAILANA VALIENTE, con Dona ANDREA ALBINA LERENA, oriental, soltera, de
   TREINTA Y DOS anos, HIJA LEGITIMA DE DON VITALIANO LERENA Y DE DONA ANDREA
   ETCHEBERSE."
The mother is an ETCHEBERSE. Her surname is broken across the page opening -
"ANDREA" at the foot of the left page, "ETCHEBERSE." at the head of the right -
and the index gave her the FATHER'S surname instead. That is the same fault
that made Barbara a Lerena at San Jose de Mayo an hour earlier.
Two of the four, one mechanism, now written into data/false-zeros.tsv: an index
with a MOTHER field will fill it from the nearest surname when the act does not
fill it the way the schema expects. So a parent-pair query cannot tell a
marriage from a slave-holding, or a mother from a line break - AND WHERE BOTH
PARENTS SHARE A SURNAME THE ENTRY IS MORE SUSPECT, NOT LESS, because that is
exactly the shape the failure produces. This archive ran a worldwide query on
precisely that shape yesterday.
Four more corrections off the same plate: the groom is ETCHEBERSE and not
Echeberse; he was THIRTY-THREE, not the index's "tres anos"; the priest STRUCK
OUT "legitimo" and wrote "natural" over his parentage, which no index carries;
and the index's marriage date of "26 March 1000" is 1906.
WHAT SURVIVES IS STILL WORTH HAVING. Vitaliano Lerena is real - a man of that
rare forename at Santisima Trinidad, with a daughter born about 1874 and married
there in 1906, in the town this archive has swept and in none of the sweeps.
Four people entered from the act: the groom's parents and the two witnesses.
One observation, not a conclusion: the bride's mother shares the groom's
surname, and the act records "sin ningun impedimento ni canonico ni civil".
603 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: "Esclava de D.n Alejandro Lerena" was indexed as a marriage
commits.body:
The first of yesterday's four new Lerena-married-a-Lerena couples, opened
because an index entry contradicted a man this archive thinks it knows. San
Jose de Mayo, 28 April 1846:
  "di sepultura en el ANGELORIO al cadaver de CARMELO ANSELMO, HIJO NATURAL DE
   BARBARA, ESCLAVA DE D.N ALEJANDRO LERENA, murio ayer de enfermedad, de edad
   de SIETE DIAS, y se le hizo oficio rezado, de que certifico."
There was no marriage. Barbara was an enslaved woman in his household. The
indexer read "esclava de D.n Alejandro Lerena" as a parent pair, made Alejandro
the father, and GAVE BARBARA THE SURNAME OF THE MAN WHO HELD HER. The child is
hijo natural, with no father named and no surname of his own.
All three rows are renamed to what the act says, and three addresses minted
yesterday are retired to redirects today. She is BARBARA, with no surname,
because the act gives her none and this archive will not lend her one. He is
CARMELO ANSELMO, seven days old, buried in the angelorio. And Alejandro is a man
of San Jose de Mayo in April 1846 who held a woman in slavery - not merged with
the elder Alejandro who married there in 1825, though the town, the decade and
the style of address all fit, because the act names no wife, no age and no
parents to test it with.
SHE IS THE FIFTH PERSON THIS FAMILY IS KNOWN TO HAVE HELD IN SLAVERY, after
Juana, Antonio, Jose and Teresa in Sancho Llerena's household at Canelones in
1812, and Juana's daughter Maria Mercedes born into it. This one is thirty-four
years later, a different household and a different department.
On the date this archive states only what it knows: the act says "esclava" in
April 1846, and which stage of Uruguay's abolition applied at San Jose then is
NOT established here. That is for the next session, and this act does not
answer it.
THE COUNT PUBLISHED YESTERDAY IS WRONG BY AT LEAST ONE, and the retraction has
been propagated to searched.json and to open question 1: thirty-eight is a count
of INDEX ENTRIES, not of marriages. A parent-pair query cannot tell a marriage
from a slave-holding - and this archive ran a worldwide one.
The lesson is not that indexes are wrong; it knew that. It is that an index
which must output a father and a mother will MANUFACTURE them from whatever the
act supplies, and here what it supplied was a sentence about ownership.
599 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: Put the empty index on the page that asks the question
commits.body:
Open question 1 now carries the null and the control: thirty-eight couples in
the world with a Lerena father and a Lerena mother, not one of them a Juan
Carlos, in an index that returns the couples this archive already holds.
It also says which index. The earlier nulls on his name were full-text searches
reading words off page images; this one catalogues parents as fields. Two
different indexes, both empty on the same man - which is worth more than either
alone, and is the kind of thing a reader can only know if the page says it.
And it says the seam is not exhausted: the same query produced four Uruguayan
couples nobody here had met, one at Trinidad and one at San Jose de Mayo in 1846.

commits.subject: Thirty-eight Lerena-married-a-Lerena couples in the world, and none is his
commits.body:
Pablo Armando's enrolment card names JUAN CARLOS LERENA and MARIA LERENA - a
Lerena father and a Lerena mother. That is a question the record index can be
asked directly, with both surnames EXACT, and this archive had never asked it.
The earlier nulls on "Juan Carlos Lerena" were FULL-TEXT phrase searches, which
read words off page images; this is the NAME index, which catalogues parents as
fields. Two different indexes, now both empty on the same man.
Thirty-eight couples worldwide. Not one father is a Juan Carlos.
THE CONTROL IS BUILT INTO THE QUERY: it returns couples this archive already
holds - Eloy Lerena and Felisa Lerena at San Jose de Flores in 1912, Alejandro
F. Lerena and Natalia Lerena at Trinidad - so it finds what it should.
AND IT FOUND FOUR URUGUAYAN COUPLES NOBODY HERE HAD MET.
  Antonio Lerena and Sabina Lerena, whose daughter MARIA married Joaquin
  Costales at San Francisco de Asis - this archive's own parish - on 25 May 1865.
  VITALIANO LERENA and ANDREA LERENA at TRINIDAD, FLORES, the town this archive
  has worked hardest, with a sweep of its own and a founding kindred drawn from
  three expedientes. Their daughter Andrea Albina was born there in 1874.
  ALEJANDRO LERENA and BARBARA LERENA at SAN JOSE DE MAYO, whose son Carmelo
  Anselmo was born on 20 April 1846 and died on the 27th. The right town and the
  right decade for the elder Alejandro already here, and a wife nobody has heard
  of. Either he married twice or there is a third Alejandro; an index will not
  decide it and the 1846 baptism will.
  Florencio Lerena with a TERESA Lerena, which collides with the Florencio here
  whose wife is Juana Recuero. Three readings are open, including the dull one -
  an index putting a mother's maiden surname where her married one belongs.
Fourteen people entered, all index-level, every row saying so.
AND I ALMOST ENTERED A FAMILY THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD. Aurora Lerena, her
husband Manuel Vaquero and their daughter went in from the query before I
noticed they were here already as Aurora LERENA Fernandez, found by the Trinidad
birthplace sweep yesterday - the index's "Elmira" being her Delmira Eugenia,
born 13 November 1892, with the D dropped. The build refused only because Manuel
Vaquero collided with himself by EXACT NAME. The other two would have passed
every gate, because a duplicate under a different spelling is not a duplicate to
a name check. Backed out, and her row now records both the near-miss and the
corroboration: two different routes, the same parents, the same five children.
One pair written by hand because the gate did not raise it: the card's MARIA
LERENA against the Maria Lerena who married Costales in 1865. She is the closest
configuration the index has produced - a Maria Lerena born of two Lerenas - and
the arithmetic does not forbid her, but it requires a widowhood and a second
partnership that no record shows. Recorded so nobody quietly promotes her.
599 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: Bring the Argentine-branch section up to the day, and stop calling him a doctor
commits.body:
The page said "a second doctor of the name", which in English means a physician.
Doctor on a Uruguayan act is the style of an abogado as much as of a medico, and
Arturo's daughter's marriage act and his own death act both give him plainly as
"de profesion abogado". Corrected, with a line saying what the title does and
does not carry - and Ambrosio keeps the title and loses the implied profession,
because nothing on the 1880 act says which he followed.
Added: the death act of 2 March 1936 at Treinta y Tres 269; the sibship of six
with Cora Maria AVELINA and Roberto AMBROSIO carrying their grandparents' names;
and the two things the documents will not close - one Ema among five survivors
where this register holds two born on 18 May, and three secondhand ages giving
1857-58 against one baptism giving 1861, with a note that FamilySearch's own
tree has merged the two men and that a tree is not a document.

commits.subject: Arturo Lerena died at two in the morning, and the act still will not settle him
commits.body:
Montevideo, acta No. 8, 2 March 1936:
  "declarando que a las DOS HORAS del dia de hoy y en TREINTA Y TRES 269,
   fallecio ARTURO LERENA... NACIDO EN MONTEVIDEO, de SETENTA Y OCHO ANOS DE
   EDAD, de estado casado, DE PROFESION ABOGADO... Que el finado era HIJO DE
   A[V]ELINO [L]ERENA y de AMBROSIA TR[A]IBEL, AMBOS FALLECIDOS... era casado
   con [E]MA REGULES, de cuyo consorcio quedaron CINCO HIJOS llamados EMA,
   MARIO, EDUARDO, CORA y ROBERTO."
It confirms his parents a second time and the ABOGADO correction a second time,
and it gives him a death: 2 March 1936, at Treinta y Tres 269, aged 78.
IT DOES NOT SETTLE WHETHER HE IS JUAN ARTURO LERENA TRAIBEL, and the reason is
worth keeping. Seventy-eight in March 1936 means 1857-58, which agrees with
twenty-two in June 1880 and sixty-two in January 1920 - three independent
statements - against one baptism of a "JUAN ARTURO" on 16 February 1861. But
all three ages are secondhand: the declarants here were an Italian employee of
forty and a young man of twenty-three, neither of them family, which is the
ordinary shape of a city death registration.
FamilySearch's own tree has merged them already, attaching this record to a
profile "Juan Arturo Lerena Traibel, 1861-1936". That is a tree, not a document,
and this register keeps them apart until an act does the joining.
The five surviving children name only ONE Ema, where this register holds two
born on 18 May - 1881 and 1885. That tilts the question without closing it:
five surviving of six is also what the act would say if a sister had died. Both
rows now carry the count and neither is merged.
Four people entered from the act, because it is about one of our own: the
registrar Luis Barbe, the declarants Carlos Bastos and Marcos S. Acuna, and
Dr Jorge Calvette, who signed the medical certificate - the first doctor in this
register who is certainly a physician, which is worth saying on the day the
other two turned out to be lawyers.
One prose fix so the tooling could read it: his row listed his son's death as
"d. 6 May 1949" beside his own, and last-alive.py refused to choose between two
death years on one row - correctly. Re-worded; he now carries 1936-Mar-2.
585 people, 40 with an exact death date. All gates green.

commits.subject: Six children, and two of their names prove their grandparents
commits.body:
One parent-pair query - father Arturo Lerena, mother Emma Regules - returned
eight records and the whole known sibship:
  Ema Justina Felicia   b. 18 May 1881, San Jose
  Arturo Mario          b.  9 Apr 1884, San Jose; d. 6 May 1949, Montevideo
  Emma                  b. 18 May 1885, San Jose; m. Yeregui 1909
  Eduardo               b. 22 Apr 1886, Montevideo; m. Razzetti 1920
  Cora Maria AVELINA    b.  8 Jun 1887, christened at the Union 23 Oct 1887
  Roberto AMBROSIO      b.  1 Nov 1896, Montevideo
AVELINA and AMBROSIO are Arturo's own parents' names - Avelino Lerena and
Ambrosia Traibel - in the feminine and the masculine. So the 1880 marriage act's
parentage is corroborated by the next generation's forenames, without opening a
second act. A household names its children for its own parents, and this one did
it twice.
The family moved: San Jose from 1881 to 1885, Montevideo from 1886. Nine years
separate the fifth child from the sixth, which in a household of this period
usually means children this query did not reach.
TWO THINGS LEFT UNRESOLVED RATHER THAN TIDIED.
Ema Justina Felicia, born 18 May 1881, shares a birthday with Emma, born 18 May
1885 - same day, same month, same department, same parents. Two daughters
genuinely born on one date four years apart; one daughter with a mis-indexed
year; or an elder child who died and whose name and date were reused, which this
register has met before and warned about. Not merged: the 1909 marriage act is
explicit that the bride was born in 1885, and it is the only one of the two that
has been read as an act.
And the index gives EDUARDO a birth of 1868 where his own marriage act says
1886. A digit transposition that would have cost a day if it had been believed -
which is the argument for opening acts, in one line.
All index-level. No act opened, and every row says so.
581 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: Arturo is a lawyer, not a doctor - and Eduardo has a sister
commits.body:
The lead left open last night was a "Dona Emma Lerena Regules" marrying in the
Montevideo civil registers with Arturo Lerena and Emma Regules as her parents.
She is there, and the act corrects this archive's reading of her father.
Montevideo, acta No. 16, 9 August 1909:
  "Dona EMMA LERENA REGULES... NACIDA EL DIA DIEZ Y OCHO DE MAYO DE MIL
   OCHOCIENTOS OCHENTA Y CINCO EN SAN JOSE... hija de don ARTURO LERENA de
   estado casado DE PROFESION ABOGADO... y de EMMA REGULES... Fueron testigos,
   Don JUAN ZORRILLA DE SAN MARTIN, de CINCUENTA Y TRES ANOS, de estado viudo,
   de profesion ABOGADO, domiciliado en la calle RINCON."
ABOGADO. In Uruguay "Doctor" is the style of a lawyer as much as of a medico,
and the 1880 marriage act's "el Doctor Don Arturo Lerena" carries no more than
the title. This archive put "doctor" in an occupation field, which in English
means a physician, and then wrote about "two professional men" in a way that
suggested medicine. Corrected on both rows - Dr Ambrosio Lerena keeps the title
and loses the implied profession, because nothing on the 1880 act says which he
followed. Nothing was wrong with the transcription: a title was carried into
English where it means something narrower. A title is not an occupation, and a
title translated is a claim.
The sister: EMMA LERENA REGULES, born 18 May 1885 at SAN JOSE, named for her
mother, married FERMIN CARLOS DE YEREGUI - born Montevideo 4 November 1879, son
of the late Fermin de Yeregui and Mercedes de Melis, of calle Zabala 164.
So the household was at SAN JOSE in May 1885 and at MONTEVIDEO in April 1886,
where Eduardo was born. ELEVEN MONTHS APART, which is possible and tight, and is
recorded as a tension rather than resolved. In 1909 the parents are given at
different addresses - Colonia 2200 and Colonia 228, both "de estado casado". The
numbers differ by a factor of ten and a transcriber's slip is likelier than a
separation. Also not resolved.
Both witnesses were lawyers, and one of them is JUAN ZORRILLA DE SAN MARTIN:
fifty-three, widower, abogado, of calle Rincon - the national poet of Uruguay on
every count except a document that says so. Entered with no inference drawn, as
this archive entered the president who stood godfather to a Lerena child and the
bishop who dispensed a Lerena's banns. All it shows is that Arturo Lerena the
abogado moved among Montevideo lawyers.
Seven people entered. 576 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: Put the Argentine branch on the page, with what it does not prove
commits.body:
/uruguay/#s-argentine-branch tells the evening in order: two uncompared rows,
a plate that corrected the surname to RAZZETTI, a marriage act that settled the
pair on the bride's PARENTS rather than on anybody's name, and Arturo's own
wedding of 1880 naming Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel.
The last paragraph is the one that mattered to write. None of it touches Pablo
Armando. Sancho's whole house is still unplaced in this register - which here
means unjoined to the man the archive exists for - and adding a fourth
generation to a line that does not reach him changes nothing about that.

commits.subject: The Argentine household is not a namesake: it is Sancho's great-grandson
commits.body:
Searching the two surnames together - Lerena and Regules - found Arturo's own
marriage, and it reaches the trunk.
Catedral de Montevideo, 23 June 1880:
  "el DOCTOR DON ARTURO LERENA, natural de esta Republica, soltero, de VEINTE Y
   DOS ANOS de edad, HIJO LEGITIMO DE DON AVELINO LERENA Y DONA AMBROSIA
   TRAIBEL, con DONA EMMA REGULES... de DIEZ Y SEIS ANOS de edad, hija legitima
   de DON WENCESLAO REGULES y DONA JUSTINIANA MELILLA: fueron testigos el DOCTOR
   DON AMBROSIO LERENA y Dona Justiniana Melilla de Regules."
The banns were dispensed by Bishop JACINTO VERA himself; the Presbitero JUAN
JOSE BRID authorised the act.
So the chain found this evening runs: Sancho Llerena - Avelino Lerena Fernandez
and Ambrosia Traibel - Dr Arturo Lerena and Emma Regules - Eduardo Lerena, born
Montevideo 22 April 1886 - who married Maria Mercedes Razzetti at Santa Lucia in
January 1920 and baptised his daughter in a rural partido of Buenos Aires
province a year later. The Argentine household that began this afternoon as two
uncompared rows with an Italian surname is a branch of this archive's own trunk.
ARTURO IS A DOCTOR, and the witness AMBROSIO LERENA is a second doctor of the
name, new to this archive and most simply read as another of Ambrosia Traibel's
sons - which is a naming habit, not a parent, and is not claimed. Two
professional men in one generation, two after Sancho.
NOT MERGED WITH JUAN ARTURO LERENA TRAIBEL, and the objection is three years.
That man was born 16 February 1861 and christened at the Cordon, so he was
NINETEEN in June 1880, not twenty-two - and the 1920 act independently makes
Arturo sixty-two, which is 1857-58 again. An age on a marriage act bends by a
year; it does not usually bend by three, and two documents agree against one.
The couple already have eleven known children, so a twelfth is no strain.
Emma Regules married at SIXTEEN with her mother standing as a witness - the
second time this register has met a mother as a formal witness, after Ambrosia
Traibel at her own son's wedding in 1892.
Five people entered: Wenceslao Regules, Justiniana Melilla, Dr Ambrosio Lerena,
the priest Juan Jose Brid, and Bishop Jacinto Vera - the last with a note that
no acquaintance is claimed, a bishop signing dispensations by the hundred.
Two leads left open: a "Dona EMMA LERENA REGULES" marrying in the Montevideo
civil registers of 1907-08 with these same parents, and the Las Piedras
religious marriage book 1915-1937, which should hold the church half of
Eduardo's wedding.
569 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: The marriage act names his parents, and the NOT MERGED note lasted four hours
commits.body:
This morning two rows were kept apart with a line saying what would settle it:
"the Montevideo marriage act behind the 1919 dispensation, which will name his
parents". That line is a research instruction, and it was followed the same day.
Canelones, acta No. 4, Santa Lucia, 11 January 1920:
  "comparecen: don EDUARDO LERENA, de nacionalidad ORIENTAL, NACIDO EL DIA
   VEINTIDOS DE ABRIL DE MIL OCHOCIENTOS OCHENTA Y SEIS EN MONTEVIDEO, de
   profesion EMPLEADO... hijo de ARTURO LERENA, de nacionalidad oriental, de
   estado casado, de SESENTA Y DOS anos, domiciliado en MONTEVIDEO, y de EMA
   REGULES... de CINCUENTA Y CINCO anos; y dona MARIA MERCEDES RAZZETTI, de
   nacionalidad ORIENTAL, NACIDA EL DIA VEINTICINCO DE JULIO DE MIL OCHOCIENTOS
   NOVENTA Y NUEVE EN COLON... hija de DOMINGO RAZZETTI, de nacionalidad
   italiano, de CINCUENTA Y NUEVE anos, domiciliado en la CUARTA SECCION de este
   departamento, y de JOSEFINA BERTOGLIO, de nacionalidad italiana."
What proves the merge is not the names but HER PARENTS. Domingo Razzetti and
Josefina Bertoglio stood godparents to this couple's daughter at Adolfo Alsina,
Buenos Aires, on 19 January 1921 - entered here this afternoon from the plate,
when all that could be said of Domingo was that he carried her surname and so
was "her father, her brother or her uncle". He is her father. The same four
people in two countries, thirteen months apart.
So: one Eduardo Lerena, not two. Born at Montevideo on 22 April 1886 - an exact
birth date, which this archive has for very few of its people - an empleado at
Santa Lucia, married at twenty-three to a girl of twenty.
A NEW HOUSEHOLD, AND IT IS THE RIGHT GENERATION TO BE CAREFUL ABOUT. ARTURO
LERENA, ORIENTAL, born about 1857, alive and married in Montevideo in January
1920, husband of EMA REGULES. He is NOT Arturo Lerena Garcia, the SPANISH
journalist already in this register with sons surnamed Lerena Diaz; nationality
separates them on the face of two acts and they are kept apart, not excluded
forever.
And Ema Regules is now a candidate for something found earlier today: an "Ema.
Lerena" stood godmother at the Cordon in 1900-02 beside an EDUARDO LERENA. A
wife appears in a parish book under her husband's name, and her son Eduardo was
fourteen to sixteen then. Recorded as a candidacy with its own objection
attached - fourteen is young to stand godfather - and not merged.
The bride is Uruguayan, not Italian: born at Colon on 25 July 1899, the first
generation born here of an Italian couple. She signs her own name Razzetti,
which is the spelling this register now uses.
564 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: A fourth pair of Lerenas at a font, and a boundary the rule does not draw
commits.body:
The second Cordon volume, August 1900 to October 1902. One Lerena entry and it
is two people: EDUARDO LERENA and "Ema. Lerena" stood godparents together to
Juan Eduardo, son of Juan Silva and Toribia Martinez.
Neither is identified and both are entered as themselves. This register now
holds FOUR men called Eduardo Lerena and none is merged with another: the father
of Ana Maria Lerena Razzetti at Adolfo Alsina in 1921, the man dispensed banns
at Montevideo in December 1919, Avelino Eduardo Lerena Traibel, and this one.
The Cordon is the Lerena Traibel parish, which makes Avelino Eduardo the nearest
candidate and is not an argument - he is "Avelino Eduardo" on every act read of
him, never Eduardo bare. The godmother could be Ema Sixta Lerena Juanico, born
1876, or Maria Ema Lerena Lenguas, christened 1857; the panel gives "Ema." with
an abbreviating stop, no age and no second surname, and a third Ema cannot be
excluded. Both pairs recorded rather than guessed.
AND A BOUNDARY IS WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN SETTLED QUIETLY. The Silva household
is not admitted. The rule in check-people-named.py admits everyone named on an
