act our person is a PARTY to, and a godparent is a party - so by the letter of
it, Juan Silva, Toribia Martinez and four grandparents should all be in this
register. They are not, and the same choice was made at the Cordon act of
1891-92 a few hours earlier without being noticed. The reason is that a baptism
is ABOUT the child's household and a Lerena standing at the font is a guest at
it; admitting the guests' hosts would fill this register with families no Lerena
belongs to. The rule does not yet say this. Both rows name the household in full
so nothing is lost if it is later drawn the other way.
The date within the volume is not established - the book runs fourteen months
and this was read from the names panel, not the page.
562 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: ROZZETTI is RAZZETTI, and the plate says it twice
commits.body:
Chasing a duplicate, not a spelling. This register held an EDUARDO LERENA
dispensed the conciliar banns at Montevideo on 22 December 1919 to marry "Dona
MARIA MERCEDES RAZZELLO, feligresa de LAS PIEDRAS", and a second EDUARDO LERENA
in Buenos Aires married to a MARIA MERCEDES ROZZETTI. Two rows, never compared.
The test was the daughter's act. The index gives her as Ana Maria Lerena
Rozzetti, born 12 January 1921. The plate, in a clear hand:
  "bautizo solemnemente a ANA MARIA que nacio el dia doce de Enero del ano mil
   novecientos veintiuno, HIJA LEGITIMA de D. Eduardo Lerena y de D.a Maria
   Mercedes RAZZETTI, domiciliados en ESTE PARTIDO. Padrinos: D. DOMINGO
   RAZZETTI y D.a JOSEFINA BERTOGLIO."
The surname is written twice on one line by one scribe - once for the mother,
once for the godfather who carries her name - so the reading is confirmed inside
its own sentence. ROZZETTI was never on the page.
The index is wrong about the place too. It normalises the event to "Buenos
Aires City" while its own original-place field says ADOLFO ALSINA and the act
says "este partido" - a rural district of the province, four hundred kilometres
from the capital.
Both published addresses redirect. The slug ledger keeps the dead keys, as it
did for the ZALSAMENDI rows: a corrected surname is not kept in a URL for
tidiness.
And the pair it was opened for got stronger without being proved. RAZZELLO and
RAZZETTI are one hand read twice - far closer to each other than either is to
the index's ROZZETTI - and a couple dispensed in December 1919 with a first
child born 12 January 1921 is thirteen months, which is what a marriage looks
like. NOT MERGED: no act yet read calls the Buenos Aires man oriental, and a
merge would carry a Uruguayan origin onto an Argentine household on the strength
of a date and two forenames. What would settle it is the Montevideo marriage act
behind the 1919 dispensation, which will name his parents.
Ana Maria gains a birth date, a baptism, a parish, a priest and two godparents.
Three people entered: Domingo Razzetti, Josefina Bertoglio, and the cura Jose
Serrano Lopez.
NOT MINE, AND LEFT ALONE: site/package.json, site/package-lock.json and
site/.kitpin are modified in this tree by another session bumping the archive-kit
pin from 3c9214e9 to 22e5fc93. That install ran while my build was running and
broke it once with "Cannot find module .../lib/assetv.js"; the new kit moves lib
under kit/lib and maps it through exports, the file is there, and a re-run is
clean. Those three files are not in this commit.
560 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: The eighteen silent findings, worked through one at a time
commits.body:
Not one list of eighteen things. drift.py reports each watched person's FIRST
unpublished emphasised claim and then moves on, so publishing one surfaces the
next - the count fell to 14, then 13, with different claims each time. Chasing
it to zero by writing prose would mean publishing every emphasised sentence in
the register, which is the opposite of what a page is for. So each was opened
and sorted by what it actually was.
THREE WERE GENUINELY UNPUBLISHED AND ARE NOW WRITTEN UP.
/uruguay/#s-fernandez-knot, a new section: the kindred married its cousins
twice over and only one knot is made of Lerenas. Socorro's own marriage of 1855
was dispensed in the second grade by the transverse line, and that degree runs
down the FERNANDEZ side - her mother Margarita Fernandez Alvarez and her
husband's father Manuel Fernandez Alvarez. For a day that was an inference from
the degree and the compound surname; the 1825 act names Margarita's parents as
Juan Fernandez Alvarez and Barbara Sotura, and the 1855 expediente gives
Serapio's grandparents as "Don Juan y Dona Barbara Sotura". Same couple. Five
dispensations across three generations of one small inland town. The section
also carries Antonina the elder - a priest drew that parentage in 1858 and a
juez de paz wrote it into her death act in 1911, two record systems neither
copying the other - Alejandro's two birthplaces and why the 1858 plural looks
like a clerk collapsing them, and the two Juan Pelaez.
/argentina/#s-villademoros-flores: the Lerena Villademoros at a Buenos Aires
font in 1918, Membrillar 96, with the warning that THIS Flores is not the
Uruguayan department this archive spends its time in, and her stated age
recorded as a conflict rather than resolved.
/south-africa/: the transcribers made a different man of Nuno on each folio -
"Huno" on one, "Jan Fernando" on the other - and the clerk wrote NUNO plainly
both times. What identified him was not his name but the 6.10.24 date of birth
the deeds register keys on. The identifier the clerk never misspelled is the one
that was not a word.
SEVEN WERE THE ARCHIVE'S OWN BOOKKEEPING. That a row was merged, that a slug
moved, that a birth year was invented here for an hour and withdrawn. They are
published - on /corrections/ and /worklist/, which this check EXCLUDES BY DESIGN
as "ledgers OF the work, not places a reader meets the story". So it was
demanding that bookkeeping appear somewhere it had itself ruled bookkeeping out
of. drift.py now skips them, with every pattern carrying the claim it was
written for.
SEVEN WERE ALREADY PUBLISHED and tripped a word-matcher - the page says "polling
district" and the register says STEMDISTRIK. Each is now in PUBLISHED with where
it was published and why the words differ. I opened every page before writing
the entry, because adding a name to that list is a claim that somebody looked.
AND THE EXCEPTION LISTS THEMSELVES HAD ROTTED. Three of fourteen names in
PUBLISHED, and one of nine pairs in CHECKED_PAIRS, named people the register no
longer holds: renames and a corrected birth year had left each exception
pointing at nobody, so the finding it excused came back wearing a new name. The
Carolina Suarez entry in consistency.py says in as many words that "a renamed
row silently un-declares its own pair, which is why this list is checked after
every rename". It was not being checked. A comment is not a check. Both tools
now report a stale key, and both were made to fail before being believed.
drift: "nothing looks stale". consistency: "nothing contradicts itself".

commits.subject: Record the two plates the audit re-read
commits.body:
Both are reads of film 007713376, and the second is the control for the first.
Image 01689 deleted a person: the act says "Nieto Pat.o de D. JOAQUIN RODRIG.z"
where this archive's own page had quoted it with DOMINGO inside square brackets.
Image 00601 is the other grandchild's act, read to see whether the two name the
same paternal grandparents - they do, which is what licensed merging the two
Juanas rather than leaving the merge on a single reading.
63 searched rows.

commits.subject: A dek that said eight while the eyebrow counted nine
commits.body:
/tree/ renders its eyebrow from the chart - `${drawn} people` - and had the
sentence under the title typed by hand: "eight people, and then the doors
close". The chart reached NINE and the sentence stayed at eight, so the page
contradicted itself in two lines of the same heading. A number written beside a
number that computes itself will always lose, so the dek computes too, spelling
it in words as the prose wants.
Swept the rest of the site for the same shape - spelled numbers next to people,
lanes, walls, generations, children - and the others hold: Sancho's EIGHT
children at Canelones, the Taylors' NINE, Gilberto's EIGHT by Julia Salvanach
are three different families, not one disagreement.
/uruguay/ was contradicting itself at distance. Near the top it says Socorro's
parents "are not named, so that link is inferred and not proved"; two hundred
lines down, the 1855 and 1858 expedientes make her and Bernabe both children of
Alejandro and Margarita, and the page says so plainly - "it was an inference for
a day and it is a document now". No gate can see this one: check-superseded.py
fires on claims RETRACTED in corrections.tsv, and this was never wrong, only
open, and then closed. The inference is left standing where it was written,
because the point of it is that it was made before the document was found - with
a forward pointer, so a reader meeting it first does not have to scroll to learn
that it closed.

commits.subject: The changelog had been stale for a month, and nothing ran the generator
commits.body:
/changes/ exists to list every change to this archive. It was showing five days
ending 14 September. The repository had twenty days of commits ending this
morning. Fifteen days of work - every find of the last month, on the day it was
found - was simply absent from the page that exists to list it.
The cause is dull and worth naming: build-changes.py sat in tools/ and was run
by nothing. Not verify.sh, not package.json, not CI. A generator nobody runs is
a stale page with extra steps. It is now the third line of verify.sh, beside
build-pages and build-people.
Rebuilding it immediately broke the build, which is the system working. Thirty-
five commits in this history quote register prose and carry its *** emphasis
markers; SIX carry an ODD number, where a quotation opened an emphasis and ended
at the line break. changes.astro renders commit text through emph(), which
converts PAIRS - so the orphans survived and three raw *** reached the page, and
check:pages refused it.
A commit message cannot be rewritten, so build-changes.py now drops a trailing
unmatched marker. The TSV guard that FAILS on an odd count is untouched: there,
an unbalanced marker is an author's mistake to fix, and the author is available.
Here the author is the past.
650 changes across 20 days, today's 37 at the top.
Also on /name/: the page has long argued from Forebears that "there is exactly
one real Lerena cluster in Spain, and it is in La Rioja", at forty times the
national rate. This morning's consular find puts a household in Navarrete,
"provincia de Logrono" - which IS La Rioja, under the name it carried until
1980. The two halves of that page had not been introduced. They are now, and
the paragraph says plainly that agreement is not proof: La Rioja is where a
Spanish Lerena is likeliest to be found, so finding one there was the likeliest
outcome. What the household adds is its shape, not its region.

commits.subject: Fifteen people's pages said nothing was known while we held their marriage
commits.body:
/people/carmen-lorente/ said "No relationships are recorded for this person"
while data/relations.tsv held "Avelino LERENA Villademoros | spouse | Carmen
LORENTE". Fourteen others were the same.
A marriage is symmetric and was being read one way only. build-people.py
reverses father/mother edges into children - fixed on 13 September for exactly
this reason, when every parent in the archive showed an empty children list -
but nobody ever reversed spouse. So the wife named on her husband's row got
nothing on her own page.
That sentence is word for word the one check-evidence.py was written to abolish
in September. It came back through a door that gate was not watching: everything
in it guards data/person-evidence.tsv, and nothing looked at relations.tsv. A
gate that names one file guards one file.
So the gate now also refuses when a person named in relations.tsv has no
relationship drawn on their page. Tested by removing the fix and watching it
report all fourteen, then restoring it - a gate that has never been seen to fail
is not known to work.
One person was left over after the mirror: the unnamed infant son of Roque Luis
Armando Lerena, dead at Bloemfontein in 1932. His only edge was written "Roque |
child | the infant", and the builder reverses parent edges into children but not
child edges into parents, so his page drew nothing at all. He was the only one of
36 in that position - the other 35 child edges sit beside an explicit parent edge
- so the edge was rewritten in the direction the builder reads rather than
teaching the builder to guess which parent a "child" edge means.
Zero people now have an edge the site does not draw.

commits.subject: A man in square brackets: Don Domingo Rodriguez never existed
commits.body:
Found by auditing the site rather than by looking for him.
This archive quoted the 1840 Catedral act on its own page as "Nieto pat[erno de
D. DOMINGO] RODRIG.z" - and the forename inside those brackets was supplied by
the reader, almost certainly because the CHILD being baptised is called Domingo.
A person row was then built from it, published at /people/don-domingo-rodriguez
for three weeks, drawn on his grandson's chart, and given a wife.
The plate says JOAQUIN. Re-read at 4000px off the deepzoom tile: "Nieto Pat.o de
D. JOAQUIN RODRIG.z y D.a Juana del Espiritu S.to: ambos nat.s de la Colonia del
Sacram.to". The act's own names panel independently gives "Pats. Joaquin
Rodriguez". The paternal grandfather is MAYOR DON JOAQUIN RUIZ DE CARVALLO, who
was already in this register, named on the other grandchild's act of 1827, under
this register's known second spelling of the surname - which his own row has
said all along while the phantom sat two rows away contradicting it.
The same bracket split one woman into two. "Dona Juana del ESPIRITU SANTO" was
entered as the phantom's wife; "Dona Juana SUAREZ" sat here as Joaquin's. Both
acts name her as the mother of Capitan Antonio - Juana Suarez in 1827, Juana del
Espiritu Santo in 1840 - so they are one woman, and the only obstacle to saying
so was a misread forename. Merged into Suarez, the inherited name, with the
devotional form kept in her prose so a search still finds her. The 1840 act also
gives her birthplace, which neither row had: the COLONIA DEL SACRAMENTO.
Both published addresses now redirect to the people the act actually names.
Two further readings off the same plate: the godfather is "D. JOAQUIN SOSA DE
CRUZ SECO" - this register had "Don Joaquin Sosa", the machine panel "Juaquin
Losada Cruz Seco" - and BALVINA SUAREZ as godmother stands confirmed.
It surfaced only because a soft warning was read instead of skimmed.
consistency.py had been listing the two Juanas among EIGHT things to look at,
and THREE of those eight were a bug in the gate itself: a row whose prose quotes
"hija legitima de X y de Y" twice was appended to its own sibling cohort twice
and compared with herself, reporting people as 0 months apart from themselves.
Fixed, and the three clear pairs are now in CHECKED_PAIRS with reasons. Noise in
a soft list is worse than silence - it teaches the reader to skim it.
THE LESSON IS ABOUT SQUARE BRACKETS. This archive uses them for honest editorial
reconstruction of damaged text, and that is right. But a reconstruction inside a
quotation reads exactly like a transcription once it is three weeks old. A name
supplied by a reader must never become a person row.
Also: the ark for the Pocitos plate of 15 August 1903 was carried by three rows
citing it and missing from four. Added.
557 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: Four things to do next, written down where the next session will find them
commits.body:
Navarrete's parish and civil registers; the twelve unread Uruguayan hits for
the phrase "Lerena y Lerena"; the second Registros Consulares volume of 1909;
and "el Doctor Lerena" in the 1889 Aguirre probate - with a warning attached to
that last one, because in this corpus "lerena" is very often the transcriber
reading the word herencia.
205 rows.

commits.subject: Adolfo Lerena was standing at fonts twelve years earlier than we knew
commits.body:
The Cordon is this family's own parish - Alejandro Maximo Lerena married Elisa
Villademoros there in 1871, and the Lerena Traibel were christened there - and
its 1891-92 baptism book had never been opened here.
One Lerena entry in the volume, and it is two people. ADOLFO LERENA and MARIA
MERCEDES LERENA stood godparents together to Balvina Maria, daughter of Manuel
Cabrera and Balvina Valdivia.
This archive knew Adolfo only as the godfather at Pocitos in August 1903, where
it reasoned that a Lerena at the font of a Lerena woman's child is probably her
brother. He was an adult at the Cordon by 1891.
The woman is new, and she is NOT merged with any of the four Mercedes already
in this register - Mercedes Micaela Lerena Traibel born 1863, the Catedral
godmother of 1880, the Mercedes who married Luis P. Marquez in 1883, and
Mercedes Lerena de Martinez of Mendoza in 1902. Each pair is recorded with its
own reason. The forename runs through this family too hard to separate anyone,
and the names panel gives her no age, no parents and no second surname. She
carries no married name either, which is why brother and sister is the likeliest
reading of the pair and is not proved.
Said plainly on both rows: the date within the volume is NOT established. The
book runs January 1891 to July 1892 and this was read from the names panel, not
from the page, so the act itself is still worth opening.
559 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: Two Lerenas at a font, and the Larriera grandparents fall out of it
commits.body:
The phrase "Lerena y Lerena" mostly finds two Lerenas joined by "and" rather
than the compound surname - "padrinos Avelino Lerena y Adelina Lerena" - and in
this archive that is worth more, because two Lerenas standing together at a
font is a relationship.
Fifteen of the 27 hits are Uruguayan. This one is the christening of MARIA
ADELINA LERENA LARRIERA, a row carried as index-level since 21 September with
the ark recorded and nothing read.
The names panel gives all four grandparents. Paternal: Avelino Lerena and
Ambrosia Traibel, already known here as the head of the Lerena Traibel branch.
Maternal: MIGUEL LARRIERA and CAROLINA CHAVARRIA, who were not known at all.
They are the parents of Maria Ines Larriera - a woman whose row said "nothing
else in this archive names her", and which has now been corrected twice, first
by eight children and now by two parents.
It also corrects a generation. Her brother ANGEL MIGUEL AVELINO was said on his
page to carry his GREAT-grandfather's name; Avelino Lerena Fernandez is his
grandfather. The edges in relations.tsv were right the whole time, so the chart
on the page disagreed with the prose beneath it and nothing checks that those
agree. What made the error obvious was learning the OTHER grandfather's name:
Angel Miguel Avelino is named for BOTH of them, Miguel Larriera and Avelino
Lerena. A naming pattern is evidence only when you know both sides of it; with
one side it is a story.
Two more details worth keeping. The christening is at the Montevideo cathedral
although she was born in the Departamento de San Jose. And the transcriber
spells this family four ways on one page - Lerena, Lereña, Serena, Levena -
which is the ordinary condition of this surname and the reason this archive
searches by shape rather than by letter.
Five same-name pairs cleared, one of them by hand and deliberately: "Maria
LERENA" - the mother on the enrolment card, the woman this archive exists to
find - against Maria Adelina Lerena Larriera, who was two and a half years old
when Pablo Armando was born.
558 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: The brother who stayed in Navarrete kept its civil register
commits.body:
A phrase search for "Lerena y Lerena" - which cannot produce the herencia
false positive, because herencia is one word - returned 27 results. The second
is a Madrid government pension file of 1896, and it is signed by a man entered
in this register twenty minutes earlier:
  "D. Jose Dolores Lerena y Lerena, Juez municipal suplente de esta villa,
   encargado de la Jurisdiccion por ausencia del propietario, y tambien del
   Registro Civil de la misma. Certifico: Que en dicho Registro, seccion de
   Defunciones, al folio ciento noventa y uno del tomo undecimo se encuentra
   el acta que dice asi..."
- the death at Navarrete on 11 November 1895 of Juan Manuel Chavarri Oteyza of
Fuenmayor, aged seventy.
His brothers' power of attorney of 1900 calls him "casado y propietario",
which understates him: he was the acting magistrate of the town and the man
who kept its civil register.
Nobody from that death act is admitted - not Clemente Huergo, not Chavarri
Oteyza, not the judge Briones y Briones, not the secretary Velasco de la Plaza.
He is the official of record and they are the business of his office. That is
the boundary written into check-people-named.py two days ago, and this is the
second Lerena registrar it has been applied to in two days, after Vicente
Lerena Diaz at Pueblo Brugo.
Which makes three men of this name holding a register or a jurisdiction in
three countries: Ramon Lerena, Alcalde de la Santa Hermandad del Partido del
Rosario, 1796-1800; Jose Dolores Lerena y Lerena at Navarrete, 1895-96;
Vicente Lerena Diaz at Pueblo Brugo, Entre Rios, 1938. No connection is
claimed and there is no reason to think one exists - a village needs a
literate man, and these are three different villages a hemisphere apart. It is
written down because this archive would otherwise meet the coincidence again
in six months and mistake it for a pattern.
It also opens something concrete: the Juzgado Municipal of Navarrete kept its
deaths in numbered volumes, tomo 11 at folio 191 by November 1895. The civil
register of the one village where Lerenas married Lerenas exists and is
described.
A control was run first and passed. The phrase "Juan Carlos Lerena" returns
two results in the whole corpus, exactly the two found on 15 September, both
already excluded - so a month of corpus growth has still produced no other man
of that name anywhere in the world.

commits.subject: Most of those 700 hits are the word "herencia"
commits.body:
Opened the 1795 Convento de San Francisco probate because it is from Ramon
Lerena's decade. The transcript says "que las Gallego admitio absolutamente LA
LERENA, y que no hizo inventario de bienes", and three lines up, "verificarse
LA LERENCIA".
The word is HERENCIA. Admitir la herencia - to accept an inheritance, here
without benefit of inventory - is ordinary legal Spanish, and "la lerena" means
nothing. The same page of results offered "non lerena rece en el" and "as
lerena le coma con la tras", both the same word.
So in a corpus made entirely of probate files, the commonest word in the corpus
impersonates the surname this archive searches for. "700 full-text hits for
Lerena in Argentina" was never 700 appearances of a rare name. The real number
is unknown, much smaller, and only reading each hit can tell.
This archive has been careful about false ZEROS for a month and had no name for
a false POSITIVE. data/false-zeros.tsv now carries one, with the general rule:
before trusting a full-text count, find out what your surname is a misreading
of in that language and that document type. A name that collides with an
ordinary word of the register's own vocabulary will be found everywhere, mean
nothing, and do it most in the records that look most promising.
The same page did yield a real man. The case "Escalada, Carlos M.; Lerena,
Carlos A." is TITLED with him, so he is a party: in February 1890 CARLOS A.
LERENA sued the estate of Don Carlos Maria Escalada "sobre cobro de pesos",
claiming "la comision por la compraventa a que se refiere". The estate's
lawyer A. Ferreyra asked for dismissal with costs because the claim rests on
his bare word - "no acompana documento alguno en que conste lo que asevera. NI
TAMPOCO PUEDE ACOMPANARLO". A Lerena working as a broker in Buenos Aires in
1890, which is the right city and decade and nothing more; kept apart from
Carlos Lerena of Mendoza. 91 images, one read, outcome unknown.
556 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: Five deaths this archive knew and the tool could not read - fixed in the prose
commits.body:
The new ALIVE AT report named 52 rows where the prose says somebody died and
the death pattern could not get a date out of it. Five of those deaths were the
person's own, all written in the most natural order there is:
  Died as an infant, 28 Aug 1937.
  Died at Montevideo 12 December 1897 aged twenty-five, unmarried.
  died Montevideo 24 August 1940.
  died at Montevideo on 22 January 1922.
  Died at Montevideo on 5 January 1914.
I first tried to teach DEATH to step over a place name and over this register's
*** emphasis markers ***, and threw the attempt away. It moved 19 rows instead
of 5: two people LOST death dates they already had, and Juan Zalduondo, Dolores
Pou de Zalduondo and Angelica Maria Lerena Villademoros were all three given
the SAME death date, 22 August 1913 - which is one person's death act naming the
other two. That is exactly the bug the 8 October comment in this tool warns
about, reintroduced by widening the pattern rather than ranking its matches.
So the prose was fixed instead, which is what the tool's own report asks for and
cannot leak onto anybody else: the date now follows the word and the place
follows the date.
39 exact death dates, up from 34. The report is down to 47 rows, and the rest
are deaths that belong to SOMEBODY ELSE on the row - a wife's death act, a
mother's registration, a husband's. Those stay unparsed on purpose.

commits.subject: The sixth Lerena who married a Lerena, not the first - and I had found the fifth that morning
commits.body:
Published twenty minutes ago on /method/, /uruguay/, /argentina/, /name/ and
open question 1: that the Navarrete household proved a Lerena could marry a
Lerena, and so removed a reason to doubt Pablo Armando's enrolment card.
The register already held five such couples. Two at Trinidad (1894, 1913), the
double-first-cousin dispensation of 1911, Alejandro - and Eloy Lerena with
Felisa Lerena, both "natural de Espana", baptising their daughter Juana at San
Jose de Flores on 10 November 1912. That one was found THE SAME MORNING and
written into THE SAME TABLE a few hours earlier, and his row says in capitals
that he "MAKES A FIFTH LERENA-MARRIED-A-LERENA COUPLE".
So the objection I claimed to have weakened had already been answered, by me,
before lunch.
What Navarrete actually adds survives the correction and is worth having: the
first such household outside South America, the first where the children carry
the name doubled as a surname of record - signing themselves "Lerena y Lerena",
not merely having two Lerena parents - and the first time the practice has a
place on a map whose parish registers can be opened.
Caught by an audit of tools/last-alive.py, which had nothing to do with it: a
sloppy regex of mine flagged Eloy's row, and reading it to clear the flag
showed the sentence. No gate could have caught this. A claim of novelty is not
a claim about a person, a date or a link, so no consistency check touches it;
the only defence is to search this register for the thing you are about to call
new, and I did not.
Re-worded in all five places, with the overclaim and its correction left
visible rather than quietly edited out.

commits.subject: last-alive could only read deaths, so everyone else was "birth only"
commits.body:
The file is called LAST DEMONSTRABLY ALIVE and until today it computed nothing
of the kind for anyone without a death date. A man who stood in front of a
notary and signed his name on a stated day was filed as "born_est only - a
floor, not an attestation", as though nothing were known of him after his
birth. The four Lerena y Lerena of Navarrete arrived that way and the gap
stopped being tolerable.
New tier ALIVE AT: 122 of 553 people. It is the last day this archive can SHOW
someone living, and it says nothing about when they died.
It is deliberately the most timid thing in the file, because the first version
was wrong 13 times out of 82 and every failure is written into the tool:
  - SEVEN HAD A 2026 DATE. This archive stamps its own prose - "TRANSCRIPT READ
    11 OCTOBER 2026", "withdrawn 9 October 2026" - so nearly every good note
    carries the day somebody worked on it, and the tool read that as the day a
    man born in 1836 was last seen alive. Dates in the archive's own working
    years are now refused outright; they cannot be a living person either,
    because living people carry no dates here at all.
  - SIX WERE DEATH OR BURIAL RECORDS whose one date is the day the person was
    registered dead.
  - TWO WERE DEATHS THE OLD PATTERN COULD NOT READ. "*** Died *** *** 28 AUGUST
    1937 ***, aged *** 1 ***" and "died Montevideo 24 August 1940" both defeat
    DEATH, which wants the date to follow the word; emphasis markers and an
    interposed place name break it. So a hole in the older pattern was being
    filled by the newer one with the wrong label, on the wrong side of the line
    between living and dead. Any mention of a death now stops ALIVE AT, and
    where the prose names a death DEATH cannot parse, the tool prints it -
    49 rows, holes to be fixed in the prose rather than hidden by a tier.
  - AND THREE LEAKS WERE ONE BUG IN THREE HATS: "Death Records" beat
    \bdeath record\b, "FreeBMD deaths" beat \bdeath\b, and "los finados" - an
    act calling a man and his wife THE DEAD - beat \bfinad[oa]\b. Every pattern
    here now tolerates the plural.
A candidate must also fall inside the person's own possible lifetime, and the
row must hold exactly one full date, so there is nothing to rank - the same
corroborate-don't-rank rule the 8 October bug forced on the death side.
Audited: 122 promoted, no death record, no self-date, nothing before a birth.

commits.subject: A Lerena really did marry a Lerena - in a village in La Rioja
commits.body:
The Spanish consulate in Buenos Aires kept its own notarial register, and this
archive had never opened one. They are worth knowing about: a Spaniard appears
in them with his VILLAGE of origin and a consular roll number, which no
Argentine civil act gives.
Escritura 368 of 14 November 1900: "comparecieron los hermanos Don Prudencio
Benito y Don Juan Jose LERENA Y LERENA, mayores de edad, solteros,
dependientes, naturales de NAVARRETE, provincia de LOGRONO, vecinos de esta
Capital e inscritos en este Consulado con los numeros novecientos cincuenta y
novecientos cincuenta y uno... confieren poder... a su madre Dona Isabela
Lorena y Basaran, VIUDA, y a su hermano Don Jose Dolores Leerena y Lerena,
CASADO Y PROPIETARIO, los dos vecinos de Navarrete, para administrar los
bienes que los dicentes poseen en Espana."
Pablo Armando's 1908 enrolment card names Juan Carlos Lerena AND Maria Lerena,
and the cheapest way to dismiss that card has always been to say a clerk wrote
the surname twice. Here is a household who really were Lerena y Lerena: a
Lerena mother, a Lerena father she survived, three sons carrying it doubled.
That is not evidence about his parents - it removes a reason to doubt the card.
No connection is claimed and none is likely. These are Riojan Spaniards and
every lane this archive has drawn is Banda Oriental stock from the 1790s, so
they go on /name/ as a namesake household - the first namesake there that is a
whole documented family rather than a stray index hit. The CEMLA extracts
already showed a traffic of young Lerena men out of Logrono into Buenos Aires
commerce (Martin at 14 in 1907, Jose M. at 16 in 1909, Jose at 16 in 1924,
Emilio and Jose Maria in 1930); the married brother at home with the land, and
the bachelors in shops across an ocean, is what that traffic looks like from
the inside.
It also probably identifies a row that has sat here as four bare facts:
"Juan Jose LERENA, b.1876, Logrono, soltero, comercio", landed 1920, 1928,
1929. Same forenames, province, civil state, trade and city, and 1876 makes
him 24 that November. NOT MERGED - CEMLA records a province and the act
records a village - and recorded in _person-pairs.txt as the strongest
unmerged pair in the file.
Open question 1, the one this archive exists to answer, now carries the
weakened objection and a new place to look: the parish registers of Navarrete.
Sixteen same-name pairs had to be cleared to get this green, and they are
worth a word of warning: the duplicates gate pairs people who share a forename
and a canonical surname AND whose notes share vocabulary, so a long note on one
row made it read like a dozen unrelated Juans. Each pair was compared on birth
date, birthplace and nationality and recorded as distinct.
553 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: In 1794 a widow picked him to count her cattle; by 1796 he was the magistrate
commits.body:
Two more Buenos Aires probate files, both found by paging past the first page
of a 700-result set instead of stopping at the first hit.
The 1796 one dates the office: "lo proveyo, mando y firmo D. Ramon Lerena,
Alcalde de la Santa Hermandad del Partido del Rosario ... octubre de mil
setecientos noventa y seis". So he held it 1796-1800, not in the single year
this archive had.
The 1794 one is the find, because in it he is not the magistrate. The alcalde
of the day walks out to "la estancia del finado Don Clemente Garcia" and there
"parecieron ante mi y testigos Don Geronimo Alonso y Don Ramon Lerena, sujetos
nombrados por la viuda para contar y tasar el ganado y caballos de dicha
estancia". They were sworn separately and signed where there was no notary.
That is a career rather than a date: a competence in livestock, a standing
good enough for a widow to trust him with her son's inheritance, and a rise to
office two years later - more than this archive holds for any other Lerena
before 1850, and none of it a birth, a marriage or a death.
It also corrects us twice. Clemente Garcia is already "el finado" in 1794 and
Celestina Gonzalez already "la viuda", so he died before 1794 and the 1800
court order is a second reckoning of an estate inventoried once already; and
the estate includes an estancia with cattle and horses, on top of the shop,
the mill and the house.
Both row titles were therefore wrong and both are renamed - and neither URL
moved, because slugify() strips parentheses. I had first written a correction
saying the date was stuck in his address and the row must carry a wrong title
forever; checking build-people.py took one grep and showed it was not true.
The frozen ledger keys were moved by hand so don-clemente-garcia and
ramon-lerena-2 still answer.
Four people admitted from the 1794 act, which Ramon Lerena was a party to:
Geronimo Alonso de Villagomez, Lorenzo Martinez de Olalla, Guillermo Hurtado
de Villagomez, Fulgencio de los Santos. None from the 1796 act, where he was
only the official of record - that is yesterday's boundary, tested on the same
man in two roles on one day. What the 1796 case was about is recorded on his
own row instead: a power of attorney challenged on the ground that the wife,
"criada sin instruccion al lado de sus padres indios guaranies", had not
understood what she signed.
549 people. All gates green.

commits.subject: A Lerena keeping a register in Entre Rios, 138 years after one kept order at the Rosario
commits.body:
The last of row 200's three snippets, opened. VICENTE LERENA DIAZ is the
Jefe del Registro Civil of PUEBLO BRUGO, Departamento Parana, Entre
Rios. The acts open and close in his name: "ante mi VICENTE LERENA DIAZ,
de Registro Civil, comparecio..." and "Ante mi: Vicente Lerena Diaz. Es
conforme con la partida que tengo a la vista."
A STRONG CANDIDACY, NOT MERGED. Arturo Lerena Garcia and Amalia Diaz had
sons surnamed LERENA DIAZ, and this register holds two: Juan Fernando,
dead at ten months at Valparaiso in 1894, and ANTONIO, who married at
CRESPO, DEPARTAMENTO DE PARANA in 1924. Vicente keeps the register of
Pueblo Brugo in THE SAME DEPARTMENT fourteen years later. A rare
compound, a small department, the right generation. The act gives him no
parents and no age, so it is not merged - and the test is named.
AND A HARDER PAIR CAME WITH IT. This register already held a VICENTE
ANTONIO LARENA at Gualeguaychu, also Entre Rios, a father in 1906 and
1913 and so born about 1875-85 - which would make him about
fifty-eight in 1938, an ordinary age for that office. The spelling is no
separation here, and neither is the department. NOT MERGED AND NOT
EXCLUDED, with what would decide it written down.
Row 159, which asks for Entre Rios to be mapped, now has three reasons
where it had one. Entre Rios is not a blank; it is three questions.
A BOUNDARY WAS ADDED TO YESTERDAY'S RULE, because this record broke it.
He signed a volume of 113 images of OTHER PEOPLE'S deaths. Read
literally, "a person named on an act this archive has read is a person
in this register" admits a day-labourer called Felix Velazquez and an
infant Albornoz, and the register fills with strangers a Lerena merely
wrote down.
SO: the act must be ABOUT one of our people, or our person a party or a
witness to it - then everyone on it is admitted. Where our person is
only the official of record, THE OFFICE IS RECORDED AND THE BUSINESS OF
THE OFFICE IS NOT. That is already how this archive behaved without
saying so: the Juez de Paz who married Angelica is here, and the other
couples he married that year are not. The line is whether our person is
in the record or merely holding the pen. In the gate and on /method/.

commits.subject: What Ramon Lerena was sent to value: a shop and a mill
commits.body:
Row 200, continued. Three more frames of the Clemente Garcia probate,
and they turn the man whose estate Ramon Lerena inventoried from a name
into a trade.
THE FIRST ITEM APPRAISED is a rancho of twenty-two varas by seven, stone
walls rendered and whitewashed both sides, FOUR DWELLINGS - one of them
a PULPERIA with counter, shelving, back-shop, parlour and bedroom. Then
a house of six doors, three with lock and fittings, and five windows,
paved floor and corridors both sides, at 746 pesos. A stone-walled,
thatch-roofed building of eleven varas by seven, at 314. And an ATAHONA
- a mill - "compuesta de casa, rueda, piedras, palo-fierro, linterna y
demas utensilios", at 310. Then the tools: stone-picks, an adze, axes, a
turned round table, a pine chest, a crowbar, a spade, a hoe.
So the man whose estate a court in Buenos Aires sent an alcalde to value
kept THE SHOP AND THE MILL OF HIS DISTRICT. That is also why the case
was worth a capital court's attention.
THE PEOPLE IN THE ROOM. The two sworn appraisers are DON BARTHOLO GARCIA
and ANDRES BRIVAQUI, who swore on a cross before Ramon Lerena to value
faithfully. A new witness, LUIS POCHEZ. And CELESTINA GONZALEZ COULD NOT
WRITE - "no firmo porque dijo no saber" - so her husband signed for her.
THREE PEOPLE IN ONE DAY'S READING COULD NOT SIGN THEIR NAMES: Sancho
Llerena, the witness who deposed before him, and the woman holding the
shop and the mill in trust for her son. Ramon Lerena signed twice. That
is not a flourish, it is what an alcalde was for in a district the
record says had no notary at all.
A CORRECTION TO THIS MORNING, not yet applied. The "Don Bartolo. Partia"
entered from image 26 is almost certainly the BARTHOLO GARCIA of image
29 - same forename, same room, same business, five days apart. His row
now says so and he is NOT renamed, because this archive does not rename
a person on a probable reading of a mangled transcript. The test is to
open both frames as images.
Still not found: the minor son's name. He is "su hijo menor" throughout.

commits.subject: Point the front page at the lines, and correct my own count
commits.body:
Three small things, one of them a mistake of mine.
THE DRAWING WAS LINKED FROM NOWHERE BUT ITS OWN PAGE. /index/ opens
with "One tree, and the joint that is missing" - the single-joint
version of exactly the question the lines drawing asks - and did not
link to /name/ at all. It now carries a note saying the break in the
tree is one joint in one line, and that there is a wider version of the
same question five lines across.
I CALLED IT SIX LINES AND THERE ARE FIVE. The heading and the contents
entry both said "Six lines of one name" while lerena-lines.tsv holds
five lanes. Nobody had read it yet, but it is the kind of slip this
archive gates against everywhere else, and it was mine. Corrected in
both places.
AND THE SIGN-OUT IS RECURRING, NOT A ONE-OFF. Three times today the
session lost FamilySearch - once partially, with index pages readable
while the images alone were shut, and twice completely with the search
redirecting too. Recorded ONCE on row 200 rather than three times, with
the operational fact worth having: a session here lasts roughly an hour,
so plan the expensive reads first and re-check the instrument after each
null rather than before. Nothing was read and no null was taken from
either signed-out state.
Row 200 stays running. 680 of 700 Argentine results unread, 244 frames
of the Clemente Garcia probate unread, and the Entre Rios snippet still
unopened.

commits.subject: Six lines of one name, drawn side by side
commits.body:
David asked whether this archive has the picture the Defranceski one
has - the several families of a shared surname drawn together so they
can be told apart. It did not. It had three descent ladders, a tree with
the missing joint broken open, and a page about the rarity of the name,
and nothing that put the distinct families beside each other.
It needed it more than most, because the question the drawing asks is
this archive's central structural question: ARE THESE ONE FAMILY OR
SEVERAL? Row 137 has said since September that the Trinidad sweep is
"the only way the Trinidad nest will ever be joined to Sancho, or shown
to be a separate family."
FIVE LANES, each with a documented beginning and a documented end:
Sancho's house out of Canelones into Montevideo; Ramon's out of Rosario
del Colla into Trinidad - whose first node is this morning's find, a man
holding office in 1800; the direct line from Rosario de Santa Fe to the
Cape; the Spanish arrivals into Buenos Aires; and Arturo Lerena Garcia
through Chile to Entre Rios.
THE RED LANE IS DRAWN BROKEN AT ITS LEFT END, because Pablo Armando's
parents are named on one card in 1908 and appear in no other record
anywhere. A solid line there would be a lie.
AND HALF THE HONESTY IS UNDER THE RULE. Five real households on no lane
- including the Lerena Larriera of San Jose, tested on 14 September and
recorded as "NOT ours", because a worked negative is worth as much as a
lane. Then the namesakes, dashed: the Italian Lerina, the Lerena of
Arequipa, a Colombian Lerrena. A picture that places everything is a
picture that is lying about something.
NO JOIN IS DRAWN BETWEEN ANY TWO LANES, and the note says why: whether
the Trinidad kindred joins Sancho's house is open with no evidence
either way. An undrawn line is a statement too.
The kit HAS this drawing - BranchRivers.astro, promoted out of
Defranceschi, and better than mine: it supports candidate-join BRIDGES,
which is exactly what Sancho-to-Trinidad will need the day any evidence
appears. It could not be used. At line 226 it prints "- the commonest
patronymic in Italy" OUTSIDE the map, so it renders unconditionally, on
a name Forebears puts at 1 in 3,431,048. That is the same fault its own
docstring records fixing once for the caption and missing here. Row 201
raised against the kit with the one-line fix; when it lands, this
archive should switch and delete its own component.

commits.subject: The court says which Rosario: "en la otra Banda Oriental"
commits.body:
Row 200, resumed. This morning Ramon Lerena's row read "the place is
indicated, not proved" - a Ramon signing as Alcalde de la Santa
Hermandad del Partido del Rosario in 1800, with the OCR around the word
ORIENTAL broken so the sentence could not be read whole.
IMAGE 22 IS THE COURT ORDER AND IT SETTLES IT. Jose Riera, Alcalde
Ordinario de Segundo Voto and Juez de Menores of Buenos Aires, addresses
"El Alcalde de la Santa Hermandad del PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO, EN LA OTRA
BANDA ORIENTAL de este [Rio]" - so the Rosario is URUGUAYAN, not the
Argentine Rosario and not Villa del Rosario in Cordoba. And the widow is
"Dona CELESTINA GONZALEZ, VECINA DEL COLLA".
This register has called him "Ramon Lerena of Rosario-Colla" since its
early weeks, on the strength of a kinship diagram a priest drew in 1858.
THE COURT PUTS HIM IN EXACTLY THAT PLACE, HOLDING OFFICE, IN 1800.
And the file gives five weeks of one man's work. Riera ordered the
inventory because the widow was RESISTING it, having "pasado a segundas
nupcias, teniendo hijo menor". On 14 October 1800 Ramon went to her
house with Juan de Urdinaran and Francisco Perez de Ceballos and
notified her IN THE PRESENCE OF HER SECOND HUSBAND. On the 15th he began
at "la nominada Villa del Rosario". On 6 November he decreed and signed.
On the 11th he returned with Perez de Ceballos, Bartolome Partia and
Andres Pais. On the 12th the appraisal continued before Nicolas
Yrigoyen. Throughout he certifies "a falta de Escribano Publico ni Real,
por no haberlo en esta Jurisdiccion" - and signs his own name, where
Sancho Llerena nine years earlier could not.
Six people admitted under yesterday's rule, including the judge whose
letter is the proof. Celestina Gonzalez and Clemente Garcia are now of
the Colla, not of Buenos Aires - the file sits in a Buenos Aires court
only because the Juez de Menores of the capital had jurisdiction over
the whole viceroyalty.
Recorded as an observation and NOT an argument: the 1858 diagram puts
RAMON LERENA and MARIA GONZALEZ at its apex, and the woman at the centre
of this file is a GONZALEZ of the Colla. Gonzalez is among the commonest
surnames in the Rio de la Plata and no connection is claimed.
/method/ and /argentina/ render this from the TSV, so both pages
corrected themselves.

commits.subject: The rule nobody had written: no role is furniture
commits.body:
A PERSON NAMED ON AN ACT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ IS A PERSON IN THIS
REGISTER, WHATEVER THEIR ROLE. Principal, parent, spouse, child,
godparent, witness, declarant, notary, priest, physician, judge - and
the other family's principals too, when our people appear inside their
file.
It is now in tools/check-people-named.py and on /method/, under the
section already called "Search for the people standing next to the
person", because it is the same sentence. Sancho Llerena was found
deposing in a stranger's marriage investigation. Ramon Lerena was found
inside a probate filed under Clemente Garcia's name. IF THE PEOPLE
STANDING NEXT TO OUR PEOPLE ARE NOT PEOPLE, THE METHOD HAS NOWHERE TO
PUT ITS OWN RESULTS.
Twenty admitted under it. The clergy who married and baptised them -
Canonigo Martin Pinero, Jose M. Ojeda of the Cordon, Presbitero Antonio
Jenara of San Jose de Flores. Joseph del Rios, the notary who took
Sancho's deposition and signed it for him because Sancho could not
write - this archive has Sancho's voice because a notary wrote one down.
Dr Bordoni Posse, whose archived certificate is a record never sought.
The Juez de Paz Eduardo J. Moratorio, with a note against the tempting
inference about the Moratorio Lerena children. The two declarants at
Eduardo Zalduondo's death, with their ages and one address.
And the people our people were standing next to: FLORENTINO GOMEZ, whom
Sancho knew from "la linea de Vitoria" and swore for - THE ONLY NAMED
ASSOCIATE OF SANCHO LLERENA THIS ARCHIVE HAS - with his bride Ana Gomez;
Clemente Garcia, dead by 1800, and his widow Celestina Gonzalez, whom
Ramon Lerena notified in person on the only day in 1800 we can place
him; and Francisco de los Santos de Acuna, the witness who deposed just
before Sancho and whose age clause is why we know Sancho's absent age is
the document's silence and not a failed search.
Plus four husbands of Lerena women at Trinidad and Amelia Lerena Cardozo
- who is NOT the Amelia merged into Angelica this morning, and whose row
says so.
13 more relation edges, so they reach the graph and not just the list.
The living rule still overrides all of it, and the gate says so.

commits.subject: No, we were not keeping every finding as a person
commits.body:
David asked. The gate said green. The gate was watching five files and
every one of them was Taylor, Brayley or South African - it was blind to
the larger half of this register, which is Uruguayan.
MEASURED: 39 of 45 people named in one session's work had no row.
Among them VIOLETA BLANCA LERENA, born 29 October 1915 - whose existence
IS this archive's published argument that the 1911 dispensation was
granted. A keystone of a page, and a reader could not click on her. And
ten other Trinidad children with birth dates and named parents,
published since 27 September. And Eduardo Zalduondo's own BROTHER, with
a death date, a birth year, both parents and a wife - left out on an
afternoon when this session created a row for a godmother about whom
nothing whatever is known.
THE FAULT WAS INCONSISTENCY, NOT OMISSION. A Juez de Paz and a witness
were admitted the same day a documented brother was not.
THE FIX IS NOT THE TWENTY-ONE PEOPLE ADDED. It is that
tools/check-people-named.py now watches the Trinidad sweep too. Its own
docstring says "the gate grows by being made to", and it had been grown
once before - on 8 October, when David asked a version of this same
question and the honest answer was "half no". It has now been asked
three times. The gate can no longer go green while the Uruguayan side
goes unadmitted.
ADDED: the eleven Trinidad children; Isidora Cardozo, Petrona Fernandez
and Rosaura Alvarez, the mothers they were born to; Rodolfo Bernardo and
Ismael Lerena, two fathers who appear once and are not placed; Juan Jose
Zalduando Pou with his wife Elisa Carlevaro and their daughter Maria
Elisa; and Rafael Costa and Leontina Soasani.
WIRED: 21 parent edges in relations.tsv, so they reach the bloodline
graph and the ancestor charts rather than sitting as isolated rows -
which was the actual complaint behind the question.
Two conflicts carried rather than smoothed: Gualberto's two children
eight months apart in 1901, and a mother the index calls Rosana on one
entry and Rosaura on the other.

commits.subject: Put the day's findings on pages, not only in data/
commits.body:
An audit against the built HTML, because this archive's documented
failure mode is a page stopping where data/ went on - five recorded
instances. Today's biggest findings reached only /register/ and the
person pages. Three now have narrative sections and the pages link to
each other.
NEW: data/fulltext-finds-2026-10-11.tsv - five findings, each with what
the document says and what it changes, including the two uncertainties
left standing (the broken OCR around "Oriental", the two candidate
Felisas).
/method/#s-two-indexes - the lesson, next to "A null is not a finding
until a control says so", where it belongs. The record index transcribes
entries into fields and catalogues principals and parents; the full-text
corpus reads the page and finds a name in a margin, a witness list or a
deposition. Before writing "not in the indexed corpus", NAME WHICH
INDEX. And a control can do more than validate a null - it can explain
it, as the Santa Fe coverage gap explains the zero for Pablo Armando.
/uruguay/#s-second-index - the Cordon marriage of 28 December 1871 and
Sancho Llerena's deposition, with the two-brothers-married-two-sisters
result and its link to the Trinidad double wedding.
/argentina/#s-buenos-aires-fulltext - the 1800 alcalde and the 1912
Spanish family, with the contents list updated as that page's gate
requires.
Every section is generated from the TSV, so none of them can drift from
the data the way a hardcoded page would.
Two build notes worth keeping. The astro build was SIGTERMed twice while
another session ran Record Atlas builds; it passes when they are not
competing, and ARCHIVE_OUT is NOT a workaround here because the link
checker still reads site/dist and reports every page unreachable. And
argentina.astro's own comment says new imports go at the TOP - inserting
one lower matched "import.meta.url" and broke the build, exactly as the
comment warns.

commits.subject: Ramon Lerena, Alcalde de la Santa Hermandad, 6 November 1800
commits.body:
The second of row 200's leads, opened. He is "ALCALDE DE LA SANTA
HERMANDAD DEL PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO", signing on 6 November 1800 in the
estate of Don Clemente Garcia and notifying the widow Dona Celestina
Gonzalez about inventories left to a minor. He certifies "a falta de
Escribano Publico ni Real, POR NO HABERLO EN ESTA JURISDICCION" - there
was no notary in the district at all.
AND HE SIGNS HIS OWN NAME, TWICE. Sancho Llerena, nine years earlier and
a few leagues away, could not. Two men of this family on either side of
that line, and the archive now has both on the same day.
THE PLACE IS INDICATED AND NOT PROVED, which is the difficulty worth
stating rather than burying. This archive's Ramon Lerena is "of
Rosario-Colla, fl. c.1800-1820" and stands at the apex of the kinship
diagram the Cura Vicario of Trinidad drew in 1858; the date fits
exactly. The file mentions a "vecindad del partido ORIENTAL", which
points across the river to Rosario Oriental in Colonia. But there is a
Partido del Rosario on the Argentine side too, the probate was
administered at Buenos Aires which held jurisdiction over both banks,
and the OCR around the word ORIENTAL is broken so the sentence cannot be
read whole. NOT MERGED INTO HIS ROW AS FACT.
ONE FRAME OF 249 HAS BEEN READ. An alcalde's jurisdiction is normally
stated in full somewhere in a file like this, so the test is simply to
read on - and a probate file is the record class that names heirs,
widows and neighbours. The frame and the image group are recorded.

commits.subject: A passenger-list name becomes a family, almost
commits.body:
The first of row 200's three snippets opened. San Jose de Flores,
Buenos Aires, baptism No. 461 of 10 November 1912: JUANA, born 25 June
1912, hija legitima of D. ELOY LERENA, natural de Espana, twenty-six,
and Dona FELISA LERENA, natural de Espana, twenty-one. Godparents
GREGORIO LERENA and ROSA DEFENARI.
BOTH PARENTS ARE LERENAS. That is the fifth Lerena-married-a-Lerena
couple in this register - and the first that is Spanish and urban rather
than Uruguayan and rural, which is worth noticing before anyone explains
the pattern by the smallness of a country parish.
AND IT WAS NOT MERGED WITH THE PASSENGER LISTS, WHICH IS THE POINT.
This archive holds a Felisa and a Gregorio Lerena who landed together at
Buenos Aires on 7 December 1911 off the INDIANA from Barcelona, and
nothing whatever else about either. A Felisa and a Gregorio stand in
this parish eleven months later. The temptation is obvious and the
arithmetic is not clean:
  the act makes Felisa 21, so born about 1891
  the 1911 passenger list makes her 1893
  the archive's OTHER Felisa, arrived 1923, is recorded 1891 exactly
and the roles do not line up either - the 1911 pair travelled TOGETHER,
which usually means a couple or siblings, but here Gregorio is only the
GODFATHER and the husband is ELOY, who is on no passenger list held
here. Both candidate rows now carry the comparison so the next session
tests it instead of inheriting it.
Three new people: Eloy, Juana, and Rosa Defenari - whose surname reads
Italian rather than Spanish, recorded as an observation and not a claim.
The other two leads - the Ramon Lerena alcalde probate of 1800 and the
Lerena Diaz keeping a register in Entre Rios in 1938 - remain unopened
snippets, and the working log still says so.

commits.subject: Row 200 opened: 700 Argentine full-text results, 503 of them legal files
commits.body:
The seam found while running a control an hour ago, worked for the first
twenty of seven hundred results.
THE SHAPE OF IT. "Lerena" returns 44,012 full-text results worldwide,
9,516 in South America, 700 in ARGENTINA. The largest Argentine
collection by far is BUENOS AIRES CITY LEGAL 1522-2011 with 503 -
probate estate case files and notarial records, indexed by CASE TITLE
and therefore invisible to the record index. Catholic Church Records
give 12, Migrations 20, Civil Registration 3. AND THERE IS NO SANTA FE
COLLECTION AT ALL, which is why the Rosario baptism cannot be found here
and why that null means nothing.
THREE LEADS IN THE FIRST TWENTY.
A RAMON LERENA signing as ALCALDE inside a Buenos Aires probate file of
1800 - four matches on one file. This register's Ramon Lerena of
Rosario-Colla is recorded as flourishing c.1800-1820 and stands at the
apex of the 1858 Trinidad kinship diagram. The date fits and the place
does not. A candidate, not a match.
A VICENTE LERENA DIAZ keeping the civil register of Pueblo Brugo,
Parana, ENTRE RIOS in 1938. The compound is the point: Arturo Lerena
Garcia married Amalia Diaz. Bears on row 159.
SPANISH-BORN LERENAS in San Jose de Flores baptisms of 1909-1912 - Eloy,
Felisa and Gregorio, each "natural de Espana". This register holds a
Felisa and a Gregorio from CEMLA passenger lists and NOTHING ELSE about
either. First chance to turn an arrival into a life.
ALL THREE ARE OCR SNIPPETS WITH ELLIPSES AT BOTH ENDS AND NO ACT WAS
OPENED. No register rows were created from them, and the file is
declared a WORKING LOG rather than published: putting snippets in front
of a stranger as findings would be the same error made with ZALSAMENDI
this morning, where a reading nobody had checked was argued for in
public. It becomes a page when the acts are read; the books are named so
that is cheap.
Also recorded: the Place filter is behind an "Expand Place" button with
off-canvas checkboxes, but once applied the filter lives in the URL and
can be reused directly. That URL is in the file.

commits.subject: A null the control explained rather than merely validated
commits.body:
The full-text corpus had cracked two standing nulls today, so it was put
to the question this archive exists to answer. "Pablo Armando Lerena"
returns ZERO. "Juan Carlos Lerena" returns two, both Uruguayan - the
Montevideo dispensation already held, and a death of 2001.
THE CONTROL WAS RUN AFTER THE NULL, AND IT DID MORE THAN PASS. "Rosario
de Santa Fe" returns 245 pages, so the instrument works and it does
reach Argentina. But the Argentine holdings it surfaces are BUENOS AIRES
PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES, SHIP INSPECTION FILES and notarial records -
NOT SANTA FE PARISH REGISTERS.
So this is a COVERAGE null and not an absence. The corpus has not read
the books that gap needs, and a zero from it says nothing about whether
the Rosario act exists. Without that control the same zero could have
been written up as a third independent confirmation that the baptism is
not there - which is precisely the error this archive made with
ZALSAMENDI this morning, in the other direction.
AND IT OPENED A RECORD CLASS NEVER TOUCHED HERE. New row 200: Buenos
Aires probate estate case files and ship inspection files. A probate
file names heirs, widows, children, addresses and property in one place.
This archive already has a Buenos Aires thread - the 1918 San Jose de
Flores baptism, Juan Carlos Llerena born there in 1910, Alejandrina
Llerena at a font in 1910 - and has never looked at a probate file for
any of them. These files are indexed by CASE TITLE, not by the people
inside them, which is exactly why the record index cannot see into them
and the full text can.

commits.subject: Sancho Llerena could not write
commits.body:
The named follow-up from an hour ago: open the next frame of his
deposition and read his age. HIS AGE IS NOT THERE, and that is a
property of the document rather than a failed search - the witness
before him closes in the standard form, "dijo ser mayor de cuarenta y
ocho anos", so the file states ages when it has them. Written down so
nobody opens this frame again hoping.
What it gives instead is smaller and sharper. His declaration continues
onto frame 341 and ends: "que dijo NO SABER ESCRIVIR, y la firmo su
merced conmigo el presente Notario, que lo doy fe. Ante mi, JOSEPH DEL
RIOS, Notario Eclesiastico." The judge signed in his place.
This archive has held Sancho since its first week and has never known
anything about the man rather than his relationships - whose father,
whose husband, whose grandfather. Now: a man who had spent years on a
frontier line, who was trusted to swear to another man's freedom to
marry, and who could not sign his own name.
The expediente closes by decreeing no canonical impediment and ordering
the marriage of Florentino Gomez and Ana Gomez to proceed.
A NAVIGATION TRAP, recorded because it cost three attempts: an image ark
PINS one image, and ?i=N is silently ignored when an ark is present. The
route that worked is the viewer's own image-number box. And
/search/film/008166573?i=341 would not have worked either - this volume
is ITEM 8 of that film, and a film query resolves against item 001,
which is a trap this archive already recorded in September.

commits.subject: Sancho Llerena speaks, and three nulls turn out to be about one index
commits.body:
Finding the 1871 Cordon marriage by full text raised a question about
everything else this archive had declared unfindable. Four work-list
rows were found reasoning from an index null. Two were re-tested the
same hour.
SANCHO LLERENA, row 26. His death is still not found and that null
stands. What turned up instead is his VOICE. A full-text search returns
four pages, one of them the marriage investigation file of FLORENTINO
GOMEZ before the Juzgado Eclesiastico of Canelones, 1776-1806, where
Sancho is a sworn witness and deposes in the first person - a role no
index ever showed him in, because the record index catalogues principals
and parents and he was neither.
He says he had "andado en la linea de Vitoria algunos anos" and knew the
groom there. WHAT THAT LINE IS, THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT KNOW AND DOES NOT
GUESS: a "linea" in the Rio de la Plata is ordinarily a military
frontier, and Vitoria is also a Basque city and a common Brazilian and
Spanish place name. The open question on whether this family is Basque
or Extremaduran is NOT advanced by it, and the row says so.
His age is on the next frame - where a deposition states it, and where
the witness before him says "mayor de cuarenta y ocho anos". That frame
has not been opened and is recorded as a cheap, named follow-up.
JOSE LORETO LERENA, row 68. Re-tested and STILL NOT THERE: "Loreto
Lerena" returns three hits, none Uruguayan. The control was run AFTER
the null, not before - "Ambrosia Traibel" returns three pages including
Montevideo parish records - so the instrument demonstrably reaches these
registers. That null now holds in TWO independent indexes, which is a
far stronger statement than the row could make yesterday.
THE RULE, added to false-zeros: the record index is built by
transcribing entries into fields and loses everyone who is not a
principal or a parent; the full-text corpus is built by reading the page
and finds a name in a margin, a witness list or a deposition. BEFORE
WRITING "NOT IN THE INDEXED CORPUS", NAME WHICH INDEX.

commits.subject: The Cordon marriage of 1871, and two brothers who married two sisters
commits.body:
Row 185 twice concluded that the marriage of Alejandro M. Lerena and
Elisa Villademoros "is not in the indexed corpus and must be walked by
image". That was true and it was not the whole truth. THE RECORD INDEX
AND THE FULL-TEXT CORPUS ARE TWO DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS, and the act is
in the second. One phrase search on "Elisa Villademoros" returned the
Cordon's Religious Marriage Records 1866-1872 - this row's own parish
and its own window. The row had named the right book and never asked the
right index.
28 DECEMBER 1871, Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Cordon. "D.
ALEJANDRO MAXIMO SERENA, soltero, natural de Montevideo, hijo de D.
AVELINO y de Dona AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, con Dona ELISA VILLADEMOROS, del
mismo estado y oriundez, hija de los finados D. PEDRO y Dona ANGELICA
VILLADEMOROS." Two conciliar banns dispensed by the Obispo Vicario
Apostolico. Witnesses: Dr Joaquin Requena and DONA AMBROSIA T. DE
SERENA - the groom's own mother, and so alive that December.
The "M." is MAXIMO.
AND THE LAST CLAUSE PAYS FOR THE WHOLE SEARCH. Celedonia Villademoros is
the daughter of Pedro Villademoros and Angelica Mendez. Elisa is the
daughter of the late Pedro and Angelica Villademoros. THEY ARE SISTERS -
a reading this archive has carried as "probably" since September - and
since Alejandro Maximo and Avelino Eduardo are both sons of Avelino
Lerena Fernandez and Ambrosia Traibel, TWO LERENA BROTHERS MARRIED TWO
VILLADEMOROS SISTERS. The Lerena Villademoros cousins are double first
cousins: the same structure found at Trinidad this morning, a generation
earlier and in another department.
It also settles the 1873 godmother. A mother dead before December 1871
cannot stand at a font in May 1873, so that Angelica Villademoros is a
third sister - which is what the row had reasoned and could not prove.
WHAT IT DOES NOT GIVE is the groom's age, which is what row 185 wanted
most: it would have separated the 1843 and 1845 readings of the La
Mauricia act. The act states status and birthplace and no number. That
question is untouched and stays open, and the row says so.

commits.subject: The bride who was the groom's mother
commits.body:
A correction to a sentence this session wrote two hours earlier. A clean
parish-index row - "Socorro Lerena, Bride, Marriage 15 July 1885,
Santisima Trinidad, Spouses Serapio Fernandez" - was written into her
register row as a dated marriage. It has every field a sourced marriage
needs and it is wrong.
Socorro Lerena was born about 1832 and in 1885 was a widow and a
property owner with a grown son - and that son is the Serapio Fernandez
of this very act. A woman cannot be both the groom's mother and his
bride. The index gives its bride as thirty, soltera, born 1855.
OPENING THE RECORD SHOWS HOW IT HAPPENED. The bride carries the groom's
own attributes field for field: age thirty, born 1855, born at Santisima
Trinidad, resident at Santisima Trinidad, single - every one identical
to his. That is not a bride. It is one party's details copied onto a
Lerena name the parser found elsewhere on the page, and the Lerena name
on that page is the mother's.
So the act of 15 July 1885 is almost certainly the marriage of SERAPIO
FERNANDEZ (hijo) to ANTONINA LERENA, dispensed three weeks earlier on
26 June 1885 for a second grade of consanguinity. Antonina's row now
carries that as a PROBABLE date, not a fact: the plate is unopened, and
the index's "thirty" sits against her own "about twenty-three".
The rule, added to false-zeros: WHEN BOTH PARTIES TO AN INDEXED MARRIAGE
SHARE EVERY ATTRIBUTE, ONE OF THEM HAS BEEN MANUFACTURED FROM THE OTHER.
A real couple almost never matches on all five.
The search row looked complete, which is why it was believed. Opening
the record cost one fetch.

commits.subject: Row 137's last two men: neither name was one man
commits.body:
EMILIO LERENA is at least three. A Spanish immigrant from Logrono
already in this register, arrived in Argentina 1930. A boy born at
Trinidad on 2 January 1906 to Florencio P. Lerena Fernandez and Juana
Recuero - so the sweep's "Emilio" is a SON of that generation, not a
father of it. And an older Emilio married to PAULA CASARES, whose son
Emilio Delfino has a marriage registration at Flores in 1931, which a
man born in 1906 cannot have. That third man is the father row 137 met
in September; he is attested and NOT placed.
ALEJANDRO F. LERENA survives as a named parent and nothing more:
husband of NATALIA LERENA and father of AURORA, born about 1868, named
only on his grandchildren's registrations. A forename sweep returns 533
Uruguayan Alejandros and he is not among them. Whether he is a son of
Alejandro Lerena the elder and Margarita Fernandez Alvarez - which would
make the "F." Fernandez, and this branch does produce Lerena Fernandez
compounds - is argued in _person-pairs.txt as a hypothesis and is not
asserted.
A CAUTION WORTH MORE THAN EITHER MAN. The Uruguayan civil registration
INDEX CARD series 1900-1937 looks like a census of the whole country and
is nearly useless for identity: it gives a name and a department and
withholds every date that would let two namesakes be told apart. Both
Emilios and most of this row's difficulty come from that one property.
Row closed on its own terms - its stated remainder was these two men -
but the larger sweep it describes, four departments one collection at a
time, is NOT done and the row says so.

commits.subject: Row 187 answered: two of the three San Jose mothers had husbands
commits.body:
Four forename searches - Manuel, Olegaria, Estefania, Felicia - did what
a father-line surname search cannot, and answered most of a row that had
stood a fortnight.
FELICIA LERENA married at the Catedral Basilica San Jose on 19 December
1874, and the act names her parents: MAURICIO LERENA and CASIMIRA
MONTANO, the couple married at Colla in 1837. So she is a SECOND CHILD
of the Rosario-Colla house, alongside Manuel - and a woman married in
December 1874 mothering a child at San Jose in 1875 is exactly what row
187 recorded without being able to explain.
ESTEFANIA LERENA married SERVANDO GONZALEZ, and her six children are
indexed GONZALEZ LERENA. That is the compound-surname principle working
precisely as this archive states it: a Lerena father-line search cannot
see her, and the compound reaches her at once. Whether this joins the
Gonzalez Lerena thread already here is NOT established - different
departments - and it is not merged.
OLEGARIA remains what the row called her: one record in the whole
Uruguayan corpus, mother of Juana de las Nieves Lerena, the child
carrying her surname because no father was named.
The MANUEL search separated three men by their mothers' surnames -
LERENA MONTANO, LERENA LEONARD, LERENA MARINO - which is the only thing
that can separate men sharing a forename in one small country. It also
found the civil registration of the 1882 Trinidad marriage filed at SAN
JOSE, a departmental conflict recorded and not resolved.
A HYPOTHESIS WAS RAISED AND WITHDRAWN WITHIN THE HOUR. On finding that a
Manuel Lerena married a Juana Galarza at the Cordon in February 1890,
this session suggested row 187's "Manuel x Juana FERREIROZ, 1891" was
the same couple misread. Their daughter Felicia then turned up in TWO
separate collections, both naming the mother Ferreiroz. One index
mangling a surname is ordinary; two independent records agreeing on it
is evidence. Both rows now carry the withdrawal.
Ten people added. All INDEX ONLY; no act was opened.

commits.subject: A double wedding in 1889 explains the 1911 dispensation
commits.body:
Row 188 was a sweep stopped after one page in September. The lesson is
general: THE FIRST PAGE IS BAPTISMS AND THE LATER PAGES ARE MARRIAGES.
The September pass came away with children; pages two to four carried
the acts that explain them.
THREE WEDDINGS IN THIRTEEN MONTHS, at Santisima Trinidad:
  22 March 1888 - Bernabe Lerena x Florinda Cardozo
  25 April 1889 - Maria Lerena x Eliseo Cardoso
  25 April 1889 - Casimira Lerena x Juan Basilio Cardoso
The last two on ONE DAY. A Lerena brother and his two sisters married a
Cardozo sister and her two brothers. That is how double first cousins
are made, and in 1911 Custodio Lerena - Bernabe and Florinda's son - had
to be dispensed to marry Ema Cardozo. This archive has held the priest's
two kinship diagrams for weeks without the weddings behind them.
And the 1911 marriage itself is found: 18 September 1911. The grant was
previously inferred from the birth of their daughter in 1915; it is now
on the act.
Seven people new to the register. A second sister, Casimira, whom this
archive did not hold. ALEJANDRO F. LERENA x NATALIA LERENA - a fourth
Lerena-married-a-Lerena couple, and the first record to give row 137's
"Alejandro F." a wife and a child. Their daughter Aurora x Manuel
Vaquero with five children at Trinidad. And MANUEL LERENA, son of
Mauricio and Casimira Montano of the 1837 Colla marriage, marrying at
Trinidad in April 1882 - a second, independent thread from the
Rosario-Colla house into Flores.
Two conflicts recorded rather than smoothed: Gualberto's two children
eight months apart in 1901, and Aurora's Herminia and Gerardo six months
apart and christened the same day, so one birth date is misindexed.
One record was deliberately not taken - a Trinidad birth and death of
September 1980 naming a living generation's parents.
Still not shown: which Cardozo fathered Ema. If Eliseo or Juan Basilio,
the doubling is accounted for exactly. All of this is INDEX ONLY; not
one act was opened.

commits.subject: Birth years from the 1897 act, and a gap in the last-alive ledger
commits.body:
The marriage act gave Juan Zalduondo (80), Dolores Pou (58), Celedonia
Villademoros (55) and Fernando Moratorio (50) their first birth years,
and Eduardo an exact one. last-attested-alive regenerates accordingly.
New row 199 records what that exposed: the ledger files Juan and Dolores
as 'BIRTH ONLY' when this archive knows they were alive on 20 November
1897 and dead by 22 August 1913 - a fifteen-year bracket it cannot see,
because the tool reads born_est and nothing else. The same is true of
every witness, godparent and named parent here. Not fixed: the facts
live in prose, and parsing dates out of prose is the method the
corrections gate records as tried and abandoned.

commits.subject: Row 185: the same null, now from the wife's side too
commits.body:
The technique that found the 1897 marriage an hour earlier - search the
rare surname bare - was turned on row 185 and failed. VILLADEMOROS bare
returns 649 in Uruguay; Elisa Villademoros returns 33, and every one is
accounted for. Four carry the role 'Other', which is where this index
hides people it cannot place and therefore where a marriage party could
sit, and none of them is a marriage: two are Angelica Maria's own
baptism, one is an 1891 christening where Elisa stands godmother, the
rest are other Villademoros households.
So the null holds from both spouses and under four spellings, and the
instrument demonstrably works - these searches returned 649 and 33, not
zero. The image walk of Cordon and Union marriages 1868-1872 is the only
route left, which is what the row already said; it now says it on twice
the evidence.
Found on the way and recorded as a lead, not a fact: an 1891 Montevideo
christening carrying 'Alejandro M. Pero' beside Elisa, almost certainly
the couple standing godparents. Computer-indexed, not opened.

commits.subject: The marriage, found four hours after it was called missing
commits.body:
Row 186 wanted the act that joined Angelica Maria Lerena Villademoros to
Eduardo Zalduondo. This morning the archive wrote it down as not found
and filed it as open question 10. It is Montevideo, fourth section,
civil act No. 83 of 20 November 1897, folio 42, expediente 94, at five
in the afternoon, before the Juez de Paz Gallo Pareja. Plate read.
THE METHOD WAS EMBARRASSINGLY SIMPLE: search the GROOM. Every previous
attempt went through Lerena and its manglings - Lerma, Lorena, Zerena -
and reached only the death and the children. One search on the bare
surname ZALDUANDO, no given name and no date, returned the marriage in
the first ten rows, plus a brother and a niece. A rare surname searched
bare beats a common surname searched cleverly.
ONE ACT, FOUR ANSWERS.
Eduardo was born 15 August 1860 at Montevideo - an exact date, which
makes his own death act's "fifty-two" wrong by a week: he had turned
fifty-three seven days before he died.
Angelica's father AVELINO EDUARDO LERENA TRAIBEL died IN CANELONES in
1895, a death this archive did not have, stated by his widow, who was
party to the act. This makes the withdrawn "La Paz, Canelones" reading
legible without reviving it: that claim was about his FATHER, who died
at Montevideo in 1890, and the retraction stands - but there is an
Avelino Lerena who died in Canelones, and it is the son. The secondary
tree looks less like invention than like a confusion of two men with one
name. Nothing in this act says La Paz.
The Zalduondo parents are not Spanish immigrants. The form has a
nacionalidad blank for each and it is filled: Juan is ORIENTAL, aged
eighty and on a pension; Dolores Pou is BRASILENA. Her row had reasoned
from the surname that she was "Catalan or Balearic" and said so twice.
The surname may well be Catalan; she was not. Logged as a correction -
the error was not the guess, which was labelled a guess, but letting a
labelled guess stand while the document that settles it went unsought.
And the "Legitiman" line is BLANK, so no child existed in November 1897
and all three were born after it. That excludes Maria Elena Zalduondo
from being the Maria Elena Lerena who married in 1906 - a pair this
register had been unable either to match or to rule out hours earlier.
An empty field on a form did that.
Also corrected: a note written this morning said the recurring MORATORIO
surname "is not evidence of anything". It was right about the Juez de Paz
and wrong about the family. Fernando Moratorio, fifty, of commerce,
witnessed this marriage, and he is the husband of Josefa Lerena Traibel,
the bride's aunt. "No connection is claimed" and "there is no connection"
are different sentences.
She signed the act herself - "Angelica Lerena", her own hand and her own
spelling, against an index that had called her three other things.

commits.subject: ZALSAMENDI was never on the plate. It is ZALDUONDO
commits.body:
David signed the session in and the two blocked plates were read. Both
overturn what this archive published four hours earlier, so this commit
is largely a retraction.
THE SURNAME. The 1903 Pocitos baptism heads its entry "Maria Zalduondo",
names the father "Eduardo Zalduondo" and the paternal grandmother
"Dolores Pou de Zalduondo". The 1913 Montevideo death act, certificate
553, says "ha fallecido Eduardo Zalduando ... era hijo de Juan Zalduondo
y de Dolores Pou, fallecidos". ZALSAMENDI appears on neither page. It was
a misreading of the 1903 hand and it stood here for three weeks.
THE ARGUMENT THAT FAILED, which is worth more than the fact. When the
civil index spelled the man ZALDUANDO, this archive reasoned that a plate
outranks an index and published ZALSAMENDI. But it was not holding a
plate - it was holding another session's READING of a plate, and treating
the two as the same thing. The index had been right all along. There was
a tell in plain view and it was read backwards: the archive's own note
recorded that a MACHINE transcript of this act produced "Del Suando".
Two readers failing on one hand is evidence the hand is hard. And a
second tell was ignored outright - the index called the child MARIA
MARGARITA LUISA, a fourth name the 1903 reading had dropped, and the
plate has it.
THE WIFE. The forename question was framed as plate-against-index and it
was plate-against-plate: 1903 says AMELIA, 1913 says ANGELICA. They are
one woman, and the record forces it rather than the archive choosing -
the 1913 act places Maria Margarita inside the union with Angelica and
the 1903 act places the same girl inside the union with Amelia. One child
cannot be inside two unions. "Amelia LERENA" is merged into ANGELICA
