MARIA LERENA VILLADEMOROS; the name is kept as a recorded variant rather
than erased, so a reader meeting her in the Pocitos register can find
her. Why a priest wrote Amelia is not explained, only outvoted two to
one, and the row says so.
GAINED FROM THE PLATES: his birthplace (Montevideo), that he was retired
on a pension at fifty-two, angina de pecho, calle Juan B. Blanco 9, both
his parents already dead, the declarants and the Juez de Paz, LUISA for
the daughter, and a THIRD CHILD - MARIA ELENA - who is a name and nothing
else.
URLS. The archive's first rename and first merge. Five published person
slugs were orphaned; they are kept in the ledger, never deleted, and
redirected in astro.config.mjs to the same human being. Seven other keys
were deleted and the rule was not broken to do it - they were minted in
the previous eighteen hours by a session that built a duplicate family
and removed it, and not one was ever deployed. Two of those deletions
gave real people back clean addresses the churn had taken.
Open question 10 is rewritten from "Amelia or Angelica?" to the record
neither plate is: her marriage act, still not found, which is why work
list row 186 stays open.

commits.subject: Split the 1927 parish film into its own searched.json row
commits.body:
DGS 008166595 was riding inside the row for DGS 008165206, which would
have told the atlas one film carried work done in two. Neither film
resolves to a waypoint - absent from the atlas's fs-volumes data and
reached by index ark, so no wc=/owc= was ever seen - so both are
recorded by film number with the waypoint left unset.

commits.subject: The Zalduando was already here, under Zalsamendi
commits.body:
Row 186 asked who Angelica Maria Lerena Villademoros married. Four civil
index entries answered: Eduardo Zalduando Pou, dead at Montevideo on
22 August 1913 aged fifty-two, son of Juan and Dolores Pou, with two
children. They were written up as a family new to this register.
They were not new. Every one of them was already here under ZALSAMENDI,
entered on 21 September off the plate of a Pocitos baptism of 1903. The
agreement is fivefold and none of it depends on the disputed surname:
the husband Eduardo, his father Juan, his mother Dolores Pou, a Lerena
wife of Avelino and Celedonia, and a daughter Maria Margarita. The
duplicates gate caught it before anything was committed.
A plate outranks an index, and this index writes Lerena as "Lerma" and
Avelino Lerena as "Arabia Larena Lerena", so ZALSAMENDI is the better
reading. There is even a tell: a machine transcript of the same 1903 act
read the father as "Del Suando", far closer to "Zalduando" than to what
the plate says. The same hand defeats the same kind of reader twice.
One difficulty closed itself on the way. Amelia Lerena's row has asked
since 14 September how her parents could be "Avelino y Celidonia B. de
Lerena" when Avelino Lerena Fernandez married Ambrosia Traibel. The
Avelino is not him - it is his son, Avelino Eduardo Lerena Traibel,
whose wife is Celedonia Villademoros. The Pocitos household joins to the
Lerena Villademoros, and through them to the Lerena Traibel. Nothing was
discovered; two rows that had sat here three weeks were read together.
What is NOT settled is the wife's forename. The plate says Amelia, the
index says Angelica, and the parents match exactly in both. That is now
open question 10, and the two women are not merged. The test is one
plate - DGS 008165206 image 283 - and on 11 October the image viewer
answered with a sign-in page. Recorded as unread, not empty: new row 198
is blocked on a signed-in session, and false-zeros gains a disguise,
because the index page read perfectly and passed its own sign-in control
while the images behind it did not. "Am I signed in?" is not one
question.
Genuinely new people: two. A son, Eduardo Avelino, born about 1901 at
La Paz in Canelones, who married Maria Ester Costa there in 1927 - which
puts a branch of this Montevideo family in Canelones - and his wife.
Also caught before commit: the first draft of all of this was written
onto Maria Angelica Julia Lerena Salvanach, born 1886, by a prefix match
on "Maria Angelica". The chronology stopped it - she would have been
fifteen when this couple's eldest was born. Name order is not identity.

commits.subject: The Villademoros branch is in Buenos Aires in 1918
commits.body:
Finishing the half of row 87 the Trinidad side had crowded out: the
Montevideo compounds against the dispensation series. Neither reached a
dispensation. "Lerena Salvanach" returns ZERO in full text — controlled
by "Lerena Villademoros" run minutes earlier in the same session, which
returns one.
That one was worth the search. Basílica San José de Flores, Buenos Aires,
acta 446, 20 January 1918: BEATRIZ ELIZA DEL CORAZÓN DE JESÚS, born 17
November 1917, "hija legítima de D. EUGENIO MARCOS ABELLA, natural de
URUGUAY, de cuarenta y un años, y de Doña JACINTA LERENA VILLADEMOROS,
natural de URUGUAY, de treinta y seis años, domiciliados en MEMBRILLAR
96".
So a Montevideo branch crossed to the Argentine capital, with a husband,
an address and a daughter.
A NAME TRAP WORTH WRITING DOWN, because this archive works both countries
at once: the parish is SAN JOSÉ DE FLORES in BUENOS AIRES CITY. That is a
different Flores from the Uruguayan department where the Trinidad kindred
lives, and a different San José from the one where the Lerenas married in
1825 and 1837. Three unrelated places sharing two names.
AND THE AGE DOES NOT AGREE. She is given as thirty-six in January 1918 —
a birth about 1881 — where this archive holds her baptism of 19 September
1876, which would make her forty-one. A stated age on a baptism act is
the parent's own account and is often short, and this archive does not
move a baptismal date on the strength of one. The identification rests on
the rare compound surname and the Uruguayan birth; the conflict is
recorded rather than smoothed.
Two people added.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 459 people.

commits.subject: Row 87 done — and the compound technique's failure mode found with it
commits.body:
The row asked for the compound-surname technique to be crossed with the
Montevideo dispensation series. The crossing itself returned almost
nothing: of the compounds tried, only "Lerena Cardozo" reached a
dispensation, and it was the 1911 Lerena–Cardozo already held.
What the compounds found instead has been committed separately — four
acts from "Lerena Peláez" that rebuilt three generations and confirmed
the 1858 kinship diagram from the civil register.
AND THE TECHNIQUE'S SPECIFIC FAILURE MODE TURNED UP IN THE SAME HOUR. Two
Durazno birth registers of 1915 matched "Lerena Cardozo" and looked
exactly like children of the 1911 couple — right surnames, right years.
Neither act is about a Lerena at all. PEDRO S. LERENA signed at the
request of an illiterate declarant and SATURNINO CARDOZO witnessed the
same act, so the two surnames fall adjacent in the signature block.
A COMPOUND SEARCH CANNOT TELL ONE PERSON'S TWO SURNAMES FROM TWO PEOPLE'S
ONE SURNAME EACH. This archive already held the same error in another
service — Trove treats a whole family-notices column as one article, so
"Brayley Bideford" matched two terms set in the same column of type.
Proximity read as relationship, in a new place. The tell is cheap: if the
two surnames appear in a list of SIGNATURES rather than in a person's
name, it is not a compound.
The accident was not wasted. It found PEDRO S. LERENA, literate, at
Tejera in the Segunda Sección of Durazno in 1915, signing for neighbours
who could not write — which is what a schoolmaster, a policeman or a
storekeeper did. He is entered with no age, no parents and a middle
initial written S. once and J. once, neither read off the plate, and
nothing connects him to any branch here. Six same-name pairs declared
against him, each saying the same honest thing: a man who exists only as
a signature can be neither matched nor ruled out.
Still open and cheap: the Montevideo compounds — Lerena Lenguas, Lerena
Salvanach, Lerena Villademoros — were not run against the dispensations,
because the Trinidad side paid so heavily it consumed the session.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 457 people, 27 false-zero
disguises.

commits.subject: A priest drew it in 1858; a Juez de Paz wrote it in 1911
commits.body:
Work-list row 87 asked for the compound-surname technique to be crossed
with the Montevideo DISPENSATION series. "Lerena Pelaez" returns four
documents in the entire full-text corpus. None is a dispensation. All
four were opened and two were read off the plate.
THE ONE THAT MATTERS. Flores death act No. 9, 28 July 1911: ANTONINA
ISABEL LERENA DE PELÁEZ, nacida en MONTEVIDEO, de NOVENTA Y DOS AÑOS,
widow, dead on her own estancia at Cerro Colorado — "hija legítima de Don
RAMÓN LERENA y de Doña MARÍA GONZÁLEZ, fallecidos".
That is the apex of the kinship diagram the Cura Vicario of Trinidad drew
in 1858 to prove an impediment, confirmed fifty-three years later by a
Juez de Paz in a different record system. Two independent documents, one
couple.
It also names her four surviving children — CASIMIRA JOSEFA, MALBINO
HIPÓLITO, MARÍA INOCENCIA, JUAN FABIÁN — three of whom this archive held
as separate people from separate acts. Casimira married Bernabé Lerena;
María Inocencia married Rafael Sánchez; Malbino Hipólito is the
Malbino/Balbino of the 1880 witness list. And her husband is JUAN PEDRO
Peláez, not simply Juan.
AND IT COST AN INFERENCE. This register had her born about 1830, reasoned
from a daughter aged thirty in 1880 — sound arithmetic on the only number
available, and eleven years out. The act states ninety-two. It also gives
MONTEVIDEO where the 1858 expediente says "naturales de San José";
recorded as a conflict, not deleted.
THE OTHER THREE:
- ALEJANDRINA LERENA DE PELÁEZ, d. 1926 aged 74 — the woman this archive
  could only infer yesterday as "a daughter of his by Isidora Chouriño".
  Her act confirms Alejandro the younger's own parentage seventy-two
  years after the expediente that first gave it, and spells Isidora a
  THIRD way: Chousiña.
- AMADOR LERENA PELÁEZ, d. Durazno 1937, 35, a barber born in the Sexta
  Sección — a SECOND child for the couple dispensed in 1894, and the
  first terminus this archive has for either parent's death.
- LUIS and AURORA, confirmed at Trinidad, children of Balbino Peláez and
  Alejandrina Lerena; and a new MARGARITA LERENA as a sponsor.
Six people added. A candidate declared and NOT merged: an "Antonia Luisa"
christened at Cordón in 1819 to Ramón Llerena and María Josefa González.
Same year, same city, same parents — and Antonia Luisa is not Antonina
Isabel, which is exactly the size of difference this archive has been
wrong on twice this week. The Cordón act is on film and unopened.
Two things worth carrying: a COMPOUND surname reaches WOMEN, who are
invisible to a father-line search — three of these four acts are about
women. And the Flores volume titled "March 1918 – January 1919" contains
acts of 1926, so a volume title is not a bound on its contents.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 456 people.

commits.subject: Cajón 985 finished: one true null, and a card the index read three ways wrong
commits.body:
Both of these were searched earlier today on a session that had silently
signed out, and both results were withdrawn. Redone signed in, with the
control re-run AFTER each null and not only before it.
LEANDRO LORENA and LLANOS is a true null. The constraint binds and
returns eleven rows carrying that surname across Bolivia, Spain,
Colombia, Mexico and Peru — and exactly one is this couple: the army card
itself. No baptism, no marriage, no civil registration, in any country.
That is what a controlled null looks like when the search is working.
CONCEPCIÓN LERENA WAS NEVER A NULL. Her son's MILITARY FINGERPRINT CARD
sits in a different drawer and a different record class from the
enrolment fichas of Cajón 985 — reached through the person, not the
drawer, which is why this archive had never opened it.
The plate corrected the index three times over:
- the surname is LERENA, in his own signature, where the index says SERENA;
- the index gives him a father, "Spouses Carlos" — THE CARD'S FATHER FIELD
  IS STRUCK THROUGH WITH A PEN, and the indexer took CARLOS from the son's
  own forename;
- the index puts his birth at Mendoza; the card says CAP. FEDERAL. This
  archive had copied that one into its own working file four weeks ago.
So the drawer summary's "(mother only)" was right all along, and
Concepción Lerena is not a father at all — one of the four men
/open-questions/ has been asking strangers about is a woman with no
husband on the record.
AND IT STRENGTHENS THE EVIDENCE THIS ARCHIVE RESTS ON. These clerks
CANCELLED a parent they did not know rather than leaving the line blank.
Pablo Armando's card names both — Juan Carlos Lerena and María Lerena —
so her name was positively supplied, not defaulted. It still does not
decide maiden against married, which is what question 1 actually asks.
Cajón 985 is now worked to the end: five fathers traced, one true null,
one who turned out to be a mother.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 450 people.

commits.subject: Arturo Lerena is Spanish, and a journalist — which breaks a pattern
commits.body:
Signed in again, the control re-run first and it passes. Then the record
the last correction named as the open route: Arturo's son's marriage in
Entre Ríos, because that province's form asks what the Chilean one does
not.
Acta 144, Crespo, departamento de Paraná, 24 October 1924, a printed form
with a "de nacionalidad" blank beside each parent:
  "hijo de ARTURO LERENA, de nacionalidad ESPAÑOLA, de profesión
   PERIODISTA, y de AMALIA DÍAZ, de nacionalidad PERUANA"
He signed as a witness too — "Arturo Lerena, de cincuenta y [units digit
not read] años, de profesión Periodista, de estado casado, domiciliado en
PARANÁ" — so born about 1865–1874, and the age is what proves the witness
is the father and not his twenty-eight-year-old son of the same name. ON
ANY MARRIAGE ACT, READ THE WITNESS LIST: the same person can appear twice
with different facts attached.
AND IT BREAKS A CLAIM THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED YESTERDAY. data/cajon-985-
origins.tsv has said since 13 September that of the drawer's traceable
fathers "EVERY ONE is Uruguayan or married in Uruguay", and I strengthened
it on 9 October by adding Carlos as a Montevidean. Arturo is a Spaniard
married to a Peruvian. Five are traceable now and the generalisation
fails on the fifth; what survives is only that none of them is Argentine.
THAT COSTS SOMETHING REAL. /open-questions/ was leaning on that pattern
as a base rate — that an Argentine Lerena of this generation is usually a
Uruguayan family's son, and that a Juan Carlos absent from Rosario fits
the shape. A drawer holding a Spaniard and a Peruvian is a drawer of
IMMIGRANTS, not a drawer of Uruguayans. The question now says so instead
of quietly keeping the stronger version. The honest form was always
available: "three of three", not "every one".
It also explains an index this archive could not parse — FamilySearch
renders Amalia on one army card as "Amalia Dias Peruane", reading her
nationality as part of her name — and adds a birthplace the drawer did
not give: Antonio Lerena Díaz, born about 1896 at BUENOS AIRES.
The method, twice over now: GO WHERE THE FORM ASKS THE QUESTION. Mendoza's
printed baptism form placed Carlos in a city where its own prose could
only say "orientales"; Entre Ríos's marriage form placed Arturo in a
country where a Chilean death register could not. When a man cannot be
placed from one record class, the question is which form asks what you
want to know.
Four people added, including the bride's German-colony family at Crespo.
And Arturo is the first documented Spanish-born Lerena this archive has
found in Argentina, with his mother's surname known — García — which is
the shape open question 5 has been asking for.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 448 people.

commits.subject: Three conclusions withdrawn: the session had silently signed out
commits.body:
I went back for Arturo's Entre Ríos marriage and found the same URL
returning fuzzy noise that had returned true hits an hour before. The
cause was not FamilySearch. THE BROWSER SESSION HAD SIGNED ITSELF OUT,
and a signed-out search returns a restricted tier — twenty-one rows of
United States census for every query, whatever the constraint.
The page said so, in one line above the results: "Create a free account
or sign in to see all available results."
WITHDRAWN:
- that Leandro Lorena and Llanos are absent from the index, recorded as
  a CONTROLLED null;
- that Concepción Lerena is absent;
- and the method finding that a parent-pair query and a spouse-pair query
  reach two different index shapes, which was built on a clean 0 Results
  for Carlos Lerena and Adela Carniglia. That zero has a simpler
  explanation.
THE PROOF IS THE CONTROL ITSELF. The Carniglia spouse-pair query returned
three true hits earlier the same day — I read two of those acts off the
plate — and now returns twenty-one rows with not one carrying the name.
THE LESSON IS EXACT AND IT COST THREE CLAIMS: a control run BEFORE a null
proves nothing about the null if the service can change state in between.
On any signed-in service the control must be re-run AFTER the null it is
meant to protect. The cheapest detector was on the page the whole time —
the account name in the header.
And this archive already held this trap, as false-zero disguise
seventeen: "THE SESSION THAT LOGGED ITSELF OUT AND DID NOT SAY SO". I
walked into it anyway, which is why the two false-zero rows written an
hour ago are rewritten rather than deleted: the observation in them was
right and the explanation was wrong, and that pairing is worth more than
either half.
WHAT SURVIVES, AND WHY: everything read OFF A PLATE. Carlos Lerena
natural de Montevideo, Arturo Lerena García, the Valparaíso act of 1894 —
those are transcriptions of images I looked at, not search results, and
they do not depend on who the service thought I was.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed.

commits.subject: Two controlled nulls, and two query forms that are not the same search
commits.body:
Leandro Lorena and Concepción Lerena, the last two untraced fathers of
Cajón 985, are both absent from the index. The method finding is worth
more than the nulls.
A PARENT-PAIR QUERY AND A SPOUSE-PAIR QUERY ARE NOT THE SAME SEARCH.
q.fatherSurname + q.motherSurname asks "whose CHILD has these parents",
and it returned a clean, confident 0 Results for Carlos Lerena and Adela
Carniglia — a couple whose three children this archive read off the plate
the day before. Those records are indexed with the FATHER as principal,
so the child has no parent fields to match. q.surname + q.spouseSurname
finds all three at once.
I caught it by running the control before believing the null, on a pair
I had just proved exists. Every parent-pair null this archive holds
should be re-run in the spouse form before it is trusted.
AND THE OPPOSITE FAILURE, IN THE SAME HOUR. When a filtered search
matches nothing, this service does not say zero: it silently widens to
fuzzy surname matches and returns a full page. Twenty-one rows for
Lerena-with-spouse-Llanos, twenty-one for Salvador Lorena 1893-99, and
not one row carried the constraint — Llorens, Lorraine, Lohren, Lorene,
Lorino, all United States census. One trap hides a true result behind a
confident zero; the other hides a true zero behind a page of results.
Count the rows that carry your constraint, not the rows that come back.
So Leandro Lorena is a CONTROLLED null — the same form on Carniglia
returns three true hits in the same session, so the form is sound and the
pair is genuinely absent. Concepción's null is weaker and I have said so:
the mother filter does not bind at all. But her son's 1899 Mendoza
baptism should lie in Santiago Apóstol y San Nicolás, Baptism Records
1899–1901, DGS 004597291 — the volume already read twice this week — and
that is a page-by-page read, not a search. A card naming only a mother is
itself evidence: it usually means no father was recorded at the birth.
/open-questions/ question 1 now asks for what is actually open. Of the
four fathers it listed yesterday, two are traced — Carlos to Montevideo,
Arturo to a mother surnamed García — and two are nulls with their routes
named. The one genuinely open to a stranger is Arturo Lerena García:
mother a García, wife Amalia Díaz, family at La Pampa 1889, Valparaíso
1893-94, Mendoza 1896, Entre Ríos 1897. His marriage, or any Entre Ríos
registration of his children, would give his nationality.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 26 false-zero disguises.

commits.subject: Arturo Lerena García — a mother's surname, and Chile
commits.body:
The second of the untraced fathers of Cajón 985, by the same shape that
traced Carlos: search the man's WIFE. Surname Lerena with spouse surname
Díaz returned Chilean civil registrations, because the family crossed the
Andes.
A COMPOUND SURNAME NAMES A MOTHER. The death registration of his infant
son at El Almendral, Valparaíso, 18 September 1894, writes him ARTURO
LERENA GARCÍA — the first thing this archive has ever held about his
parents, and a searchable handle.
AND IT CONFIRMS A WITHDRAWAL MADE ON DOUBT ALONE. His working row was
first written as "Montevideo 1858, son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia
Traibel" and retracted the same day as a conflation with Juan Arturo
Lerena Traibel. A man written LERENA GARCÍA is not a son of Ambrosia
Traibel. The retraction was right, and it is now right on evidence.
CHILE HAS NEVER BEEN A PLACE THIS ARCHIVE READ A RECORD IN — it existed
here only as a surname-distribution figure and a DNA probe. The
transferable point: a parent-pair query is not constrained by country,
and a family that lived at Mendoza is one pass from Valparaíso. An
Argentine search should expect Chilean hits and not discard them.
La Pampa 1889, Valparaíso 1893–94, Mendoza 1896, Entre Ríos 1897. The
dates sit in order and the route is the ordinary one.
The act read off the plate: entry 54, page 28, "nombre Lerena Diaz Juan
Fernando, sexo masculino, nacionalidad CHILENA, edad DIEZ MESES, estado
párvulo, domicilio Victoria 81", died at one in the afternoon of
pulmonía, buried Playa Ancha. THE AGE CORRECTS THE INDEX, which estimates
his birth as 1894 from the death year: ten months on 18 September 1894 is
about November 1893. An estimated birth year derived from a death year is
not a birth year.
HE IS STILL NOT PLACED IN A COUNTRY. The Chilean form records nationality
for the DECEASED only and never asks where the father was born — where
the Mendoza printed form, the same afternoon, placed Carlos Lerena in a
city. He is recorded as a Lerena García and nothing more. The test is his
marriage to Amalia Díaz, or an Entre Ríos registration of one of his
other children, which in that province gives the parents' nationality.
Three people added, including the first in this register born in Chile.
No waypoint recorded: the film page offers MLKY-SPJ with three segment
ids and it was not checked against the atlas's volume data.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 444 people.

commits.subject: Four work-list links to /gaps/ now go to the section that holds the gaps
commits.body:
/gaps/ folded into /open-questions/#may-never-close in 5f6c52b; these four markdown links in
work-list rows still went through the redirect. Retargeted by exact string. The full
npm build chain passes and no built page links /gaps/ or /photograph-these/ any more.

commits.subject: Carlos Lerena is natural de Montevideo — and the printed form is why
commits.body:
The cheapest next step this archive named an hour ago was the second
Mendoza daughter's act. It paid.
The 1900 baptism is PROSE and could only say the parents were
"orientales". The 1902 baptism, same parish, same couple, is a PRINTED
FORM — "Partidas de Bautismos de la Parroquia Matriz de Mendoza" — with a
"natural de" BLANK beside each parent. Both blanks read MONTEVIDEO.
SO CARLOS LERENA, one of the four fathers /open-questions/ asks strangers
about, IS A MONTEVIDEAN, not merely a Uruguayan. And Adela Carniglia too
— an Italian surname in Mendoza by way of the Banda Oriental.
THE TRANSFERABLE PART IS ABOUT THE FORM, NOT THE FAMILY: when a parish
switches from prose to a printed register, go back and re-ask the
questions the prose could not answer. Two years apart, same clerk's
parish, and the second act answers what the first could not.
So four traceable fathers in that drawer and NOT ONE OF THEM ARGENTINE —
Gilberto Lerena Lenguas (Montevideo 1855), Alejandro M. Lerena (Uruguay
1844), Nemesio Ramón (married Salto 1903) and now Carlos (Montevideo).
That names nobody. It is the frame against which a Juan Carlos Lerena who
left no trace at all at Rosario should be read.
AND A SECOND LERENA GODPARENT, AGAIN BY PROXY. Avelino Lerena stood
godfather in 1900 through Domingo Simois; MERCEDES LERENA DE MARTÍNEZ
stood godmother in 1902 through the child's own mother. A godparent who
must be represented lives somewhere else — and somewhere else, for this
family, is Montevideo. The child is named for her.
She is not identified. This register holds three Mercedes Lerenas at
Montevideo and, separately, a CAROLINA Lerena de Martínez married to
Julián Martínez — a Lerena-Martínez marriage under a different forename.
Each of the three is declared on its own merits in data/_person-pairs.txt:
Mercedes Micaela Lerena Traibel (38 in 1902, Montevideo, no husband
recorded) is a real candidate held open; the 1880 godmother is a
candidate whose evidence has the same shape on both sides, which is why
it proves nothing; and the one who married Luis P. Márquez in 1883 would
be "de Márquez", and the married surname is the one thing these acts do
record about a woman.
María Mercedes Lerena born 10 March 1902 in the city of Mendoza, with
Eduardo Carniglia as godfather in person. Two people added.
A note for anyone following the films: /search/film/<DGS>?i=N resolves
against ITEM 001 only and lands silently on the wrong volume — this act
is in item 003. Use the index record's own VIEW ORIGINAL DOCUMENT button.
And no waypoint is recorded here: the film page offers Q633-3DR, verified
for item 001, but this is a different item, and a year range that fits is
not a confirmed match.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 441 people.

commits.subject: One of the four untraced fathers is Uruguayan — search the wife, not the man
commits.body:
/open-questions/ question 1 asks strangers for the origins of four men
named as fathers on the Lerena cards of army drawer Cajón 985. This
traces the first, and the method is the transferable part: a man who is
only a name on his son's card still has a WIFE, and a distinctive
married-in surname cuts the whole corpus to a handful. LERENA with
spouse surname CARNIGLIA returned three records in one query, every one
a child.
The first of them, read off the plate — there is no AI transcript for
this image — is the baptism of MARÍA ADELA at the Iglesia Matriz de
Mendoza on 6 January 1900: "es hija legítima de D. Carlos Lerena y Adela
Carniglia, ORIENTALES, domiciliados en este Curato".
SO CARLOS LERENA IS URUGUAYAN, where cajon-985-origins.tsv had him as
"Not established". That makes four of that drawer's traceable fathers
and every one of them Uruguayan or married in Uruguay. It names nobody.
It sharpens the base rate against which a Juan Carlos Lerena who left no
trace at all in the Rosario registers should be read — and Rosario is
exhaustively read: 798 consecutive baptisms act by act, both confirmation
registers complete.
AND AN AVELINO LERENA STOOD GODFATHER TO HIS DAUGHTER, BY PROXY —
"padrinos Domingo Simois POR ABELINO LERENA y Lucía L. de Simois". That
file called the Avelino of this family "suggestive only", because Carlos
named a son Avelino Carlos in 1904. It is no longer only a forename:
there was a real Avelino Lerena in his circle.
WHICH Avelino is not established and is not guessed. This register holds
four of the name — and the row directly above Carlos's in the same
working file was once written as a son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia
Traibel and WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY as a conflation with Juan Arturo
Lerena Traibel. A name this archive has already misidentified once
deserves the most care, not the least.
Two daughters added, and a spelling corrected: the act and the army index
both write CARNIGLIA, where this register has carried CAMIGLIA since 13
September. Also corrected: an hour-old error of mine on /open-questions/,
which listed "the Ramón of the Concordia pair" among the untraced — he is
traced, married at Salto in 1903. The fourth is Arturo Lerena.
AND THE VOLUME CARRIES A WAYPOINT, which almost none of this archive's
work does. Q633-3DR, checked against the Record Atlas's own volume data
before it was written down: "mendoza, 1899-1903, Bautismos 1899-1903",
and the act is 1900. Inside the range.
Note: another session's commit ccd9363 repinned the kit and added
check:nav, which the installed node_modules predated, so the local build
was red through no fault of this work. Running npm install brought the
working copy in line with their pin; package.json, package-lock.json and
.kitpin are untouched and unstaged.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 439 people.

commits.subject: Repin the kit to 3c9214e and make the Evidence menu a gate
commits.body:
Sixteen kit commits behind. The new pin brings checknav.py, which compares the BUILT
Evidence menu with the estate's canon; npm run build (which CI runs) now ends with
check:nav, strict: exit 1 on a departure, 2 if it cannot see a menu at all. Shown
failing on a doctored copy of built output in the D'Arcy repin.
What the repin changes for a reader, measured by building this archive at the old
and the new pin and comparing every page: 966 pages both times, no link or element
id differs, and the visible text differs on ONE page: the work list now renders
*Dominga Llarena* as emphasis instead of showing the literal asterisks (the kit's
markdown renderer improving).
The full npm build chain passes at the new pin, every gate, into a private directory.
SHARED GROUND: site/package.json and site/package-lock.json (the kit pin), and
.kitpin, changed at David's request as step 4 of kit/data/evidence-menu.json.
Collision risk: any other session editing the pin; read it with
'git show HEAD:site/package.json'.

commits.subject: The archive's first question was sending strangers to a drawer already read
commits.body:
/open-questions/ exists so that strangers can help, and its first
question — "Who were Juan Carlos and María Lerena?", the question this
archive exists to answer — told them two things that were not true.
IT SAID THE LERENA CARDS OF ARMY DRAWER CAJÓN 985 WERE "SITTING UNREAD".
They were read on 10 September, the same day the question was written.
data/cajon-985-scan.tsv holds all 39 frames, images 650 to 688, with
every card's indexed parents; data/cajon-985-origins.tsv traced the
fathers on 13 September. Twenty Lerena cards, and no Juan Carlos on any
of them except Pablo Armando's own.
AND IT SAID THE DRAWER IS "FILED ALPHABETICALLY". It is not: the same
scan found it is GROUPED BY SOUND — Lera, Lerena, Lorena, Serena, Sera,
Era, Leza, Perena, Perella and Hereijo interfiled. That is a finding in
its own right, and the reason the index's manglings survived in it.
I found this by going to do the work the page asked for. It is the fifth
instance today of a page stopping where data/ went on, and the worst
place for it: a stranger following that question would have spent an
evening re-reading a drawer and looking for it in the wrong order.
The question now carries what the drawer actually gave — the three
Uruguayan branches its fathers trace to, the base rate that follows, the
798 consecutive Rosario baptisms read act by act against the 1945 index,
and both Rosario confirmation registers complete — and its ask is
rewritten to what is genuinely still open: a Uruguayan Lerena line with a
Juan Carlos born in the 1840s or 1850s married to a María; THE FOUR
UNTRACED FATHERS of that drawer, any one of whom could be his brother —
Carlos Lerena, Leandro Lorena, Concepción Lerena and the Ramón of the
Concordia pair; and the consular matrícula, lodged with the Archivo
Histórico de Cancillería on 9 September and still unanswered.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed.

commits.subject: Fold What we cannot close into Open Questions and Photograph these into Errands
commits.body:
Two list pages that did a neighbour's job. Each said so itself: the gaps page
opened with "not the same page as the open questions" and photograph-these is
an errand in every field the kit's Errands row has (a place, why the picture is
worth the trip, what it would settle, nobody asked yet).
- /open-questions/#may-never-close holds the seven gaps whole, with their
  explanation, and the count in the page's prose is derived from the data.
- /errands/#photographs holds the six places, ranked as before, with the
  separate 'what to capture' line, and the closing note about the kerb.
- /gaps/ and /photograph-these/ redirect to those sections (astro redirects;
  this archive had none before), so the published addresses keep working.
- the nav drops both from Investigations; links from the index, the searched
  page and the South Africa page now point at the new homes.
- tools/build-pages.py indexed the 13 rows against the old addresses; they
  now point at the sections. That is the whole search-index change: 13 rows
  retargeted, none added or lost, and no other data file moved.
Not folded, deliberately, and read to decide: Hypotheses is fourteen argued
propositions with tables and an image analysis of the 1812 padron, and the
build checks its contents list against its sections; Roadmap is an argued
ranking with results ("walked, and the answer is no"). Neither is a list, so
folding them would flatten them. They stay under Investigations.
worklist.json and changes.json still contain links to /gaps/ and
/photograph-these/; they were left alone (this archive's session edits the work
list constantly) and resolve through the redirects.
Verified on a clean worktree of HEAD with the archive's full npm build chain
into a private directory, every gate: exit 0, kit gate ok on 966 pages
(site/dist did not exist, so it can only have read the private build). Read off
the built HTML: both redirects carry their anchors, #may-never-close and
#photographs exist and are linked, 7 gap panels, the Errands eyebrow reads
'1 answered, 3 still out, 20 need a person, 6 places to photograph'. checknav
conforms.
SHARED GROUND: site/astro.config.mjs (redirects), site/src/layouts/Base.astro
(the nav) and the derived site/public/searchindex.json, changed at David's
request as step 2 of kit/data/evidence-menu.json.

commits.subject: Gerdview, Germiston — and a street name read at too low a magnification
commits.body:
The township where Nuno Fernando Lerena bought two stands is GERDVIEW,
GERMISTON. His death notice MHG 6746/71 gives his residence as 24 Leiden
Road, Gerdview, Germiston, and Cologne Road — where lot 245 lies — is a
street in Gerdview, postal code 1401. So he bought two stands from the
Township Owners in the township he lived and died in.
THE DEATH NOTICE HAD BEEN READ ON 16 SEPTEMBER AND WAS SITTING IN
data/death-notices-read.tsv. Work-list row 197, opened two hours earlier,
named that exact document as the cheapest route to the answer without
checking whether the archive already held it. It did. The check took one
grep — which is at least the right order, and the reason this one cost
minutes instead of a day.
AND THE STREET SCHEME CAUGHT A MISREADING OF MY OWN, PUBLISHED THIS
AFTERNOON. Gerdview's streets are named for Dutch and German cities —
Leiden, Weert, Cologne. "London Street", which I had just put on
/south-africa/, in the register and in the work-list row, did not belong
to that scheme. So the plate went back under a harder magnification:
it reads LENDIN — a plain e where London has an o, and an n before the d
where London has none, with the i-dot sitting after the d. Withdrawn.
It is not demonstrably "Leiden" either, although that is the likeliest
intended name given where he lived: Leiden puts the i before the d and
this hand does not. Recorded as "Lendin (so written; not resolved)"
rather than guessed.
THE LESSON IS THE MAGNIFICATION. The first read resolved "Nuno Fernando
Lerena" and "T/Ship Owners" perfectly and was still too coarse for a
six-letter word in the same hand, on the same folio, two inches away. A
reading is only as good as the smallest thing it rests on.
And one negative worth keeping: that death notice leaves father and
mother BLANK — both marked only "Deceased", no names. The one document of
Nuno's that could have named Pablo Armando does not.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed.

commits.subject: The South African full-text seam, worked to the end — and two sons' lives
commits.body:
Nine hits under the Africa facet, every one now opened or excluded with a
stated reason. The seam is worked out for this surname.
ROQUE LUIS ARMANDO LERENA HAS AN ADDRESS, A TRADE AND A TENURE. A second
roll of polling district 770 — the first was read on 8 October, where the
OCR columns could not be aligned and the note said his address "needs the
plate read by eye". It was read by eye: "1399 Lerena, Roque Luis Armando
... 14 FLORENCE VILLAS ... FIREMAN ... O ... SOLE TENANT ... E". Sole
tenant of his own address at about twenty-two.
And the district has a name. One line of the same page carries "Louis
Botha Hostel, OBSERVATORY" — the only locality on the sheet — and the
street column runs Lower Main Rd, Trill Rd, Scott Rd and Salt River. The
roll names its own district; no atlas was needed.
His father was a horse-dealer in 1911 and a trainer by 1940. THE ELDEST
SON WENT TO THE RAILWAY. That "Fireman" means a locomotive fireman is an
inference from the company he keeps on the page — Loco. Cleaner,
Engine-driver, Signalman, Guard, Shunter — and not from the word, which
alone could mean a fire brigade. Flagged as inference.
NUNO FERNANDO LERENA HAS A SECOND PROPERTY: lot 210, London Street,
14,560 sq ft, bought from the TOWNSHIP OWNERS, transfer 22 August 1953 —
beside lot 245 in Cologne Road. The transcribers called him "Jan
Fernando" on one folio and "Huno" on the other; the clerk wrote NUNO both
times, plainly. And the folio settles what the date beside his name is:
it carries the transfer date in its own column, so 6.10.24 is an identity
date, his birth date, held independently from the 1950 estate and death
notice 6746/71. The township is still not placed — two streets, no
district, nothing guessed. New work-list row 197.
A SECOND SOUTH AFRICAN FAMILY OF THE NAME, EXCLUDED FOR THE SECOND TIME.
A Transvaal deeds folio names "late Lucas Lerena" and "Rachel Lerenia
(born Maleka)". With Seko Lerena of the Kranspoort mission congregation,
excluded on 8 October, that is two records forty years and a hundred
miles apart. Recorded because an exclusion is evidence: anyone meeting
"Lerena" in a Transvaal record should know there are two unconnected
families of the name.
Three that are not evidence, said plainly: a Bulawayo Pioneers' Society
application for a LIVING person, a De Jager descendant — named nowhere
here, no date, no place, under this archive's own rule; a Fauresmith
court file of 1855–71, excluded on chronology, whose "hit" is the
fragment "Knap Lerena" in garbled bilingual testimony; and school
admission applications by living children in Sierra Leone, WHICH WERE NOT
OPENED, because no evidential purpose justified reading them.
AND THE NEGATIVE RESULT IS THE IMPORTANT ONE. The corpus holds NO CAPE
CIVIL REGISTRATION. So Careen Maria's parents and Pablo Armando's own
father cannot be reached this way, and row 74 can no longer be answered
by full text — recorded on that row.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 437 people.

commits.subject: Close a work-list row that was done in September, and retire six claims
commits.body:
AUDIT OF THE WORK LIST AGAINST data/. The queue turned out to be in
better shape than the heuristic suggested: of twelve "next" rows flagged
as touched since their own date, ten carry dated in-place updates and
are genuinely still open. One was not.
ROW 75 asked for the 1911 marriage record of Pablo Armando and Mary
Septima Taylor. The record has been in data/marriage-1911.tsv since 16
September, read from the family's own papers, with the witnesses taken
off the plate on 20 September. Worse, the row's premise was false: it
said a South African marriage record "would give ... his father's name -
and his father is the whole question of this archive". THE CAPE MARRIAGE
REGISTER OF 1911 HAS NO COLUMN FOR THE FATHERS OF THE PARTIES. That
document cannot name Juan Carlos Lerena, and its silence is a fact about
the form, not about the family. Closed, with what it did buy: he was a
Catholic married in a Catholic church, a horse-dealer in 1911, and
settled at the Cape with banns called.
Rows 137 and 78 updated for today's work - Alejandro Lerena is no longer
on 137's unworked list (there are two of him and both now have acts),
and 78's Spanish target now has a spelling in a priest's hand.
SIX CLAIMS RETIRED into tools/check-superseded.py, so the build fails if
any is asserted again: Bernabé unattached; the "same place of origin";
row 75's premise; the expedientes as "a separate series"; the
Margarita-Manuel sibship as "not written down in either act"; and the
merged Juan row.
AND TWO MORE WERE WRITTEN AND WITHDRAWN WITHIN THE HOUR. A bare "Maria
SERENA" fired on a twelve-year-old in an 1858 census who has nothing to
do with the 1922 act; a bare "Cipriano LERENA Montana" fired on two
files correctly citing the indexed record of that name. Both were name
collisions. THIS ARCHIVE HAD ALREADY RECORDED THAT BULK-GENERATING
RETIRED CLAIMS FAILS EXACTLY THIS WAY - 39 hits, all collisions - and
the lesson was written down and then repeated. A retired claim must be a
SENTENCE this archive asserted, never a NAME it mentions.
AND THE GATE CAUGHT ITSELF. It failed five sentences that were
retracting the very claims it guards, because "WITHDRAWN" - this
archive's commonest retraction verb, used four times in today's
corrections alone - was not in RETRACT. That is precisely the failure
its own docstring warns of. Added.
One real defect fixed: Manuel Fernández Álvarez's register row asserted
the sibship was "written down, not inferred" and then, in the same
sentence, that it was "not written down in either act".
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 18 retired claims.
