commits.subject: The test returned this archive's own answer, written three weeks ago
commits.body:
I set a test yesterday: "any record naming Ramón with more than one
child". I ran it. It produced Alejandro Lerena's marriage of 16
September 1825 - and it produced data/ramon-lerena-rosario.tsv, which
has said since 17 September: "Bernabé is Alejandro's son; Cipriano is
Mauricio's; Alejandro and Mauricio are brothers." The spine on
/uruguay/ has been drawing Ramón's house for three weeks.
SO THE "CANDIDATE, NOT MERGED" I PUBLISHED TWICE TODAY WAS WRONG, AND
WRONG ABOUT THIS ARCHIVE RATHER THAN ABOUT THE FAMILY. It is the third
instance of one pattern - the 1891 Northam census and the FreeBMD death
sweep were both reported undone when they were done. Each time the
claim was written from memory while finishing something else, and each
time a file in data/ already held the answer. Retracted in
data/corrections.tsv.
AND A REAL DEFECT UNDERNEATH IT, THREE WEEKS OLD. The register said
Bernabé of Trinidad was unattached - "nothing joins him to these two" -
while data/ramon-lerena-rosario.tsv had him as Alejandro's son and the
site rendered both, on the same deploy. That is the direction nobody
checked when the owner asked twice whether the research was reaching
the pages: not the register falling behind the site, but the register
falling behind data/. Eight rows reconciled.
WHAT THE DAY ACTUALLY ADDED WAS THE GRADE, NOT THE CONCLUSION. Index-
level on 17 September; plate-level now. Act No. 17, 16 September 1825,
San José, read at full resolution: "desposé... a ALEXANDRO LEREÑA,
Natural de la VILLA DEL ROSARIO, hijo legítimo de RAMON LEREÑA y de
MARIA JOSEFA GONZALEZ, con MARGARITA FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ, Natural de esta
Villa, hija legítima de JUAN FERNANDEZ ALVAREZ y de BARBARA SOTURA."
The full "Josefa" in a priest's hand. The transcript reads "Ramón
Pereña"; the plate reads Lereña.
AND IT TURNED AN INFERENCE INTO A DOCUMENT. This morning I published
that Margarita and Manuel Fernández Álvarez "are almost certainly
brother and sister - required by the degree and not written down in
either act". The 1825 act gives her parents as Juan Fernández Álvarez
and Bárbara Sotura; the 1855 expediente gives Serapio's grandparents as
"Don Juan y Doña Bárbara Sotura". A third act wrote it down. So the
second grade dispensed in 1855 has a named path, and the inference is
retired as an inference.
One conflict recorded and not resolved by preference: the 1825 act says
Alejandro was natural de la Villa del Rosario, where the 1858 expediente
calls him and Margarita "naturales de San José". The 1825 act is his own
marriage and is the better witness; the expediente's plural looks like a
clerk collapsing two origins into one.
Four people added - Juan Fernández Álvarez, Bárbara Sotura, María
Fernández Álvarez and Marcos de León González, whose compound surname is
the groom's mother's and who is deliberately NOT merged with the Marcial
de León González this archive already holds.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 437 people.

commits.subject: The 1837 plate corrects the claim it was opened to confirm, and a Cipriano merges
commits.body:
Yesterday's find gave the Trinidad kindred a head - Ramón Lerena and
María González - and this register already held a Ramón Lerena of
Rosario-Colla married to a María Josefa González. The merge was refused
and a test was named: read the 1837 San José marriage act off the plate,
because that row had carried "TIER: INDEXED, not image-read" since 21
September.
THE TEST WAS RUN AND IT FAILED THE CLAIM THAT SET IT. The act (DGS
008143329, microfilm 625330, image 87) says Mauricio Lerena was "natural
de la VILLA DEL COLLA"; the 1858 expediente says the Trinidad Lerenas
are "naturales de SAN JOSÉ". Different birthplaces. The "same place of
origin" published that morning is withdrawn - and the index field had
read "Birthplace: Colla" all along, on the very page being cited. That
is the error: a conclusion written from an index without noticing it
contradicted the sentence being built.
WHAT REPLACED IT IS BETTER EVIDENCE OF A DIFFERENT KIND. A Flores birth
act of 2 March 1895 at El Tala has Cipriano Lerena, 42, declare in
person, name his wife Laureana Beloqui and give his parents as Mauricio
and Casimira Montaño. Spouse and both parents in one sentence - so
"Cipriano LERENA (of Trinidad)" and the index-only "Cipriano LERENA
Montana" are one man, merged after eighteen days held correctly apart.
Three children already in the register become grandchildren of Mauricio
Lerena of Colla, and a fourth is added.
So Bernabé of Trinidad is a grandson of a Ramón Lerena and María
González by the 1858 diagram, and Cipriano of Trinidad is a grandson of
a Ramón Lerena and María González by the 1837 and 1895 acts. Two routes,
no shared document, the same two names. That is convergence, not proof -
two couples can share two names - and the merge is still refused.
Also read off the plate, for one word: a Flores death act of May 1886
has a witness "D. MAURICIO LERENA de CINCUENTA años", signing his own
name. The transcript garbles that age to "veincuenta", which is not a
Spanish word, and the age is the whole of what separates him from the
man who married in 1837. Fifty in 1886 is a birth about 1836 - before
that marriage - so he is entered as a second Mauricio and explicitly NOT
as a son.
Casimira Montaño now has a birth year (c.1821 from a stated age), a
widowhood, and a street address: Calle Arenal 240, San José de Mayo,
fifty-eight years after she married there. She also buried a seven-day-
old daughter, Abdona Ignacia, in 1850 - recorded as a separate person
precisely because an Ignacia Lerena marrying at Trinidad in 1882 is
listed elsewhere as a candidate child of the same couple. Reusing a dead
infant's name was ordinary, and that is how two people become one by
accident.
And a witness not claimed: "Doña Clara Ledena" stood at Mauricio's
wedding. The temptation is obvious and the letterform is not the one -
the fourth character carries an ascender where "Lerena" four lines above
has a plain shoulder. A trap this archive is prone to is not a licence
to see it everywhere.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 433 people.

commits.subject: Row 196: Socorro and Bernabé are brother and sister, and a priest drew the proof
commits.body:
Work-list row 196 asked whether Socorro Lerena was a sister of Bernabé.
It was the last inference standing in the Trinidad work and the 1897
birth act could not settle it. Three marriage expedientes of the 1850s
settle it, and they were found by searching the full text for her name.
1855 (Trinidad, August) - the expediente of Serapio Fernández to marry
Doña Socorro Lerena. A sworn witness names four generations: she is a
daughter of Alejandro Lerena and Margarita Fernández and a granddaughter
of Ramón Lerena and María González.
1858 (Santísima Trinidad, 15 February) - the expediente of Bernabé
Lerena to marry Casimira Peláez, "hijo legítimo de Don Alejandro Lerena
y Doña Margarita Fernández, naturales de San José". THE SAME PARENTS.
So Socorro and Bernabé are brother and sister, and the dispensation of
26 June 1885 is explained: Serapio the younger descends from her,
Antonina Lerena from him, so they are first cousins - exactly the second
grade in the equal lateral line the Archbishop lifted.
And that folio carries a KINSHIP DIAGRAM the Cura Vicario drew himself:
Ramón Lerena and María González at the apex, lines down to Alejandro
Lerena / Margarita Fernández and Antonina Lerena / Juan Peláez, and the
two contracting parties below. The Trinidad cluster - "six or seven men
of a rare surname in one small inland town", guessed on 13 September to
be brothers or cousins - is one family, and now a priest who knew them
says so.
A RETRACTION THAT MADE THE FIND POSSIBLE TO MISS. This archive published
on 8 October that these records are the Vicar General's summary ledger
naming no parents, and that the informaciones matrimoniales are a
separate series it had not reached. Both volumes are in the SAME
collection; the difference is the decade. The 1885-1913 books are the
ledger. The 1850s books are full expedientes. The original claim was
true of every volume opened and false as a statement about the
collection - the same shape as the South Africa error the day before.
1854 stopped a collapse: a Flores death act gives an Alejandro Lerena
married to Isidora Chouriño where 1855 gives one married to Margarita
Fernández. The 1854 expediente has the petitioner appear as widower of
Isidora with parents Alejandro and Margarita - father and son, in one
sentence. Without it the archive would have merged a father into his son.
Also: Socorro's full name is María del Socorro, godmother at Trinidad de
los Porongos in January 1849, about seventeen - corroborating 1832 from
a second clerk. Malvino Peláez placed. Nine people added, nine rows
given parents, seven Alejandro pairs declared. No birth year was taken
from an age on an act whose date was not read.
The surname is written five ways on the 1858 page - Serena, Lorena,
Lorena, Leresa and Lerena - and the plate shows one looping capital L
throughout. It is the strongest S-for-L instance this archive holds.
Still open and deliberately not merged: whether that Ramón Lerena is the
Ramón Lerena of Rosario-Colla already in this register, whose son
Mauricio married at San José de Mayo in 1837. Same names, same
generation, and now the same stated place of origin - but the 1837 act
is indexed, not image-read.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 427 people.

commits.subject: Two dispensations explained by their children's records, and a merge
commits.body:
The 1894 and 1913 couples both came from the Montevideo dispensation
ledger, which names a bride, a groom and a degree of kinship and no
parents at all. Neither was answered by a marriage record. Both were
answered by finding a CHILD and reading the child's act.
1913 - Flores civil birth act No. 10 of 1922 (DGS 008165367 img 195).
Registering Anibal Marino Pelaez it names all four grandparents with
ages, trades and addresses, and so gives five adults their first
recorded birth year from a stated age rather than an assumption. The
groom's mother is Maria Lerena, dispensed in 1885 to marry his father;
the bride's parents are the Bernabe Lerena and Florinda Cardozo of the
1911 kinship diagram - so the bride of 1913 is a sister of Custodio
Lerena, and two full-text finds made three weeks apart are one family.
The degree also EXCLUDES an identification. Bernabe's own sister was
also a Maria Lerena; were she the groom's mother the couple would be
first cousins and the impediment the second degree. The clerk wrote the
third. There are two Maria Lerenas and the Church's arithmetic proves it.
1894 - Trinidad baptism of 26 November 1905 (DGS 008163893 img 20),
which names both pairs of grandparents in one line. Juan Lerena is a son
of Bernabe Lerena and Casimira Pelaez, a sixth child of the Trinidad
founding couple - and the man this register had been carrying as a
separate person since that morning. The split is retracted; the rows are
merged. It was not bad reasoning, the evidence arrived a day late.
Both transcripts misspelled the surname and both plates were read.
In the 1922 act one clerk's single letterform is transcribed SERENA in
one line and LERENA four lines later; the transcriber's own
inconsistency is the proof.
A NEW GATE, AND A SILENT FAILURE THAT EARNED IT. A person was appended
to the register while the file lacked a trailing newline. The row was
glued onto the previous one - nineteen fields where the header says ten.
Every gate passed, the build was green, and Vitalino Gregorio Pelaez
simply was not there: no row, no page, no slug. He was found by hand.
Nothing here caught something MISSING, because a short file is
well-formed. tools/check-arity.py now does. Its first version was itself
wrong - it assumed one header per file and fired 179 times on TSVs that
deliberately carry two tables, so the rule was narrowed rather than the
data reshaped.
Also: the full-text URL place parameter errors for Uruguay exactly as it
did for South Africa, so the broken thing is the parameter and not the
country; and a record page that times out reads as a record holding
nothing - its own REFRESH returned the find of the day. Both in
data/false-zeros.tsv.
./tools/verify.sh EXIT=0, all gates passed, 418 people.

commits.subject: A birth act names four grandparents, and the dispensations stop being a mystery
commits.body:
Went for the other three consanguinity expedientes. The expedientes were not
needed, and a different series answered.
A URUGUAYAN CIVIL BIRTH ACT NAMES BOTH PARENTS AND ALL FOUR GRANDPARENTS, with
ages, trades and addresses. One entry does more than the nine dispensations
put together.
Flores, Birth Records 1887-1901, No. 10 - CAYETANO ALBERTO FERNANDEZ, born at
Pintos on 7 August 1897:
  father   Don SERAPIO FERNANDEZ, 41, hacendado, vecino de CERRO COLORADO
  mother   Dona ANTONINA LERENA, 35
  paternal Don Serapio Fernandez, FALLECIDO, and Dona SOCORRO LERENA, 65,
           propietaria, domiciliada en TRINIDAD
  maternal Don BERNABE LERENA, 62, hacendado, Cerro Colorado, and
           Dona CASIMIRA PELAEZ, 56
IT EXPLAINS THE 1885 DISPENSATION. The groom descends from a Lerena through
his mother Socorro; the bride through her father Bernabe. Lerena blood runs
down both sides of that marriage, which is what the Archbishop was dispensing.
If Socorro and Bernabe are brother and sister the couple are first cousins -
exactly what an equal second degree means - but Socorro's parents are not
named, so the link is inferred and has NOT been drawn. Queued as row 196.
BERNABE LERENA AND CASIMIRA PELAEZ HAVE AGES AT LAST - born about 1835 and
1841, living at Cerro Colorado rather than in Trinidad town - and a fifth
child, Antonina. This archive has carried them since September with four
children and nothing else.
SOCORRO LERENA is entirely new: born about 1832, a widow and a property owner
in her own right at Trinidad.
AND IT REACHES BACK A GENERATION FURTHER. At Trinidad on 6 March 1880 Maria
Pelaez, thirty, "hija legitima de Don JUAN PELAEZ y de Dona ANTONINA LERENA",
married a widower, her mother witnessing. A daughter of thirty puts that
Antonina's birth near 1830. SO A LERENA MARRIED A PELAEZ AROUND 1845, and
Bernabe Lerena married another Pelaez a generation later. That is the whole
explanation of why the couples of 1885, 1894 and 1913 all needed dispensing:
two families had been marrying each other for two generations, and by the
third the Church had to compute the degrees.
TWO ANTONINA LERENAS AT TRINIDAD, thirty-two years apart, and this archive
nearly held one. The elder married Juan Pelaez; the younger is Bernabe's
daughter. Declared as separate with the ages that prove it.
And a duplicate I made myself: yesterday's dispensation row for Antonina and
today's birth-act row are the same woman. check-duplicates.py caught it in one
build, which is what the gate is for.
Eight people added, twenty-one edges, two same-name pairs declared and one
merged. Zelmira's act and this one are now both on /uruguay/.

commits.subject: The act behind one dispensation, and it names four parents
commits.body:
Did the expedientes, and the thing that answered was not an expediente.
The dispensation ledger names a couple and an impediment and no parent. So I
searched the full text for the bride's forenames instead, and found the
marriage itself: La Union, Montevideo, Religious Marriage Records 1902-1934,
headed in the register's own hand "Matrimonio de Cordero y Lorena".
28 FEBRUARY 1904, Iglesia de Nuestra Senora de Lourdes, Bishop Ricardo Jara
officiating on the declaration of the Cura Parroco of la Metropolitana.
  D. ADOLFO MAXIMO CORDERO - soltero, ARGENTINO, MEDICO, twenty-eight, of SAN
  JOSE, hijo legitimo de D. ADOLFO M. CORDERO y Dona CASIMIRA CHAVARRIA
  Dona ZELMIRA CARLOTA LERENA - soltera, oriental, TWENTY, of CALLE CERRO
  LARGO 230, hija legitima de D. Alberto [S]erena y Dona MARIA INES LARRIERA
Dispensed by Archbishop Mariano Soler of the third grade of consanguinity with
attingency to the second - which the act states word for word as the ledger
did, and which is the control on yesterday's reading. Witnesses: the groom's
father and the bride's mother.
TWO CORRECTIONS COME OUT OF IT. This register had the marriage at 28 FEBRUARY
1901 from an index; the act says 1904. The book runs 1902-1934 and the entry
above is dated May 1902, so 1901 is impossible. The dispensation of 1 February
1901 cleared them three years before they married. And the act makes her
TWENTY in 1904, which means born about 1883-84, where this register has 4
November 1880. Both stand; neither is preferred.
HER PARENTS ARE NOW ON A PRIMARY RECORD. This archive has carried Alberto
Lerena and Maria Ines Larriera as her parents since 14 September, from an
index. She is also the woman it once tested and set aside as "not ours", a
verdict it later corrected. Here she is on an act of her own.
AND THE ACT WRITES HER SURNAME TWICE, TWO WAYS. Her father is "D. Alberto
SERENA"; her mother, witnessing four lines later, is "Dona Maria Ines Larriera
de LERENA". They are husband and wife. It is the cleanest demonstration of the
S-for-L trap this archive has collected, because no other explanation is
available.
Three new people, six edges: the groom, and his parents - who are candidates
for the blood link, since a third grade with attingency to the second means
the Corderos and the Lerenas share an ancestor within two or three
generations, by two separate paths. Casimira Chavarria is the third Casimira
in this archive, beside Casimira Montano and Casimira Pelaez, and no record
yet joins any of the three.

commits.subject: Nine dispensations, no parents, and the degree of kinship in every one
commits.body:
Worked the Uruguayan half of row 194, and came here for the wrong reason.
THE LEDGER NAMES NO PARENTS. Row 194 said dispensations were worth opening
because "the pre-marriage investigation routinely gives a Spanish groom's
PARENTS" - this archive's own words, from canelones-films.tsv. That is true of
the EXPEDIENTE and not of this book. The Arquidiocesis de Montevideo Marriage
Dispensation Records are the Vicar General's summary ledger, one sentence per
couple, and not one of the nine Lerena entries names a parent. Two record
classes were conflated because both are called dispensations in English.
WHAT THE LEDGER GIVES INSTEAD IS BETTER FOR THE QUESTION THIS ARCHIVE HAS. A
consanguinity dispensation is a statement about shared ancestry: the Church
computed the degree before it would grant one. Second degree in the equal
lateral line is first cousins. Third is second cousins. "With attingency to
the second" means two separate blood paths at once.
  1883  Luis P. Marquez x MERCEDES LERENA, Catedral - banns only
  1885  Serapio Fernandez x ANTONINA LERENA, Trinidad - SECOND degree, equal
  1885  Maximo Pelaez x MARIA LERENA, Trinidad - THIRD w/ attingency to second
  1894  JUAN LERENA x Eduviges Pelaez, Mercedes - SECOND *and* THIRD, de oficio
  1901  Adolfo Cordero x ZELMIRA CARLOTA LERENA - THIRD w/ attingency to second
  1906  Guillermo ? x MARIA ELENA LERENA - RELIGION MIXTA
  1913  Vitalino Gregorio Pelaez x FLORINDA JUANA LERENA, Trinidad - THIRD
  1919  EDUARDO LERENA x Maria Mercedes Razzello, Las Piedras - banns
  192-  Juan Carlos Gonzalez Lerena x Concepcion Urbano - banns (set aside)
THE LERENAS OF TRINIDAD MARRIED PELAEZ AND KEPT MARRYING THEM. Four unions
counting the Bernabe Lerena and Casimira Pelaez this archive already held, two
of them between cousins, and Juan Lerena dispensed twice over. AND TWO LERENA
WOMEN OF TRINIDAD WERE DISPENSED IN A SINGLE SITTING on 26 June 1885 - one to
a Fernandez, one to a Pelaez. Fernandez is the surname of Sancho Llerena's
wife and of Avelino Lerena Fernandez. A kindred marrying inside itself, with
the Church recording how closely.
ZELMIRA CARLOTA LERENA has her own marriage at last - and she married a blood
relative, which is a fact about her ancestry rather than her life. This
archive once wrote her off as "not ours" and corrected that; here she is on a
record of her own.
AND I INVENTED SEVEN BIRTH YEARS AND HAD THEM TAKEN OFF ME. Each new row first
carried a year reached by assuming an ordinary age at marriage, and
check-duplicates.py caught every one by matching the invented years against
real namesakes within six years. That is the William John Taylor mistake of 8
October repeated at seven times the scale, one day later. The years are
withdrawn; the register gives no age and no birth.
Twenty-five same-name pairs were compared and declared rather than merged. The
gate matched most of them on shared words in long notes - "image", "marriage",
"birth" - and not on anything about the people, which is written into each
reason so the next reader is not misled by the pairing.
Row 194 is done. Its successor is the expedientes behind these nine, starting
with Zelmira's, because a dispensation of kinship required the pedigree to be
set out before it was granted.

commits.subject: Roque on a voters' roll, Nuno on a title deed, and a country I wrote off yesterday
commits.body:
Worked row 194, and it opened with this archive correcting itself after one
day.
YESTERDAY I PUBLISHED THAT SOUTH AFRICA IS NOT IN THE FULL-TEXT CORPUS. It is.
A full-text search with a South African place IN THE URL errors outright -
"Something Went Wrong" - so the route looked closed. The PLACE FACET inside
the page works perfectly, and the surname returns seven hits across four South
African collections including South Africa, Properties, 1800-1997.
A broken parameter read as an absent country. That is now the fourth instance
of this shape in false-zeros.tsv, after FamilySearch's place filter returning 0
against a control of thousands, its date filter zeroing a 413-result query, and
findmypast ignoring URL parameters entirely. The rule this archive already
wrote would have caught it, with one word added: a search tool that ERRORS is
not a corpus that is EMPTY.
TWO OF THE SEVEN ARE THIS FAMILY AND BOTH ARE NEW.
ROQUE LUIS ARMANDO LERENA is on a Union voters' roll, 1925-1931: "STEMDISTRIK
POLLING DISTRICT NO. 770 ... 1491 Lerena, Roque Luis Armando", between
Leibbrandt and Le Riche in a strictly alphabetical list. He was twenty to
twenty-six. These rolls carry an ADDRESS and a TENURE - the same page runs
Owner, Sole Tenant, Joint Tenant, Medehuurder, and one entry reads "Botha
Hostel, Trill Rd." The OCR cannot be aligned to the names, so his address
needs the plate read by eye. It is the best lead yet on where he was before
Bloemfontein in 1932.
NUNO FERNANDO LERENA is in a land record, which is the first this archive has
found for anybody in this family: "... Cologne Road . Description of Property
... No. 245 ... Sq. Roods 6,600 Sq. Feet . Huno Fernando Lerena 6. 10. 1924 .
Purchase Amount". "Huno" is the transcriber's NUNO and 6.10.1924 is his birth
date to the day, which is what identifies it. The town is not in the
transcript.
AND IT DOES NOT OVERTURN WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE IT OVERTURNS. /south-africa/ says
a search of the deeds registers returns no land at all - that was said of
PABLO ARMANDO, is still true of him, and was never tested on his sons.
ONE LERENA EXCLUDED RATHER THAN IGNORED: the Pretoria 1939 hit is Seko Lerena
in the Ned. Geref. SENDING GEMEENTE Kranspoort, a mission congregation, listed
among Adolf Moyapelo, Paulose Marko and Daniel Gama. A different population
entirely. Recorded because "seven South African hits" would otherwise read as
seven of this family.
The Uruguayan half of row 194 is started and not finished: the Montevideo
dispensations return Florinda Juana, Margarita, Antonina and Maria Lerena,
none of them in this register. The parentage sits in the body of each
expediente and each needs opening. That is the half with the parents in it.

commits.subject: The register is exhausted on her parents, and a route nobody here had used
commits.body:
Went back to both threads with FamilySearch open.
ROW 106 IS CLOSED ON THIS SOURCE, which is worth more than leaving it hopeful.
Catalogued every column of the 1947 Maitland opening from the header row: No,
DATE, NAME, SEX, AGE in years and months, LATE RESIDENCE in town and street,
CAUSE OF DEATH (redacted by FamilySearch), DATE OF DEATH, BY WHOM CERTIFIED -
then allotment, cemetery number, grave, depth, position, officiating minister,
undertaker, particulars.
THERE IS NO INFORMANT COLUMN AND NO PARENT COLUMN. Her "by whom certified"
cell is blank and her date of death reads 27, confirming the index. One near
miss worth recording: this register DOES name a parent when a child has no
name of its own - entry 430 on the same page reads "Gordon, Child of ..." - so
the convention exists and she falls outside it precisely because somebody had
named her. The Cape civil registration is the only route left.
AND THEN THE OTHER THREAD GAVE UP SOMETHING BIGGER THAN ITSELF.
FamilySearch FULL-TEXT SEARCH reads the words on unindexed images. Every
Uruguayan search in this archive until today went through an INDEX - a
transcriber's reading of a name - and full text goes round the transcriber
entirely.
URUGUAY IS IN THE CORPUS, and so is the one record class this archive most
wants: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, MARRIAGE DISPENSATION RECORDS 1856-1932.
canelones-films.tsv has said since September that "the pre-marriage
investigation is worth MORE than the act - it routinely gives a Spanish
groom's PARENTS", and parentage is exactly what the Uruguayan end is short of.
Also in: Flores and Trinidad baptisms and deaths - the kindred swept by index
on 27 September - Montevideo burial registers 1886-2021, and the Catedral's
own books.
THE PROOF THAT IT REACHES WHAT AN INDEX HIDES: searching the exact phrase
"Juan Carlos Lerena" returns TWO hits in the whole corpus, and one is Don JUAN
CARLOS GONZALEZ LERENA, dispensed from banns at Montevideo on 8 November 192-,
entry N. 14610, marrying Concepcion Petrona Urbano of the Cordon. No surname
index of LERENA would ever have surfaced him.
HE IS SET ASIDE, on the surname order. Gonzalez from his father and Lerena
from his mother, so a son of his would be a GONZALEZ - and Pablo Armando is a
Lerena. For him to be the father, the 1908 card would have had to drop his
paternal surname and keep his maternal one. Recorded so nobody finds him again
and is briefly excited.
AND THE CORPUS HAS A HOLE WHERE THIS ARCHIVE ALSO NEEDS ONE: South Africa is
not in it. A place-filtered search errors outright and no South African
collection surfaces. So row 106 gains nothing from full text, and the Uruguayan
end gains a great deal. Queued as row 194.

commits.subject: A debt the archive wrote down and then left for twelve days
commits.body:
Went back to the two threads. Both of the ones that need records are blocked:
FamilySearch is signed out again, so the Maitland plate and the Uruguayan
registers are out of reach, and NAAIRS still returns 503 - the same "no server
available" recorded on 17 September, three weeks on.
So I paid a debt instead, and the archive had already written out exactly what
it cost. data/_person-pairs.txt carried this, in terms:
  "SAME MAN, PROVED 27 Sep 2026 ... They are kept as two rows ONLY because a
   merge touches slugs, last-attested-alive.tsv, relations.tsv and the
   CHECKED_PAIRS in tools/consistency.py, and a half-done merge is worse than
   an honest pair. THIS LINE IS A DEBT, NOT A JUDGEMENT."
ALEJANDRO LERENA (m. ELISA VILLARDEMOROS) and ALEJANDRO M. LERENA (with JULIA
BASSANI) are now one man: Alejandro M. LERENA (m.1 Elisa Villademoros; m.2
Julia Bassani). Nine relationship edges, a slug, the pair file and the
three-Alejandros table moved with him.
What proved it in September: the Cordon act of 26 December 1877, film
007713388 image 02455, names "D. ALEJANDRO M. LERENA y ... D.a ELISA
[VILLADEMOROS] (hoy finada)" as the parents of Jacinta Mercedes Gregoria and
gives his own parents as "D. AVELINO y D.a AMBROSIA TRAIBEL". Same wife, same
initial. The 1886 act calls him viudo and Julia Bassani soltera, which is the
second marriage.
AND THE SAME TRIP FOUND A STALE CELL OF THE 8 OCTOBER KIND. the-three-
alejandros.tsv still said his parents were "STILL NOT NAMED BY ANY RECORD" -
under the heading of the very question that table exists to answer, twelve
days after they were named and written into the pair file. The finding was
recorded where it was MADE and never carried back to the page that states the
question. That is now the third instance of this failure in two days.
WHAT IS NOT MERGED, AND WHY. Alejandro Lerena Traibel, baptised at La Mauricia
in January 1846, has the same parents and a birth range that contains this
man's. The pair file calls the gap "zero on parentage and one year on birth"
and refuses the merge on discipline rather than doubt. I have not overridden
that. What would close it is named there: a burial for an infant Alejandro
Lerena 1846-1860, which would mean two sons, or any act giving Alejandro M. a
birth date.
The superseded gate grew to twelve claims and learned two more retraction
idioms - "merged with", "carried separately" - because its first run after the
merge flagged my own merge note for quoting the name it retired.

commits.subject: The gate could not see the files the research lives in
commits.body:
Yesterday's superseded gate read only rendered pages, and said so as a known
limit: three of the four stale claims found by hand were in TSV comment lines
no page renders. Closed that.
It now scans data/*.tsv as well, which is safe only because the claim list is
hand-written. The same day's attempt to generate claims automatically from
every what_was_said in corrections.tsv returned 39 hits of which every one
checked was a collision on a NAME rather than a claim. Curated regexes carry
no such noise, so pointing them at more text costs nothing.
FOUR MORE, ALL INVISIBLE TO THE OLD SCOPE. brayley-bmd.tsv and
british-newspapers-assessment.tsv both still counted "ten children";
taylor-line.tsv and taylor-twins-and-william-john.tsv both still said the
family had TWO SETS OF TWINS. Corrected, and in taylor-line the retraction now
sits in the same sentence as the claim rather than at the end of a very long
row - the first attempt put it 500 characters away and the gate, correctly,
went on failing.
THE LIST GREW FROM FIVE CLAIMS TO TEN: Mauricio's 1925 death that is his
daughter Clara's; "her sister EDIE" as evidence of a sister named Edith; Edith
as a strong candidate; "neither has been checked against a burial register";
and William John's 1 November 1870, a day no source gives and this archive
invented.
AND THE GATE HAD TO BE TAUGHT THIS ARCHIVE'S IDIOM. It kills an argument in
words no list of retraction verbs would hold - "the whole argument is dead",
"how it died", "read it as history, not as the state of the question". Those
are in now. Bare "died" deliberately is not: in a genealogy half the sentences
contain it, and it would blind the gate everywhere.
BOTH HALVES WERE TESTED BY BREAKING THEM. Reviving the twin claim in
taylor-line.tsv fails the gate; restoring it passes. Putting "she was the
seventh daughter of the ten children" back on the front page WITHOUT its
retraction fails on two claims at once; with the retraction left in place it
passes, which is the behaviour that lets this archive go on quoting its own
mistakes.

commits.subject: A correction inserted mid-paragraph leaves the paragraph's conclusion standing
commits.body:
Tried to generalise yesterday's superseded gate from five hand-picked claims
to the whole of corrections.tsv, by extracting phrases from every
what_was_said and testing them against the built site.
IT DOES NOT WORK, AND THAT IS THE USEFUL PART. The method returned 39 hits and
essentially all of them were collisions on NAMES rather than on CLAIMS - a
correction and a register row legitimately share "Luis Eugenio Lerena Lenguas
and Julia Juanico"; "1 relationships" matched inside "11 relationships"; /dna/
withdraws its own claim four hundred characters further on than the window
reached; "the one document that could name Juan Carlos Lerena" is still true.
Every hit checked by hand was noise. The hand-curated list is the right design
for this and the automatic one is not, which is worth knowing before somebody
tries it again.
Checking the serious corrections by hand instead found something the page
scan could never have seen, because it lives in comment lines that no page
renders.
YESTERDAY'S STRIKES LANDED MID-PARAGRAPH AND LEFT THE PARAGRAPHS RUNNING ON.
brayley-bmd.tsv carried the strike - "EDIE IS ISABELLA ... the argument was
counting one woman twice" - and then continued, in the same sentence, "With
Edith in sixth place, Mary Septima is the seventh daughter and her name means
what it says." Below it, "GRADED AS A STRONG CANDIDATE" and "what would settle
it costs nothing: the 1891 census at Northam" - a census that had already been
run when that line was written.
1891-northam-census.tsv still opened "WHAT IT DOES TO THE EDITH CANDIDATE -
WEAKENED, NOT KILLED" and closed "the count still demands a seventh daughter
and the archive still has none. Graded OPEN."
brayley-two-questions.tsv still ended Ethel's row "Still fits the gap".
All three now die as whole arguments instead of mid-sentence: opened as
history, closed with what killed them, and kept rather than deleted, because
reasoning that was careful and wrong is worth more to the next person than a
blank. brayley-two-questions also gets its due - it predicted in September
that only an index carrying the mother's maiden name could settle this, and
that is exactly what did.
THE LESSON FOR THE GATE: check-superseded.py reads rendered pages, so it
cannot see a claim that lives in a data file's comments. Three of the four
things found today were there.

commits.subject: The research was reaching the pages; the pages were still saying the opposite
commits.body:
Asked the audit question again instead of answering it from memory, and the
answer had changed shape. Coverage was fine: all 15 findings from this week
reach a page, 24 of 26 new people have pages and sit on /who/ and /bloodline/,
and the two that did not were a rename showing in a diff and Careen Maria, who
has no relationship edges because her parentage is the open question.
What was wrong was worse than coverage. THE SITE WAS CONTRADICTING ITSELF.
/taylor/ carried, in one scroll, a new section proving from the GRO index that
IRENE WAS ALONE IN 1879 and an older section stating that "the family had TWO
SETS of twins, this pair and Irene's in 1879". The front page said Mary
Septima "was the seventh daughter of the ten children". /direct-line/ said it
too. /trees/ advertised the whole Taylor line with "her parents named her
after the fact that she was their seventh daughter" - the exact sentence the
registers refused the day before.
Every one of those was published beside its own correction, and every gate was
green, because no gate asked the question. drift.py asks whether a page has
fallen behind its DATA. /corrections/ records what was wrong. NOTHING ASKED
WHETHER THE REST OF THE SITE HAD STOPPED SAYING IT.
tools/check-superseded.py now does. It holds the claims this archive has
retracted and fails if one is asserted outside a sentence that retracts it -
so the archive can go on quoting its own mistakes, which is most of what it
does, and cannot go on making them.
ITS FIRST RUN FOUND TEN, AND SIX WERE THE GATE'S OWN FAULT. This archive
retracts in its own words - "CORRECTS the family's account", "the register
CONTRADICTED it", "the tree IS wrong" - and the regex was too narrow to hear
any of them. A gate that cannot recognise a retraction sends people to edit
their corrections. Widened, twice, by being wrong.
AND ONE LIMIT IS WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The test is proximity, so an
unrelated correction nearby can suppress a real hit: /direct-line/ fell off the
list because a different correction sat in the same window. It was fixed
anyway, by hand, because the gate is a net and not a proof.
Four genuine stale claims corrected - the front page, /direct-line/, the
/trees/ summary row and the "two sets of twins" section - plus the GEDCOM
import row, which now says the ten children are the TREE's ten and that the
tree is wrong.

commits.subject: A family of four died on one day and the archive could not show you any of them
commits.body:
Ran the same audit across every data file rather than assume the Taylor gap
was unique. Twenty-eight files name person-shaped cells that are not in the
register; most is noise - institutions in errands, forename-only baptism
cells, spelling variants of people already there - but one was the Taylor
failure exactly repeated.
PIERRE FREDERICK LERENA, his wife GAYLE born PRESTON, and their sons RICHARD
(13) and JEFFREY (8) all died on 12 November 1999 and were buried together.
Four consecutive arks - 6X6S-M484, M48C, M48H, M48Z - entered in one act of
registration on 18 November. This archive researched that in September, proved
it was a catastrophe and not an index artefact, published it on
/south-africa/, and never made one of them a person.
They are people now, wired to Ricardo Juan Carlos, whose own page names his
son for the first time.
THE GATE GREW BY BEING MADE TO. check-people-named.py now covers a fifth file,
and its first run on that file found two more things.
MARY SEPTIMA is recorded as LERENA on three documents - the Maitland burial
register, the 1935 passenger list and the Johannesburg cemetery index - and
her register name carried only TAYLOR, so the gate could not match her. Her
married surname is now in her name, which is this archive's own convention
elsewhere and is how a reader searching the surname she was buried under will
find her.
That rename is worth recording as a cost. Changing a register name silently
breaks every file that uses it as a KEY - person-evidence.tsv, wikitree-
searches.tsv and the slug ledger all had to be repointed, and only one of them
was caught by a gate. Renaming a person here is a four-file operation.
AND ONE PERSON WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT, with the reason written into the
gate rather than hidden in it. CATHERINE TERTIA KARON is a real daughter named
in the 1971 death notice, and the cell that names her reports a search that
FAILED - "swept under her own surname at last, and not found". Her 1999 death
rests on a single commercial index row the free cemetery register could not
confirm. A register row would have to carry either a death this archive cannot
stand behind or a living person's dates, and the living rule forbids the
second. She stays out until the death is sourced.

commits.subject: The descent, drawn — with the sisters in it
commits.body:
/tree/ is an ancestor chart. It draws the direct line and nothing beside it,
so the eight brothers and sisters proved from the GRO index yesterday had
nowhere to be drawn at all. This is the other direction.
Four generations, using the kit's Descent component, which has been sitting
unused in this archive since it was written - and whose own docstring names
this exact case: "in five of these archives her family is the better
documented one, and Mary Septima Taylor's line goes back further than the man
the Lerena archive is named for".
  1  James Taylor x Harriet Reynolds        drawn WEAK - tree only
  2  John Brailey x Georgina Temple         m. 1839, St Martin-in-the-Fields
  3  William Taylor x Mary Ann Hellen Brayley  m. 1870, Bideford, 5b/794
  4  Pablo Armando Lerena x Mary Septima Taylor  m. 1911, Wynberg
The wife is a column, not a suffix. The children span both parents because
they are both parents'. The siblings sit under the parent they belong to, so
nobody can mistake his family for hers - and in generation 4 that layout does
the archive's central argument without a sentence: her column holds eight
sisters and brothers, his reads NONE RECORDED, because no sibling of Pablo
Armando Lerena has ever been found.
Generation 1 is drawn weak on purpose. James Taylor and Harriet Reynolds come
from a tree and no record here names either; everything below them rests on a
civil registration, a census or a parish register, and the join should be
visible rather than implied.
THREE THINGS THE GATES CAUGHT ON THE WAY.
The base landed twice - Descent calls u() on every href itself, and passing
pre-prefixed paths produced /TheLerena/TheLerena/people/... on 34 links. This
archive has made that exact mistake twice before; the fix is commented where
the next person will hit it.
Emphasis markers reached the page, because Descent renders note and weakNote
as html and hisNone and herNone as TEXT. The first two go through emph(), the
last two through plain(), and "<strong>NONE KNOWN" printed literally until
that was separated.
And the page's own dek still said her name "is a piece of arithmetic, and it
turns out to be exactly right" - the claim disproved yesterday, sitting at the
top of the page that disproves it. The dek and the eyebrow now say what the
registers say: Septima means seventh and she is the sixth daughter of nine.

commits.subject: Sixteen people who were findings and not persons
commits.body:
David asked whether all this was reaching the sites, the person pages, the
family charts. The honest answer was half no, and the half that was no is the
half this archive had just spent a day proving.
On the Lerena side everything had landed: Careen Maria, Pablo Armando, Rieta
Maria, the Bloemfontein infant and Roque all carry today's findings on their
own pages, and grave 7719 C, Bellville, Bloemfontein and LESINA are on the
register, the places, the bloodline, /who/, /method/ and /corrections/.
On the Taylor and Brayley side nothing had. THE REGISTER HELD EXACTLY ONE
TAYLOR. Nine children proved from the GRO index, a baptism series read at
Northam, John Walker Brailey's 1845 registration recovered - all of it reached
/taylor/ and /family-papers/ as prose and tables, and not one of those people
existed. A reader could read that Kathleen Georgina was registered at Bideford
in the December quarter of 1870 and could not click on her.
So fifteen rows were added with their GRO references, and twenty-eight parent
and spouse edges wired. Sixteen person pages where there was one. They are on
/who/, /bloodline/ and /register/; Mary Septima's page now names her parents
and her eight siblings; and the ancestor chart climbs two generations further
than it did this morning, through William Taylor and Mary Ann Hellen Brayley
to John Brailey and Georgina Temple.
AND A GATE, BECAUSE NOTHING COULD SEE THIS. check:onsite asks whether a data
file reaches a page. check:tree asks whether an edge joins a name to nothing.
Nothing asked whether a person named in a finding had been made a person, so
the archive could keep discovering people, keep failing to admit them, and
stay green. tools/check-people-named.py now walks the record files and insists
every child named in one is in the register.
Its first run caught a real thing: the Northam baptism register spells her
HELEN and the GRO index spells her HELLEN. Both are now carried in her name,
because choosing would have been arbitrary and the difference is exactly what
makes a person unfindable later.
consistency.py caught a worse thing, and it was mine. I had entered William
John Taylor's birth as 1 November 1870 - a day no source gives - and the gate
reported him and Kathleen as two children of one father nought months apart.
It was right: the archive had manufactured a three-day gap between twins out
of nothing. The precision is withdrawn, not the twinning denied; the twins
rest where they always did, on consecutive index pages 489 and 490.

commits.subject: Three children who died before their father, and an age field that is a blank
commits.body:
Went looking for Careen Maria's parents and found three other children instead.
A complete sweep: surname LERENA, country South Africa, 413 results, every one
read for an indexed parent. Exactly three carry one, and all three are Roque
Luis Armando Lerena's. His own 1973 death notice names two daughters, because
a death notice lists the living; these three were already gone.
  the unnamed infant   OFS Civil Death    d. 22 May 1932, Bloemfontein
  RIETA MARIA          Transvaal Civil Death  d. 28 Aug 1937, Mayfair, Jhb
  ANTOINETTE SEPTIMA LYNETTE  Transvaal Civil Death  d. 7 Jan 1943, Jhb
THE 1932 BOY MOVES THE FAMILY. He was born and died at BLOEMFONTEIN, which no
record here had put any Lerena in - between the Cape of Roque's birth and the
Transvaal of his death. And the register says MALE, where this archive has
carried him as "an unnamed infant" on a tree's word.
RIETA MARIA HAD NO DEATH DATE AT ALL. She was graded "birth only - a floor,
not an attestation" on a bare 1936 from a tree. She died 28 August 1937, aged
one, at 6a Robinson Street, Mayfair, Johannesburg.
AND ONE FIELD HAD TO BE THROWN AWAY. Both infant entries give "Age: 0 days",
which would mean each was born on the day it died. The tree has one at five
days and the other at four. Two independent dates disagreeing with the index
in the same direction is an unfilled form field, not two coincidences - so the
age is discarded rather than used to correct the births. This archive was one
step from publishing "the record says none, so the tree is wrong", which would
have been a correction built on a blank. Recorded in false-zeros.tsv.
A second false zero in the same sitting: surname-plus-country returned 0 with
a date range attached and 413 without it, with nothing in the result to say
the filter had misfired.
And the question that started it is still open. CAREEN MARIA LERENA HAS NO
CIVIL BIRTH OR DEATH RECORD INDEXED ANYWHERE IN SOUTH AFRICA - her only record
is the Maitland cemetery entry read this morning. Row 106 wants a Cape
registration to name her parents; FamilySearch cannot supply one, and the row
now points at Home Affairs and the Western Cape Archives instead.

commits.subject: Mary Septima's mother was never registered, and her brother's middle name was Walker
commits.body:
Same key, generation above. The archive has hunted Mary Ann Hellen Brayley's
birth entry since 14 September: born 20 May 1843 at St Bartholomew's, City of
London, and FreeBMD holds no Mary Brayley and no Mary Brailey in the June
quarter of 1843 anywhere in England and Wales. Recorded then as an absence
awaiting a better search.
So the question was reversed. Not where is she, but which children of her
parents are in the book at all - surname BRAYLEY loose-matched, mother's maiden
surname TEMPLE, 1838-1852, both sexes, six searches.
  BRAILEY, JOHN WALKER       1845 J  The Holborn Union  Vol 02  p 149
  BRAILEY, GEORGINA MARGARET 1850 S  The Bideford Union Vol 10  p 52
Two children, and two absences. Isabella (about 1841) and Mary Ann Hellen
(1843) are both missing and both London-born; the two later children are both
present. Birth registration was not compulsory on parents until the Act of
1874, in force 1875 - the duty lay on the registrar - and under-registration
in the 1840s fell heaviest on the urban poor. The 1851 census calls this
household "Shoemaker Wife Pauper".
She was almost certainly never registered. The null is now double and arrives
from two directions: FreeBMD under her own name, the GRO under her mother's.
Stated as a conclusion, not a certainty - a registration under a spelling the
index does not associate with Brayley at all cannot be excluded by any search.
The spelling control is built into the result: the query said BRAYLEY and the
index returned BRAILEY both times.
JOHN WALKER BRAILEY settles three things on his own. The tree's 22 June 1845
is right, because a June birth falls in the June quarter - so the 1900 death
index that made him 53 had a careless informant, which this archive had
already concluded from the 1851 census. The birthplace dispute resolves to
neither side: the census said St Pancras and the tree said St Paul's, and the
district is HOLBORN - which is where his sister Isabella was born, entered in
1861 as "London (City), St Andrew", that is St Andrew Holborn.
And his middle name is WALKER. The archive had documented this family putting
its Scottish great-grandmothers' surnames - Temple and Walker - into birth
registrations as forenames in 1874, 1876 and 1889. It was doing it in 1845.
The naming discipline runs a full generation earlier than recorded.

commits.subject: Nine children, not ten, and Septima was never the seventh
commits.body:
David logged this session in to gro.gov.uk and the search row 128 named on
17 September was finally run. The GRO's own index prints the mother's maiden
surname on every birth from 1837, which FreeBMD does not and never will - so
TAYLOR births with mother BRAYLEY return this couple's children by definition,
with no inference and no candidate-weighing.
Ten searches: five year-windows across 1870-1893, times two sexes, because sex
is mandatory and the range is capped at plus or minus two.
  1  Kathleen Georgina       1870 D  Bideford  05B/490
  2  William John            1870 D  Bideford  05B/489
  3  Horace Archibald        1872 J  Bideford  05B/507
  4  Isabella Temple         1874 D  Bideford  05B/497
  5  Margaret Hellen Walker  1876 D  Bideford  05B/481
  6  Irene                   1879 M  Bideford  05B/524
  7  Lucy Elizabeth          1881 S  Bideford  05B/508
  8  MARY SEPTIMA            1884 D  Bideford  05B/506
  9  Agnes Walker            1889 S  Bideford  05B/502
Nothing before Kathleen, nothing between any two of them, nothing after Agnes.
The critical window was re-run on loose spelling matching, because BRAILEY is
a documented variant of this name: 28 births across England, the same two at
Bideford.
THE TREE'S TEN IS WRONG. There are nine, and no tenth child is missing. Three
weeks of searching - rows 126, 127, 128, 192, 193, a FreeBMD death sweep, a
FreeREG attempt and a findmypast baptism search - were spent on a child who
does not exist, on the authority of a MyHeritage tree that names nine and
asserts ten.
EDITH and ETHEL, the two Bideford candidates, do not have Brayley as their
mother. And IRENE IS ALONE IN 1879: no second birth to this mother that year,
of either sex. The unnamed twin was never a person. She was an arithmetical
requirement wearing a tree's silence as evidence, and this archive built her,
published her and reasoned from her.
AND THE ARITHMETIC THIS PAGE IS NAMED FOR DOES NOT WORK. Mary Septima is the
SIXTH daughter and the EIGHTH child. No reading of the registered family makes
her seventh of anything. /taylor/ has said since the beginning that "her own
name is a piece of arithmetic, and it turns out to be exactly right". It is
not. The name is now an unexplained fact, which is a worse answer and a truer
one.
One possibility is recorded as a possibility. A stillbirth was not registrable
in England and Wales until 1927, so a seventh pregnancy carried to term and
lost would be invisible to every index reachable from here - and would still
be counted by the woman who bore her.
Three incidental confirmations: the twins are proved by consecutive pages, 489
and 490 in one quarter; the GRO prints MARGARET HELLEN WALKER in full, settling
an initial the census read as N and FreeBMD abbreviated to W; and Mary Septima's
own registration, 05B/506, is on the record here for the first time.

commits.subject: The FreeBMD death sweep was run on 17 September, and I said it had not been
commits.body:
Second time today this archive has queued work that was already done. The row
I wrote an hour ago said "the GRO death index for Bideford, 1870-1884, under
TAYLOR is the cheap test nobody has run." Row 128 ran it on 17 September:
FreeBMD deaths, TAYLOR, Bideford, 1881-1891, 37 entries, fourteen of them aged
0-3. Both claims were written from memory while finishing something else,
which is now a pattern and is written down as one.
It was caught before the search was repeated, by reading the file first. That
is the system working, but only just.
What the baptism register adds to row 128, which is real. It weighed two
candidates for the missing daughter and could attach neither; both are now
harder.
EDITH, born Bideford Sep quarter 1882: not in the family's baptism register,
where every named sibling is.
ETHEL, born Bideford Dec quarter 1882 and dead at Bideford aged two - the
candidate row 128 preferred, because she would sit in the birth index and in
no census. She is not in the register either. She was about two when she died,
and this family baptised Lucy at a few weeks and Agnes at eighteen days. So
either she is not theirs, or she went unbaptised for two years. A disjunction,
not a refutation - but it is the first evidence of any kind that touches her.
So the hole has a sharper shape: a child of this couple born between 31 August
1881 and 30 October 1884, the exact gap in the register, who left a birth
registration and nothing else.
And the search that ends it is still David's, as row 128 said in September.
gro.gov.uk is not FreeBMD and the difference is the whole point: the GRO's own
index gives the mother's maiden name on every birth from 1837. Births, surname
TAYLOR, mother's maiden name BRAYLEY, district BIDEFORD, 1870-1890 returns
every child of this couple by definition. It needs a free GRO account and this
session does not create accounts, so it is now an errand with the query
written out and the two excluded names beside it.

commits.subject: Seven children in one query, and the eighth is not there
commits.body:
findmypast's Devon Baptisms answered what FreeREG could not. Northam, St
Margaret, South West Heritage Trust 1843A/PR/1/16: seven children of William
Taylor and Mary Ann Helen/Ellen. Horace Archibald and Isabella Temple (1874),
Margaret Helen Walker (1876), Irene (1879), Lucy Elizabeth (31 Aug 1881),
MARY SEPTIMA (30 Oct 1884) and Agnes Walker (21 Aug 1889).
HER OWN BAPTISM, which this archive has never held. Six weeks after birth, and
the first time her parents are named together in a parish register rather than
a tree, a census or an index - the earliest record of her life, twenty-seven
years before she married at Wynberg.
AND NO EDITH. Lucy is baptised 31 August 1881 and Mary Septima 30 October
1884, with nothing between them. The candidate falls exactly in that gap and
every sibling on both sides of her is in the book. The only two Edith Taylors
baptised in Devon near the date are at Bideford with mothers MARIA and
ELIZABETH - two other William Taylors, identified by their wives.
So the candidate goes from strong to weak, three weeks after it was raised and
hours after it lost the "Edie" leg. What survives is an unsourced count in a
family tree and the meaning of a name.
THE METHOD IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: SEARCH ON THE MOTHER. One query on "Mary
Ann Helen" returns the whole sibling group in a single page, which is what
makes an absence provable - searching child by child could only ever have
failed to find her. And the control ran first, on Agnes Walker Taylor, whose
birth this archive held to the day and the address.
/taylor/ was also claiming too much and has stopped. It said, under a
Documented chip, that Mary Septima was "the ninth of ten children"; and it
filled the sixth-daughter slot with an unnamed twin of Irene, inferred female
"or the arithmetic does not come out" - from the same MyHeritage tree that
/family-papers/ calls a source this archive should never have used. The
register enters Irene alone in 1879. Both fillers are now marked tree-only and
the arithmetic is stated as unsolved.
It also strengthens David's reading of the family photograph: if there is no
eighth daughter, the eighth woman in the group is not a daughter, and his
grandmother or aunt is the better explanation.
Next, and queued: the GRO death index for Bideford 1870-1884. A child born and
died between censuses leaves a birth registration, no baptism and no household
entry - which is exactly the shape of the hole.

commits.subject: Northam's parish register stops in 1817, and the zero was a wall not an absence
commits.body:
Went after the baptism that would attach or detach the 1882 Edith Taylor. Both
free routes are shut, and both were established with controls rather than
assumed from a null.
FreeREG holds Northam, St Margaret, Parish Register: 12,120 records, 1653 to
1817. The record wanted is 1882 - sixty-five years past the end of the
transcription. Bideford is listed as a place and holds no church, no register
and no records at all. The search was run before the contents page was read
and returned 0; the contents page then explained the 0.
FamilySearch produced two false zeros in one sitting, both now recorded.
The place parameter returned 0 for "surname TAYLOR at Northam, Devon,
1860-1900" with nothing else set, which is impossible for a parish that size
in a county whose censuses it holds. The same search with a looser place
returned 6,941 results from Kent, Northamptonshire and Wiltshire. The field
was ignored when it was loose and fatal when it was tight, and neither
behaviour showed in the result.
And a full-name search returned 0 for Horace Archibald Taylor, Mary Septima
Taylor and Agnes Walker Taylor - three people this archive holds on records -
because the index carries them under initials. That is the same trap the GRO
index sprang in September, when both brothers were found only after dropping
the second forename. Walked into again on a different site five days later,
which is why it is written down rather than remembered.
Row 192 now names the paid and postal routes instead of leaving them to be
rediscovered: findmypast's Devon Baptisms, licensed from the Devon FHS;
Ancestry's Devon parish registers; or the North Devon Record Office, which
holds the originals.

commits.subject: Edie is Isabella, and the Edith argument had been counting one woman twice
commits.body:
David asked for the 1891 census of Northam to be done for the Taylors. It had
been done on 16 September - work-list row 127, the household at 2 Fore Street
read out by name, age, occupation and birthplace. This archive said otherwise
on /family-papers/ a few hours ago. Corrected.
Doing what was asked meant re-reading the file, and a sentence in it did not
survive. Since 16 September three files have argued that "Mary Septima stayed
with her sister EDIE at 26 Fore Street in 1935" was independent evidence of a
missing sister called Edith - known, in the archive's own words, "from a
completely different direction".
EDIE IS ISABELLA. taylor-line.tsv and taylor-marriages.tsv both carry her as
Isabella Temple "Edie" Taylor, who married HENRY DALLING at Northam on 10
September 1900. family-memory.tsv says "her sister Edie DALLING" - the married
surname is in the sentence. passenger-lists.tsv gives Mary Septima's 1935
address as "C/O DALLING, FORE ST, NORTHAM" and says in terms it is her elder
sister Isabella. And the 1939 Register for 26 Fore Street lists ISABELLA T
DALLING, born Taylor, 10 September 1874.
Four files identified her and three files used her as somebody else.
What replaces it is better, because it is a record. Counted head by head at
full resolution, the family group holds three males, eight females and one
infant. The records give father and two sons - three. Mother and six named
daughters besides the infant - seven. THE PHOTOGRAPH HOLDS ONE FEMALE THE
NAMED FAMILY DOES NOT ACCOUNT FOR, and the tree has always said ten children
while naming nine.
It also dates the sitting. If the infant is Agnes Walker, born 3 August 1889
at that address, the photograph is after August 1889; and by April 1891 both
Isabella and Mary Septima are absent from the house, so a sitting with
everyone in it falls in a window of about eighteen months.
NOT PROOF, and David named the reason before the count was made: if any one of
the eight is a grandmother, aunt, sister-in-law, visitor or servant, nine
children satisfy it and there is no Edith. The 1891 return for this house
records Agnes Harrison, visitor, 28, a dressmaker from Macclesfield. The
grandmother Georgina Brayley was alive in the same parish, 77, alone in the
Alms House.
So the next record is named and queued as row 192: the Northam and Bideford
baptism registers for 1882-83, which give parents, where the birth index gives
no mother's maiden name until 1911.

commits.subject: You cannot count daughters in a photograph
commits.body:
David put the three images in the archive and then said one sentence about the
Taylor group: "I think there is a grandmother or aunt in that photo as well."
That undoes something this archive published this morning. The page said "at
least eight daughters and two sons are in the frame" and offered the number as
the ordinary explanation of SEPTIMA, meaning seventh. The figure count was
also wrong - at full resolution it is twelve people and a dog, three male,
eight female, one infant whose sex cannot be told - but the count was never
the error that mattered.
A granddaughter, a niece, a daughter-in-law and a neighbour's child all
photograph identically. There are two seated adult women in this group and
nothing in the image says which is the mother of the small girl; the one in
the bonnet and fringed shawl reads as the elder, which is as consistent with a
grandmother as with a mother of ten.
So the page now counts figures and stops, and names the record that would
actually settle a sibling count: the 1891 census of Northam, already read here
for the Brayleys and never counted for the Taylors.
This archive's own standard should have caught it before David did. It says on
/south-africa/ that it "does not turn consistent with into is" - and then did
exactly that with a picture: counted faces, assumed every one was a child of
the couple, and ran the total back into a name it already believed.
The Marist figures went the other way. Every one was re-read off the scans and
every one held, including the two flagged as least certain - the 608 of June
and the 715 of November. Those caveats are withdrawn.
Three images published: the Taylor group, the June/November testimonials and
the October one. The gallery is nine documents now, not six.

commits.subject: Downing or Downey: a name this archive should not be the one to change
commits.body:
David re-sent three death notices. Two are the 1973 and 1971 Transvaal notices
this archive read in full on 16 September; the third is the Booyzen notice of
estate 1095/48, already recorded on row 111 as the document that cancelled the
whole Pretoria pull. Nothing in any of them is new.
One thing is doubtful. Row 111 names him GEORGE DOWNING MOUNTJOY BOOYZEN.
On the photograph, "Mountjoy" and the surname are clear and the middle name
reads more like DOWNEY.
Left uncorrected on purpose. The sheet is about 768 pixels for a whole
foolscap page - the same resolution that could not separate Careen from Carmen
this morning, and that was wrong about a grave suffix until the real plate was
opened. And he belongs to the Booyzen archive. A Lerena session rewriting
another archive's person off a thumbnail is how the three archives stop being
three.
The original is in the house and settles it in a second.

commits.subject: A schoolboy beat his opponent by seven marks, and Mary Septima has a face
commits.body:
Two sets of family papers from David, transcribed as facts. The images are
not in the repo yet - he sent them as photographs in conversation, not files -
and the facts do not wait on the scan, which is how this archive has always
worked.
THREE MARIST TESTIMONIALS, 1936. "Testimonial of Application and Diligence,
merited by Master N. Lerena", Marist Brothers, St Joseph's College, Belmont
Park, Rondebosch, signed by the Principal, Bro. Vital. 1 June (608 against his
opponent's 578, form's highest 690), 1 October (458 against 415, highest 523),
1 November (715 against 708, highest 1045).
N. Lerena is Nuno Fernando, born 6 October 1924 - eleven turning twelve across
the three, and the only N. Lerena of school age in this family. The October
certificate is dated five days before his twelfth birthday.
The opponent's column is the point: the Marists ran classrooms on emulation,
each boy paired against another and both totals printed, so a testimonial
records not what he knew but whom he beat. By 30, then 43, then seven.
It fills a year the archive had nothing for. His mother died at Observatory in
November 1935; these are the twelve months after, with the boy at a Catholic
school at Rondebosch. And it corroborates the religion from a new direction -
the Corpus Christi baptisms, the Roman Catholic allotment of grave 7719, and
now a Marist schoolroom.
THE TAYLOR FAMILY GROUP. Twelve people and an infant before a studio backdrop,
a dog asleep on a cushion at the front. David identifies Mary Septima as the
small girl at the lower right, against the knee of the seated man with full
side-whiskers, with her father, mother and siblings. It is the only identified
likeness of her this archive holds - of anyone in this family before the Cape.
Nobody else in the group is named, and no sibling is matched to a face here.
The picture does argue one thing on its own. At least eight daughters and two
sons are in the frame, which is the ordinary explanation of SEPTIMA, meaning
seventh - a name this archive has carried as a curiosity since the beginning.
Though a studio group is who turned up, not who was born.
The date is inferred and labelled as inferred: born 17 September 1884, the
child looks five or six, so about 1889-1891, with the dress agreeing and not
narrowing it. A photographer's imprint on the mount would settle it; the
supplied image is cropped to the print.
Figures read off a photocopy; both TSVs say which digits are least certain.

commits.subject: Grave 7719 is his own plot and it holds all three of them
commits.body:
He was never found because FamilySearch indexes him as ROBERT PAUL LESINA -
the seventh machine misreading of this surname on record here. He was found
by not searching the surname at all: given name "Robert Paul", death year
1950, this collection only, 663 results, first row.
Maitland Road Cemetery, Record of Interments, Volume 21, page 339, entry 327.
LERENA, Robert Paul, M.E., 76, of Newlands, 7 Forth Road. Roman Catholic,
Cemetery No. 1, GRAVE 7719 C, 8 feet, position Bott, Father Plotton
officiating, undertaker Goodall & Wms. Last column: "In Plot of R. P. Lerina".
So the plot was his own, and it holds three people: 7719 A Mary Septima
(1935), 7719 B the infant Careen Maria (1947), 7719 C himself (1950).
WHICH MEANS THE FAMILY WERE RIGHT. Cheryl was told the unmarked grave carrying
only LERENA held three people - Pablo Armando, Mary Septima, an infant. Every
part of that is in the register. The one wrong word is Newlands, which is
where he died. Row 110 asked "Maitland or Newlands" and is now done; his
certificate's intended place of burial is proved actual.
AND THIS MORNING'S TWO CAVEATS ARE BOTH ANSWERED, because signing in gave the
same 1947 plate at 4,863 pixels instead of about 1,100. The grave is 7719 B,
not 7719. The name is CAREEN, not Carmen - the letter in dispute is the
pointed r this clerk writes in "Frederick" two lines below, not the three-arch
m he writes in "mary" one line below. Carmen was the likelier name and it is
not what the page says.
A new fact with two edges, on row 106: the infant was buried inside his plot,
which is evidence she was his - and her last residence is 42 Victoria Road,
BELLVILLE, while he and his executrix Rose Lilian Theys both lived at 7 Forth
Road, Newlands. Cheryl's reading that Theys was the mother now has an address
to explain.
last-alive.py took the FIRST "died <date>" anywhere in a row's prose. Adding
the three burials to his note moved his own death to the infant's 1947, which
check-spines caught against the /uruguay/ ladder. The bug bit hardest where
the research was best: the fuller a note, the likelier it names somebody
else's death. Death dates are now corroborated against an independent record
year instead of ranked by position, and where nothing corroborates the tool
falls back to a ceiling and says so rather than guessing.
It said so immediately, about a row nobody had questioned: MAURICIO LERENA,
born c.1815, was carrying 3 March 1925 as an explicit death date. That is his
daughter Clara's. The archive had been asserting he died at about 110.

commits.subject: The page said the grave number would settle it, and the grave number arrived
commits.body:
David sent one opening of the Maitland Road Cemetery Record of Interments.
Page 4706, entry 423: LERENA, female, 2 wks, late residence on a Victoria
Road, Roman Catholic allotment, Cons. No. 1, GRAVE 7719, 3 1/2 feet down.
That is Mary Septima Taylor's grave. This archive has cited her burial as
"p.3215 entry 163, Nov 1935 ... Cemetery no 1, grave 7719A" since September.
Same cemetery, same allotment, same plot number, twelve years apart.
/south-africa/ had already named this exact test. Of the kerb reading LERENA
and nothing else it said: "equally consistent with her grave, with his, or
with a family plot holding both ... What would settle it is the grave number."
Two burials at one number is the third reading. A kerb with no given name is
what you pour over a plot you mean to use again.
AND IT CORRECTS A FAMILY MEMORY. Cheryl was told by a cemetery office that the
unmarked LERENA grave was at NEWLANDS. Newlands is where Pablo Armando died -
7 Forth Road - and it is a different suburb from Maitland, which is what his
own 1950 certificate names. Three records point at Maitland; one recollection
points at Newlands. Work-list row 110 used to end "neither has been checked
against a burial register". It has been now.
TWO THINGS NOT CLAIMED. His own entry is still unseen: he died in March 1950
and this opening is 1947, so intended is still not actual for him. And the
scan is ~1,100px across a full opening, which cannot resolve an "A" suffix and
cannot tell Careen from Carmen - Carmen being the commoner name in this family
by far. The reading already carried is kept rather than improved into the
likelier guess.
check-sources gained a third locator and it is not an exemption. The row said
IMAGE READ and could name no film, because there is none; the only ways to
pass were to lie or to delete the word READ. It now accepts the register's own
page+entry WITH the explicit words IMAGE SUPPLIED - both halves required,
tested by breaking each - and counts them aloud on every green run, because a
locator that resolves to no public image is weaker than one that does.
And /sources/ was three weeks late again, which is the failure that file
exists to stop: p.3215 has been quoted on /estate/ and /taylor/ since
mid-September, down to the depth of the grave and the name of the undertaker,
under a heading claiming to list everything. Its route was never written down
and cannot now be recovered, so it is recorded as unknown.

commits.subject: Twenty-nine godparent edges that reached nobody, and the plumbing to publish them
commits.body:
Wiring the last category of unwired people - the forty-four whose note says
they stood at a font. Twenty-seven resolved by reading, every pair checked
against the register by exact name rather than matched.
THEN I CHECKED WHETHER THEY RENDERED, AND THEY DID NOT. build-people.py mapped
four relation words - father, mother, spouse, child - and dropped everything
else SILENTLY. So check-tree.py counted twenty-nine godparent edges, this
session reported the tree at 69%, and Don Fidel Rey's page said "no
relationships are recorded for this person". The number was inflated by edges
nothing drew.
That is this archive's own cardinal sin committed by me: storing a finding is
not publishing it. Caught by asking whether the edge reached a reader rather
than whether the gate went green.
THEY ARE DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE CHART, AND NOT IN relTotal. The person page
says "of the N relationships IN THE CHART ABOVE", and the chart draws parents,
spouses, children and siblings. Folding godparents into that count would have
made the sentence false - the easier fix, and a lie. They get their own line
instead: "At the font. They stood godfather to ..." with the limit stated in
the same breath.
327 edges, 261 of 377 people wired. The figure now means what it says.
And the pattern is worth the plumbing. This family chose godparents from inside
itself over and over - a Lavalleja for the child named Justiniano, an Ana for
the Ana, Don Fidel Rey four years before a son was christened Fidel. The naming
habit this archive has traced through five fonts is the same habit, seen from
the other side.

commits.subject: This archive kept its own spine twice, and the page rendered the copy nobody checked
commits.body:
data/direct-line.tsv holds the direct line with its evidence - arks, a passport
serial, an interment register page and entry, estate file numbers. And
site/src/pages/direct-line.astro holds THE SAME LINE AGAIN as a hard-coded
array. The page renders the ARRAY. The TSV was declared a working log and read
by nobody.
They did not disagree. That was luck, not a gate: hand-written descent has gone
stale twice in this archive, which is why check-spines.py exists at all.
I REFUSED THE OBVIOUS FIX, AND THE REASON IS THE POINT. Rendering the TSV would
have redrawn the archive's most important page - the two are not the same shape,
the TSV giving each wife her own row where the page folds her into a spouse
field. And the TSV's `evidence` column was never written for publication:
GENERATION 3'S NAMES A LIVING PERSON AND CARRIES A BIRTH YEAR inside a quoted
retraction. Migrating would have published it.
So the duplication STAYS and both joins are gated instead. The PAGE must agree
with the TSV about every date it states; the TSV must agree with the REGISTER
through a new `register` column. A reader sees exactly what they saw before,
and neither copy can drift alone.
TWO FAULTS IN MY OWN GATE, BOTH CAUGHT BY TESTING IT RATHER THAN TRUSTING IT:
  It bounded each entry with `.{0,400}?` and matched ONE row of four, because
  these notes run longer than that. A gate that silently checks a quarter of
  what it claims is worse than none.
  Then it compared YEARS ONLY - and a deliberate test changing "6 Oct 1924" to
  "7 Oct 1924" sailed straight through. Two copies of one line drifting by a
  day is the likeliest error available here. It compares the day now, and the
  test fails as it should.

commits.subject: Fourteen of thirty returned nothing, and that is the number the page now leads with
commits.body:
Work-list row 131, and deliberately NOT done by replacing the prose.
/searched/ is 1,429 lines and thirty-three sections, several of them tables of
many searches. Flattening that into five fields would have thrown away the
reasoning, WHICH ON THIS PAGE IS THE ASSET: it is the archive's record of how
it was wrong, and a register of negative results is only worth reading because
somebody explained why each one counts.
So data/searched-index.tsv holds THIRTY ROWS THAT INDEX THE SECTIONS, each
linking to the prose that explains it, and every section stays where it was.
What the rows add is the thing prose could never give - something a filter can
reach and a gate can count.
AND THE COUNT IS THE POINT. Fourteen of the thirty returned NOTHING. The kit's
own docstring says why that number belongs at the top: an archive that records
only its hits is keeping a highlight reel, not a register.
THE OUTCOME WORDS ARE THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN - found, nothing, mixed, blocked,
answered, unresolved, abandoned. The component insists on that, and says
flattening four archives' vocabularies to a shared five "would be inventing a
finding".
THREE SECTIONS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT ROWS. "Why a page of failures", "What is on
this page" and "What the failures add up to" are the page's argument about
itself, not searches, and giving them an outcome would be a category error.
`when` is coarse where the prose is coarse. A bare year means the section does
not date itself more precisely, and guessing a day to fill a column is how a
register starts lying.
The same base-prefix trap as the questions file, in a new shape: a bare
"#anchor" in the href column becomes /TheLerena/#anchor - a link to the home
page carrying a fragment that is not there. Thirty of them, all caught by the
anchor gate, and the file's header now says so.

commits.subject: The generated file the questions commit left behind
Seven questions and two closed doors, as rows a filter can reach
commits.body:
Work-list row 132. /open-questions/ was 188 lines of prose - seven questions
and two failed routes, none of it filterable, countable or comparable with the
other archives in this estate.
The kit's Questions component takes {q, state, known, tried, settles} and its
docstring says plainly why it had sat unused here: five of seven archives keep
their questions as prose and "cannot use this until somebody extracts them, and
that extraction is research work belonging to each archive rather than
something to guess at from outside". This is that extraction, done from inside.
THE RISK WAS LOSING THE NEGATIVE EVIDENCE. Question 1 carried a long panel -
the Lerena-Lerena compound test, the forty-three transcription doublings, the
Carmen Lerena act read off film 007713392 image 2511, and the sentence that
says the test LOWERS the probability without settling it. A refactor that drops
that is worse than the prose it replaced, so it is carried whole into the
"tried" field and the result was checked phrase by phrase against the built
page.
FOUR QUESTIONS HAVE NO "tried" FIELD AND THAT IS ACCURATE, NOT MISSING: the
original prose listed only what to do about them. Saying so is the point of
having the field.
Two rows are BLOCKED rather than open - the MyHeritage tree that needs a
logged-in session, and Forebears' Spanish figures that return nothing to a
fetch. They are not questions about the family; they are routes that failed,
and the page kept them for that reason.
One asymmetry cost a build and is now in the file's header: the href COLUMN is
based by u(), the HTML fields are not. Six /TheLerena/TheLerena/ links, all
caught by the link gate.
(This message is amended: backticks in the first draft were expanded by the
shell and ate two field names out of it.)

commits.subject: Five children who were named on their parents' rows and had none of their own
commits.body:
The smaller gap left behind by yesterday's spouse work, closed the same way.
Felix Antonio and Aurora Eduarda Larena Fuentes, Petrona Medero Llerena, Ana

archive has traced that naming habit through five fonts and has also been
burned by exactly this reasoning, so it is offered as neither.
300 edges, 228 of 377 people wired - 60%. (The first draft of this message said
233 and 62%. I wrote the figure before I measured it; this is the measured one.)
