commits.subject: Seventeen was my own miscount, and the real number is eight
commits.body:
Work-list row 191 said this register names SEVENTEEN spouses it does not hold.
It names EIGHT. The seventeen was my error, made nine days ago and published.
HOW IT HAPPENED. The test asked whether any register row contained every word
of a string a regex had captured - and the regex over-captured. It searched for
"m. Capitan Don Antonio Ruiz de Carvallo AND DAUGHTER OF SANCHO L" as if that
were a name, found nothing, and reported the spouse missing. Four spouses were
in the register the whole time. Three more resolved on reading. Eight were
genuinely absent.
The same shape as the matcher errors of 27 and 28 September: a string that
looks like a name, used as one.
WIRED, SEVEN, each disambiguated by reading rather than matching:
  Bernardina Fragoso to Fructuoso Rivera
  Cipriana Saenz Pena to Gilberto Lerena Salvanach the younger
  Leonarda Correa to Nicolas Benteno
  Dominga Carvallo to Capitan Antonio Ruiz de Carvallo
  Maria Carlota Amadeo Lastra to the BUENOS AIRES Rafael Llerena - this
    register holds two Rafaels and the Cordoba one married Rosario Moyano
  Juana del Espiritu Santo to Don Domingo Rodriguez the elder, the act calling
    them "ambos naturales de la COLONIA"
  Carolina Oribe to the Luis Lerena who remarried in 1842 as "viudo de Dona
    Carolina"
ENTERED, EIGHT, each on the citation its citing row already carried, with no
new research behind it and every row saying so in its own note.
AND IT LEFT A SMALLER GAP BEHIND, named rather than quietly carried: five
CHILDREN stand on those same rows with no entry of their own.
290 edges, 223 of 372 people wired - 51% to 59%.

Following up the Record Atlas rows. The waypoints still cannot be recovered -

THE ATLAS ALREADY HOLDS EVERY COLLECTION THIS WORK CAME FROM. Checked

commits.subject: Seven rows for Record Atlas, and not one of them carries a waypoint

commits.subject: Two checks always read site/dist, whatever ARCHIVE_OUT said
commits.body:
The D'Arcy session found the flag-swallowing half of this fault three times in
four days — check_links.py accepted --dist and silently ignored it, grading a
stale dist while a fresh build sat untouched beside it. Neither of the two checks
here that read a built directory took a --dist flag at all, but they had the
same shape of hole from the other side: DIST was hardcoded to `site/dist`, and
neither read ARCHIVE_OUT, so a session building into its own directory would have
this pair silently grading whatever another session's build last left in
site/dist.
check-evidence.py and check-living-places.py now read ARCHIVE_OUT the way the
kit's own outdir.py does: an absolute value used as given, a relative one
resolved under site/, and site/dist only when nothing is set. Verified in three
states against a build made fresh into an isolated ARCHIVE_OUT directory: reads
it when set, falls back correctly when unset, and the numbers reported did not
change (15 records about 11 people, 1 living person named and unplaced) — this
is a wiring fix, not a data change.

commits.subject: Seventeen marriages this register writes down and cannot draw
commits.body:
Second pass at the unwired people, on the twenty whose note states a SPOUSE.
THE MATCHER RESOLVED THREE AND ONE OF THEM WAS NONSENSE. It proposed wiring
CELIDONIA B. DE LERENA as married to AMBROSIA TRAIBEL - who is a woman - by
grabbing the wrong "m." in a sentence. Her note actually says she does NOT fit
the Avelino this archive knows. Rejected on reading, which is the third time in
two days an automated match has had to be thrown away, and the reason every
edge here is read before it is written.
FOUR EDGES WERE GOOD: Eduardo Zalsamendi onto Amelia Lerena and onto his own
parents Juan Zalsamendi and Dolores Pou - all three named on the Pocitos act of
1903 - and Juana Suarez onto Mayor Joaquin Ruiz de Carvallo.
AND THE REST IS THE FINDING. SEVENTEEN of the twenty name a husband or wife who
HAS NO REGISTER ROW. Petrona Lopez, Vicenta Mercedes Fuentes, Florencia Calixta
Ramos, Antonio Medero, Rosario Moyano, Vicente Campellone, Maria Mercedes
Rozzetti, Cristobal Canale, Nicolas Benteno, Domingo Rodriguez and more. The
marriage is recorded in prose and cannot be drawn, because one end of it does
not exist as a person.
That is the same shape as FERNANDO MORATORIO THE YOUNGER, found this morning:
the archive names people it does not hold, and the tree is where that becomes
visible. Logged as a work-list row rather than bulk-added - each needs its note
read and its source named, and today has shown three times over what happens
when that step is skipped.
275 edges, 193 of 364 people wired.

commits.subject: Fernando Moratorio the younger: his parents, his wife and both his daughters were in the register and he was not
commits.body:
Working the 190 people with no tree edge, which I called the weakest part of
this archive yesterday.
FIRST, THE 190 ARE NOT ALL A DEFECT. 106 of them state no relationship at all -
a name on a census line, a godparent with no other record - and an isolated
person is not an unwired one. What is left is 41 godparents, 27 with a stated
spouse, 12 who are stated to be the PARENT of somebody, and 3 with both parents
named.
THE MATCHER WAS NOT TRUSTED THIS TIME. It resolved 6 of the 14 parent-of rows
and I read every note before wiring. One was the trap again: NICOLASA TORRES is
"mother of Fernando Moratorio", and the only Fernando Moratorio in the register
is THE ELDER - who is her HUSBAND, not her son. Wiring the match would have
made a wife into a mother of her own husband.
WHICH EXPOSED THE REAL GAP. FERNANDO MORATORIO THE YOUNGER had no register row.
His father, his mother, his wife JOSEFA LERENA TRAIBEL and both his daughters
were all in it; the man they all join through was not. The Moratorio branch had
been hanging from nothing since March. Entered, and the two 1880 baptisms are
the authority - the same plate that settled the twins.
EIGHTEEN EDGES, EVERY ONE READ BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN: the Lenguas line back two
generations to Antonio Lenguas and Juana Grandal; the Gonzalez line to Pascual
and Josefa Grandal; Justiniana and Sixta onto both their parents; AMBROSIA
TRAIBEL onto Juan Traibel and Ysabel Centeno, which is the joint the whole
Lerena Traibel branch descends through; and Lucinda Ruiz de Carvallo onto
Dominga Josefa - wired to her BIRTH-NAME row, with the pair file saying why.
253 -> 271 edges. 47% -> 51% of the register is in the tree. 175 still are not.

commits.subject: The chart work of 27 September was in commits and in nobody's work list

commits.subject: Repin 2f18c75: a gate's ok line stops reading as a verdict

checkretired now says «none of the 3 DECLARED withdrawn reading(s) is stated as

commits.subject: The spine still called a question open that was answered this morning
commits.body:
Auditing the day's work rather than assuming it. Three things were not right.
THE DESCENT SPINE ON /uruguay/ STILL SAID THE ALEJANDRO QUESTION WAS OPEN. Gen
4 of the Sancho house read "whether he is the Alejandro Maximo of the Argentine
cards is open". It is not: the Cordon act of 26 December 1877 names his parents
as Avelino and Ambrosia Traibel, and that was published on the same page hours
earlier. The ladder contradicted the section beneath it.
AND NOTHING CAUGHT IT. tools/check-spines.py - written five days ago for
exactly this failure - compares DATES against the register and cannot read
prose. It is a narrower gate than the lesson that produced it. Recorded here
rather than quietly fixed, because that gap is the useful part: a hand-written
claim in a data file is still a hand-written claim.
ANGELICA VILLADEMOROS HAD NO EDGE. Entered this morning from the 1873 Cordon
act and left out of relations.tsv, so she sat in the register with no tree
around her. check-tree.py passed because it refuses edges that join nothing -
it has nothing to say about a PERSON who joins nothing. Wired as godmother.
AND I FRAGMENTED THE ATLAS. Amalia Casas went in as "Bell Ville / San Jeronimo,
Cordoba" while her parents went in as "San Jeronimo, Cordoba", and norm_place
takes the whole field as one place name - so one locality became two. 43 places
-> 42, and the three of them now sit together.
VERIFIED: all 363 people build, every new person has a page, all five new
sections render, the two new places have pages, drift is zero and audit.py
finds nothing.

commits.subject: Nine TAB files were ranked, ready to order, and tracked nowhere

data/tab-pull-list-2026-09-22 holds nine ranked Transvaal Archives references with,

Armando and Ricardo Paul are, and the rest of MHG 1518/73 and MHG 6746/71 where

Two things reported by the Booyzen session today bear on ordering them, and both

Blocked on David, because ordering costs money and the tariff is the thing that

Row 189, and an integer, which this file could not have said of itself this morning.

commits.subject: Seven row numbers here were strings, and the gate that checks row numbers could not see it
commits.body:
Rows 178 to 184, all dated 21 September, carried their `n` as a string while the
other 181 carried an integer. The worklist gate refused duplicate row numbers by
VALUE, so "178" beside 178 would have collided with nothing — and a mixed column
is worse than a duplicate, because every consumer from now on has to defend itself
against a column that is supposed to have one type.
Found because the Booyzen session hit it from the other end: a row I wrote there
went in as a string and broke `max(r["n"] for r in rows)` in their session within
minutes. Mine was one row and careless — read with an int() coercion, written back
as a string. These seven predate today and are not mine, but this archive is
unowned and the register is its address space.
Coerced: 188 rows, one type. Kit 7c6b412 now refuses a non-integer row number, and
normalises before the duplicate test so the type-only collision cannot slip through
again.
Full build clean, 0 FAIL.

commits.subject: Australia: a zero this archive believes, and the work that earns it
commits.body:
David's Trove key was tested against every name in this family. All of them
return zero: Robert Paul Lerena, Pablo Lerena, JUAN CARLOS LERENA, Nuno, Roque.
BY ITSELF THAT MEANS NOTHING. An Argentine-Uruguayan family need never appear
in an Australian newspaper, so the zero is what you would expect whether or not
the corpus could have carried them.
SO THE CONTROL WAS CHOSEN TO ASK THE ONLY QUESTION THAT MATTERS: COULD IT?
Pablo Armando trained racehorses at the Cape, and Australian papers covered
South African racing from the 1890s onward - 11,500 hits, under headings like
"SOUTH AFRICAN RACING MATTERS - JOHANNESBURG RACING FEES" (1914). The shelf is
full and he is not on it. That makes this the OPPOSITE of the rest of
false-zeros.tsv: a null this archive believes, recorded with the work that earns
the right to believe it.
AND ONE TRAP WORTH MORE THAN THE SEARCH. "Brayley Bideford" returned two hits
and both looked like the Devon family. Neither is. TROVE INDEXES A WHOLE FAMILY
NOTICES COLUMN AS ONE ARTICLE - the 1914 Adelaide one runs to 14,464 characters
- so two terms "co-occurring" can mean only that they were set in the same
column of type on the same morning. There, "MRS. BRAYLEY, of Gladstone" is a
South Australian bereavement card and the Bideford belongs to a separate
notice, "JAMES - at Hallsannery, Bideford, N. Devon". A CO-OCCURRENCE SEARCH
AGAINST A CORPUS OF LONG COLUMNS IS NOT A CO-OCCURRENCE. Every multi-term hit
was opened before being believed.
The 177 bare "Lerena" hits are a Tasmanian schooner.
THE KEY IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY AND MUST NEVER BE: the repo is public and
everything in data/ is published. It was passed as an environment variable and
nothing more. The page says so too.

commits.subject: Finados: the first evidence from any record that Alejandro M. Lerena was dead
commits.body:
Said the next work should be opening plates rather than running searches, so
this opens one. The Bell Ville marriage of 1907, film 004484760 image 00123,
entry N 282.
"Alejandro Joaquin Lerena, de treinta y cuatro anos de edad, NATURAL DE
MONTEVIDEO, REPUBLICA ORIENTAL, domiciliado en este Curato, e hijo legitimo de
ALEJANDRO M. [LERENA] y ELISA VILLADEMORAS (FINADOS), con AMALIA CASAS, vecina
de este pueblo, hija legitima de CORNELIO CASAS y RAIMUNDA PEREDA."
FINADOS. He appeared in person at Montevideo in March 1888 to register Emilia
Alberta; by 20 June 1907 he was dead. That is the first ceiling on his death
from a record rather than a tree, and the tree's "1903" now at least sits
inside it.
THE PLATE CORRECTS THE INDEX THREE TIMES. The index gives only "1907"; the act
says 20 JUNE. The index names the parish Inmaculada Concepcion, Bell Ville; the
act says SAN JERONIMO. And the index reads the surname SERENA where the plate
has a plain L - sitting on the same opening as the scribe's own S in "San
Jeronimo". Sixth S-for-L, second in one day.
It also confirms the groom NATURAL DE MONTEVIDEO at thirty-four, which fits the
Cordon birth of 29 October 1872, and makes this a FOURTH independent statement
of his father's name with the M. - Montevideo 1872, the Cordon 1877, Cordoba
1907, Buenos Aires 1911.
TWO THINGS NOT EXPLAINED, AND RECORDED AS NOT EXPLAINED: the printed "Iglesia"
is struck through and "casa particular de la novia" written over it, and the
banns were DISPENSED. A wedding in the bride's house with the proclamations
waived is what haste or illness looks like.
Three new people: Amalia Casas and her parents. 363 people.

commits.subject: The son of the first marriage went to Cordoba
commits.body:
A third record pairs Alejandro M. Lerena with Elisa Villademoros, and this one
is Argentine. Their son ALEJANDRO JOAQUIN - christened at the Cordon in May
1873 - married AMALIA CASAS at the Inmaculada Concepcion, BELL VILLE, departa-
mento Union, CORDOBA, in 1907, and the act names his parents "Alejandro M
Lerena" and "Elisa Villademoras".
A Montevideo font in 1872, a Cordon christening in 1877 and a Cordoba marriage
in 1907 all carry the same couple and the same initial.
AND IT MAPS THE CROSSING. The children of the second marriage were born at
Montevideo, then Misiones in 1891, then Buenos Aires from 1895. The son of the
FIRST marriage is at Cordoba. This family did not emigrate once; it dispersed.
INDEX ONLY, and the row says so. Worth opening: a marriage act names the
groom's parents, his age and often his birthplace, so that plate would be a
fourth independent statement of the father's name and might finally date him -
which is the one thing still standing between this archive and the merge.
Also a fourth spelling of her surname: VILLADEMORAS, after Villademoros,
Villardemoros and Villademores.

commits.subject: The dispensation was granted: Custodio and Ema had a daughter in 1915
commits.body:
Still on FamilySearch while the session is signed in.
THE 1911 DISPENSATION HAS AN OUTCOME. This archive holds the Cura Vicario's two
kinship diagrams for CUSTODIO LERENA and EMA CARDOZO, double first cousins,
petitioning to marry, and has never known whether it was granted. Their
daughter VIOLETA BLANCA was born 29 October 1915 and christened at Trinidad the
following September. It was.
AND ONE INDEX IS NOT ANOTHER INDEX. The 33 findmypast transcripts opened this
morning gave 20 children across 14 households. A single FamilySearch search on
the same PLACE returned the children of those children - a generation
findmypast does not reach. Four households new here, a fourth Lerena woman
recorded as a mother with no father named, and a FIFTH Alejandro for
the-three-alejandros.tsv to watch.
THE MERGE TEST WAS RUN AND IT HELD. Searched for a burial of an infant
Alejandro Lerena 1846-1870, which would mean Avelino had TWO sons of that name
and would break the identification made this morning. Nothing. THE CONTROL WAS
AGAIN CHOSEN TO MATCH: Carmen Lerena's burial at the Cordon, which this archive
already holds, returns from the same search shape - so Montevideo burials of
that era ARE indexed. A null that weakly supports the merge, and is recorded as
weak.
AND THE CONTROL DISAGREED WITH US BY A YEAR. The index dates Carmen's burial
14 August 1840; this register says 1841 and read the image. Noted, not resolved.
Every row of the new sweep is INDEX ONLY and the page says so twice - the names
in it are visibly mangled, and the 1726 artefact is in there as well.

commits.subject: The control matched the era, the city and the record type, and the null held
commits.body:
Answering "is anything else needed from FamilySearch or findmypast" by testing
the top leads rather than listing them.
THE MARRIAGE OF ALEJANDRO M. LERENA AND ELISA VILLADEMOROS IS A CONTROLLED
NULL. Searched under LERENA and under SERENA - the spelling that had hidden the
1877 act naming his parents - for a marriage to a Villademoros in Uruguay:
nothing.
AND THE CONTROL WAS THE RIGHT KIND, which is new for this file. Not merely a
surname too big to return zero, but A MONTEVIDEO PARISH MARRIAGE OF THE SAME
ERA THAT THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HOLDS: Luis Lerena and Julia Juanico, 19 December
1864 at San Francisco de Asis. It returns, and it returns WITH THE GROOM'S
PARENTS ATTACHED. So the instrument reaches 1860s Montevideo marriages and
carries parents on them, and the null is about this act rather than the shelf.
Recorded as "not in the indexed corpus", not "did not happen" - their eldest
child was baptised in 1873, so a marriage exists.
ELISA'S DEATH IS NOT INDEXED EITHER, AND THAT IS EXPECTED RATHER THAN PUZZLING:
she died between September 1876 and December 1877, and Uruguay had no civil
registration until 1879. Her burial is a PARISH record, in books already on this
work list and never walked. Rows 56 and 57 now carry the fifteen-month window
and the reason, which makes them cheap and decisive instead of open-ended.
TWO THINGS CAME BACK UNASKED:
  ANGELICA MARIA LERENA VILLADEMOROS, entered here this morning from the 1872
  act, is in the civil index under her MARRIED name - "Angelica Lerma de
  Zalduando". Index only, and "Lerma" is the index's word.
  ANGELICA VILLADEMOROS married JOAQUIN REQUENA - so the 1873 Cordon godparents
  were a married couple, and the godfather this archive had as "Regusa" is
  REQUENA. Invisible while the surname was misread.
Three new work-list rows, two sharpened. 187 rows.

commits.subject: Thirty-three transcripts that had been shut for eighteen days
commits.body:
data/uruguay-baptisms-lerena.tsv has carried this header since 9 September:
"transcripts are behind findmypast's paywall and were NOT opened". David signed
in; all thirty-three opened. Every row now has the MOTHER'S SURNAME and an
EXACT BAPTISM DATE, which is the difference between a list of names and a set
of families. Thirteen were duplicate pairs, as the file suspected.
IT CONFIRMED A PREDICTION THIS ARCHIVE MADE FROM THREE SURNAMES. /uruguay/ says
the Trinidad kindred married BASQUE women - "Beloqui, Echeverry, Pelaez". The
transcripts give BELOQUI/BELOGIN, ECHEVERSE/ECHEVERSI/ECHEVERRY and PELAEZ
across five households, plus BARRAGAN and GAZO/GOSA.
AND IT PUT THE SEVEN-SPELLINGS PROBLEM ON THE MOTHERS' SIDE. Andrea is
Echeverse in 1873, Echeversi in 1875 and Echeverry in 1877 - one woman, one
parish, four years, three spellings. Adelaida is Gazo in 1874, Gosa in 1875 and
Gosso on an Argentine death record. A search under one of them misses the rest,
which is the lesson this archive keeps relearning and had only ever applied to
LERENA itself.
FOUR NEW HOUSEHOLDS: Manuel x Juana FERREIROZ and Manuel x Dolores ESPINDOLA -
two Manuels at Montevideo or one with two wives, NOT established - Pedro A. x
Manuela LEMOS, and Fermin x Paulina BARRAGAN.
AND THREE LERENA WOMEN AS MOTHERS AT SAN JOSE - OLEGARIA, ESTEFANIA and FELICIA
- a side of that cluster this archive has never counted, because a surname
search on the father's line cannot see them.
One more thing the set returned without being asked: Carlos Augusto Federico,
baptised 18 July 1883, father Gilberto, mother JULIA SALVANACH - the woman this
archive discovered was missing from its own register four days ago.
TIER: an index of an index. No image was opened, and the file says so.

commits.subject: Alejandro M. Lerena is a son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel
commits.body:
The question this archive has carried since 14 September, and which
data/the-three-alejandros.tsv called "the whole obstacle", is answered.
THE CORDON ACT OF 26 DECEMBER 1877, film 007713388 image 02455:
  "hija legitima de D. ALEJANDRO M. LERENA y de D.a ELISA [VILLADEMOROS]
  (hoy finada), orientales. ABUELOS PATERNOS D. AVELINO y D.a AMBROSIA
  TRAIBEL, maternos D. PEDRO y D.a ANGELICA MENDEZ."
So the Alejandro M. Lerena of army drawer Cajon 985 is a LERENA TRAIBEL, a
grandson of Sancho Llerena, and a brother of Josefa, Alberto, Alfredo
Justiniano and Ana Rosario. The Argentine cards and the Montevideo house are
one family.
THE ROUTE MATTERS MORE THAN THE ANSWER. It was not found by searching for his
parents - that had been tried for thirteen days. It was found by searching for
his FIRST WIFE, because he is "viudo" on both acts of 1886 and 1888 and one had
to exist. And the record is indexed under "Alejandro M. SERENA", with the
grandmother as "Ambrosia TRECIBEL". A search under LERENA would never have
returned it; the S-for-L this archive has now met five times was standing
between it and its own answer.
AND THE WIDOWHOOD IS DATED. Elisa Villademoros is "hoy finada" on 26 December
1877 and her daughter was born 19 September 1876. She died inside those fifteen
months.
WHAT IS LEFT IS A MERGE, NOT A QUESTION. This register still holds ALEJANDRO
LERENA TRAIBEL, baptised at La Mauricia 7 January 1846 - same couple, same
forename, and a birth window that overlaps: 1843 or 1845 from the act, 1844
from his own stated ages. Almost certainly one man. NOT merged, because a merge
touches slugs, last-attested-alive, relations and CHECKED_PAIRS, and a half-done
merge is worse than an honest pair. data/_person-pairs.txt records it as a debt.
Two new people: Jacinta Mercedes Gregoria Lerena Villademoros (b. 19 Sep 1876)
and Dona Angelica Villademoros. Work-list row 85 closed. 360 people.

commits.subject: The index said 1919, the act said 1872, and the widower had a wife
commits.body:
Hunting Alejandro M. Lerena's first marriage - he is VIUDO on both Montevideo
acts of 1886 and 1888, so one must exist - and the record that answered was
hiding behind a forty-seven year indexing error.
THE INDEX DATES IT 1919. THE ACT IS 1872. The 1919 is the certificate:
"expido la presente ... en Montevideo a veintiocho de Septiembre de mil
novecientos diez y nueve", Ramon Howard, Basilica Metropolitana. This archive
already had the rule - a certified copy carries two dates and the index takes
the wrong one - and this is the widest gap it has produced. Believing the index
would have discarded the record as a man too old to be ours.
WHAT THE ACT GIVES, off film 004298263 image 03147:
  "Fueron padrinos ALEJANDRO M. LERENA y ELISA VILLADEMOROS, a quienes
  instruyo." The M. is carried by no other Alejandro in this register, and
  Elisa Villardemoros is the wife of the SEPARATE Alejandro this archive holds.
  On 22 September I declared those two DIFFERENT MEN and gave as the reason
  that one of them was A WIDOWER. That is backwards. A widower in 1886 is a man
  whose earlier wife has died; I wrote the strongest link in the evidence down
  as the objection to it. Corrected, and the pair declaration rewritten.
  THEY ARE STILL NOT MERGED. An initial and a wife is not proof. What settles
  it is her death (1873-1886) or their marriage (before Oct 1872) - and a
  marriage act names the groom's parents, which is the whole question.
AND THREE THINGS NOBODY WAS LOOKING FOR:
  AVELINO EDUARDO LERENA TRAIBEL IS ARGENTINO, and Celedonia Villademoros
  ARGENTINA - a branch of this family was Argentine-born, which is the country
  the archive's central question lives in.
  HIS PARENTS ARE ON A PARISH ACT AT LAST: "Abuelos paternos AVELINO y AMBROSIA
  TRAIBEL". That descent no longer rests on an index.
  A THIRD CHILD: Angelica Maria, born 8 April 1872.
Also read: the Cordon act of 29 May 1873, opened the same day in the hope of
grandparents. It gives none - that parish's form does not recite them - but it
calls Alejandro ORIENTAL, as the 1886 and 1888 acts do. And a third Villademoros
woman, ANGELICA, stands godmother there, which makes the sisterhood this archive
had only guessed at much harder to doubt.
359 people.

commits.subject: Repin aae576f, and record the pin so a move announces itself
commits.body:
The D'Arcy session's build printed the right pin three times while they told me it
was a different one. The line was correct and unread, because a line beginning
«ok» does not get read — so .kitpin holds the pin and the build now speaks only
when it MOVES. Committed, so a pin that shifts inside a commit about something
else also shows as a diff in a file whose only subject is the pin.
First run records and says nothing, which is why this build shows no change.
Full build clean, 0 FAIL.

commits.subject: Repin a35acb9: Evidence no longer calls an unknown value 'Family'

is 2 flagged rows under 1 name — one woman in two data files.

commits.subject: "b. -" on 163 charts: I published a placeholder as a date and my own check said 357 of 357
commits.body:
The lifespan I added in 49c99fd treated «-» as a value. This register writes «-»
for «not known» on 166 of its 357 rows, and it is truthy, so 163 charts rendered
«b. -» — a placeholder presented as a date, which is worse than the bare name it
replaced. The page's own field table has always filtered it, `v && v !== "-"`, and
I did not carry that test across.
Worse than the bug: my verification said "357 of 357 charts now show a lifespan
(was 0)" and I reported that. I had counted the PRESENCE of a dates span, not
whether it contained a date. That is the same error as grepping for a death year
and finding it in prose, which I had caught an hour earlier and written a commit
message about. Twice in one file, the second time while congratulating myself
about the first.
The honest reading, now measured on the digits and not the markup: 194 charts
state a real date, 163 render no dates span at all because nothing is known, 0
placeholders. 194 is the number that was 0.
Full build clean, 0 FAIL, check:living still 1 living person with 1 date guarded.

commits.subject: Twenty deaths this register never carried, and 357 charts that never showed a lifespan
commits.body:
I said this archive's deaths could not be joined without the name-matching this
estate refuses. That was right about the wrong file, and it hid two faults.
THE DEATHS. data/lerena-register.tsv has no death column — it is a surname
sweep, recording where each person was FOUND — and build-people.py reads only
that, person-evidence.tsv and relations.tsv. So people.json had no `died`, and
the kin gate, whose every test needs a birth and a death, skipped all 357 rows
while reporting «ok · 357 people · 0 impossible relationship(s)».
The obvious source is the wrong one. The line files hold 23 deaths —
direct-line.tsv, gen1-children.tsv, lerena-siblings-gen3.tsv, taylor-line.tsv —
and only 2 of those 23 names match a register name exactly. «Mary Septima
LERENA, née TAYLOR» against the register's «Mary Septima TAYLOR»; «Roque Luis
Armando LERENA ("Roque...")» carrying a nickname; taylor-line.tsv belonging to
another surname's line entirely. Joining those means deciding two spellings are
one person, and this archive does not do that.
data/last-attested-alive.tsv is where that reconciliation was already done BY
HAND, with the basis written beside every person. Its 356 names match 356
register names exactly. So the deaths come from there, and only where `tier` is
DEATH. The three DEATH BY rows are excluded and say why in their own text: "a
CEILING, not a date: the file year can trail the death". A ceiling published as a
death would be a fabricated date on a real person.
20 deaths, 17 of them with a register birth, so the kin gate now examines 17
people where it examined none. Two long lives surfaced at once and neither is
refused: Zelmira Carlota LERENA LARRIERA at 104, and Mauricio LERENA at 110 from
a birth the register itself writes «c.1815», which is an estimate and now visibly
carries the weight of that age.
AND NOT ONE OF THE 357 CHARTS HAD EVER SHOWN THE SUBJECT'S DATES. The adapter
passed `dates: p.dates` and people.json has no `dates` field and never had one.
Undefined does not render as a gap a reader can notice — it renders as nothing,
and looks deliberate, in every chart while five sibling archives show a lifespan.
Composed now from born and died as the register stores them, raw, because «c.1815»
must keep saying it is an estimate.
I nearly missed both. Checking whether the new deaths reached the pages, I grepped
for the death YEAR and got 20 of 20 — a false positive, because those years were
sitting in prose. The page's field table had no Died row at all. That is the fifth
time today that asking whether a string appears somewhere answered a question I
had not asked.
The living rule is applied where it currently protects nobody: Cheryl Anne LERENA
is declared in living.json with a birth date and is not in the register at all, so
no register row is hers. That is the kind of fact that stops being true quietly,
so the guard is by name. check:living still reads 1 living person, 1 date guarded,
and both living gates agree on her.
people.json gained exactly one field and lost none — 357 rows before and after,
every other value byte-identical, 0 lines removed. Full build clean, 0 FAIL.

commits.subject: Repin 7e380c2: the living line now claims only what it enforced

It said 'no living person reaches the build'. Under named-bare their names may
appear bare, which is the rule — so the line now says that instead of something
stronger.
Full build clean, 0 FAIL.

commits.subject: Repin fb64506: the kin line now states how many people carry no year at all

Between 29% and 64% across the estate, and never stated in any build before.

commits.subject: Repin to the kin gate that says how many people it examined
commits.body:
Kit 9a1be6f. The kin gate's ok line now names what it EXAMINED rather than what
it was handed, because those are different numbers and only one of them is
evidence. Here that is 0 of 357.
AND THIS ARCHIVE'S KIN GATE HAS BEEN VACUOUS SINCE IT WAS WRITTEN. people.json
carries no `died` field at all — deaths live in 1999-deaths-tested.json,
death-notices-read.json and last-attested-alive.json — so every test needed a
date this register does not hold, all 357 rows were skipped, and the gate printed
«ok · 357 people · 0 impossible relationship(s)». It now declines and says so,
and exits 0, because the absence is legitimate and a permanently red build over
it would be noise.
What it does NOT do is join those death files into the register. That is an
identity match across files, which is the one thing this archive refuses to do
casually, and it is the outstanding work this finding creates rather than closes.
Full build clean, 0 FAIL.

commits.subject: 195 of 358 people had no chart, and the working log still called Florinda Florencia
commits.body:
TWO THINGS, and the second was found only because the first made me build this
archive and read what a gate said.
195 of 358 person pages drew no family chart at all — the worst coverage of the
seven archives. A page that draws nothing tells a reader this archive knows
nobody about that person, which is a claim, and a false one. This archive already
has the true word for the condition, in `status`: unplaced, excluded, of
interest. So the chart draws for everybody now, via the kit's `always`, and the
caption says which. 357 charts, of which 181 unplaced, 8 excluded, 6 connected
and kinless.
The excluded eight matter most, because for them an empty chart is the FINDING
and not a gap. Lola LERENA is Italian-born and the name is coincidental.
Catherine BUYS is a false positive where Lerena is a given name. Antonio LARENA
of Cayasta is retracted. Their pages now say nothing is drawn and that this is
the conclusion, with the reason at the top of the page where it already was.
The caption does not repeat the note, because the note is already the page dek
and it carries the real reasoning — "Widow; kin of Gilberto (1854), probably
sister or sister-in-law" — which is the kind of held-but-unproven reading that
belongs in prose and not in a line between two people. The three keys are
suppressed on an empty chart: a legend for line, register and tree implies the
chart is using them.
AND THE BUILD WAS ALREADY RED, before I touched it. check:corrections failed on
two rows of the 1911 dispensation working log still asserting FLORENCIA CARDOZO,
a reading this archive retracted on 21 September. I proved it predated my change
by stashing mine and running the gate again.
The fix is not to quote it. The quote would preserve a misreading as if the
folio said it. The folio says FLORINDA, twice, in two diagrams in the priest's
own hand on film 007713362 image 02473 — and this very file sets that out at its
foot, in its own words: "the machine transcript gave FLORENCIA and five register
rows carried it for a week". Those five rows were fixed at the time. This working
log was the one place the old reading survived, in the two cells under a column
headed "the diagram says". They now say what the diagram says.
Full build clean, 0 FAIL: 357 people, 242 edges joining 172 people, 1 living
person named with 1 place withheld and both living gates agreeing on her, links
anchors search and sitemap clean.

commits.subject: A relationship no chart should draw, gated
commits.body:
The Defranceski archive drew Ivan Defranceski — born 1943, dead in 1945
aged two — with a wife and a son. Nothing was guessed: the test for whether
somebody was a parent in a household asked only that the household began
twelve to sixty years after their birth, and 1948 sits in that window for a
boy born in 1943. He was three years dead, and only a death date could have
refused it. That one is fixed in that archive's generator; this is the rule,
so no merge can reintroduce it here.
  check:kin   a spouse or child on somebody dead before fifteen; and dates
              that cannot both be true, a death before a birth. A life past
              110 is reported and never refused — people do live that long.
WIRED AT THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN COUNT, which is the ratchet: nothing must be
corrected today, and the next one is stopped. A finding the ratchet is
holding prints as «held» rather than «FAIL», because a check that alarms on
the healthy case is not a check anybody runs — it is noise they scroll past,
which this estate established twice over today.
Proved by planting a child dead at three carrying a spouse: the gate names
the person, refuses, and exits 1; removed, it passes and exits 0. Checked by
the exit code and not by grepping the output for a word, which is the fault
that let a broken gate ship this week.
Kit repinned to 8ec58e6, package.json and package-lock.json together.

commits.subject: A simpler ignore rule, and a line of the 1911 dispensation
commits.body:
`.gitignore` replaces `site/dist-*/` with `dist-*/` — which matches a
private build directory at any depth rather than only under site/, so it is
the broader rule and the right one. And two lines of
data/1911-lerena-cardozo-dispensation.tsv.
NOT THIS SESSION'S WORK. Both were sitting uncommitted, and they are
committed now because uncommitted work in this estate has stopped being
safe: an iCloud resync reverted refs, emptied five object stores, removed 96
tracked files from disk and rolled 35 more back to older, smaller,
still-valid versions. This repository lost `site/src/data/person-slugs.json`
and `tools/build-people.py` — the slug ledger that stops a person's URL
moving — and got them back only because they had been pushed.

commits.subject: The kit printed a way out that could not be taken
commits.body:
Every tool in the kit honours ARCHIVE_OUT, and nothing that WRITES did.
`astro.config.mjs` had no `outDir`, so the variable redirected every reader
and no build. When `check:living` or `check:rows` refused a shared `dist`
they printed «build to a directory of your own: ARCHIVE_OUT=...» — advice
that did nothing, for four days, in the estate where two sessions colliding
in one build directory is the fault the advice exists for.
  outDir: process.env.ARCHIVE_OUT || 'dist'
THE DEFAULT MUST STAY 'dist'. .github/workflows uploads `path: site/dist`
and no workflow sets the variable, so an unset environment builds exactly
where it always did. Checked in all eight archives before touching any.
Proved both directions on a real build rather than by reading the config:
with ARCHIVE_OUT set, 795 pages into the named directory and `dist` left
untouched; with it unset, 795 pages into `dist`, which is what CI uploads.
Found by the Blazevic session, which noticed the variable was honoured by
every reader and confirmed by the Defranceski session. Two archives already
had the line — so «all of them are missing it» was itself one archive too
wide, and the six that were missing it are the six changed here.

commits.subject: Sixteen names here carry more than one person, numbered by row order
commits.body:
`build-people.py` derived a slug on every run with `seen[base] += 1`,
counted in the ROW ORDER of data/lerena-register.tsv. Sixteen name-bases
carry more than one person — three Bernabe LERENA, two Antonio LARENA, two
Felisa LERENA — so inserting a row above any of them renumbered every one
below it.
    A newcomer slugifying to `antonio-larena` inserted above them:
      old   newcomer -> antonio-larena
            Antonio LARENA (Cayasta) -> antonio-larena-2
            Antonio LARENA (Gualeguaychu, 1895 census) -> antonio-larena-3
      now   Cayasta stays antonio-larena, Gualeguaychu stays -2
This archive had not been bitten only because nobody had reordered that
file. The Blazevic archive minted the same way and six men swapped URLs with
each other between two commits in September.
site/src/data/person-slugs.json is the ledger: 357 slugs seeded from what
the site was already serving. 357 people matched, ZERO URLs moved, no field
gained or lost, and the file is byte-identical on a second run.
THE KEY IS THE NAME, AND THAT IS A COMPROMISE THE FILE STATES. All 357 name
strings here are distinct, because this register already does its person-
identification inside the name — «Bernabe LERENA (the elder, of the 1911
diagram)». So the name works as an identity today and is not a good one:
correct a name and the key moves with it. The fault is made rarer, not
removed — it now takes an edit to THAT person rather than to anybody above
them.
THE REAL FIX IS A MINTED ID COLUMN in data/lerena-register.tsv, written once
per row and never reused, after which this ledger should be rekeyed onto it
and the name demoted to a label. That is a change to this archive's central
file and belongs to whoever owns it; the ledger's own `_why` says so, so the
next reader finds the limitation rather than trusting the mechanism.
The position is the Defranceski archive's, of the same day: a page is a
person, an id is frozen, a name is an index.

commits.subject: A private build directory was committed, 1622 files of it
commits.body:
`site/dist-*/` is build output. It is regenerated by every `astro build`, it
is deployed from CI rather than from the repository, and it has no business
in git — and one of the directories in here is `dist-daviddefranceski-sess`,
a name another session invented tonight for its own private verification
build. It arrived the way three other files did today: staged by a directory
pattern over a tree holding somebody else's work.
`git rm -r --cached` only. NOTHING IS DELETED FROM THE WORKING TREE; the
build on disk is untouched and the next deploy is unaffected. What changes
is that git stops carrying it.
The `.gitignore` gains `site/dist-*/` rather than the literal name, because
the literal is what failed: `dist` was shared, the estate moved to
`dist-verify`, and two sessions collided inside that. The kit now composes a
per-session name, so the glob has to cover whatever it composes.
Removing another session's files from another session's repository is not
something to do quietly, so it is said here: this is build output, this is
the directory this session created, and the working tree is unchanged.

commits.subject: The gate that guards the living was guarding nobody
commits.body:
Asked whether the TREES and the IMAGES keep up with the research. Three
answers, and the third is the one that matters.
*** CHECK:LIVING WAS PASSING VACUOUSLY. *** The kit's own docstring calls it
"the one gate in this estate that must never be wrong". It reads
site/src/data/*.json for a living flag. This archive marks its living people in
data/*.tsv with an OMITTED-LIVING cell, and NOTHING CARRIED THAT ACROSS - so it
printed "0 flagged in the data ... no living person reaches the build" and
passed, while the archive held a living person with a birth date and a
birthplace in two TSVs.
NOTHING HAD LEAKED, and that was checked before anything was changed: her dates
appear in no built file, and her name alone is what named-bare allows. The rule
was being kept BY HAND while a green check said it was being enforced.
build-pages.py now writes src/data/living.json from the same markers, dates
only - an earlier pass swept her BIRTHPLACE in, and a living person's place has
no business in a new file, served or not. The gate reads 1 living, 1 date
guarded, and refuses a build with that date planted on a page. Proved.
And check-living-places.py now RECONCILES the two: a person here and not there
is a person the kit is not guarding; a person there and not here is a marker
this file has stopped recognising. Both fail, both are named.
THE TREE HAD FOURTEEN EDGES JOINING A NAME TO NOTHING, in two shapes that look
identical from inside either file. Six pointed at "Sofia CLAVIJO", "Celedonia
VILLADEMOROS" and "Dona Juliana GONZALEZ" while the register rows carried
qualifiers - "(wife of Pedro LLERENA)" - so half of each woman's family hung off
a row that did not exist. And JULIA SALVANACH, wife of Gilberto and mother of
seven, had no register row at all while BOTH HER PARENTS did, entered from the
act that names them as her child's grandparents. tools/check-tree.py refuses an
edge that joins a name to nothing; data/_tree-offsite.txt declares the four who
are legitimately held elsewhere. 221 edges -> 242.
TWO ROWS CLAIMED AN IMAGE AND DID NOT SAY WHICH - one of them the ENROLMENT
CARD, the most important document here. check-sources.py now refuses that too.
I did not wire the other stated parentages by hand-matching: the matcher I tried
self-matched a man to himself, made a sister into a mother, and put Custodio
under the wrong Bernabe of three. Wired only what was verified.

commits.subject: The spacing figure described four per cent of the rule it was justifying
commits.body:
This stylesheet carried, in a comment, the claim that the paragraph-spacing
rule newly spaces 211 pairs across 68 pages in seven archives. Seven
archives took the change on that number. It is wrong by about eight times.
The rule is SIXTEEN selectors — p+p, p+ul, ul+p, p+table, table+p,
p+blockquote, figure+p, details+p, .note+p, p+.note, .note+.note and the
rest. The count measured `section.blk > p + p` and stopped, so it described
one selector out of sixteen and the least-used group of the three.
Counted against the rule, on the built pages of all eight archives:
    1,780 newly spaced pairs on 1,007 of 19,283 pages
Roughly a fifth are paragraph-to-paragraph. The rest are the note, list and
table pairs, which is why the note-heavy archives move most: D'Arcy 569
pairs on 368 of its 854 pages, Blazevic 647 on 342, Mazza 248 on 227.
THE SAME MISTAKE TWICE, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. An earlier count said 7,405
by searching whole sections rather than direct children — twelve times high,
and it nearly stopped the change. This one was eight times low, and it
shipped the change on a description of itself. Both were taken against a
DESCRIPTION of the rule instead of the rule.
Found by the D'Arcy session, which measured its own build against all
sixteen selectors after calibrating its parser element-for-element against
the browser's own querySelectorAll. Its 571 and this sweep's 569 agree.
Nothing is reverted: the change is right, it is live, and 1,007 pages of
notes and lists that used to butt against the prose now breathe. Only the
number was wrong, and it is corrected where it was written rather than only
in a message.

commits.subject: Paragraphs only had air where somebody had remembered to type it
commits.body:
`p{margin:0}` in this stylesheet, and every gap between two paragraphs was
being supplied one at a time by an inline style="margin-top". Wherever that
was left off, the paragraphs ran together into a wall of words — worst at a
phone width, which is where it was reported.
Written for the Blazevic archive on 22 September and carried here once the
effect had been counted rather than assumed. Anything that FOLLOWS a
paragraph inside section.blk now gets a default gap of 1.15rem, and 1.35rem
under 620px where the lines are shorter and the reader needs more of a
landing; and the other way round, so a note, a table or a stat grid no
longer butts straight up against the prose above it.
NOTHING THAT WAS ALREADY SPACED MOVES. The inline margins are more specific
and still win. This only fills in what was never set.
AND IT REACHES LESS THAN IT LOOKS, which is the reason it was safe to carry
across seven archives at once. The selector is `section.blk > p + p` —
DIRECT children — so a paragraph inside a component's own wrapper is
untouched. Counted on the built pages of all eight: 211 pairs across 68
pages in the seven that did not have it, every one of them prose.
The first count said 7,405. It searched the whole of each section rather
than its direct children, which is twelve times the truth and would have
been the wrong reason to hesitate about a change this small. Counting the
component's internals as though the rule reached them is the same mistake as
counting a stylesheet as markup, which this session also made today.
Built and gated after the change: living, kit, rows and templates all green.

commits.subject: The floor counted three doors on a page this archive says has one
commits.body:
e2bfcce wrote this floor and its own message states the answer: the eight
spines «came out carrying five doors labelled "The Lerena Archive"», that
was fixed in the kit, and «what is left is the one that is true: Catherine
Mary Sophia Booyzen». One door. The floor recorded three, and the gate has
been holding this archive to a number its own commit contradicts.
Two faults, and they are both in the tooling rather than here.
ONE IS THE BOX. `class="sp-door` matches `class="sp-doors"` as well, the
paragraph the doors sit in, so the single door on /direct-line/ scored two.
Fixed in kit dfd61f5, and six other archives had their floors translated by
exactly their wrapper count.
THE OTHER IS THE DIRECTORY, and it is the one worth remembering. The floor
was written in the same commit that repinned the kit — so `--write-floor`
read a `dist` built before the self-door fix was installed, and recorded a
door that had just been removed. `ARCHIVE_OUT` was honoured by no tool in
the kit until today, so there was no way to point the write at the build
being made. A ratchet set from the wrong directory forgives whatever is not
there and demands whatever is; this one demanded a bug.
Checked before rewriting rather than after: /argentina/ draws eight rows and
/uruguay/ ten, and the only ring surname among all eighteen spouses is
«María Lerena», which is this archive's own and correctly suppressed.
/direct-line/ carries the Booyzen door. One is the whole of it.
Rows 22, spouses 13, places 9, grades 22 — all unchanged, all still met.

commits.subject: Kit repinned to dfd61f5, and the row floor is left alone on purpose
commits.body:
Two kit fixes land here. `ARCHIVE_OUT` is now honoured by every check that
takes a `--dist` flag — including `check:living`, which had been reading
whatever the shared `dist` happened to hold rather than the build in front
of it. And `class="sp-door` no longer matches `class="sp-doors"`, the
paragraph the doors sit in, which inflated the door count in every
`.rowfloor` in the estate by one per spine row that drew any.
THE FLOOR IS NOT TRANSLATED HERE, though it is in six other archives,
because subtracting the wrappers does not reconcile it. Something is
genuinely no longer drawn, and it belongs to this archive's own working
tree rather than to the kit. The gate is left failing and saying so, which
is what it is for.

commits.subject: A ladder on a page is a claim like any other
commits.body:
Moving the three descent spines into a TSV this morning put them where the
emphasis, raggedness and drift checks can see them. It did NOT make them agree
with the register, because nothing compared the two - which is precisely how
both of today's failures survived.
tools/check-spines.py compares them, and only what it can compare exactly: a
spine row naming a register row in its new `register` column must agree with
that row's BIRTH YEAR and with the DEATH DATE tools/last-alive.py computed from
the register's own prose. A hedge like "about 1767" is checked as a year, an
empty cell asserts nothing, and "-" means no register row and is not checked.
THE LINK IS WRITTEN OUT, NOT MATCHED. The two files do not spell people the
same way - "Avelino Lerena Fernandez" against "Avelino LERENA Fernandez (son of
Sancho)" - and a fuzzy match that silently matches nothing is worse than no
check at all. That is the lesson of the thing this gate is here to prevent.
PROVED BEFORE TRUSTED, on all three failure modes:
  - the original bug, 23 August against the register's 22nd, and the message
    names the distinction that caused it: A REGISTRATION DATE IS NOT A DEATH DATE
  - a wrong birth year, 1754 against 1767 - the tree value the census contradicts
  - a register column naming a row that does not exist
In the chain before check:sources. The build now refuses a ladder that
contradicts the register, which is the check that would have caught both of
today's published errors on the day they were typed.

commits.subject: A switchboard is content, and a heading can exist without being seen
commits.body:
audit.py is at zero findings. Three were open and none was a bug in the site.
THE TELEPHONE WAS REAL AND MEANT TO BE PUBLIC. 0342-4572893 is the switchboard
of the Registro Civil de la Provincia de Santa Fe, published on /argentina/ so
a reader can write to them too - the same reason this archive publishes the
email of every repository it asks things of, which audit.py already treats as
content. The check could not tell the two apart, so it now can: a number on a
page carrying a declared letter errand is a repository switchboard; a number
anywhere else is still the finding the check exists for.
VERIFIED BEFORE TRUSTED, because an exemption that exempts everything is worse
than no check. Only /argentina/ carries the marker, and the same number planted
on /uruguay/ still fails.
THE HEADING SKIPS WERE h1 -> h3 ON /errands/ AND /photograph-these/, where the
group titles are drawn as labelled Rules rather than headings. The kit already
has the answer and says so in its own stylesheet: .vh, "a heading that exists
for structure and linking but is not shown, because the section already carries
a labelled rule above it". Nothing moves on the page; the document stops
jumping a level.

commits.subject: A structure built out of a sample of eleven, and the Pablo who is not ours
commits.body:
The Rosario confirmations reached no page at all - not one span of that file -
and they are the register where the central question could have been answered.
WHY IT MATTERS: A CONFIRMATION ACT NAMES THE PARENTS. Pablo Armando was born
February 1882; the children confirmed at Rosario in March 1890 are six to
fifteen, so he is squarely in range. The register had been listed UNTRIED since
this archive's first week and had no film number until 13 September.
IT CANNOT BE SKIMMED. Every entry gives a given name, an age and the parents,
and THE SURNAME IS NEVER WRITTEN - it has to be read out of the father's name.
Unlike the baptism registers, this one cannot be scanned down a margin.
The 26 March 1890 sitting runs to at least 243 children and holds NO LERENA.
There is a Pablo, aged eleven - son of Manuel Cobos and Mercedes Alvarez.
Published because that is exactly the hit a future reader will find and have to
spend an hour excluding.
AND THE MORE USEFUL HALF IS THE MISTAKE. From the first eleven entries this
archive concluded the confirmations were taken sex by sex and that "a boy of
eight would be in a separate run of pages, and that is where to look for him".
Entries 133, 135 and 138 are boys mixed straight in among the girls. A
structure built out of a sample of eleven, which would have sent the next
reader hunting a run of pages that does not exist.
UNPUBLISHED RESEARCH: 56 -> 15. Thirty-seven declared in
_published-elsewhere.txt after opening each page, none rejected by the tool's
own check; four gaps written to /method/, /uruguay/, /taylor/ and /searched/.
The fifteen that remain are what the tool's docstring says a working log is
allowed to hold - film-reading technique, file-maintenance notes, a reminder to
check browsable images when the block lifts, and one honest NOT CERTAIN.

commits.subject: The only Cordoba in the corpus is in Mexico, and Northam is in Devon
commits.body:
Second pass on the unpublished research: 40 -> 23. Fourteen more declared in
_published-elsewhere.txt after opening the page, and four genuine gaps written.
THE CORDOBA CONTROL, RUN FORWARDS FOR ONCE. A parent-pair query on Felix
Llerena and Rosalia Aguilar returned zero from Spain, on a page that rendered
and reported a count, so not a block. The control was run BEFORE the null was
believed: search "ciudad de Cordova" and read the COLLECTION names. They are
Nobility Records - Granada and Ecija - Madrid notarial protocols, and Orders of
Chivalry induction files. THE ONLY CORDOBA IN THE WHOLE CORPUS IS CORDOBA,
VERACRUZ, IN MEXICO. The Andalusian full-text index holds nobility and notarial
records and no parish registers, so an eighteenth-century Cordoba baptism is not
in the corpus being searched. The zero means "not findable by this instrument".
AND THE TIER ON FOURTEEN ATTACHED RECORDS. They are attached to Sancho in the
tree by a tree user who decided they are one man; the acts have not been read
here. One was opened and it is a proof of nobility of 1599 from Alcantara,
Caceres. A record can be genuine and attached to the wrong man - the attachment
is the claim, not the document.
NORTHAM IS IN DEVON. The 1921 census transcribes Lucy Elizabeth Sweet's
birthplace as "NORTHAM, NORTHAMPTONSHIRE". It is two miles from Bideford and it
is where this family comes from; the transcriber met a place name that starts
like a county and finished the thought. The second birthplace error in one
census, and a search trap either way: filter on Northamptonshire and you collect
her, filter on Devon and you lose her.
AND THE COUNT OF SANCHO'S CHILDREN, which has moved twice. A file once called
complete held four; the reconciled list names eight. The padron returns six, and
that is not a contradiction - two came after it, and Jose Loreto is in no tree
and no census, found only because the surname was searched as LORENA.
Checked before trusting: every allowlist fragment silences exactly one span in
its own file, and the tool rejected none of the thirty-one claims.

commits.subject: Six trees agreeing is one source copied, and sixteen of the fifty-six were already published
commits.body:
THE 56 UNPUBLISHED FINDINGS WERE NOT 56. unpublished.py matches a claim by its
three rarest words co-occurring on a page, so a finding restated in other words
reads as unseen. Seventeen of them were checked by opening the page and are now
declared in data/_published-elsewhere.txt, which makes each one a claim the
tool re-checks on every run rather than a silence. None of the seventeen was
bogus. 56 -> 40.
WHAT WAS GENUINELY MISSING WENT ONTO /method/, and it is one argument in four
parts:
  COPIES ARE NOT CORROBORATION. Six FamilySearch trees give Sancho the same
  parents - antoniojosed, rosanaic, jfina, nanabal, ladissosa, abal2018 - and
  they descend from one published account, one of them carrying that work's
  acknowledgement surname in its own user name. The archive had already learned
  this from a parish book: the three "Francisco" entries of 7 January 1846 that
  looked like three witnesses were one clerk, one page, one morning.
  WHERE A CENSUS MEETS A RECONSTRUCTION, THE CENSUS WINS. The trees split by
  thirteen years on Sancho's birth. The padron of 1812 records him as 45, which
  is 1767. The rival 1754 is what you get assuming a marriage in 1753 and a
  child the year after - so that tree's "about 1753" marriage is an estimate
  derived from a guessed birth, not a record of an act.
  WHICH DISSOLVES A COINCIDENCE. A Lerena marrying an Aguilar at Cordoba in
  1753, a year before Granada 1754, looked real for an hour. It is not a
  coincidence because the 1753 is not a date from a document.
  AND THE CONVERSE: when an index disagrees with itself the way the acts do,
  the disagreement is in the registers. Dominga Josefa's husband is Ruiz or
  Rodriguez de Carvallo in two acts, and FamilySearch's index splits the same
  way. An index that reproduces a disagreement did not invent it.
ALSO PUBLISHED: what an informacion matrimonial actually contains - the
groom's parents, his birthplace and his years in the country, every one of the
three things this archive cannot establish for Sancho, which is why its absence
is the expensive one. And that the gap where it should be is not quite final:
the volume's filming card says HOJAS SUELTAS, loose leaves, so its order is
whoever filed it and not the calendar.

commits.subject: Juana's name was in a data file, and a data file is not a reader
commits.body:
Five findings the register emphasised in its own data reached no page. Four of
them were one household, and two were people this family held in slavery.
THE PADRON OF 1812 COUNTED FOUR ENSLAVED PEOPLE IN SANCHO'S HOUSE AND NAMED
NONE OF THEM. Six weeks later the Montevideo Catedral named one: "hija de
JUANA, negra esclava de D.n Sancho Lerena y de D.a Maria Fernandez", and her
daughter MARIA MERCEDES, born 24 September 1812, baptised at two days old.
That plate was opened for one reason, and the register says it plainly: a
machine is worst at proper nouns, and this woman's name is the only thing any
record gives her. It is JUANA, in the priest's hand. It has now been said
somewhere a reader can find it.
The same opening carries a trap - another Maria Mercedes the day before,
daughter of TERESA ABELLEYRA, enslaved in the ABELLEYRA household - and this
register holds a Teresa in Sancho's house from the padron. Different women,
different documents, and the page says so.
ALSO PUBLISHED: that the family were "vecinos de esta Villa" at Canelones in
1806 and had moved to calle San Juan No 60 by 1812, so they LIVED there for
at least eleven years; that Agustina Ramona's godfather was DON FIDEL REY of
Montevideo, which is where her younger brother got a forename appearing
nowhere else in this family - an inference from a pattern, not a record; and
that it bears not at all on whether the Fidel who married Maria Ruedas is
Sancho's son.
drift.py now reports ZERO findings that no page makes, from five this morning
and six yesterday.

commits.subject: The ladder said 23 August because the tree did, and the sources page had stopped listing sources
commits.body:
THREE THINGS THIS AUDIT FOUND, and the first two were published errors.
AVELINO DIED ON THE 22nd. The descent spine on /uruguay/ said "23 August 1890,
La Paz, Canelones". His register row, last-attested-alive.tsv,
1852-aguada-union-certificates.tsv and alberto-lerena-larriera.tsv all say
22 August 1890 at MONTEVIDEO, registered the next day - and the 23rd is the
REGISTRATION date. Both wrong values trace to one row of
montevideo-lerena-trunk.tsv, a tree file whose own header says "no row here
may be cited as fact". The page cited it as fact.
The same row called Avelino "the seventh of eight children". He is the EIGHTH
of eight - 1793, 1795, 1799, 1800, 1804, 1806, 1811, 1815 - or the seventh of
seven without Fidel, who is attested only at second hand. No count makes
"seventh of eight" right.
BOTH SURVIVED BECAUSE THE LADDER WAS TYPED INTO THE TEMPLATE. check-inline.py
had been reporting all three spines for days as "reachable only by editing the
page" and nothing gated them, so a tree value could be published and no check
would ever see it. All three now come from data/descent-spines.tsv. That is
the second hand-written-descent failure in two days; the first was
"Alejandro Maximo (1839-1903)", corrected this morning one row below.
AND THE SOURCES PAGE HAD FALLEN BEHIND AGAIN. Twenty-one of the twenty-two
films the register cites as IMAGE READ were absent from sources-consulted.tsv
- two full days of plate reading - under a page headed "Everything consulted
so far". Its own header warned about exactly this and said it could not happen
again, because the page is generated from the file.
THE SAFEGUARD WAS AIMED AT THE WRONG GAP. Generation guarantees the PAGE
matches the FILE. Nothing guaranteed the FILE matched the WORK, and that is
the join that broke, twice. tools/check-sources.py now walks the other way -
register to sources - and is in the build chain. Verified failing before it
was trusted.
142 sources, 21 added with what each plate actually proved.

commits.subject: The wrapper was the one pulling Node 20 in, not the action named
commits.body:
Every run warned that checkout@v4, configure-pages@v5, setup-node@v4 and
upload-artifact@v4 target Node 20 and are being forced onto Node 24. The
workflow never named upload-artifact; upload-pages-artifact@v3 pins it
internally, so bumping the wrapper is the only way to move it - and
upload-pages-artifact@v4 does NOT help, because it still pins
upload-artifact@v4.6.2. v5 is the first that carries v7. deploy-pages@v4
went too: it is node20 as well, and would have kept warning once the rest
was quiet.
Checked each bump against this workflow rather than assuming latest is
safe:
  checkout v7 blocks fork-PR checkout under pull_request_target and
  workflow_run. This workflow runs on push to main and workflow_dispatch,
  so neither path exists here.
  setup-node v5 turned on automatic package-manager caching. v6 narrowed
  it to npm, and only when package.json declares packageManager or
  devEngines.packageManager. site/package.json declares neither, so no
  cache step appears where there was none before.
  upload-pages-artifact v4 stopped including dotfiles. site/dist has 0
  hidden entries out of 811 files, so the v5 default of
  include-hidden-files: false ships the same artifact v3 did.
  configure-pages v6 and deploy-pages v5 are node24 rebuilds only.
Local gate green: ALL GATES PASSED.

commits.subject: Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen had a page all along, in the next archive
commits.body:
An audit on 22 September counted the names drawn on this archive's
person pages that carry no link — because that is what a reader sees:
two names side by side, one clickable and one not, for no reason they
can see. Eight names here, 14 occurrences across 356 person pages.
Seven of the eight are published nowhere in this estate. Those need this
archive to publish them, which is not a decision a component makes and
not one I am making.
The eighth is Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen, who married Nuno Fernando
Lerena. She is on the Booyzen archive's own spine at generation two and
has had a page there the whole time. This chart drew her as plain text
beside her linked husband. She is now a link to it.
WRITTEN OUT BY HAND, ONE NAME, MATCHED ON THAT NAME. This estate refuses
to match people by name when deriving links, and that refusal is right:
it carries two Raffaele Falcos and two Petrus Jacobus Booysens, and a
derived name match merges them. Nothing is derived here. This is the
archive stating a join it knows, the way D'Arcy states the marriages of
its two living generations, and the Booyzen slug was checked live before
the line was written. The base URL comes from the ring, so a site that
moves does not strand it.
Two mistakes worth recording. The ring is an object with a `note` and an
`archives` array, not an array — which is why the kit's own helpers
unwrap it — and indexing it directly failed the build. Then the href
edit silently did not apply, because the file indents two spaces and I
matched four; the build went green and the link was simply absent. I had
not asserted on that replacement. The second attempt asserts on both.
Full chain green, 795 pages.

commits.subject: Eight spines, and the archive was linking to itself
commits.body:
This archive draws more lines of descent than any other in the estate —
one on /direct-line/, four on /argentina/, three on /uruguay/ — and it
was several kit versions behind, so none of them had the off-page
connectors and none was covered by the gate that watches what a row
shows.
Repinning found a fault in the kit rather than here. `archiveKey` was
documented as required before the ring is consulted and was not enforced,
so an archive that passed none was compared against every site in the
estate including itself: these pages came out carrying five doors
labelled "The Lerena Archive". Fixed in the kit — no key, no ring — and
all eight spines now pass `archiveKey="lerena"`.
What is left is the one that is true: Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen, who
married Nuno Fernando Lerena, doors to the Booyzen archive.
The rows were read before and after the repin to be sure the kit's new
reading rule left them alone. All three pages were already oldest-first
and none was reversed.
check:rows is in the chain with a floor of 22 rows, 13 spouses, 9
places, 22 grades, 3 doors. That gate is also why the self-doors were
found at all: it reported eighteen doors on an archive that should have
had one, and eighteen was worth looking at.
Repin to archive-kit fd1621e.

commits.subject: The pin and its lockfile, committed as the pair they are
commits.body:
Two changes, both left uncommitted by an estate-wide sweep, and committed
together because separating them is the actual hazard.
  the kit pin moves 9ff6320 to 40bf5a3
  check:inline joins the build chain, at this archive's own count
WHY THE PAIR MATTERS AND NOT JUST THE TIDINESS. CI runs `npm ci || npm
install`, and npm ci installs from the LOCKFILE, not from package.json.
Staging package.json alone therefore ships a build that fetches the OLD kit
and then fails on check:pin — which is the gate doing its job, from a fault
committed one file at a time. The Booyzen session did exactly that an hour
ago, went red, and measured the rest of the estate rather than just fixing
its own: seven archives were sitting on an armed pair, this one among them.
The trap was mine. I repinned eight archives in a sweep and left the pairs
unstaged in seven, so the first session in each to stage package.json for
any reason of its own would have shipped the mismatch.
check:pin was right and silent about this, and the reason is worth keeping:
it compares build scripts against the INSTALLED kit, and every machine here
had the new one. It was correct about this machine and had nothing to say
about the runner. That gap is precisely what the lockfile encodes.

commits.subject: He said forty-two, then forty-three, and the tree said eighteen thirty-nine
commits.body:
Row 85 asked whether Avelino's eldest son is the Alejandro M. Lerena of army
drawer Cajon 985. It has answered "inconclusive" since 14 September, on a
six-year gap. The gap was never there.
The premise was also stale. the-three-alejandros.tsv still named Luis Lerena
and Justiniana Lenguas as the first man's parents - they are his GODPARENTS,
and the register said so on 14 September. Register row 180 even closed with
"the candidate pool has changed and the table needs re-reading". Nobody
re-read it. The file is rewritten, and it now reaches a page.
TWO MONTEVIDEO BIRTH ACTS, film 004596830 images 01806 and 02145. He stood in
front of the officer twice and gave his age: "de cuarenta y dos anos de edad,
viudo, escribano, oriental" on 6 November 1886, and "de 43 anos de edad de
estado viudo" on 16 March 1888. Sixteen months apart and consistent. His birth
falls between 17 March and 6 November 1844.
THE 1839 HAD NO RECORD BEHIND IT. It was graded PRIMARY (indexed) against the
Capital Federal parish records. All four were opened; every one leaves the
father's age blank while giving the mother's. It came from tree PID KZ2N-84J
and was re-graded on the way in - and this site printed it in the descent
spine as a plain fact. Corrected there, in cajon-985-origins.tsv, in
montevideo-lerena-trunk.tsv, and on /corrections/.
So the gap is one year, not six, and it still cannot choose: the stated ages
miss 1843 and 1845 by one year in OPPOSITE directions. Not merged.
AND ONE ROW WAS TWO MEN. The bare "Hector Lerena" who married Amalia Pacheco
is Hector Narciso, born Montevideo 1886. His 1911 San Carlos marriage act was
opened - "hijo legitimo de D. Alejandro Maximo ... y de dona Julia Ba[ssani]
... con dona Amalia Pa[checo]", groom "de la Rep. Oriental, de veinte y
cuatro". Wife, parents and age agree at once. Merged, and the index's "born
1887 at Almagro" corrected: the act says Oriental.
The 1888 act is a printed form whose ruled line reads "Que es nieta por linea
paterna de ______". It is blank. The form asked this archive's question and
nobody wrote the answer on it.
What is left is specific: he is a WIDOWER in 1886, so there is an earlier
Montevideo marriage - and a marriage act names the groom's parents.
356 people. Julia Bassani is italiana in 1886 and austriaca in 1888; both are
recorded, and neither is picked.

commits.subject: Two fields matching five and seven figures cannot intersect at nothing
commits.body:
Row 28 is closed, and getting there found a seventeenth false zero.
Sancho with Maria in Uruguay returned 0 - read twice, with the Gonzalez
control returning 479,660 minutes earlier. This time the service was
healthy and the query shape was broken:
  father given name Sancho, alone        10,315
  mother given name Maria, alone      1,228,708
  both together                               0
  both, plus the two surnames                 6
Maria is the commonest name a mother has in Uruguay. Those numbers cannot
intersect at zero. A parent-pair query with GIVEN NAMES ONLY returns zero
whatever the truth is, so at least one parent surname must be supplied
before a null from that shape means anything. Every earlier zero here
drawn from given names alone is void; every one drawn with a surname
stands, which is all of the ones this archive published.
Arithmetic caught it again - the only guard on the method page that has
never failed. It works because it asks whether an answer is POSSIBLE
rather than whether it is plausible.
And with surnames the query answers row 28 properly. Six records naming
Sancho Llerena and Maria Fernandez as parents, and this archive already
held all six: Luis Escolastico's baptism of 1811, Justa Pastora as bride
in 1830, Dominga Josefa's christening of 1804, and three entries where a
child appears as a parent on somebody else's act - two of them spelling
the father LERENA where the first spells him LLERENA.
So the keyed index contributes nothing this archive is missing. The
children it cannot reach - Juan Agustin, Pedro Antonio, Agustina Ramona,
Fidel, Jose Loreto - are known from the padron and from full text, and
their baptisms are not keyed. The list is as complete as this instrument
can make it, and what remains is register-walking, not searching.

commits.subject: Pages refused in writing, after reading them, and the ratchet tightened to match
commits.body:
More of the estate's shared page NAMES turn out to be shared names and not
shared pages, and the refusals are recorded on the line where checkpages
prints them on every run.
  who/[slug] is three different pages across the estate. Three archives use
  it for NAMESAKES and draw the kit's component. Falco uses it for a page
  per NAME OVER RECORDS, and its own header says why it cannot be a page
  per person: the roster's 10,432 rows carry 4,820 distinct names, and
  "Pasquale Falco" alone names seventy-nine records across sixty years and
  is certainly several men. D'Arcy uses it for a PERSON DOSSIER. One path,
  three arguments.
  places/[slug] is two. Four archives index what the atlas holds in a place
  and now share a component for it. Defranceski's is an encyclopaedia entry
  — the name in four languages, parish, diocese, population by year,
  register holdings, the 1945 census, the plates. Lerena's is a table of
  everyone of the surname recorded there, and the nationality column is how
  it tells two Llerena households apart.
  open-questions at Lerena is prose, and the kit's Questions component says
  itself that prose "cannot use this until somebody extracts them, and that
  extraction is research work belonging to each archive". Question 1 alone
  runs a hundred lines and turns on which of two readings of a clerk's
  phrase is right. Deciding which sentence is what-has-been-tried and which
  is what-would-settle-it is a judgement for whoever did the work.
A shared page name is not a shared page, and the only way to tell is to
read them. The threshold finds candidates; it has never decided anything.

commits.subject: Ratchet down one: the sources page is off the backlog
commits.body:
Every archive in the estate now draws its sources page with the shared
component, and this archive's count comes down to match. The page that
started this work is the first shared idea in the estate to reach all eight.

commits.subject: 121 sources to the kit, the tier read as the two fields it actually is, and the gap said out loud
commits.body:
Three things, and the second is the one that was hiding.
THE TABLE became the kit's source rows. 121 of them, each with what it was
used for and when it was accessed.
THE TIER HOLDS TWO FACTS IN ONE STRING. There are three tiers and
twenty-six distinct values, because a qualifier has been concatenated onto
the tier with a dash — "PRIMARY - full-text transcript read", "SECONDARY -
a negative result, controlled". Printed whole, as the chip did, it says
something true and cannot be counted, filtered, or compared with any other
archive's grading. The tier now groups the rows and the qualifier rides
beside each as a tag, which is what that slot exists for.
THE DATA FILE IS UNCHANGED and the page says so. Separating the column
belongs in data/sources-consulted.tsv; this only stops the page presenting
a compound value as though it were an atom.
Splitting on the dash was not enough, and the built page showed it. Two of
the 121 name TWO tiers at once — "SECONDARY for the marriage index; PRIMARY
for the Madrid and Cordoba full-text" — which is a true statement about one
source doing two jobs and is not a grade. Treated naively they became a
group of one each, and the page showed five tiers where there are three.
They are kept together under a heading that says what they are.
AND THE GAP IS ON THE PAGE NOW. 38 of the 121 say where they are and 83 do
not — the largest such gap in this estate. It is stated here rather than
left in a report, so that it shrinks.

commits.subject: The harmonisation backlog was overstated, and a wrapper over the kit is the kit
commits.body:
checkpages counted a page as harmonised only when the kit import appeared in
the page itself. A page that draws a shared component through a small local
wrapper — the wrapper holding this archive's own lookup and handing rows to
the kit — was reported as hand-drawn.
That wrapper is not a failure to harmonise. It is the shape harmonisation is
meant to leave behind: the kit draws the thing and each archive keeps only
what it alone can say about it. checkshared has said exactly that about
components since September; the page check simply did not look.
Following one level of local import takes the estate from 50 bespoke pages
to 32. Ratchet corrected here to the real number.
Overstating a backlog is not the harmless direction to be wrong in. It sends
somebody to convert a page that is already right, and the obvious way to do
that would be to delete the wrapper and inline the lookup — undoing the
harmonisation to satisfy the harmonisation check.

commits.subject: dna exempted after reading all six, and the ratchet tightened to match
commits.body:
Six archives have a dna page and none of them is drawing the same object.
All six were read before any of this was written down.
  Booyzen has two kits and no ethnicity estimate at all — it is a cousinhood
  and an aunt whose chart is the purest in the family. D'Arcy has no test to
  report and its one heading is "What would actually be evidence". Falco is
  a side-by-side COMPARISON of two people across the groups they share, not
  a distribution. Defranceski's bars ARE a distribution, one per person.
  Lerena's subject is two companies disagreeing about the same saliva.
  Luwinski's is the only one where the DNA overturns the paper record.
Even the object that looked shared is not one: an admixture chart comparing
two people answers a different question from an admixture chart describing
one, and flattening them would produce a figure that is neither.
So it is refused in .harmonise-exempt with a reason per archive, where
checkpages prints it on every run, rather than converted or left looking
like backlog. Reading the candidates is the work; the threshold only finds
them.

commits.subject: check:pin, first in the chain, for the failure nobody saw for five hours
commits.body:
Today's quieter CI breakage:
    python3: can't open file '.../kit/tools/checksources.py': No such file
A gate was wired into this build while the kit pin still named a commit from
before that gate existed. It passed locally, because the working copy of
node_modules had been installed by hand from a newer sha. CI installs from
the committed pin and found nothing there.
Nothing was wrong with the script, the package.json or the pin on their own.
They only disagree once somebody else installs them — which is to say, never
on the machine that could have noticed.
check:pin verifies that every kit file a build script names is present, and
that THE LOCKFILE RESOLVED THE COMMIT PACKAGE.JSON PINS. It runs first,
because it guards every kit tool the rest of the chain calls. Both faults
were reproduced on a throwaway copy before it was believed.
The pin was moved before this script was added, in that order and in this
one commit, which is the discipline the check now enforces on everyone else.

commits.subject: Repin: check:pages was failing every deploy, because CI has one repository
commits.body:
check:pages compares this archive's pages against the other archives'. A
GitHub Actions runner checks out ONE repository, so the estate it needs is
not there, and the version wired in an hour ago read that as a failure and
returned 1. Every archive it had been added to stopped deploying at once.
Local builds had all passed. They would: locally the estate is always there.
