-rf before build, so a previously failed build can never poison the next.

commits.subject: RootsChat: nobody is researching Lerena, and five people are on the Taylors
commits.body:
The forum search is login-only - "You are not allowed to search for posts in
this forum" - and this assistant does not create accounts. A limit on the
method, not a finding about the family.
But the Surname Interests Table is public, and answers a better question
than the boards could: who else is working on this family right now.
LERENA: ZERO ENTRIES. Nobody on RootsChat is researching the surname - a
clean null against a control of 603 Taylors. It matches WikiTree, which
holds no Lerena profile either. This family has no British research
community at all, which is itself worth knowing.
FIVE CONTACTS OVERLAP THE TAYLOR SIDE, and one is exact:
 "Welsh Jen"      TAYLOR  Bideford, Devon
 "Muddy Waters"    DALLING  Swimbridge / Landkey / Barnstaple
 "Burnell"       BRAYLEY  Somerset & Devon
 "kingsgate"      NORRISH  Devon
 "natcole", "Jean.Y"  SWEET   Plymouth
Welsh Jen is on the exact registration district of William Taylor, Mary Ann
Helena Brayley and seven of their ten children. Muddy Waters is worth a
second look: FamilySearch carries a WILLIE DALLING marrying a SUSIE TAYLOR
at Swimbridge in 1905 - a second Dalling-Taylor marriage in north Devon,
five years after Henry Dalling married Isabella Temple at Northam. Susie is
not one of the ten, and whether the Dallings are kin is untested.
Messaging needs an account and two forum posts, so it is logged as David's
errand rather than left as a suggestion - with the note that this archive
has a great deal to OFFER such a person, which is the right way round for a
first message.
AND verify.sh EARNED ITSELF ON ITS FIRST REAL RUN. It refused this commit
twice: once for an unpaired marker, then for literal reaching the
errands page - and chasing that exposed a malformed row that had put a
whole paragraph into the STATUS column, which is a controlled vocabulary.
Three errands were being published under the wrong chip, including one
marked DONE that the page was calling blocked. A field can be internally
consistent and still be the wrong field.

commits.subject: A pipe into tail swallowed every exit code today
commits.body:
Every verification in this session ran as
    python3 tools/consistency.py | tail -1
and a pipeline exits with the status of its LAST command. tail always
succeeds. So consistency.py's exit code gated nothing for an entire day,
and the commits chained behind it with && could never have been stopped by
a hard contradiction.
It finally showed. An unpaired emphasis marker went into errands.tsv while
the checker was printing CONTRADICTION on screen - the output was right
there and had simply scrolled past.
Fixed the marker, and fixed the calling. tools/verify.sh now runs all five
gates as one script under set -e with no pipes: build the data, check the
register against itself, build the site, check the links, check for drift.
It prints ALL GATES PASSED or it fails.
The lesson is this archive's own, arriving somewhere new. A guard that
cannot fail is not a guard - and this time the guard was sound and the way
it was CALLED was broken. Three times today I hardened a checker; none of
that mattered while its exit code was being thrown away.

commits.subject: Santa Rosa de Lima: 57 of 141, paused on a hardening rate limit
commits.body:
Three more read on the retries - images 7, 54 and 60, all clean. That takes
the second Rosario parish to fifty-seven images with no Lerena under any of
seven spellings.
Still not read: 22, 59, 64, 65, 67, 68, 69. Image 22 has now failed three
separate times. Never attempted: 70-141.
THE ECONOMICS CHANGED THROUGH THE DAY. Four images a batch held this
morning. By evening it is one to two, even with thirty-second gaps between
images - the limiter has tightened as the session's cumulative reads have
piled up. Finishing from here is seventy-nine images at that rate.
So the cheap fix is time, not technique: this film is free and permanent,
and the quota resets. Recorded rather than ground out at a rate that would
mostly produce empty transcripts - which this archive counts as NOT READ,
not as "no Lerena", and which is exactly how a false negative gets
manufactured at scale.

commits.subject: FreeBMD: six marriages and a death get their references, and one loses its
commits.body:
David named FreeBMD as the cheapest thing left on the Taylor side. It was.
The archive already had the husbands' names from the Devon parish index;
this gives the quarter, district, volume and page a certificate is ordered
from - documented replacing family.
  Irene            Sep 1900  Bideford   5b 900
  Isabella Temple      1900  Bideford   5b 901
  Margaret Hellen W Dec 1903  PANCRAS   1b  43
  Lucy Elizabeth   Jun 1909  Totnes     5b 373
  Agnes W          Mar 1918  Devonport  5b 588  (spouse WOOD printed)
  Mary Ann H Brayley Mar 1870 Bideford  5b 794
  William Taylor, d. Dec 1902 Bideford  5b 326  (age given as 75)
IRENE AND ISABELLA ARE CONSECUTIVE PAGES of the same volume. Married eleven
days apart at the same church, and the registrar wrote them up one after
the other - the civil index carrying as fact what the parish register only
implied.
AND MARGARET IS THE ANSWER TO A QUESTION THIS ARCHIVE COULD NOT SETTLE. Her
banns were called at Northam in November 1903 and her marriage registered
at PANCRAS, LONDON. Eighty-four Margaret Bells were searched in the 1921
census and three hundred and sixty-two in the 1939 Register, across all
England, with none born in Devon - because she had not merely left the
county, she married out of it.
AND ONE RECORD LOSES ITS FOOTING. Horace Archibald Taylor was written up
this morning as having married Mary Jane Marshall. The BANNS are real; the
marriage is not evidenced - there is no Horace Taylor marriage anywhere in
Devon between 1893 and 1895. Banns are an intention, not a wedding.
A decoy nearly settled it the wrong way. A "Taylor, Horace" married a
MARSHALL in the same quarter at BOSMERE, SUFFOLK, which would have tidily
explained his absence from every Devon census - until the page was read
directly and gave the bride as LAURA EMILY, not Mary Jane. Before 1912 the
GRO index does not print the spouse: FreeBMD infers it from a shared page,
so a match is an inference, and two couples of the same surnames in one
quarter produce a false one.

commits.subject: Fix the broken build: the kit pin was stale, not the page
commits.body:
The site has not built since commit bd87842, which imported
PlaceSpark.astro into index.astro. The component was missing and the whole
build failed while astro still exited 0.
The import was right and the pin was wrong. PlaceSpark was published to
TheArchiveKit at 275cef0 ("A plot, not a map, for the five home pages with
no drawing", 06:18); site/package.json was still pinned at b46be72 from
04:20. The component was two commits ahead of the pin that was meant to
carry it.
So the fix is the pin, not the page - nothing of the other session's work
is touched. Bumped to 275cef0 and reinstalled.
595 pages build, 0 broken links, consistency clean, and the sparkline
renders on the home page rather than merely compiling - checked in the
output, not assumed from a green build.

commits.subject: Three ways in, and a drawing, on every front page
commits.body:
Three archives opened with exactly three doors under the hero. Three offered
a flat list instead — D'Arcy's front page carried forty-eight links, which is
a directory rather than an offer — and one offered nothing at all.
The shape is fixed at three and the CHOICES are left alone, because they are
the only thing a front page is for: Defranceschi opens with the story, a
person and a map; Booyzen with why a letter of the surname was changed;
Blažević with one woman. Card links keep the job they were actually good at,
which is the long list further down.
And the drawing. Five of these pages had none — the same gap the trees had
before the chart was shared. Every archive now has coordinates, so every one
can show a plot of its own places: no tiles, no coastline, no borders,
because an archive that has not got a coastline should not draw one. A dot
per place, sized by how many people stand in it.
Every count in the caption is read from the atlas data rather than typed. The
first version said "46 places" under 47 dots.

commits.subject: A checker that cannot fail on nothing is not a gate
commits.body:
check-links.py has just reported "0 pages, 0 html files, 0 ids ... 0 broken"
and PASSED. The deploy is gated on this script, so it was reporting success
over a site that did not exist.
The cause was a broken import leaving `astro build` exiting 0 with nothing
written - the exact failure this archive documented on 11 September, when a
render error left eight pages missing and 3,433 dead links behind a green
build. The gate was added for that. It still could not see an empty dist,
because zero pages means zero broken links.
It now refuses to pass on fewer than fifty pages, and says why: an empty
build means astro failed while still exiting 0, so read its output rather
than its exit code.
Verified by running it against the empty dist - exit 1.

commits.subject: Santa Rosa de Lima: 54 of 141 read, stopped by rate limiting
commits.body:
Read and clean, no Lerena under any of seven spellings: images 6, 8-21,
23-53, 55-58, 61-63 and 66. Fifty-four images of the second Rosario parish,
covering Bishop Cagliero's rounds of July 1890 and September-October 1891.
NOT read, because the transcript came back empty: 7, 22, 54, 59, 60, 64,
65, 67, 68, 69. Never attempted: 70-141.
WHY IT STOPPED. FamilySearch rate-limits after a long session. Earlier a
one-minute pause cleared it; by image 67 it did not - three consecutive
empties survived a sixty-second cooldown. An empty transcript is not "no
Lerena on this page", it is "this page was not read", and pushing on would
have manufactured false negatives at scale. That rule has already cost this
archive seven pages on the Catedral film today, and it is the reason this
commit says 54 rather than 64.
The errand carries the resume procedure, the pacing that holds from cold,
and the caution that the register's own index page says PAGES MISSING.

commits.subject: Santa Rosa de Lima: images 6-46 read, no Lerena
commits.body:
Progress marker only. Images 7 and 22 returned empty transcripts twice and
are recorded as NOT READ rather than clean - the rule that cost seven pages
on the Catedral film this morning.
Still to read: 47-141, plus those two retries. The errand carries the loop,
the pacing that holds against throttling, and the caution that the
register's own index page says PAGES MISSING.

commits.subject: The home page spine, finished on all seven
commits.body:
Every archive already opened with a one-line thesis and closed with the
sibling footer. In between, a grammar had been started and abandoned: a
numbers block on four archives under four names, a claim-card block on four
more under two names, and "what is still missing" on two.
Now all seven carry the same four, in the same order, under the same names:
what this archive has established · the archive in numbers · what is still
missing · the other archives.
Nothing was invented to fill them. Every card states a finding the archive
had already published somewhere on its own site, and every figure is read
live from that archive's own data rather than typed — so a count cannot drift
away from the page it points at.
The heading lost its number, because it was wrong twice: two archives said
"Four things this archive has established" over seven cards and five.

commits.subject: The British press: nothing found, and the reasons are the finding
commits.body:
Searched the British Newspaper Archive through findmypast, which the plan
does cover. Nothing of ours. Recorded in full so nobody spends another day
on it.
"Lerena" returns 1,344 articles and the surname is drowned by THREE
separate sources of noise, each named here for the next person:
  1. THE NISSAN SERENA - 1990s motor adverts, OCR'd as "lERENA". The single
     largest block of results.
  2. "GUTTA SERENA" - the old medical term for blindness of the optic
     nerve, in infirmary tables from the 1750s onward.
  3. DON PEDRO LOPEZ DE LERENA - Spanish Minister of Finance under Charles
     III, reported from the London Gazette in the 1780s as "Monf. de
     Lerena". A real Lerena of a real Spanish family, and not ours.
Exact-keyword matching does not help: the OCR text literally contains the
string, so it is a collision, not a fuzzy match. "Mary Septima" (26
articles), "Septima Taylor" (12) and "Lerena + Northam" (2) all returned
nothing of ours.
It is the same lesson the Uruguayan registers taught - a family is not
reachable by its name - arriving from a different direction and for the
opposite reason. There the name was mis-written eight ways. Here it is
collided with.
AND THE ONE LIVE SEAM IS REACHED BY SUBJECT. "Argentine Stud Book" returns
thirteen genuine articles, including Sporting Life of 28 October 1909 on
the Argentine Grand National Steeplechase - the very years Gilberto Lerena
was co-founding that book and having a Palermo Group 1 named for him in
1914. Logged as an errand: read those columns, do not search that name.
The Taylors, meanwhile, were simply not newsworthy. A cab driver's
household of ten at Northam reaches the press when a daughter passes an
examination - which is the one hit this archive already holds, the Western
Times of 4 April 1901.

commits.subject: The parish register images are the one thing this plan does not reach
commits.body:
Mapped the subscription's boundary by testing rather than assuming, because
a blocked record found at the last minute is worse than one found first.
REACHABLE: the 1921 census, the 1939 Register, incoming passenger lists,
the GRO marriage index, and the British and Irish newspapers - 1,344
articles on a "Lerena" keyword search.
BLOCKED: DEVON MARRIAGES AND BANNS, and the other Devon parish sets. They
are marked "Exclusive"; opening the transcript for Isabella Temple Taylor's
1900 marriage at Northam & Appledore redirects to an upgrade page -
"Everything", from $30.83 a month.
So the one thing this run set out to get is the one thing the plan does not
cover. The five husbands named today came from a FamilySearch INDEX of
those registers; the acts themselves, which would give their fathers' names
and occupations and turn index entries into a generation of in-laws, sit
behind that tier.
NOT BOUGHT, and not to be bought without David deciding it. Recorded as a
priced, specific option rather than a vague "paywall".
And the fact is not blocked, only the act text. The GRO index IS included
and gives Isabella's marriage as quarter 3 of 1900, Bideford district,
volume 5B page 901, with MarriageFinder naming Henry Dalling off the same
page. FreeBMD gives that free for all of them; Ancestry holds the Devon
images and this archive has never used it.

commits.subject: Every archive now opens the same way
commits.body:
Seven Start menus, seven shapes. Two of them did not begin with Home at all —
they opened "The trees · Our line, drawn · Home", which is my doing: the
naming canon went in without checking which archives already led with the
trees. Search appeared five times in one header and once in another. Six
pages were listed twice in a single nav. Timeline was "Timeline" on three
archives and "The Timeline" on three others, and the DNA page had two names.
Now: Home first everywhere. Search is the header pill and nothing else — one
route, not five. One entry per page. One label per idea. And the three pages
every archive now has — the trees, its own line drawn, the atlas — sit
together at the top of Start on all seven, in that order, rather than
scattered across "Go there" and "People & places".
The first attempt at this corrupted the arrays: a regex that required a
trailing comma silently skipped the last nav group in every archive, and the
repair dropped real entries. Reverted and redone line by line, with the item
count asserted before and after.

commits.subject: The 1939 Register: twenty-eight years, one house
commits.body:
Its strength is the exact date of birth, and it gave three. HENRY DALLING
born 9 October 1880. ISABELLA T DALLING born 10 SEPTEMBER 1874 - this
archive had only "1874" from a tree. And KATHLEEN G TAYLOR born 4 NOVEMBER
1870, confirming the archive's date to the day, and with it the reading
that she and William John were twins.
Kathleen's occupation in 1939: "INCAPACITATED". The 1921 "Home Invalid"
again, eighteen years on. She died five months after this register, on 29
February 1940.
Single at 41 in 1911. Home invalid at 50 in 1921. Incapacitated at 68 in
1939. Always at 26 Fore Street, in her sister Isabella's household. The
eldest of ten, and the only one who never left.
This archive began with a bare line and no husband, and read the blank as a
question about marriage. It was never a question about marriage.
And the Register's own marital status column against her is left EMPTY
where the others read Married and Single. Recorded as blank, not read as
single.
AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN PLAN. It listed the passenger lists as the
second priority, untried. They were tried on 9 September under an earlier
trial, and data/passenger-lists.tsv holds six voyages with masters, ship
numbers and TNA references - including the 1935 Balmoral Castle arrival
this session re-found and briefly believed new, down to the master and the
line number. The eight-year hole had been worked too: a clean negative and
two forenameless "Miss Taylor, 19" candidates of 1903 and 1904.
Read your own sources file before spending a deadline on a source.

commits.subject: Five of the ten in 1921, and the south Devon cluster confirmed
commits.body:
CHURSTON FERRERS: Alfred Sidney Wood, 39, a PAINTER for C Wace house
decorator, born South Pool; Agnes Walker Wood, 31; and SIDNEY WILLIAM
HENRY, born 1920 - a nephew new to this archive. Agnes is living in the
very parish where her sister Lucy's banns were called in 1909, three miles
from Paignton where their brother William John was in 1911. Three of the
ten in one corner of south Devon, eighty miles from where they were born.
23 HAMILTON STREET, DEVONPORT: William Norrish Sweet, 35, born Tiverton, a
SHIPWRIGHT AT HM DOCKYARD DEVONPORT; Lucy Elizabeth, 39; and their
daughter KATHLEEN ALICE, 11 - named, surely, for the eldest sister who
never married and was an invalid in another sister's house.
Lucy's birthplace is transcribed "Northam, NORTHAMPTONSHIRE" - the second
birthplace error in this one census, after Irene's Bermondsey.
NOT FOUND, and recorded as not found. Margaret Helen Walker Bell: eighty-
four Margaret Helen/Ellen Bells of the right age in England and not one
born at Northam or in Devon - she had left the county and Bell is too
common to follow blind. Horace Archibald Taylor: two Horace Taylors in
Devon, neither his. One, "WELSER H TAYLOR" born 1875 at APPLEDORE in
Northam parish, looked like a garbled Horace and was OPENED rather than
assumed - a seaman with a wife Belle and four children, and not him.

commits.subject: The 1921 census: Kathleen Georgina was an invalid
commits.body:
Findmypast holds 1921 exclusively and the trial expires tomorrow, so it
went first. Two Taylor households found, and one answer that is not a date.
FORE STREET, NORTHAM. Henry Dalling, 40, INSURANCE AGENT for the Pearl - he
was a gardener in 1911, a change of class in ten years. Isabel Temple, 45.
Ronald William, 18, a motor mechanic. Sylvia May, 10. EDITH MAY, 8, born
1913 and new to this archive. Horace Henry Charles, the eldest boy of 1911,
gone from the house at twenty.
And in the same house, aged fifty: KATHLEEN GEORGINA, sister-in-law,
occupation "HOME INVALID".
This archive asked twice whether the eldest of the ten ever married. The
answer is no, and the census says why. Unmarried at fifty, an invalid in
her younger sister's home. She died in 1940 at sixty-nine. Nothing here had
suggested it, because a tree records marriages and not infirmity.
5 KINGSLEY TERRACE, BIDEFORD. Henry Albert Burton, 45, ASSURANCE AGENT for
the Prudential - so both brothers-in-law sold insurance. Charles William,
13. Albert Edward, in the house in 1911, is not there. Two boarders.
TWO TRAPS RECORDED, both worth more than the facts around them.
The index calls Kathleen "Kathleen Georgina DALLING". She is a Taylor - the
enumerator wrote the household surname against every line. That is the
exact shape that cost this archive a retraction over the 1895 Buenos Aires
census, where "Lerena de L. Josefa" was read as a woman who married a
Lerena. The same habit, in Devon, in English, twenty-six years later.
And the return gives Irene's birthplace as BERMONDSEY. She was born at
Northam; her marriage act says so. Her husband was born at Bermondsey, he
filled the form, and he carried his own answer across to her line. Met
first in 1921, she would have been ruled out as a Londoner.

commits.subject: One .prose rule, the one the benchmark arrived at
commits.body:
Spacing between BLOCK children, not between everything. As a flex column the class made an inline or inside a

its own flex item, so a sentence came apart one fragment to a line. Verified by a full gated build: this archive passes.

commits.subject: One .prose rule, the one the benchmark arrived at
commits.body:
Spacing belongs between BLOCK children, not between everything. As a flex column, .prose made an inline or inside a

its own flex item, so a sentence came apart one fragment to a line. My first fix set p.prose to display:block, which stopped the sentence coming apart and took the paragraph spacing with it — consecutive paragraphs then butted together. Defranceschi had already solved both halves, and the comment in its stylesheet says so. The other six now carry the same three rules rather than a patch of my own. Also picks up the kit's wall-heading fix, which had been rendering "The 1 walls, and why each one is a wall" on Falco.

commits.subject: Bank progress on the second Rosario parish: 6-22 read, no Lerena
commits.body:
Santa Rosa de Lima, Confirmaciones 1890-1897, DGS 004581639. Images 6 to 22
read, no Lerena under any of seven spellings. Image 6 is the register's own
index and dates the rounds: July 1890, September-October 1891 and May 1897,
under Bishop Juan Cagliero - when Pablo Armando was eight, nine and fifteen.
Still to read: 23-141, plus retries of 7, 11, 15 and 22, which returned
empty transcripts. Empty means NOT READ, never "no Lerena" - that rule cost
seven pages on the Catedral film this morning.
The errand now carries the exact loop and the progress marker so this can
be resumed without re-reading what is done.

commits.subject: Rosario has five filmed parishes. This archive had read one.
commits.body:
David asked what had not been tried and named the Argentine Catholic parish
registers - civil registration being closed, the parish books are not. He
was right, and the gap is sharper than he put it: it is not that the parish
books were untried, it is that FOUR OF THE FIVE PARISHES WERE.
All seventeen Rosario films in this archive belong to catalogue 208788,
NUESTRA SENORA DEL ROSARIO. The index sweeps of 1731-1901, the three-year
baptism sweep, the confirmations read this morning - one parish, all of it.
The collection also films Inmaculada Concepcion, Sagrado Corazon de Jesus,
San Jose and Santa Rosa de Lima.
THE FINDING CUTS BOTH WAYS.
It STRENGTHENS the baptism null. The obvious worry - that the family used
another parish and the Catedral books would never show them - does not hold
for 1882: four of the five have no register that early, the earliest being
Santa Rosa de Lima in 1888. In February 1882 the Catedral was, so far as
the filmed record goes, the only parish in Rosario.
But it OPENS a real new source on the central question. SANTA ROSA DE LIMA,
CONFIRMACIONES 1890-1897 - DGS 004581639, 141 images, transcribed in full
text, never opened here. Its own index page reads "Confirmacion
administrada por el Senor Obispo Doctor Don JUAN CAGLIERO en el mes de
Julio de 1890", with further rounds in September-October 1891 and May 1897.
Pablo Armando was eight, nine and fifteen. If he was confirmed at Rosario
at all, he is in that book or the Catedral's.
The film warns of its own damage: the index page carries the words "PAGES
MISSING". Any null taken from it is qualified by that.
AND A METHOD NOTE, because the ordinary route failed. The catalogue search
was down again, so the DGS could not be looked up. It was recovered from
the image viewer's own page source, where the waypoint payload carries it.
Browse by waypoint, read the DGS out of the page, then use the ordinary
film loop. It works when the catalogue does not.

commits.subject: Five places on the atlas that were not places
commits.body:
David spotted that the place field was holding citations. He was right, and
it did two kinds of damage at once: eight people were missing from the map
they belonged on, and four phantom locations - "SA records", "SA +
Argentine records", "GRO + SA records", "Mendoza; later New York and Rio
crossings" - were standing on it as though they were towns.
Among the eight: PABLO ARMANDO HIMSELF, MARY SEPTIMA, and all three of
their sons. The central figure of this archive was not on its own atlas.
Now Cape Town for the five South Africans, South Africa for Anton, Mendoza
for Avelino Carlos, Montevideo for Carolina Oribe. The citations are moved
into the notes, not deleted - the crossings are still there, and the row
says why the field changed. 37 places became 33, because "SA records" was
always four people who belonged under South Africa.
AND A GUARD SO IT CANNOT RECUR. consistency.py now flags any where_found or
birthplace reading like a citation - "records", "GRO", "crossings",
"index", or a bare dash - because the atlas is generated from that field,
and a citation there is invisible in the register and loud on the map.
Verified by injecting one.

commits.subject: Plan the findmypast harvest before the trial expires
commits.body:
The trial ends 15 September. The rule for a deadline is to take the things
that exist NOWHERE ELSE first and the merely convenient last - FamilySearch
is free and permanent, so whatever it also holds can wait.
1. THE 1921 CENSUS - exclusive to findmypast, not on FamilySearch at any
   price, and the 1931 returns were destroyed by fire, so it is the last
   census before the 1939 Register. Where all ten Taylor siblings landed,
   and whether Kathleen was still single at fifty-one.
2. OUTBOUND PASSENGER LISTS (BT27) - the eight-year hole: how a Devon
   pupil-teacher of sixteen in 1901 reached Cape Town and bore a son there
   in November 1905.
3. THE 1939 REGISTER - the five sisters who lived into the 1950s-70s.
4. DEVON PARISH REGISTER IMAGES behind the five marriages found today,
   which currently rest on an index against this archive's own rule.
5. BRITISH NEWSPAPER ARCHIVE.
And a discipline note for a rushed harvest: the temptation under a deadline
is to screenshot and sort later. Do not. A folder of unread images is not
evidence, and in a fortnight nobody will remember which was which. Capture
the citation with every one.

commits.subject: An atlas, from places this archive has listed all along
commits.body:
The place list has been here since the archive was built and carried no
geography, so no map could be drawn from it. The names are resolved against a
gazetteer the estate now shares, and the people come from data this archive
already held rather than anything new.
A coordinate is a claim like any other and is marked as such: exact where the
gazetteer matched the parish, approximate where it matched a larger place or
a modern name, and the page prints how many of each. Anything that landed
outside the countries this family can plausibly be in was refused rather than
drawn, because a dot in the wrong country is worse than a missing one.
Places without a coordinate are counted in the eyebrow rather than quietly
dropped.

commits.subject: Read the Rosario confirmations page by page: Pablo Armando is not in them
commits.body:
Of everything this archive had never opened, this register mattered most,
because EVERY ENTRY NAMES BOTH PARENTS. An act for Pablo Armando would have
put Juan Carlos Lerena and Maria Lerena on a document other than the
enrolment card - the only thing this archive has ever wanted.
It had been left alone on the assumption it needed DeepZoom tiles. The
assumption was never tested and it was wrong: the film is transcribed in
full text.
SO IT WAS READ. Seventy-six images, end to end - every page from the first
register leaf, "Siguen las confirmaciones en la Iglesia del Sagrario (15
Mayo de 1885)", through to image 80 where a new section opens in 1897 under
Bishop Gelabert y Crespo. Entry numbers run from 2 to past 2,560: roughly
two and a half thousand children of Rosario, each with both parents named.
NO LERENA. Not under Lerena, Llerena, Lorena, Serena, Lerina, Levena or
Gerena.
And the period is exactly his: three years old when the register opens,
fifteen when the section closes, with children confirmed at every age from
two to fifteen. His whole plausible window is inside the pages read.
That makes it the strongest negative this archive has produced on Rosario,
and an independent one - both baptism index volumes were already read end
to end for 1731-1901, where the surname appears once in a hundred and
seventy years.
SAID AGAINST MYSELF: images 81-148 are not read (1897-1904, when he was
15-22); confirmations of 1883-84 are not on these pages; and the transcript
is a machine's, which renders one mother's surname three ways in three
consecutive lines. A strong negative, not a proof of absence.
TWO FALSE POSITIVES, both opened and dismissed. Image 64's "Lorenza Serena"
is the same mother the machine also calls "Merina" and "Jesusa" in the
lines above and below - three siblings, one woman, three guesses. Image
71's "Solerina" is a different surname containing the letters of one being
searched; the pattern was tightened to whole words after it.
AND THE ONE THAT MATTERED. Seven images returned a ZERO-LENGTH transcript
on the first pass, and every one read clean on retry. An empty transcript
is not "no Lerena on this page", it is "this page was not read". Counted as
clean, this would be claiming a complete read of a register with seven
unopened pages in it. Third time in one day this source has failed by
returning something rather than erroring - so the rule extends: a reading
loop must validate its own output.

commits.subject: The trees page never pointed at the tree
commits.body:
Start → The trees → and then a link called "The spine", or "The line", or
"Open the line", every one of them going to the direct-line prose. The chart
was reachable from the menu and from nowhere on the page whose entire job is
to index this archive's lines.
One banner now, worded identically across all seven, sitting above the rows.
The row links are untouched: each archive keeps its own name for its own
prose, which is local colour and worth keeping. What is shared is the route
to the thing every archive now has.

commits.subject: One kit commit across all eight, which is the only way a shared kit holds
commits.body:
The estate had drifted onto five different pins. Two sites can import the
same component name from the same package and get different behaviour when
that is true, which defeats the point of having extracted it.
All eight now pin the same commit and build green against it — 16,548 pages
between them, every one of the eight gated on the shared test.

commits.subject: The smallest chart in the estate, where that is the finding
commits.body:
Eight people and four walls. Two of the grandparent branches stop one
generation above the line, because Argentine civil registration is not open
and the 1908 ficha de enrolamiento names Juan Carlos and Maria and then says
nothing further. A chart makes that plain in a way three pages of prose have
not: the line does not fade out, it stops.
The Taylor side reaches one generation further than people.json alone would
give. That is not a new claim — taylor-line.json has had James Taylor as
William's father in plain text all along, and this reads the link the archive
already made.
A parent known only as a name on a document is drawn like anyone else and
simply carries no link. Leaving them off would have made the line look
shorter than the evidence.

commits.subject: "The Trees" and "The Tree" are different pages — say which is which
commits.body:
They are genuinely different and both worth having. Their own deks say so:
/trees is the INDEX of every line this archive holds, each drawn in the form
its evidence supports; /tree is THIS family's own line, drawn as one figure.
The labels did not say that. Falco had "The Trees" and "The Tree" adjacent in
one menu and "The Tree" AGAIN in another group — three near-identical labels
for two ideas, which is a reader's problem rather than a tidiness one.
Now, everywhere:
  /trees   The trees          the index of the lines
  /tree    Our line, drawn    this family's own
Duplicate links to the same page are dropped from the nav.

commits.subject: Sancho's marriage, Josefa, Rosario, Zelmira - four hunts, two unlocks
commits.body:
SANCHO'S 1791 MARRIAGE ACT: not found, and probably not digitised. The
Canelones Catedral is in full text with its baptisms, confirmations and
marriage INVESTIGATION files - and no marriage register. The investigation
files 1776-1806 remain the best hope: a Canelones marriage in 1791 should
have left an informacion there, and Sancho is already inside that bundle as
a witness at somebody else's.
BUT THE HUNT FOUND HER FAMILY. A single Uruguayan hit for "Fernandez
Tresguerras" is a Montevideo baptism of 15 May 1812 naming "DON RODRIGO
FERNANDEZ Y TRESGUERRAS y DONA ROSA FERNANDEZ" as maternal grandparents -
the first purchase this archive has ever had on Maria's own people. Her
being Rodrigo's daughter is a PLAUSIBILITY, not a finding. And the
godparents are written "Serena" and "Perena", this family's known S-for-L -
which would put a Lerena couple at a Fernandez y Tresguerras font in 1812,
exactly what a marriage in 1791 predicts. Offered as the next thing to
test.
JOSEFA'S MARRIAGE: not found either - the couple appear only ever as
PARENTS, never as bride and groom. But the search gives five children where
this archive had two, and very probably Fernando Moratorio's own baptism:
15 October 1845 at MEDALLA MILAGROSA Y SAN AGUSTIN - the Lerenas' own
parish in the Villa de la Union - son of a Spaniard and a Uruguayan.
Neighbours a generation before they married. Stated as an inference from a
name, a date and a parish.
ROSARIO - A METHOD UNLOCK. This archive has assumed for two weeks that
these registers need DeepZoom tiles. THE CONFIRMATIONS FILM, DGS 4531018 -
the one that covers Pablo Armando - IS FULLY TRANSCRIBED IN FULL TEXT, and
every entry names BOTH PARENTS. It can be read one request at a time. The
deaths film is not transcribed and covers only 1731-1864, so it cannot hold
anyone being chased. Logged as an errand with the exact procedure.
AND A HARD LIMIT MEASURED: unquoted terms are OR'd, not AND'd - "Lerena
Rosario difunto" returns 17,782,105 documents. Full text takes exactly one
quoted phrase. The place facet is a trap that answers a confident ZERO
while reporting "No filters available" - the third distinct false null
caught on this service today.
ZELMIRA: tested and ruled out. Born 4 Nov 1880 at San Jose, daughter of
ALBERTO LERENA and Maria Ines Larriera, m. Adolfo Cordero 1901, d. 1945.
The shape was right and the substance is not. Her father would be the right
age to be Alberto Octavio Lerena Lenguas - NOT MERGED, because a forename
and an age is what produced the two Arturos.

commits.subject: One living-people guard, and this archive names its policy
commits.body:
Two guards were written separately on the same day and were never duplicates:
one read committed data for a living person's DATES, the other read a GEDCOM
for their NAMES. Different rules, both right for their archive.
They are one tool now, and each archive says which rule it is under rather
than which implementation it happens to use:
  named-bare   named and nothing more — the name may appear, no date may
  absent       not published at all, name included
  declared     a hand-written list, for a site with no people file
Both hard-won lessons are kept. Dates are matched as the literal strings the
data attaches to a living person, because bare years pass vacuously on a
genealogy site and a name near a date fires on every homonym. Names are
matched as phrases minus exact namesakes and minus longer published names that
merely contain them.
The archive answers who is alive; the kit answers whether any of them reached
the build.

commits.subject: Draw the Taylor tree, and let the drawing find an error
commits.body:
The /trees/ page carried the Taylor row as DRAWABLE - its own word for
"enough people to chart, and no chart yet" - and it was the only row in
that state. It is now drawn, and the row says so.
IT USES .ptree, WHICH WAS NOT DEAD CODE. The stylesheet carried a fully
designed chart convention that no page used, and its comment explains
itself: "Every node says HOW the relationship is known: line / register /
tree." That is exactly the thing today's work is about, so the Taylor chart
derives each node's provenance FROM THAT PERSON'S OWN SOURCE FIELD - a node
turns from dotted to solid the moment its evidence does, with no second
place to update.
Read the left edges and the chart tells the story: generation B and eight
of the ten children now rest on parish registers or censuses read here.
What remains dotted is generation A - James Taylor and Harriet Reynolds,
still a tree's assertion - the twin whose name nobody wrote down, and the
infant William who died at eight months. Documented in the middle, hearsay
at the top and at the edges.
AND THE DRAWING FOUND AN ERROR THE TABLE HAD HIDDEN. The infant William was
recorded in GENERATION A, beside his own father. A fortnight of reading
that file as a table had not shown it, because a table does not care which
row is which generation; rendered as a tree, a dead infant stood next to
James as though he were an uncle. He is generation B, the elder brother of
the William born in 1826 who was named after him.
A second way of looking at the same data is a test of it.

commits.subject: Take the Taylors off a tree and put them on parish registers
commits.body:
Five of Mary Septima's siblings were recorded here as bare surnames - "m.
Dalling", "m. Bell", "m. Burton", "m. Sweet", "m. Wood" - with no forename,
date, place or source but a MyHeritage tree. A strange thing for an archive
that has opened Montevideo parish acts from 1789 to tolerate, in the
best-documented jurisdiction it touches.
ALL FIVE HUSBANDS NAMED, in under an hour:
  HENRY DALLING       m. Isabella Temple,  10 Sep 1900,  Northam
  HENRY ALBERT BURTON m. Irene,            30 Aug 1900,  Northam
  CHARLES WILLIAM BELL m. Margaret Helen Walker, banns 22 Nov 1903, Northam
  WILLIAM NORRISH SWEET m. Lucy Elizabeth, banns 1909, Churston Ferrers
  ALFRED SIDNEY WOOD  m. Agnes Walker,     1918,         Devon
and the brother HORACE ARCHIBALD TAYLOR m. MARY JANE MARSHALL, banns
Northam 17 Dec 1893 - correcting a tree's hedged "(? Mary Jane Bridge)".
TWO SISTERS MARRIED ELEVEN DAYS APART IN THE SAME CHURCH, four months after
their mother's death. Invisible until the husbands had dates.
THE 1871 CENSUS SETTLES A QUESTION THIS ARCHIVE HAD WRITTEN DOWN AND LEFT.
Kathleen Georgina and William John are both infants in the house on 2 April
1871, and the parents' banns were called 9 January 1870 - so they are
TWINS. The family had two sets.
AND WILLIAM JOHN'S WIFE WAS NOT "FANNY ELLEN JEFFEREY". The censuses name
her FANNY HELEN and date the marriage to 1892; no Devon record supports
JEFFEREY. The only Fanny Jeffreys to marry a Taylor in England married a
JAMES WILLIAM Taylor in CHESHIRE in 1893. Said as a suspicion: that looks
like where a tree picked her up. Her maiden name is unknown again, which is
better than wrong.
THE 1911 CENSUS, never read here, gives five nieces and nephews at one
stroke, Henry Dalling's trade, and KATHLEEN GEORGINA entered as SINGLE at
41 in her married sister's house - replacing a tree's silence with a
document.
AND THEY MOVED TO WHERE A RELATIVE ALREADY WAS: William John at Paignton by
1911, Lucy's banns at Churston Ferrers three miles away in 1909, both
eighty miles from Northam. The same shape this archive keeps finding in
Montevideo, showing on the Devon side for the first time.
THE PAGE IS NOW GENERATED FROM THE DATA. The ten siblings were a hardcoded
array duplicating taylor-line.tsv - so the data gained five husbands and
the page went on saying "m. Dalling". Exactly the drift this build exists
to prevent.

commits.subject: Fix the row that broke the guard it describes
commits.body:
The correction logging the unpaired-marker bug quoted the markers as an
example, so the new check failed on it - twice, once in each field that
carried an illustration.
Rewritten in words. The convention has no way to express a literal marker,
which is now recorded as a known limit of it rather than met again as a
surprise.

commits.subject: Close the two-Dominga problem on an act, and catch the Santo Oficio trap
commits.body:
THE CAUTION RAISED THIS MORNING IS CLOSED THE SAME DAY, by opening the
second image rather than reasoning about it. The Catedral act of 25 October
1840: "DOMINGO ... hijo legitimo de D. ANTONIO RODRIGUEZ DE CARBALLO,
natural de la PROVINCIA DEL RIO GRANDE, y de Dona DOMINGA LERENA ... Nieto
paterno de D. JOAQUIN RODRIGUEZ ... y por parte materna de D. SANCHO LERENA
y de Dona MARIA FERNANDEZ."
Set beside the 1827 act - "CAPITAN DON ANTONIO RUIZ DE CARVALLO ... Nieta
Paterna del MAYOR DON JOAQUIN" - the two husbands are ONE MAN whose first
surname the registers write RUIZ in 1827 and RODRIGUEZ in 1840. So there is
ONE Dominga: born 1804 at Canelones, married Antonio de Carvallo, children
Lucinda Gregoria (1827) and Domingo (1840).
The discipline is what produced this. The two records were kept apart until
an act joined them, rather than merged because both husbands were called
Antonio. Merged on the resemblance, the right answer would have been
reached for the wrong reason - and the next resemblance would have been
merged too. Two discrepancies are recorded rather than smoothed: the ranks,
and Juana Suarez against Juana del Espiritu Santo.
AND A FALSE-POSITIVE TRAP, CAUGHT BEFORE IT WAS PUBLISHED. Pages two to
four of a "Sancho Llerena" full-text search are Spanish nobility proofs and
notarial books. One was opened: it reads "familiar del SANTO OFICIO ...
LLERENA" - the Inquisition tribunal seated at Llerena, Badajoz, which the
machine reads as "Sancho, oficio". The archive was one step from recording
"Sancho is an attested forename in Spanish Llerena families", which is
false and would have been used to argue against Francisco.
AND A GUARD FOR A MISTAKE MADE THREE TIMES TODAY. consistency.py now checks
the TSVs for an odd marker count. On its first run it found two more
that check-links.py could never catch - including one carrying the central
open question about Maria Lerena - because check-links counts PAIRS in
rendered HTML, and a single unpaired marker leaves no pair to count. A
guard that looks for pairs is blind to the case of exactly one.

commits.subject: Sancho in 1789, a tally counted wrong, and a tree vindicated
commits.body:
SANCHO IN 1789 - fifteen years earlier than anything held yesterday. At the
Iglesia Matriz de Montevideo on 30 June 1789 the godparents of Juana,
daughter of "NICOLAS BENTENO, INDIO NATURAL DE LA CIUDAD DEL TUCUMAN, y de
Leonarda Correa de Buenos Ayres", were SANCHO LLERENA and Juliana Josefa
Cornejo. He is about twenty-two, in Montevideo rather than Canelones, two
years short of his own marriage.
It is the SECOND time he is found sponsoring at the margins of colonial
society - in 1804 he stood godfather to an enslaved man, here to the
daughter of an indigenous man from Tucuman. Twice, fifteen years apart.
Recorded as it stands.
AND THE SANCHO-OR-FRANCISCO TALLY HAS BEEN COUNTED WRONGLY BY THIS ARCHIVE.
Fourteen records: ten Sancho, four Francisco. But THREE OF THE FOUR
FRANCISCOS ARE THE SAME PAGE - one clerk, one morning, one legajo. They are
one witness, not three. The Sanchos come from nine separate occasions
across sixty-one years, in four parishes and two towns, twice with the man
himself standing there. So it is not ten to four; it is nine independent
occasions against two, and both of the two describe him at second hand. A
double forename remains the leading reading, but the question is no longer
evenly balanced.
A PUBLISHED TREE TURNS OUT TO HAVE BEEN RIGHT. The marriage act of 3
November 1830, now read rather than indexed, calls the bride's mother
"MARIA FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS". This archive carried that matronymic from a
tree since its first week, marked secondary - it appears in no index
anywhere. The tree was right, which raises the credit of its other unopened
claim: that Sancho and Maria married at Canelones on 8 January 1791. That
act would settle the forename and has never been opened.
AND THIS MORNING'S DOMINGA CAUTION IS HALF ANSWERED. The Catedral act of 12
May 1827 names "DONA DOMINGA LLERENA DE CARVALLO", wife of CAPITAN DON
ANTONIO RUIZ DE CARVALLO, son of MAYOR DON JOAQUIN - with the EXMO SR
GENERAL DON FRANCISCO DE PAULA MAGGESI as godfather. It also identifies the
"Dona Dominga Carvallo" who stood godmother at a Lerena font in 1850 and
whom this archive could not place: a Lerena by birth, standing for her own
brother's son. NOT MERGED - the other Dominga record is still unopened.
Eight new register rows. "Aguilar" is still unattested across all fourteen.

commits.subject: Run the sharpest test of the central question: no Lerena married a Lerena
commits.body:
The enrolment card names both of Pablo Armando's parents LERENA. Either
Maria married into the name or she was born to it - and Spanish naming
makes that testable in one query. A child of two Lerenas carries both
surnames: LERENA LERENA. In two weeks nobody had searched for it.
Four hits in the Uruguayan registers; forty-three across the whole
transcribed corpus with no country filter. Every one opened, every
transcript read.
ALL FORTY-THREE ARE TRANSCRIPTION DOUBLINGS. "Pio Lerena . Lerena" across
a line end; "Zelmira Lerena , Lerena argentino"; "Celidonio B. de Lerena
Lerena"; "G. Lerena Lerena" written across a printed title page at
Chacabuco. The machine repeats a word at line and page breaks, and it
produced the same false positive four times before the pattern was
obvious. The only genuine compounds in the forty-three are Colombian.
So no child of two Lerenas is recorded under the compound anywhere
FamilySearch has transcribed. A controlled negative: the query demonstrably
ran. IT LOWERS THE PROBABILITY THAT MARIA WAS A LERENA BY BIRTH. It does
not close it - a woman can be a Lerena by birth without her children being
written so, and Rosario's parish books are thin in full text. No
Lerena-Lerena marriage should now be asserted anywhere in this archive.
AND THE SEARCH PAID FOR ITSELF TWICE OVER.
THE ELEVENTH LERENA DISPENSATION, Montevideo July-August 1911 - the only
one that draws its own family tree. Bernabe Lerena married Florencia
Cardozo; his sister MARIA LERENA married her brother Eliseo Cardozo; their
children Custodio Lerena and Ema Cardozo petitioned to marry as DOUBLE
FIRST COUSINS. They asked to be excused the fee, "pues no pueden
satisfacerlos" - a poor Lerena household, in an archive that has spent two
days finding generals, judges and hacendados.
That is the first documented Maria Lerena of roughly the right generation.
She married a Cardozo, where Pablo Armando's mother stands beside Juan
Carlos Lerena - so she is recorded and RULED OUT ON THE RECORD, because
this archive has twice built on a Maria it had not pinned down.
Eleven dispensations now, and every Lerena in every one marries out.
Ten new register rows, including three Lerena women found in passing - one
of them, Zelmira, married to an Argentine in 1905.

commits.subject: Answer the ALEX question in public, and retest it properly
commits.body:
David asked whether anything on alex.onb.ac.at could relate to the Lerenas.
The assessment had been sitting in data/ unpublished - the drift checker
had been flagging it as an orphan for a day.
RETESTED, MORE STRICTLY. The first pass queried /cgi-content/alex-iv.pl by
GET with a suchwort parameter. The form is a POST and its field is named
"string", so a malformed request could have explained the earlier stub.
Resubmitting the site's own form with every Geltungsbereich selected
returns the form page unchanged, with no result block at all. The
conclusion stands and now rests on a properly-formed request.
The null itself was established by controls, which is why it is trustworthy:
"Konsul", "Uruguay" and "Montevideo" each returned an identical 166-byte
response. A word certain to appear in five million pages of Austrian law
returning zero is a broken search, not a null.
AND THE HONEST ANSWER ON RELEVANCE, published rather than buried: the prior
is low. This family is Uruguayan, Argentine, Spanish, South African and
British, and nothing in the record touches the Habsburg lands. The one real
hook is consular - Austria-Hungary kept consulates at Montevideo and Buenos
Aires and the Hof- und Staatshandbuch lists consuls, so an Austro-Hungarian
honorary consulship held by a Lerena in the River Plate would show. It
would NOT show Pablo Armando's own claimed consulship, which was Argentine
and at the Cape.
Noted for the sibling archive, not acted on here: ALEX is likely far more
use to the Defranceski side, where Istria and Kvarner were Habsburg.

commits.subject: Read the whole 1846 page: a branch corrected, a guard exposed, a war located
commits.body:
The baptism page of 7 January 1846 at La Mauricia was opened yesterday and
read entry by entry. Reading it END TO END changed four things.
ALEJANDRO IS AVELINO'S SON, NOT LUIS'S. The act reads "hijo legitimo de
Avelino Serena y Ambrosia Traibel ... Padrinos LUIS [L]ERENA y JUSTINIANA
LENGUAS". Luis and Justiniana are his GODPARENTS - both pairs sit in one
sentence and this archive took the wrong one. Published yesterday as "a
sixth child of Luis and Justiniana", born 1845. He is the ELDEST KNOWN
CHILD of Avelino and Ambrosia, born 29 May 1843, which pushes their
marriage back before May 1843.
AND THE PAGE EXPLAINS ITSELF. Every act on it - Lerena and not - ends "asi
consta del LEGAJO conservado en este Archivo, mandado TRASLADAR por el
Senor Obispo D. JACINTO VERA". It is loose papers copied into a book three
years late. THE CAUSE IS THE GUERRA GRANDE: the siege closed in February
1843, the three children were born February, May and July 1843, and none
was christened until 1846 - in the Villa de la Union, which Oribe renamed
the VILLA RESTAURACION and made his seat. Luis's first wife was an ORIBE;
his son's 1850 baptism is at "pueblo de la Restauracion". The family was on
the blanco side. No relationship to Manuel Oribe is claimed.
A CONTRADICTION FOUND AND THEN BROKEN BY A THIRD RECORD. Luis Eugenio's act
says 9 February 1843; his sister's act, the entry above his in the same
hand, says 30 July 1843. Five and a half months between full siblings. His
1901 death registration gives his age as 56 - a birth of 1845. Two
constraints against one clerk who wrote "ano cuarenta y tres" in the entry
above and again in the entry below. The register now reads 9 February 1845,
with the act's own words kept.
AND THE GUARD THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT. consistency.py was written for
exactly this pair - its docstring names it - and had printed "nothing
contradicts itself" for a week, because the sibling test reads a structured
parent field that 30 of 245 rows carry. A guard reporting a clean bill of
health over 12% of the data is worse than no guard. It now falls back to
compound surnames (LERENA LENGUAS = a Lerena father and a Lenguas mother),
prints its own coverage, and no longer says "nothing contradicts itself"
without adding "within the coverage printed above". On the first run after
the fix it flagged the pair.

commits.subject: Turn the parent-pair method on the central question, and catch a false null
commits.body:
The method that completed Sancho's generation was aimed at Juan Carlos
Lerena the same hour. It found nothing, and the way it found nothing is
worth more than the result.
ARGENTINA: 210 results for father "Juan Carlos" + Lerena, and the only
Juan Carlos Lerena among them is Pablo Armando's own enrolment card.
URUGUAY: 822 results, one of them a Juan Carlos Lerena recorded as a
father - opened and ruled out, an infant death registered 21 February 1983.
So the central null now survives the best method this archive has.
AND A FAILURE MODE FOUND. FamilySearch renders "Historical Record Search
Results (0)" WHILE THE QUERY IS STILL RUNNING - a complete, composed page
indistinguishable from a true empty result. Three searches were read as
nulls and were a minute from being written down as findings.
It was caught only by a control: the same query shape aimed at Sancho, for
whom five records had been pulled twenty minutes earlier, also returned
zero. That answer was known to be false, so the query was suspect rather
than the name. Results arrived 7-18 seconds later.
THE RULE, NOW ON THE METHOD PAGE: a null is not written down until a
control query in the same form returns a known result in the same session.
The archive learned this once before and more expensively, over the 1895
census. The second time it cost nothing.
Also observed: nearly every Juan Carlos Lerena in Uruguay carries Lerena
as a SECOND, maternal surname - Gonzalez Lerena, Carvalho Lerena, del
Campo Lerena, Reyes Lerena. One more argument for the compound sweep.

commits.subject: Complete Sancho's generation by searching the parents, not the name
commits.body:
Four children of Sancho Lerena and Maria Fernandez are now on record.
Searching the couple rather than the surname returned 22 results and four
things this archive did not have.
AVELINO HAS DATES: born 1815, died 22 August 1890 at Montevideo. Which
closes something filed as merely odd - his widow Ambrosia Traibel, not he,
stood witness at their son Alfredo's 1892 wedding. He had been dead sixteen
months. Three records now fall into one order.
JUSTA PASTORA'S MARRIAGE IS DATED: 3 November 1830, Cordon, to Manuel
Barros - thirteen months before the font in the same parish at which
Fructuoso Rivera stood godfather to her first child.
Both are indexes read, images not opened: secondary for the dates, while
the parentages stay primary on acts already read here.
AND A WARNING RATHER THAN A FACT. Two records name a Dominga, daughter of
Sancho and Maria Fernandez, with different husbands - Antonio Rodriguez and
Antonio Ruiz de Carvallo - on adjacent images in one register. One woman
married twice, one man written two ways, or two sisters sharing a forename.
This archive has been caught by that shape twice, with the two Arturos and
the three Josefas. NOTHING MERGED.
The method is the finding: this family is indexed under eight spellings, so
the surname box loses records the parent pair recovers.

commits.subject: The Lerena Traibel branch attaches to Sancho - and the godparents are Lavalleja
commits.body:
Found by searching AVELINO with AMBROSIA - the couple, not the surname. This
morning this archive recorded that "no record found here names Avelino's own
parents, so he is NOT shown to be Sancho's son". Two acts settle it.
*** SAN FRANCISCO DE ASIS, 12 MARCH 1858. *** Two children of Avelino Lerena and
Ambrosia Traibel baptised the same day - Alfredo Justiniano and Ana Rosario -
and both acts name the paternal grandparents:
  *** SANCHO LERENA and MARIA FERNANDEZ ***
So AVELINO IS SANCHO'S SON, and the whole LERENA TRAIBEL line descends from the
trunk: Josefa (1851-1947), Alfredo Justiniano, Mercedes Micaela, Clorinda, Juan
Arturo, Andres, Alberto, Adelina, Pedro Alberto Isabelino, Marta Adelina and a
younger Avelino.
*** SEVERAL OF THEM WERE ALREADY IN THIS REGISTER, FLOATING UNATTACHED FOR A
FORTNIGHT. *** Mercedes Micaela and Clorinda sit in the dispensation table. And
JUAN ARTURO is the man this archive conflated with another Arturo in its first
week and had to retract within the hour - he has been waiting here, unplaced,
ever since.
*** AND THE GODPARENTS ARE LAVALLEJA. *** Justiniano Lavalleja stood for
Alfredo, who is named for him; Constantino and Ana Lavalleja stood for Ana
Rosario, who is named for her. Lavalleja is one of the great names of Uruguayan
independence - Juan Antonio Lavalleja led the Treinta y Tres Orientales in 1825.
*** NO RELATIONSHIP TO HIM IS CLAIMED. Lavalleja is a surname, not a proof. ***
But the pattern is now three deep and it is on the record:
  1831  FRUCTUOSO RIVERA, President of the Republic, godfather to Sancho's grandson
  1836  an ORIBE for the bride of Sancho's son Luis
  1858  LAVALLEJA godparents to Sancho's grandchildren
Rivera, Oribe and Lavalleja are the three caudillos of Uruguayan independence
and of the wars that followed. This archive spent a fortnight calling these
people obscure.
AND A TIDY CONNECTION KILLED BY THE SAME ACT. Alfredo's middle name JUSTINIANO
looked like an echo of JUSTINIANA LENGUAS, who married into the other branch -
I flagged it as worth testing. It is nothing of the kind: he is named for his
godfather, whose name is on the same line.
Also new: JUAN TRAIBEL and YSABEL CENTENO, Ambrosia's parents.
Register: 239 -> 246 people.

commits.subject: A tenth dispensation, missed two ways at once, and a seventh spelling
commits.body:
Found by searching the rarest name in the branch - AMBROSIA TRAIBEL - rather
than the surname. That is now the fifth major find in two days that came from
refusing to search LERENA.
*** CATEDRAL BASILICA DE MONTEVIDEO, 3 FEBRUARY 1892. ***
  "dispensados por el Ilustrisimo y Rmo Senor Obispo Diocesano Monsenor Doctor
   Don MARIANO SOLER del impedimento canonico de parentesco de TERCER GRADO DE
   CONSANGUINIDAD CON ATINGENCIA AL SEGUNDO ... contrajo Don ALFREDO GERENA,
   natural de esta Republica, soltero, de treinta y cinco anos, hijo legitimo
   de Don AVELINO LORENA y Dona AMBROSIA TRAIBEL. Con Dona HERMENEGILDA
   CAROLINA GAVARRO ... fueron testigos Don Carlos Navia y Dona AMBROSIA
   TRAIBEL."
ALFREDO LERENA TRAIBEL, born about 1857 - a second child for Avelino and a
brother of Josefa. His mother stood formal witness at his wedding. The couple
were COUSINS, and the dispensation was granted personally by MARIANO SOLER, the
first Archbishop of Montevideo.
*** AND THE SWEEP MISSED IT TWO WAYS AT ONCE. *** This morning the dispensation
file said EIGHT Lerena dispensations and "every Lerena marries out". A ninth
turned up at midday - Ema Sixta's, invisible because her COMPOUND surname sat
between the two words of the search formula. This is a tenth, and it hid
differently again:
  1. The groom is written GERENA - a SEVENTH spelling for this family, after
     Lerena, Llerena, Lorena, Serena, Lerina and Sancio. And his own father is
     written LORENA in the same sentence, by the same priest.
  2. The dispensation clause comes BEFORE the names, so the formula "Lerena el
     impedimento" - which assumes the surname precedes the word - cannot match.
So the count of eight has been breached twice in one day and is certainly low.
The file says so.
WHAT SURVIVES IS NARROWER AND STILL WORTH SOMETHING: no LERENA-LERENA
dispensation has been found - Alfredo married a Gavarro. But this family DID
marry kin, at the third degree touching the second, in the generation before
Juan Carlos and Maria. That does not answer the standing question. It does
establish that the thing being asked about happened here.
Register: 234 -> 239 people.

commits.subject: The 1880 baptisms settle Josefa, and kill my census reading on a document
commits.body:
I withdrew a claim an hour ago on the strength of a FamilySearch tree
attachment - which is exactly the kind of evidence this archive refuses to
build on, whichever way it points. The withdrawal now rests on a parish act.
*** UNION, MONTEVIDEO, 8 MARCH 1880. *** Two sisters baptised the same day,
probably twins - MARIA CARLOTA and MARIA DE LAS MERCEDES MORATORIO LERENA:
  parents      Fernando Moratorio and JOSEFA LERENA
  abuelos pat. Fernando [Moratorio] and Nicolasa Torres
  abuelos mat. *** AVELINO and AMBROSIA TRAIBEL ***
  padrinos     Francisco Azarola and Manuela Otondo; Juan Arechaga and
               *** MERCEDES LERENA ***
So the Josefa Lerena who married Fernando Moratorio IS the daughter of Avelino
Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel - Josefa Lerena Traibel, 1851-1947. That link was a
tree attachment this morning. It is now a priest naming her parents.
*** AND SO MY CENSUS READING IS DEAD ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN ON INFERENCE. ***
The 1895 line "LERENA de L. JOSEFA" does not show a Lerena married to a Lerena.
She married a Moratorio, and "de L." is the enumerator's shorthand for the
LERENA HOUSEHOLD. Strictly, that the census woman is this Josefa remains an
inference - she is 43 against a birth of 1851, and a VIUDA where a later record
calls Fernando Moratorio "fallecido" - but the Lerena-Lerena reading has nothing
left holding it up.
AVELINO is also now in a parish act rather than only in a death index.
NEW: MERCEDES LERENA, godmother at one of the two fonts and very likely Josefa's
sister - another daughter of Avelino and Ambrosia. The child is named for her.
AND THE NEAR-DUPLICATE CHECK EARNED ITS PLACE AGAIN: it flagged "Maria Carlota
MORATORIO Lerena" against "Maria Carlota LERENA Salvanach". They are different
children ten years apart - Gilberto's daughter baptised at Recoleta in 1890, and
Josefa's at Union in 1880. A Lerena naming habit, not one person. Logged in
CHECKED_PAIRS with the reason, as that list requires.
Register: 229 -> 234 people.

commits.subject: ALEX assessed: its search is broken, and the controls prove it
commits.body:
David asked whether anything on alex.onb.ac.at - the Austrian National
Library's historical law and gazette collection, about five million pages -
could relate to the Lerenas. Checked rather than guessed.
*** THE SEARCH RETURNS ZERO FOR EVERYTHING. *** Its content search gives
"Suchergebnisse TOTAL (0)" together with "Diese Seite steht zur Zeit leider noch
nicht zur Verfugung" for every query. LERENA returns nothing - and so do
"Konsul", "Uruguay" and "Montevideo", each in the identical 166-byte response.
A term certain to appear in five million pages of Austrian law returning zero
is not a null. It is a broken search, and this archive documented exactly that
failure mode on FamilySearch two days ago. The controls took a minute and are
the only reason the zero was not written up as an answer.
THE HONEST ASSESSMENT, INDEPENDENT OF THE OUTAGE. The prior is low: this family
is Uruguayan, Argentine, Spanish, then South African and British, and four days
of records touch the Habsburg lands nowhere.
*** THE ONE REAL HOOK IS CONSULAR. *** The standing open question is whether
Pablo Armando was a Consul General, and consular appointments are gazetted.
Austria-Hungary kept consulates at Montevideo and Buenos Aires and listed its
consuls in the Hof- und Staatshandbuch. If any Lerena held an AUSTRO-HUNGARIAN
honorary consulship in the River Plate, ALEX could show it - and this family is
exactly the class honorary consuls were drawn from: a president at a font, a
general, a judge, an abogado.
It would NOT reach Pablo Armando's own claimed consulship, which was ARGENTINE
and at the Cape. That needs the South African gazette, already on the list.
Logged as an errand to retry when the search recovers, with what to search for.
And a note recorded but not acted on: ALEX is likely far more use to the
DEFRANCESKI side - Istria, Kvarner and Carniola were Habsburg, and Austrian
Landesgesetzblatter are the right law for them. That is this project's sibling
archive and the two are kept strictly apart.

commits.subject: Withdrawing my own claim from an hour ago: "de L." proves nothing
commits.body:
An hour ago I published that the 1895 census showed a Lerena woman married to a
Lerena man, and called it "the exact pattern the whole search turns on". Then I
went looking for the marriage act I had just said would settle it, and found
something that deflates the claim.
*** THERE IS A JOSEFA LERENA WHO MARRIED FERNANDO MORATORIO. *** Uruguayan
civil registration carries her as the mother of Josefa, Eduardo and Maria
MORATORIO LERENA. FamilySearch's tree attaches that woman to profile
K4VN-52H - "Josefa Lerena Traibel, 1851-1947" - the same candidate.
If that is her, she was "de Moratorio", and "de L." on the census line is the
enumerator's shorthand for THIS HOUSEHOLD - the Lerena house - written against
every married woman in it.
WHAT I READ RIGHT AND WHAT I DID NOT. Re-examined at DeepZoom level 13: line 4
does read "Lerena de L. Josefa", and the "de L." is formed identically to the
two lines above. The LETTER was read correctly. *** The INFERENCE was too
confident. *** Lines 2 and 3 are genuinely "de Lerena" - Justiniana, widow of
Luis Lerena, and Julia Salvanach, wife of Gilberto - so both readings fit them
equally, and neither of them tests the shorthand at all. I had no control case
and did not look for one before publishing.
THE TIERING, PLAINLY. The Moratorio marriage records are INDEX-LEVEL civil
registration - real records. The link from that Josefa to Josefa Lerena Traibel
is a TREE ATTACHMENT, which is SECONDARY and exactly the kind of claim this
archive refuses to build on. So neither side of this is settled: what is settled
is that my census reading is not evidence.
The claim never reached a narrative page - it lived in the register, a data file
and a commit message, and the changelog carries that commit as history. The
correction is on /corrections/ and the register row is retitled from "Josefa
LERENA de Lerena" to "Josefa in Gilberto's 1895 household".
Her marriage act still settles it, and still has not been found. The errand now
says Moratorio or Lerena rather than assuming the answer.

commits.subject: Avelino placed at last, and three Josefas kept apart on purpose
commits.body:
Following the Josefa of the 1895 schedule, and the Lerena Traibel branch this
archive has named since its first week finally attaches.
*** JOSEFA LORENA LERENA TRAIBEL, died Montevideo 2 April 1947, aged NINETY-SIX,
born 1851. "Parents: AMBROCIA TRAIBEL, AVELINO LERENA." ***
So AVELINO LERENA is placed - the head of a branch this archive has referred to
for a fortnight without ever naming him in a record. He is the same forename as
the Avelino Lerena who stood godfather at the Catedral de Montevideo in 1833 to
a child of Justa Pastora Lerena, Sancho's daughter. *** That is suggestive and
no more: no record found here names Avelino's own parents, so he is NOT shown to
be Sancho's son, and the branch is not yet joined to the trunk. ***
*** AND THREE JOSEFAS ARE RECORDED AS THREE ROWS, NOT ONE. *** A Josefa Lerena
stood godmother at Montevideo in 1885; a "Lerena de L. Josefa, 43, viuda" was in
Gilberto's Buenos Aires household in 1895; and this Josefa Lerena Traibel was
born in 1851 and died in 1947. The ages agree within a year and the
identification is strong.
They are deliberately not merged. This archive conflated two Arturo Lerenas
earlier in the same week and had to retract a whole branch within the hour; the
discipline that came out of that is what is being applied. data/josefa-lerena-
candidates.tsv sets out what fits, what does not, and what would settle it - her
MARRIAGE record. If she married a Lerena, the census reading "Lerena de Lerena"
is right, and this family contains a Lerena-Lerena marriage one generation
before Juan Carlos and Maria.
AND A LESSON THAT CUTS AGAINST THE LAST TWO DAYS' ENTHUSIASM. Full-text search
for the compound "Lerena Traibel" returns ZERO. The ordinary name index returns
the branch immediately. *** Full text is not a superset of the name index, and a
null in one is not a null in the other. *** Both sweeps are needed, and the
compound-surname file now says so.
Register: 226 -> 229 people.

commits.subject: The 1895 schedule, read as a household at last - and a Lerena who married a Lerena
commits.body:
This archive has cited the 1895 Buenos Aires census since its first week, for
one name at a time. *** The schedule had never been read as a household. ***
Sixteen people on one page, and it settles three things and opens the sharpest
question in the project.
SETTLED. Don Luis Lerena was DEAD BY 1895: Justiniana is entered "Lenguas de L.
Justiniana, m, 73, VIUDA". His death window closes to 1850-1895, and she was in
Argentina thirteen years earlier than the 1908 evidence.
SETTLED. Gilberto had a TRADE: "CORREDOR DE COMERCIO", a commercial broker,
aged 41. This archive has had him as a breeder and co-founder of the Argentine
Stud Book, which is what he is remembered for. In his own house he told the
enumerator he was a broker.
SETTLED, AND IT IS A CORRECTION TO THIS ARCHIVE. The register carried "Maria
E. C. Lerena, b.1869, daughter of Gilberto (1854)" - which would have made him
FIFTEEN, and which a new consistency check flagged yesterday as impossible. The
schedule shows her SOLTERA at 26, in a house that also holds a JOSEFA, widow of
43. She is not his daughter. "Daughter" was this archive reading a household,
and the household now says otherwise.
*** AND WHAT IT OPENS. *** Line 4 reads "LERENA de L[erena], JOSEFA, m, 43,
VIUDA, R. Oriental". On the two lines above her the same enumerator writes
married women as [maiden surname] + "de L." - Lenguas de Lerena, Salvanach de
Lerena. If he is consistent, *** JOSEFA WAS BORN A LERENA AND MARRIED A
LERENA. ***
That is the exact pattern the whole search turns on. Pablo Armando's enrolment
card names his parents JUAN CARLOS LERENA and MARIA LERENA, and the standing
question is whether Maria was a Lerena by birth - a marriage between kin, which
would have needed a dispensation. A Lerena-Lerena marriage in this very family,
one generation earlier, would show the pattern exists.
*** Stated as a reading of an abbreviation in an enumerator's hand, not as a
fact. *** Josefa's own marriage record would settle it and has not been looked
for - logged as an errand, with the note that the dispensation sweep which
concluded no Lerena-Lerena marriage exists is itself now known to be blind to
compound surnames.
She is also, almost certainly, the JOSEFA LERENA who stood godmother to
Gilberto's son Raul at the Catedral de Montevideo in 1885 - a woman this archive
met and could not place.

commits.subject: The living-people rule now gates this build
commits.body:
David's rule across the estate: a LIVING PERSON IS NAMED AND NOTHING MORE —
no date of birth, no date of death, no place. And his age rule: anyone more
than eighty years old is treated as deceased, because an archive that cannot
say whether somebody is alive has to presume something and that is what it
presumes.
Until now Falco was the only archive with a guard, and it had one because the
same date leaked three times — twice from code that read correctly in the
source. Every one was caught by reading the BUILT HTML. Its design is now in
the kit and runs here.
It takes the full date strings the DATA attaches to a living person and
asserts those literal strings appear nowhere in the build. Falco's two earlier
designs are not repeated: bare years pass vacuously on a genealogy site, and
name-near-date fires on every homonym. Identity lives in the data, not the
markup.
An archive that omits living people altogether passes with nothing to check,
which is correct rather than a gap — that rule is stricter than this one.
Verified by planting a guarded date in a build and watching it fail.

commits.subject: The cemetery roll confirms the death a third time
commits.body:
Continuing the compound-surname sweep. "Lerena Lenguas" returns seven
documents, five of them already known - and one that is new and settles
something.
*** DIRECCION DE CEMENTERIOS, MONTEVIDEO - "Relacion de los individuos que han
fallecido en el mes de Diciembre de 1901". *** A civil mortality return, day by
day. Against day 24:
  "24 ... LUIS LERENA LENGUAS"
Between Lucrecia Sosa and Emilia Zanola de Sanchez.
So the death of 24 December 1901 now rests on THREE independent documents: the
civil death act No. 216, the cemetery office's own roll, and his widow's sworn
statement seven years later when she registered their son's birth. And it
settles in the plainest way that he was BURIED AT MONTEVIDEO.
That matters more than it sounds. Two days ago this archive had published, in
good faith, that he was not in the indexed Uruguayan death registers at all -
a null produced by searching a surname that was filed under SERENA.
*** AND IT WAS FOUND ONLY BY THE COMPOUND SURNAME. *** A search on LERENA does
not reach a table of names like this one: the entry is four words in a column,
with no parish formula around it to match on.

commits.subject: A ninth dispensation, missed by this archive's own sweep of that register
commits.body:
The compound-surname technique found its third and sharpest result, and it is
a correction to work published here on 13 September.
*** EMA SIXTA'S MARRIAGE DISPENSATION EXISTS, AND THE SWEEP MISSED IT. ***
Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, June 1913:
  "Senor Provisor, JOSE PEDRO MASSERA ... digo: que debiendo contraer
   matrimonio con Dona EMA SIXTA LERENA JUANICO, FELIGRESA DE LA METROPOLITANA
   ... ocurro a V.S. suplicando quiera dispensarme UNA CONCILIAR PROCLAMA ...
   Montevideo, Junio 19 de 1913"
Eleven days before her wedding to the philosopher Massera.
*** AND THE REASON IT WAS MISSED IS STRUCTURAL, NOT BAD LUCK. *** This archive
swept that register on the formula "LERENA FELIGRESA", which assumes the parish
follows the surname immediately. She is written "Lerena JUANICO, feligresa".
The compound surname sits between the two words and the phrase cannot match.
EVERY CHILD OF BOTH MONTEVIDEO COUPLES CARRIES A COMPOUND SURNAME - Lerena
Juanico, Lerena Lenguas, Lerena Salvanach. The sweep was blind to exactly the
people this archive cares most about.
The dispensation file's headline conclusion - no Lerena-Lerena dispensation in
seventy-six years, every Lerena marrying out - is NOT withdrawn. But it rests on
a search now known to be blind, and it is marked as needing a re-run rather than
left standing as though nothing had happened.
THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN TWO DAYS THE SURNAME HAS HIDDEN A RECORD, and
/searched/ now carries all three together: a death filed under SERENA that a
1,502-row sweep walked past; a military rank read as a forename, making a
"Geraldo Dios Lenguas" who never existed; and now a phrase search that cannot
see a woman because her surname is two words long.
The rule is written down: search the COMPOUND surname, the MOTHER'S name, and
the rarest stable word in the household. The bare surname is the search of last
resort, not first.
Also swept and recorded: "Lerena Traibel" returns ZERO, so that branch does not
attach here; Avelino Lerena is real and in the right city in 1836 - godfather to
a foundling named ABELINA for him - but no record names his parents, so he is
still not shown to be Sancho's son.
And the last consistency warning is cleared: Ema Sixta's row now carries an ark.

commits.subject: The sixth child was a Juez de Paz, found by searching the compound surname
commits.body:
Items 13-15, and the last of them turned into the best find of the round.
*** JOSE JULIO LERENA JUANICO WAS A JUDGE. *** Thirty-five Montevideo civil
marriage acts of 1902-1914 open with the formula:
  "Por ante mi JULIO LERENA JUANICO, JUEZ DE PAZ y OFICIAL DEL ESTADO CIVIL de
   la Primera Seccion del Departamento de Montevideo"
One was read in full - Maronas, 28 August 1909. The compound surname is this
family's and no other in the archive; he is the only JULIO among the seven
children; he would be thirty in 1909. Recorded as STRONG BUT NOT PROVED: no act
read so far gives the judge's own parents.
*** AND IT EXPLAINS THE ODDEST THING IN HIS RECORD. *** Jose Julio was born in
March 1879 and his birth was not registered until September 1908, when his
widowed mother of sixty-four swore it before a Juzgado de Paz. This archive
guessed that was proof of birth for a wedding. A man appointed OFICIAL DEL
ESTADO CIVIL needs it rather more than a bridegroom does.
IT WAS FOUND BY SEARCHING THE COMPOUND SURNAME - "Lerena Juanico" - which this
archive had never tried in four days of searching LERENA. That is the same
lesson as the SERENA misindexing and the "Geraldo Dios" ghost, arriving a third
time: the surname is the least reliable handle on this family.
The same search gives a route to the last missing ark, Ema Sixta's marriage of
1913, which should be in those same Montevideo registers.
1882 carried to acts 957-962 - 798 consecutive baptisms read act by act.
What this family now holds on the record: a GENERAL, an ABOGADO, a HACENDADO, a
professor of philosophy by marriage, the co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book,
a PRESIDENT at the font in 1831, an ORIBE for a bride in 1836 - and a JUDGE.
And still no Juan Carlos. Every one of them is documented and none is Pablo
Armando's father.

commits.subject: Her name is Oribe, and this site had it right before I did
commits.body:
Items 8-12 of the fourth fifteen, and a correction that stings.
*** THE FIRST WIFE IS CAROLINA ORIBE, NOT OLIVA. *** I recorded Oliva twice on
14 September - once explicitly to correct an earlier "not confidently legible"
reading - and called it settled. The source of the error was FamilySearch's
index of the 1836 petition, which says Oliva. I read the image expecting Oliva
and saw it.
A Catedral baptism of 4 JULY 1837, in another book and another hand, names
"D. LUIS LERENA y Dna CAROLINA ORIBE" standing godparents to his brother's
child. The petition, re-opened and magnified, reads ORIBE too - a clear b.
*** AND THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN HYPOTHESES PAGE HAD CARRIED, FROM A SECONDARY TREE,
THAT HE MARRIED FIRSTLY A DAUGHTER OF AN ORIBE. *** That line has been on the
site the whole time. I never checked my reading against the page I was editing.
The secondary source was right and the index was wrong.
THE SAME ACT GIVES A SECOND BROTHER: D. PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA, "natural de
esta", same abuelos paternos D. Sancho y Dna Maria Fernandez, married to Vicenta
Vega of Cerro Largo, with a daughter Leonarda Margarita born February 1837. And
it proves Carolina was ALIVE IN JULY 1837 - married September 1836, alive that
July, dead by March 1842.
WHAT ORIBE MEANS, STATED WITH CARE. Manuel Oribe was President of Uruguay
1835-1838 and founder of the Blancos. This family's other documented padrino is
FRUCTUOSO RIVERA, his rival and the founder of the Colorados, who stood at a
Lerena font in 1831. So within five years: Rivera at the font, an Oribe for a
bride - the two men whose quarrel became the Guerra Grande. *** Nothing read
here makes Carolina kin to the president. *** Oribe is a surname, not a proof,
and no record yet names her parents. Recorded as a question, not a descent.
TWO NULLS RE-RUN PROPERLY, since the recordCountry filter was found to break
full-text silently:
- "Juan Carlos Lerena" across the whole corpus returns TWO documents, both
  already known and neither ours. THE CENTRAL NULL HOLDS.
- No child of Luis Lerena and Carolina Oribe. And this null is worth something,
